info.title: Factuarea Public API
info.description:
Public REST API for invoicing in Spain — manage invoices, quotes, proformas, delivery notes, products, clients and webhooks.

## Authentication

The API authenticates with a secret **API key**, sent on every request as:

```
Authorization: Bearer fact_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

or, alternatively, in the `X-API-Key` header. The key is issued from the Factuarea portal and must NEVER be exposed in public clients (browser, mobile apps).

## Environments: `live` and `test`

Each API key belongs to one of two environments, unambiguously identifiable by its **prefix**:

| Prefix | Environment | Data it operates on | External effects |
|---------|---------|---------------------------|------------------|
| `fact_live_` | **live** (production) | Your real company | Real: legal fiscal numbering, VeriFactu→AEAT, emails to clients, outbound webhooks |
| `fact_test_` | **test** (sandbox) | An isolated *sandbox* company | **Neutralized** (see below) |

The prefix is the **source of truth** for the environment: a `fact_test_` key always operates in test mode and a `fact_live_` key always in live. There is no request parameter that changes the environment — it is determined by the key.

### Data isolation (sandbox)

`fact_test_` keys operate on a dedicated **sandbox company** (a technical "twin company" of the account holder, automatically provisioned the first time test mode is used, which inherits the plan of your real company for faithful *feature-gating*). Thanks to per-company data isolation:

- Resources created with a `fact_test_` key are **not visible** from a `fact_live_` key, and vice versa.
- Test fiscal numbering uses the sandbox's own series and **never** consumes or alters the sequential numbering of your production series.

The functional surface is **identical** in both environments: the same endpoints and operations are available in test as in live.

### External effects neutralized in test

When you operate with a `fact_test_` key (sandbox environment), outbound effects are **disabled** so you can test your integration without real consequences:

- **VeriFactu**: the Alta record is created locally, but **not transmitted to AEAT**.
- **Email**: document emails are **not delivered** to real recipients.
- **Webhooks**: events are **not delivered** to your external HTTP endpoints.

In `live`, all these effects fire normally.

> **Recommendation**: always integrate and test first with a `fact_test_` key. Once your flow works, switch to the `fact_live_` prefix to operate in production.

post.description: Accept a TAX ID TRANSFER by presenting its `secret`: the tax ID the transfer covers moves to the account in the path, which is the credential account. It is an action on the collection and carries no identifier in the path, because whoever accepts does NOT own the transfer and cannot address it by id — all they hold is a secret someone gave them. The body carries the `secret` and nothing else: the tax ID is named by the TRANSFER, not by whoever presents it, so a `company_id` here is rejected rather than silently ignored. Accepting locks the transfer, re-validates that its tax ID still belongs to the issuing account, moves the membership (together with the sandbox company of the tax ID when the issuing account holds it), prunes the tax ID out of the scope of the issuing account credentials, removes from the tax ID the people of the issuing account who do not also belong to the receiving account (closing their web sessions and the OAuth tokens bound to it), grants `owner` of the tax ID to whoever administers the receiving account if they had no access to it, records the trail and notifies the issuing account owner, all inside ONE transaction: a transfer is accepted at most once even under concurrent requests. The 200 publishes the consumed transfer — its public `id`, the tax ID, its expiry and `status: consumed` — and never the issuing account, the consumption instant or the secret. Requires an administrative role in at least one tax ID of the RECEIVING account: 403 `forbidden_action` otherwise. The incoming tax ID becomes an ADDITIONAL tax ID of the receiving account — except for an account registered without a tax ID, where it becomes its titular and is not charged —, so the additional tax ID gate runs BEFORE anything moves, and a rejection leaves the transfer valid and the tax ID in the issuing account: the credential must reach the titular company of the receiving account, which pays it (403 `forbidden_action` otherwise), with an effective access that allows writing (403 `company_read_only` when it is read-only, `view`), the receiving account must be billed by itself (403 `billing_managed_by_provider` otherwise), hold a current plan (402 `additional_nif_plan_required` otherwise) that allows additional tax IDs — `empresario` or `enterprise`, trial included (403 `additional_nif_not_in_plan` otherwise) — and stay within its cap of active additional tax IDs (422 `business_rule_violation` with subcode `additional_nif_limit_reached`). In live mode with a paid subscription the additional tax ID is charged on acceptance: with no payment method on file it returns 402 `payment_method_required` (with `error.details.payment_setup_url`) and a declined charge returns 402 `additional_nif_charge_failed`; if the move fails after charging, the charge is compensated. Returns 422 `nif_transfer_invalid` when the secret matches no transfer, the transfer was already consumed or revoked, it is addressed to a different account, or its tax ID has already changed account (all with the SAME body: telling them apart would say whether that secret ever existed), 422 `nif_transfer_expired` when the transfer is still unconsumed but its window has passed — a DIFFERENT code on purpose, so the holder knows to ask for another one instead of looking for a mistake on their side —, 422 `business_rule_violation` with subcode `account_must_keep_one_nif` when the issuing account would keep no active tax ID, 409 `resource_conflict` when an account registered without a tax ID already holds business data in its empty company, 422 `idempotency_key_required` because moving a tax ID this way is irreversible, and 404 `account_not_found` when `{account}` is not the credential account. Requires the `nif_transfers:write` scope, which `*` does not cover: the API key must list it explicitly.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of your account. Get it from `GET /v1/me` (`data.account.id`).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

X-Request-Id.description: Identifier of this request (`req_` + ULID, or the value you sent, up to 40 characters). Quote it when contacting support.

RateLimit-Limit.description: Canonical rate-limit field (RFC 9331): maximum number of requests allowed in the current rate limit window (60 seconds). Prefer this field over its legacy twin `X-RateLimit-Limit`, which carries the same value and is kept only for backwards compatibility.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Canonical rate-limit field (RFC 9331): number of requests remaining in the current rate limit window before receiving a 429. Prefer this field over its legacy twin `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, which carries the same value and is kept only for backwards compatibility.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Canonical rate-limit field (RFC 9331): SECONDS REMAINING until the rate limit window resets — a duration, not a clock reading. Its legacy twin `X-RateLimit-Reset` expresses the SAME instant as a Unix timestamp, so the two values are deliberately different and must not be swapped: read this one as a delay and that one as an epoch.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Legacy rate-limit header, kept for backwards compatibility; the canonical field is `RateLimit-Limit`. Maximum number of requests allowed in the current rate limit window (60 seconds).

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Legacy rate-limit header, kept for backwards compatibility; the canonical field is `RateLimit-Remaining`. Number of requests remaining in the current rate limit window before receiving a 429.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Legacy rate-limit header, kept for backwards compatibility; the canonical field is `RateLimit-Reset`. Unix timestamp (seconds) at which the rate limit window resets and the counter returns to its maximum. Careful: the canonical `RateLimit-Reset` publishes the same instant as SECONDS REMAINING, so the two values never match.

Factuarea-Version.description: Effective API version (`YYYY-MM-DD`, Stripe-style date versioning) resolved for this request: the `Factuarea-Version` request header if sent, otherwise the version pinned on the API key, otherwise the latest version. Present on every response.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: Present with value `"true"` only when this response was replayed from the idempotency cache for a repeated `Idempotency-Key` (same key, same request fingerprint). Absent on the first, freshly executed request.

403.description: The request is authenticated but not allowed: the API key lacks the required scope (`insufficient_scope`), the company does not include the public API (`addon_not_active`), the module is not available with a test key (`module_not_available_in_sandbox`), the credential does not reach the titular company of the receiving account or its holder does not administer it (`forbidden_action`), the effective access of the credential to that company is read-only (`company_read_only`), the plan of the receiving account does not allow additional tax IDs (`additional_nif_not_in_plan`) or its billing is managed by another account (`billing_managed_by_provider`). The plan gate of the transfer scopes runs when the credential is issued, never on this request.

X-Request-Id.description: Identifier of this request (`req_` + ULID, or the value you sent, up to 40 characters). Quote it when contacting support.

409.description: The request conflicts with data that already exists or with a request running at the same time. `resource_conflict` with `subcode` `empty_registration_company_not_empty`: the empty company created at sign-up was going to be replaced by the transferred NIF, but it already has business data. Nothing was transferred. `customer_offer_phase_incompatible` with `param` `quantity`: the conditions already acquired for the additional tax ID seat cannot be preserved by this purchase. `details.reason` is `phase_incompatible`. No company is created or activated and no charge is attempted. `customer_offer_operation_in_progress`: an operation for the same concept is still pending. Continue that operation instead of starting another. `customer_offer_legacy_outcome_unknown`: a previous billing operation of the account is still being verified. `details.operation_id` is that operation; read its state before repeating the request.

X-Request-Id.description: Identifier of this request (`req_` + ULID, or the value you sent, up to 40 characters). Quote it when contacting support.

402.description: The operation requires a payment that could not be completed: either no payment method is on file (`error.details.payment_setup_url` links to the Billing Portal where it can be set up), the immediate charge was declined by the payment provider, the account lacks the plan or add-on this operation bills against, the annual document limit is reached (`plan_limit_exceeded`, with `error.details.period_end` indicating the end of the period — wait until it has ended or upgrade the plan to continue now), or the account has reached its maximum usage (`storage_quota_exceeded`, raised by upload operations such as signing a delivery note or attaching a file to an expense — contact support before retrying). Nothing was created or modified — resolve the cause and retry the same request. Version note: `error.type` is `payment_required_error` from `Factuarea-Version: 2026-09-01` onwards; earlier versions receive `invalid_request_error` for the three codes that predate that cut (`payment_method_required`, `employee_seat_payment_method_required` and `employee_seat_charge_failed`; every other 402 code, such as `addon_required`, `plan_limit_exceeded` or the additional tax ID codes, is newer and always carries `payment_required_error`). `error.code` is stable across every version.

post.description: Accept the deviation the three-way match found and settle the match as matched. The body carries the reason in writing and it is required: deciding to pay a supplier something different from what was agreed is recorded with its justification. The response is the match of that invoice with its resulting state and its line detail. Like its two siblings, it needs the WRITE scope of the PURCHASE ORDER and not the one of the invoice. Irreversible, and this is the part to read before calling it: accepting marks the purchase order as BILLED, and billed is a terminal state with no way out — no published operation, not unlinking and not cancelling the invoice, takes the order back to where it was. It requires an `Idempotency-Key` when the policy of your credential demands it, and repeating it with the same key returns the result of the first call without producing a second effect.

post.description: Turn a reorder suggestion into purchase orders. The body carries the articles you accept with their quantity and the supplier offer each one is bought under, and the result is one purchase order in DRAFT per supplier, each with a line per accepted article, returned with its public id and its number, plus the articles that were left out with their reason. It is all or nothing: either every order is created or none is. Articles or offers of another company are rejected as if they did not exist, and the orders always belong to the company of the path. It is NOT published as irreversible, because the orders are born in draft and can be deleted — but read this before retrying: a suggestion is not a document with an identity, so accepting the same one twice creates a SECOND set of drafts. Send an `Idempotency-Key` if you may retry; it is not mandatory here, but it is honoured when it travels.

402.description: The operation requires a payment that could not be completed: either no payment method is on file (`error.details.payment_setup_url` links to the Billing Portal where it can be set up), the immediate charge was declined by the payment provider, the account lacks the plan or add-on this operation bills against, the annual document limit is reached (`plan_limit_exceeded`, with `error.details.period_end` indicating the end of the period — wait until it has ended or upgrade the plan to continue now), or the account has reached its maximum usage (`storage_quota_exceeded`, raised by upload operations such as signing a delivery note or attaching a file to an expense — contact support before retrying). Nothing was created or modified — resolve the cause and retry the same request. Version note: `error.type` is `payment_required_error` from `Factuarea-Version: 2026-09-01` onwards; earlier versions receive `invalid_request_error` for the three codes that predate that cut (`payment_method_required`, `employee_seat_payment_method_required` and `employee_seat_charge_failed`; every other 402 code, such as `addon_required`, `plan_limit_exceeded` or the additional tax ID codes, is newer and always carries `payment_required_error`). `error.code` is stable across every version.

post.description: Reactivate several deactivated (`inactive`) tax IDs of the account in one operation, charging the combined additional tax IDs in a single invoice. Pass `company_ids`. The gate is atomic: a tax ID the system suspended (its payer was blocked or its management ended) rejects the whole batch with 422 `business_rule_violation` and subcode `nif_suspended_by_system` before anything is charged; every tax ID is validated (it belongs to the account and is `inactive`, 422 `business_rule_violation` otherwise) before any charge, so if one is invalid the whole batch is rejected without charging or activating any; a tax ID that is not part of the account returns 404 for the whole batch. The batch then goes through the additional tax ID gate: the credential must reach the titular company of the account (403 `forbidden_action` otherwise), the account must be billed by itself (403 `billing_managed_by_provider` otherwise), hold a current plan (402 `additional_nif_plan_required` otherwise) that allows additional tax IDs — `empresario` or `enterprise`, trial included (403 `additional_nif_not_in_plan` otherwise) — and keep the resulting active additional tax IDs within its cap (422 `business_rule_violation` with subcode `additional_nif_limit_reached`). In live mode with a paid subscription the additional tax ID is charged immediately: with no payment method on file it returns 402 `payment_method_required` (`error.details.payment_setup_url` links to where to set it up) and a declined charge returns 402 `additional_nif_charge_failed`; no tax ID is activated in either case. The person who issued the credential must be an owner or admin of the account, with the `user_management` section available: otherwise 403 `forbidden_action`, before anything is charged or changed. A credential whose effective access to that tax ID is read-only (`view`) returns 403 `company_read_only`, and one with no access returns the same 404 as a tax ID outside the account.

post.description: Reactivate a deactivated (`inactive`) tax ID of the account. The reactivated tax ID is an ADDITIONAL tax ID of the account, so it goes through the additional tax ID gate before anything changes: the credential must reach the titular company of the account, which pays it (403 `forbidden_action` otherwise), the account must be billed by itself (403 `billing_managed_by_provider` otherwise), hold a current plan (402 `additional_nif_plan_required` otherwise) that allows additional tax IDs — `empresario` or `enterprise`, trial included (403 `additional_nif_not_in_plan` otherwise) — and stay within its cap of active additional tax IDs (422 `business_rule_violation` with subcode `additional_nif_limit_reached`). In live mode with a paid subscription the additional tax ID is charged immediately: with no payment method on file it returns 402 `payment_method_required` (`error.details.payment_setup_url` links to where to set it up) and a declined charge returns 402 `additional_nif_charge_failed`; the tax ID only becomes `active` if the charge succeeds. A tax ID still covered for the current period is reactivated without a new charge, and trial, enterprise without a paid subscription and a test account are not charged. A tax ID that the system suspended (its payer was blocked or its management ended) cannot be activated by hand, whatever the payment state: it returns 422 `business_rule_violation` with subcode `nif_suspended_by_system` before anything is charged, and it resumes on its own when the payment or the management is resolved. A tax ID that is not part of the account returns 404, like one outside the credential scope. The person who issued the credential must be an owner or admin of the account, with the `user_management` section available: otherwise 403 `forbidden_action`, before anything is charged or changed. A credential whose effective access to that tax ID is read-only (`view`) returns 403 `company_read_only`, and one with no access returns the same 404 as a tax ID outside the account.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. post.description: Create a new person as a member of the ACCOUNT with an account `role` (`admin` or `member`; ownership is transferred, never assigned) and the required `grants` list (it may be empty; only a `member` carries grants, each one a tax ID of the account by its `company_id` UUID and a `level`: `view` or `operate`). The person receives an email to verify their address. Returns 201 with the member and a `Location` header. Because it changes the team of the whole account, the credential scope must cover every tax ID of the account (403 `forbidden_action` otherwise). Returns 400 `parameter_missing` when `grants` is absent, 422 `grants_only_for_member` for grants on an `admin`, 422 `grant_company_not_in_account` when a grant names a tax ID outside the account or your credential scope, and 422 `business_rule_violation` when the email is already registered (add existing people with an invitation), a tax ID repeats or the plan user limit is reached. Requires the `members:write` scope, which `*` does not cover: the API key must list it explicitly.

post.description: Add a single line to a purchase order — the article, its variant, the supplier offer it is bought under and the quantity in the purchase unit — without resending the lines it already has. The unit cost, the conversion factor and the tax percentages are taken from the supplier offer at the moment the line is added and are not part of the body: a later change in the catalog does not move an order that already exists, and a later receipt converts with the factor the order stored. The quantity received is never writable: it moves only by posting or cancelling a goods receipt. An order that has left the state that admits editing rejects the call as a business rule violation.

post.description: Declare one package on the shipment of a delivery note: its reference, its weight in kilograms, its three dimensions in centimetres and its notes, all of them optional — a package can be declared with nothing at all, which is what a warehouse does when it only needs to count parcels. Weight and dimensions travel as decimal strings with two decimal places and carry the ceiling of their column, so a value above it is rejected with 422 before anything is written. The POSITION is not part of the body: it is assigned deterministically as the next one of the note, so the packages keep the order in which they were declared. The total weight of the shipment grows by what you declare here, because that total is the sum of the packages and is recalculated on every read. Returns the package that was created with its public id, and a location header pointing at it. It is not published as irreversible: a package that was just added is edited or removed with its sibling operations.
post.summary: Add a package to a delivery note

get.description: List the packages declared on the shipment of a delivery note, together with how many there are and their total weight, which is the SUM of the individual weights added up on each read and never a stored total. Each package carries its public id, its position in the shipment, its reference, its weight in kilograms, its three dimensions in centimetres and its notes. Weight and dimensions travel as decimal strings with two decimal places, so nothing is lost to rounding. All of those fields are always present and any of them may be null: a package can be declared with nothing but its position. A delivery note with no packages answers with an empty list and a total weight of zero, not with an error, and a note of another company answers exactly like one that does not exist.

post.description:
Withdraw an issued invoice **with a documented reason**. `reason` is required here (3–500 characters); that is the only difference from `POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/void`, which performs exactly the same operation and persists a placeholder when you omit it. Prefer this endpoint whenever the reason has to be traceable — the text you send is kept in the invoice audit trail and, when the company is enrolled in VeriFactu, becomes the `motivo` of the AEAT cancellation record.

The invoice moves to `annulled` and `voided_at` starts reporting when that happened. The status is terminal and the operation is **irreversible**: there is no transition back to `sent` or `draft`, and the correlative number of the series is neither released nor reused.

**Effect on AEAT.** With VeriFactu enabled, annulling queues an *anulación* record to AEAT **asynchronously**: a `200` means the invoice is annulled in Factuarea, not that AEAT has already processed it — poll the invoice for its VeriFactu status. The original *alta* record is not deleted or rewritten; AEAT keeps both entries, the issuance and its cancellation. With VeriFactu inactive the annulment is purely internal and nothing is transmitted.

**Annul or correct?** Annulment withdraws the whole document; it produces no amending document, so it never restates an amount. A corrective (`POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/corrective`) creates a **new** invoice that amends the original and is the path when the operation was real and only part of it was wrong, or when the money has to be returned.

**Annulling an operation that was already paid.** By default an invoice with live payments is rejected with 422 `invoice_has_active_collections`. When the invoice was issued by mistake — a duplicated charge at a kiosk, a sale the terminal did not complete — send `revert_collections: true` (default `false`): in ONE atomic operation every live payment is reverted with the reserved reason `issued_in_error` and the invoice is annulled. If any step fails, no payment stays reverted and the invoice is not annulled. The option does not relax anything else: a corrective invoice, an invoice already fully corrected or a status that cannot be annulled are still rejected, and the payments are reverted with the same trail (instant, author and the annulment reason as the note) as any other reversal. It is an annulment, not a refund: if the customer has to get the money back, issue a corrective instead. `POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/void` has no such option.

Limits: only `issued`, `sent` or `overdue` can be annulled. A `draft` is not annulled but deleted; `cancelled` and `annulled` return 422. An invoice that **is** a corrective can never be annulled — issue a new corrective of the original instead. Use `GET /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/can-annul` to check eligibility, whether the live payments are the only obstacle (`requires_collection_reversal`) and whether a VeriFactu cancellation record will be created, before posting here.

**Signing certificate (NO VERI*FACTU).** Only when the company has VeriFactu enabled in NO VERI*FACTU mode, the annulment billing record of this operation is signed with the company's electronic certificate (art. 6.c and 14 of Order HAC/1177/2024), and a certificate that is missing, expired, revoked, issued for another tax id or unreadable is rejected **before** the invoice is annulled: 422 `verifactu_not_eligible` with `error.subcode: signing_certificate_unavailable`; `error.param` says what is missing (`certificate`: the company certificate; `representation`: the representation that lets Factuarea sign on its behalf is not active; `system_certificate`: the Factuarea certificate is unavailable, nothing for you to fix). The invoice stays exactly as it was (issued and not annulled) and nothing is consumed: upload a valid certificate in Settings → Digital certificate (or register the representation in the third-party remission modes) and repeat the same call. Companies that have not enabled VeriFactu, and companies in VERI*FACTU mode (whose records are not signed), are never blocked by this rule.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

post.description: Apply a bulk import of managed accounts and own tax IDs from a file (`multipart/form-data`: `accounts_file`, optional `customers_file` and `options`) and receive **201 Created** with the result of the execution. The import is DECLARATIVE and NOT atomic: every applicable row (`VALID`, `WARNING`, `ALREADY_EXISTS`) is applied on its own, and a row that fails is reported as `BLOCKED` or `ERROR` without undoing the others. A new `managed_account` row provisions a separate account charged on the `managed-accounts` subscription of your account, with the `access_level` of the row (`operate` by default); a new `own_nif` row registers an additional tax ID charged to your account. It never opens a checkout: it charges your existing subscription, and a row that cannot be charged comes out `BLOCKED` with its reason. Re-applying the same file reconciles: existing accounts and tax IDs come out `ALREADY_EXISTS`, their visible name, language and fiscal profile are updated while the account is not claimed, and nothing is duplicated nor charged twice; a different plan for an existing account is only applied with `options.confirm_plan_changes` (otherwise the row is `WARNING`). Every new live `managed_account` row returns its `claim_token` and `claim_url` EXACTLY ONCE, in this response only; with `options.send_email: true` the link is emailed to the holder instead and both are `null`. An idempotent replay returns the same result with every voucher as `null`: vouchers are never stored in the clear, not even in the idempotency cache. The customers of `customers_file` are imported into the tax ID of their row with the existing contact importer, only where your account can `operate` it (`customers_status`), and with `options.apply_customers_to_own_company` the ones without `account_ref` go to your own company in focus (`own_company_customers`). The environment is the one of the key: with a `fact_test_` key the `managed_account` rows create or reconcile TEST accounts, with no charge and no voucher, and the `own_nif` rows are `ERROR` `live_credential_required`. Imports of your account are applied one at a time. No `Location` header is returned: an execution has no public read operation. Limits: 5 MB per file, 100 rows in `accounts_file` and 1,000 in `customers_file`, checked before reading any row. Requires the privileged `accounts:write` scope, which `*` does not cover. Returns 403 `privileged_scope_required` without the account provider privilege granted by Factuarea or when the person who issued the key is no longer an owner or admin of your account, 409 `import_in_progress` while another import of your account is running or while the platform is already applying the maximum number of simultaneous imports (repeating the same file later is safe), 413 `import_file_too_large` for a file over 5 MB, 422 `import_row_limit_exceeded` for too many rows, 422 `import_file_invalid` for an unreadable file or a missing column, 422 on an unknown option, 422 `idempotency_key_required` because applying is irreversible, and 429 above 5 applications per minute or once the daily import quota of your account is exhausted.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

post.description: Approve a return that is still requested. It takes no body. Approving STAMPS the definitive number of the return series, which is what makes this step matter: the number is consumed at this moment and there is no operation that gives it back, so a return that is approved and later deleted would leave a permanent gap — and that is why an approved return can no longer be deleted. From here the return can be received or rejected. A return that is not in the requested status is rejected with 422 naming the transition that is not allowed, and one of another company answers as not found. Irreversible, because of the number it consumes: it requires an `Idempotency-Key` when the policy of your credential demands it, and repeating the call with the same key produces the effect once.

Returns 200 with the resolved correction.

post.description: Archive a contact: a reversible removal that parks it out of the day-to-day operations while keeping it fully readable. Archiving is ALWAYS allowed — invoices, contracts or supplier offers referencing the contact never block it — and it is idempotent: archiving an already archived contact returns 200 and keeps the first `archived_at`. The contact keeps its identity, its roles with their status, the directional profiles, the bank accounts, the legacy aliases and every document, stays retrievable by `id` with `is_archived: true`, and can be brought back with `POST /companies/{company}/contacts/{contact}/restore`. It requires `contacts:delete`, like the other two removals, because it takes the contact out of the operation. To make the contact disappear from the application instead, use `DELETE /companies/{company}/contacts/{contact}`. A UUID owned by another company returns the same 404 `contact_not_found` as an unknown UUID.

delete.description: Archive a warehouse. The operation RETIRES the warehouse from the operation and does NOT delete its row: the warehouse and its history are preserved, so the documents, the stock movements and the transfers that point at it keep pointing at something. It stops being returned among the active ones and its code is freed, so a later creation of the same company can reuse it. A warehouse that is still occupied is not archived: one with active locations, or one taking part as origin or destination in a transfer that has not reached a terminal status, returns 422 with the code that names that condition. Archiving the warehouse that was the default one leaves the company without a default — no other warehouse inherits the mark — and the default read starts failing until you set a new one. It returns no content. Irreversible: this API publishes no operation that brings an archived warehouse back, so it requires an `Idempotency-Key` when the policy of your credential demands it.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

delete.description: Archive a location of a warehouse. The operation RETIRES the location from the operation and does NOT delete its row: the row and its history are preserved, it stops being returned among the active locations of its warehouse, and its code is freed for a later one. A location that still has an active child is not archived: it returns 422 as a business rule violation and the hierarchy is left exactly as it was, so archive the children first. It returns no content. Irreversible: this API publishes no operation that brings an archived location back, so it requires an `Idempotency-Key` when the policy of your credential demands it.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

post.description: Ask for the availability of up to 100 articles in a single round trip. The body carries a list of references — each one the public id or the code of an article — and the response returns ONE row per reference SENT, in the order you sent them, so you can match them positionally. A reference that does not resolve is not an error and does not abort the rest: its row comes back marked as not found with its reason, and nothing of the article it might belong to is revealed. Repeated references are rejected, so send each one once. It is a read that travels as a POST because the list goes in the body: nothing is created, nothing is modified and no idempotency key is needed.

post.description:
Leave a company able to issue documents in one call: for every document type of the public surface (`invoice`, `quote`, `delivery_note`, `proforma`) that has no active series, create its default series with the canonical code and name. No request body.

**What comes back**

- One entry per document type, with a `status` of `created`, `existing` or `no_default`.
- `no_default` means the type has active series but none marked as default — archiving the default demotes it without promoting a replacement — and the company still cannot issue that document.
- Treat `no_default` as work still to do, not as success: the active series arrive in `candidates` and you resolve it with `POST /v1/companies/{company}/series/{series}/default`.

**Why it does not choose for you**

Picking which series numbers a company's documents has registry consequences only you can decide, so the bootstrap never promotes one for you.

**Calling it twice**

- Idempotent by business rule: a second call creates nothing, fails nothing and reports the state again.
- INDEPENDENT of the `Idempotency-Key` header: with the header, a repeated key replays the original body — `created` entries included — instead of reporting the current state.
post.summary: Bootstrap the default series of a company

post.description: Archive up to 500 contacts by `ids` with partial success. Archiving is always allowed and reversible: every contact keeps its identity, history, aliases and documents, stays retrievable with `is_archived: true` and can be brought back one by one with `POST /companies/{company}/contacts/{contact}/restore`. Every UUID is evaluated inside the authenticated tenant; the only per-row failure is a UUID the company does not own (`contact_not_found`), returned with `id`, `error_code` and a Spanish `error_message` without aborting the successful entries. To make the contacts disappear from the application instead, use `POST /companies/{company}/contacts/bulk-delete`.

parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. 402.description: The operation requires a payment that could not be completed: either no payment method is on file (`error.details.payment_setup_url` links to the Billing Portal where it can be set up), the immediate charge was declined by the payment provider, the account lacks the plan or add-on this operation bills against, the annual document limit is reached (`plan_limit_exceeded`, with `error.details.period_end` indicating the end of the period — wait until it has ended or upgrade the plan to continue now), or the account has reached its maximum usage (`storage_quota_exceeded`, raised by upload operations such as signing a delivery note or attaching a file to an expense — contact support before retrying). Nothing was created or modified — resolve the cause and retry the same request. Version note: `error.type` is `payment_required_error` from `Factuarea-Version: 2026-09-01` onwards; earlier versions receive `invalid_request_error` for the three codes that predate that cut (`payment_method_required`, `employee_seat_payment_method_required` and `employee_seat_charge_failed`; every other 402 code, such as `addon_required`, `plan_limit_exceeded` or the additional tax ID codes, is newer and always carries `payment_required_error`). `error.code` is stable across every version.

post.description: Delete up to 500 contacts by `ids` with partial success, applying to each one the same soft delete as `DELETE /companies/{company}/contacts/{contact}`: the contact disappears from every read surface while its identity, roles, aliases and documents are preserved, and its fiscal identity and `external_id` are released so they can be registered again. Every UUID is evaluated inside the authenticated tenant; the only per-row failure is a UUID the company does not own (`contact_not_found`, already deleted contacts included), returned with `id`, `error_code` and a Spanish `error_message` without aborting the successful entries. The deletion is irreversible through the API; for a reversible bulk removal use `POST /companies/{company}/contacts/bulk/archive`.


Returns a partial-success result with `total`, `successful` and `failed` counts and a `failures` list (`id` + `error_code` + Spanish `error_message`) for the ones that could not be deleted, typically because they already consumed a number or already moved goods. 413.description: The packaged download you asked for is too large to build, so nothing was generated and no file was left on the server. Two catalog codes carry this status, both with `error.type: invalid_request_error`: `export_document_cap_exceeded` (the request covers more documents than the cap for that artifact allows — narrow the date range or export in batches) and `export_byte_cap_exceeded` (the artifact would weigh more than the byte cap; `error.subcode` says whether it was rejected up front from the size estimate, `before_writing`, or aborted mid-packaging, `while_writing`, in which case the partial file was deleted and nothing is served). Retrying the same request unchanged returns the same error — ask for less, do not wait. A third, unrelated code shares this status on every write operation: `payload_too_large`, raised when the REQUEST body exceeds the 1 MB limit, which is about what you send and not about the size of what you asked to build.

post.description: Resolve the price of a whole cart in ONE request, up to the declared ceiling of 50 selections, with the same selection shape as the single resolution. It is authenticated with the publishable storefront key that travels in the browser of an anonymous shopper. Resolving line by line would be one request per line from the browser of EVERY shopper, and the admission budget of the lane counts them all, so this is the operation to build the cart on. Failures are reported BY INDEX of the input: every entry comes back with its index and either its price or an error code with its message, so one unresolvable target does not invalidate the rest of the cart and the order of the answer matches the order you sent. Sending more selections than the ceiling is rejected with a validation error and resolves nothing. As in the single resolution, the price is the server's and what you get is a preview: the order line is priced again at creation.

post.description: Move several goods receipts to the same status in one request. The body takes an `ids` array of receipt ids, up to 100, and `new_status`, one of `posted` or `cancelled`, which are the only two that are a legitimate transition target. It is applied element by element and returns a partial-success result with `total`, `successful` and `failed` counts and a `failures` list (`id` + `error_code` + Spanish `error_message`) for the receipts whose current status does not admit that transition; ids of another company are reported as not found and nothing of that company is touched. Irreversible, because it composes posting and cancelling. Supports `Idempotency-Key` for safe retries.

post.description:
Transition several invoices to a new status in one call, each through the same state-transition guard, with partial success (a rejected id never aborts the batch). `new_status` is `issued`, `sent` (alias of `issued`) or `paid`; when `paid`, `payment_date` is required and propagated as the real payment date of every invoice (never `now()`). Returns a `BulkPartialSuccessResult` with `total`, `successful`, `failed` and a per-id `failures` list (`resource_not_found` or `invalid_status_transition`).

```json
{ "ids": ["0190a1b2-c3d4-7e5f-8a90-1b2c3d4e5f60"], "new_status": "paid", "payment_date": "2026-06-30" }
```

Limits: `ids` accepts 1–50 entries; `payment_date` is required when `new_status` is `paid` and must not be in the future.

post.description: Move several purchase orders to the same status in one request. The body takes an `ids` array of order ids, up to 100, and `new_status`, one of `sent`, `confirmed` or `cancelled` — the only three a client can ask for. Returns a partial-success result with `total`, `successful` and `failed` counts and a `failures` list (`id` + `error_code` + Spanish `error_message`) for the orders whose current status does not admit that transition. Irreversible, because it composes cancellations and cancelled is terminal. Supports `Idempotency-Key` for safe retries.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

post.description: Cancel a goods receipt. It takes no body. If the receipt had been posted, the quantity it consumed goes back to pending on the lines of the purchase order and the status derived from what has arrived is recalculated with the receipts that remain posted — an order that was complete goes back to partially received. post.description: Cancel a stock transfer. It takes no body: the reason is not part of the published contract. A draft and a dispatched transfer can be cancelled; one that has already been received cannot, and returns 422 with the code that names the invalid transition. Cancelling does NOT move stock: it writes no movement and it does not give back what dispatching took out of the origin warehouse — goods that come back come back as a transfer of their own, in the opposite direction. Cancelled is terminal and no published operation reopens the transfer, so this transition is irreversible and requires an `Idempotency-Key` when the policy of your credential demands it. Returns the transfer as cancelled.

patch.description: Change the account `role` of a member (`admin` or `member`), its `external_advisor` mark, or both; at least one is required. Both changes run in a single transaction: unmarking the advisor goes before the role change and marking goes after it, so a failure leaves the member untouched. Moving to `admin` revokes the member grants. Returns 200 with the updated member. Returns 404 `member_not_found` when the member does not exist or belongs to another account, 422 `external_advisor_already_assigned` when the account already has another external advisor, and 422 `business_rule_violation` when the member is the account owner (`cannot_change_account_owner_role`: ownership is transferred), when the advisor would not be a `member`, or when unmarking the advisor would exceed the plan user limit. The credential scope must cover every tax ID of the account. Requires the `members:write` scope, which `*` does not cover: the API key must list it explicitly.

Irreversible. Requires the `members:write` scope, which `*` does not cover: the API key must list it explicitly.

patch.description: Change the `level` your account keeps on one of its managed accounts: `none`, `view` (read-only) or `operate`. Before the holder claims the account you can raise and lower it; after the claim, raising returns 422 `access_level_raise_forbidden` with no change, and lowering is always allowed. Lowering narrows at once what your credentials reach in its tax IDs. Returns 200 with the managed account and its new level. The account axis admits only a managed account provisioned by the credential account, with the management in force and in the same environment as the key; your own account, a foreign or non-existent one, one of the other environment and one whose management ended all return the same 404 `account_not_found`. Requires the privileged `accounts:write` scope, which `*` does not cover: without the account provider privilege granted by Factuarea, or when the person who issued the key is no longer an owner or admin of your account, it returns 403 `privileged_scope_required`.

patch.description: Change the plan of a managed account your account pays, also after the holder claimed it: an upgrade takes effect at once and is charged immediately in one update of your subscription; a downgrade stays pending until the end of the period (`pending_plan`). Preview the amounts first with the preview operation. Returns 200 with the managed account. Returns 422 `managed_account_plan_not_self_serve` for `enterprise` (only assigned by Factuarea by contract) and 422 `idempotency_key_required` because changing the plan is irreversible. It requires your `access_level` on the managed account to be `operate`: with `view` or `none` it returns 403 `forbidden_action` without changing anything (raise the level first). The account axis admits only a managed account provisioned by the credential account, with the management in force and in the same environment as the key; your own account, a foreign or non-existent one, one of the other environment and one whose management ended all return the same 404 `account_not_found`. A managed account whose holder took over the payment also returns 404 `account_not_found`. Requires the privileged `accounts:write` scope, which `*` does not cover: without the account provider privilege granted by Factuarea, or when the person who issued the key is no longer an owner or admin of your account, it returns 403 `privileged_scope_required`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

It takes no body and it keeps the number the order already had, because in this family the number is stamped when the order is CREATED. post.description: Close the purchase when the shopper comes back from the gateway, with the identifier of the payment session that the return address carries. It is authenticated with the publishable storefront key that travels in the browser of an anonymous shopper, it REQUIRES an `Idempotency-Key` header, and it is the ONLY IRREVERSIBLE operation of the shopper lane: when the payment holds it issues the invoice of the order, a fiscal document that consumes correlative numbering and that, with the billing register active, is filed with the tax administration — it is voided with a corrective invoice and it is never deleted. Returns three things and no more: the situation of the payment, the situation of the order, and the invoice issued — public id and number — or nothing when none was issued. Repeating the call returns the SAME outcome instead of charging or invoicing twice, and it can be exercised in a LATER visit for up to seven days with the session identifier the storefront kept, which is the net under a shopper who closes the tab on the way back. A session that cannot be read, one that is not paid, and one that belongs to ANOTHER order mark nothing and are not errors either: the answer publishes the CURRENT situation of the order, with no reason field — publishing the reason would turn this into an oracle with which to find out, by trying session identifiers, which session belongs to which order. A payment that holds whose invoice is refused — the order falls inside the window of a recurring invoice, the identity of its buyer is incomplete — answers with the code of that refusal (422 `business_rule_violation` with the subcode `sales_order_recurring_invoice_overlap` for the overlap, 422 `buyer_identity_incomplete_for_full_invoice` for the identity) and leaves the order with its payment `verified` and no document, which is the truth and not `paid`. Without the header the call is rejected with 422 `idempotency_key_required`, and the same key with a different body with 422 `idempotency_key_reused`. An order of another company answers 404 `sales_order_not_found`. With the company in TEST MODE the payment comes back as `simulated`, with no invoice and no charge.

post.description: Turn a proforma into a sales order. The body carries at most the destination series for the new order and nothing else: there is no partial line selection here, because the quantities pending per line belong to the sales order, which is the document that tracks them. The response is the sales order that was created, with its lines. Two scopes are needed, and they are not the same one: the route enforces `sales_orders:write` — the module a company may not have contracted is the sales order one — and the operation additionally requires `proformas:read` over the source proforma, so a key holding only one of the two is rejected. Irreversible: the proforma moves to `converted` and no published operation takes it back. On the entry plan the number of sales orders you may create per calendar month is capped, and this call creates one: once the cap is reached it returns 402 and nothing is created.

post.description: Turn an accepted quote into a sales order. The body carries at most the destination series for the new order and nothing else: there is no partial line selection here, because the quantities pending per line belong to the sales order, which is the document that tracks them. The response is the sales order that was created, with its lines. Two scopes are needed, and they are not the same one: the route enforces `sales_orders:write` — the module a company may not have contracted is the sales order one — and the operation additionally requires `quotes:read` over the source quote, so a key holding only one of the two is rejected. Irreversible: the quote moves to `converted` and no published operation takes it back. On the entry plan the number of sales orders you may create per calendar month is capped, and this call creates one: once the cap is reached it returns 402 and nothing is created.

post.description: Create a webhook endpoint of your ACCOUNT that receives event notifications via HTTPS callbacks. It can subscribe to the same events as a company endpoint plus the `account.*` events of the account (members, owner, tax IDs, access granted or received, managed accounts and bulk imports). `account_relationship` says whose tax IDs it hears about: `own` (the tax IDs of your account), `managed` (the accounts your account manages) or `all` (the default). The endpoint is created in the environment of the credential (`live` or `test`), cannot change environment and is invisible from the other one. The number of endpoints per account and environment depends on the plan: 402 `addon_required` when the plan allows none and 422 `account_webhook_endpoint_limit_reached` at the limit. Returns 201 with a `Location` header.

post.description: Create a new API key in your account and return its plaintext `secret` exactly once — store it now, it cannot be retrieved later. Requesting a scope above the plan of the scoped tax IDs or outside the catalog returns 422; the credential cap is counted over the ACCOUNT. Without `scoped_company_ids` the new key reaches the same tax IDs as the credential that creates it, and it can never reach more. Pass `environment: test` to mint a sandbox key (`fact_test_`) that only reaches the sandbox company, with no real-world side effects (declaring `scoped_company_ids` with it returns 422); omit it for a live key (`fact_live_`). Creating against another account returns 404 and persists nothing. A key never gives, manages or reveals more power than it has itself: a scope the calling key does not cover or an access level above its own returns 403 `insufficient_scope` and persists nothing. The wildcard `*` does not cover `accounts:*` nor the account-administration scopes (`account:owner`, `members:*`, `invitations:*`, `nif_transfers:*`), so the calling key has to list them explicitly.

get.description: List the API keys of your account with cursor-based pagination. The subject is the ACCOUNT, never the tax ID acting on the request, but the list is bounded by the scope of the credential that asks: a key is listed only when EVERY tax ID of its scope is within the scope of the calling credential, so a credential scoped to one tax ID does not see a key that also reaches another one. get.description: List the automation rules of the authenticated company with cursor-based pagination. Filter by `status`, by `trigger_type` or by creation window (`created[gte]`, `created[lte]`, …), and search by name with `search`. Pages are ordered by `id` ascending — a unique, monotonic key — so a rule created while you are paginating never shifts or duplicates a row. Only your own rules are ever returned, and a cursor issued for another company yields an empty page rather than someone else's data.

parameters.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of the company. Get it from `GET /v1/me` (`data.scope[].id`).

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor for forward pagination: pass the `id` of the last object on the previous page (the `next_cursor` of the previous response).

parameters.name: ending_before
parameters.description: Cursor for backward pagination: pass the `id` of the first object on the current page.

parameters.name: status

parameters.name: trigger_type
parameters.description: Trigger of the rule in `resource.action` form (e.g. `invoice.paid`), as listed by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/automations/catalog`. Exact match on `trigger_type`.

parameters.name: scope

post.description: Create a carrier in your company: its name, its code, its tracking kind and, depending on that kind, the template of its tracking URL, plus an optional contact with name, email and phone. The CODE is the integration key: it is unique per company, so repeating one that is already in use is rejected with 422 naming `code` and never with 409, and two different companies can each have their own `SEUR-24H`. The TEMPLATE is required when the tracking kind says the carrier publishes tracking through a URL of its own, and it has two rules, which are the two ways of sending it wrong: it has to contain the placeholder for the tracking number — without it every recipient would land on the same page — and its scheme has to be that of the web, so any other scheme, executable ones included, is rejected. An empty string is not a way to leave a field unset and is rejected as such. The CONTACT is a datum of the carrier master and not a reference to a business contact of your address book: you never have to create a contact in order to create a carrier. Returns the carrier that was created, with its public id, and a location header pointing at it.

post.description:
Issue a corrective invoice (*rectificativa*, RD 1619/2012 art. 15) that amends a previously issued invoice. Returns `201` with the **new** invoice: `is_corrective: true`, `corrective` pointing at the original, and its own correlative number in a corrective series (`R-2026-001`, `R-2026-002`… with the default numbering format — corrective invoices of simplified invoices go in their own series, `RS`). The series is `series_id` when you send it, otherwise the default series of the right purpose (`corrective` for `R1`–`R4`, `simplified_corrective` for `R5`), created automatically if the company has none; a series of another `invoice_kind` returns 422 `series_invoice_kind_mismatch`.

Flow: the original must already be issued (`issued` or `overdue`) → the corrective is born **already issued**, never as a draft → when VeriFactu is enabled its *alta* is transmitted to AEAT **asynchronously**, so a `201` does not mean AEAT has accepted it yet. The original is never modified: it keeps its number, its status and its own VeriFactu record (the corrective references it by its number). A corrective is an additional document, not an edit.

**Three ways to correct (art. 15.5 RD 1619/2012).** `correction_nature` is optional: without it, `full` with `lines` is a substitution (`S`) and `full` without `lines` and `partial` are by differences (`I`: the corrective carries the amount of the rectification, whatever its sign).
- **Void the whole invoice** — `correction_type: full`, no `lines`: every original line is copied back negated and prefixed `[ANULACION]` (a full refund). Registered in VeriFactu as `TipoRectificativa: I`, with a negative base.
- **Correct some amounts** — `correction_type: partial` with the adjustment `lines` (required): each one is a delta prefixed `[AJUSTE]`, with a negative `quantity` to subtract (`unit_price` is never negative). Also `TipoRectificativa: I`. A line only moves stock if it declares its own `product_id`.
- **Replace it with the correct version** — `correction_type: full` with the FINAL `lines` of the correct invoice (no negative quantity); `correction_nature: S` is optional here. Registered as `TipoRectificativa: S` with `ImporteRectificacion` (the base and tax of the original, plus its equivalence surcharge when it had one); the product of each line is inherited from the original line at the same index.

Incoherent combinations are rejected with 422 before anything is created: `full` with `lines` and an explicit `correction_nature: I` (`parameter_invalid_value`, subcode `corrective_full_cancellation_with_lines`, `param: lines`); a substitution or a partial correction without `lines` (`missing_required_param`, `param: lines`); a substitution with a negative quantity (`parameter_invalid_value`, subcode `corrective_substitution_negative_amount`, `param: lines.N.quantity`, with `line_index`); a partial substitution (`parameter_invalid_value`, subcode `corrective_substitution_requires_full`, `param: correction_nature`). An invoice already voided in full (a full corrective by differences) admits no further corrective at all, and one replaced in full admits no second full correction, though it still admits a partial one (both `business_rule_violation`, subcode `invoice_already_rectified_in_full`).

**Nature of each corrected line.** A line may declare `unit`, `regime_key`, `exemption_reason` and `exemption_reason_text`, with the same rules as `POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices`. They follow the presence of the key: a key you OMIT inherits the value of the original line at the same index; a key you SEND (even `null`) replaces it, and `null` means explicitly none — for example `exemption_reason: null` turns an exempt original line into a taxed one. This applies to both substitution and correction by differences.

**AEAT R code.** By default it is derived from `correction_reason`: `error_fundado` → R1, `concurso` → R2, `incobrable` → R3, everything else → R4; a corrective of a simplified (F2) invoice is always born R5 regardless of the reason. `correction_code` overrides that derivation, but is validated against the legal matrix — original F2 → only `R5`; original F1/F3 → only `R1`–`R4`. Any other combination returns 422 with the legal `allowed_values`.

Limits: `draft`, `scheduled`, `cancelled` and `annulled` originals return 422; a corrective can never itself be corrected — issue a new corrective of the original instead. List every corrective of an invoice with `GET /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/correctives`.

**Signing certificate (NO VERI*FACTU).** Only when the company has VeriFactu enabled in NO VERI*FACTU mode, the alta billing record of this operation is signed with the company's electronic certificate (art. 6.c and 14 of Order HAC/1177/2024), and a certificate that is missing, expired, revoked, issued for another tax id or unreadable is rejected **before** the invoice is issued: 422 `verifactu_not_eligible` with `error.subcode: signing_certificate_unavailable`; `error.param` says what is missing (`certificate`: the company certificate; `representation`: the representation that lets Factuarea sign on its behalf is not active; `system_certificate`: the Factuarea certificate is unavailable, nothing for you to fix). The invoice stays exactly as it was (a draft without a number) and nothing is consumed: upload a valid certificate in Settings → Digital certificate (or register the representation in the third-party remission modes) and repeat the same call. Companies that have not enabled VeriFactu, and companies in VERI*FACTU mode (whose records are not signed), are never blocked by this rule.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

409.description: The request conflicts with data that already exists or with a request running at the same time. `resource_already_exists` with `subcode` `external_id_already_exists`: another employee of the company already uses that `external_id`; `details.existing_resource_id` is its identifier. `employee_batch_billing_state_conflict`: the current billing of the account does not allow completing the batch safely. `details.reason` is `offer_requires_chargeable_seats`, `fiscal_configuration` or `phase_incompatible`. Nothing was charged. `resource_already_exists` with `subcode` `external_id_already_exists`: an `external_id` of the batch is already used by an employee of the company. Nothing was charged or created. `employee_batch_state_conflict` with `subcode` `employee_batch_missing_payment_proof`: the payment of this operation is not proven yet. Read its current state. `employee_batch_state_conflict` with `subcode` `employee_batch_payment_outcome_unknown`: the payment of the batch is still being verified. `details.operation_id` is the operation to keep following; do not charge again. `employee_batch_quote_changed`: the quote changed since the version you accepted (`param` `quote_version`). Refresh it and accept the current version. `employee_seat_mutation_outcome_unknown`: an employee seat operation is still being verified. `details.operation_id` is its reference and `details.operation_kind` is `legacy_employee`; do not repeat the charge and contact support with the reference. `employee_seat_phase_incompatible` with `param` `quantity`: the subscription has scheduled conditions that must be reviewed before its seats change. `details.reason` is `phase_incompatible`. Nothing was charged. `resource_conflict`: another request was reserving identifiers for the same kind of record at that moment and this one could not complete its reservation. Nothing was written; send the request again after a few seconds. `employee_batch_state_conflict`: the batch is in a state that does not allow this action. Read its current state. `employee_seat_operation_in_progress`: another employee operation is pending. `details.operation_id` identifies it when known; read its state before starting another.

402.description: The operation requires a payment that could not be completed: either no payment method is on file (`error.details.payment_setup_url` links to the Billing Portal where it can be set up), the immediate charge was declined by the payment provider, the account lacks the plan or add-on this operation bills against, the annual document limit is reached (`plan_limit_exceeded`, with `error.details.period_end` indicating the end of the period — wait until it has ended or upgrade the plan to continue now), or the account has reached its maximum usage (`storage_quota_exceeded`, raised by upload operations such as signing a delivery note or attaching a file to an expense — contact support before retrying). Nothing was created or modified — resolve the cause and retry the same request. Version note: `error.type` is `payment_required_error` from `Factuarea-Version: 2026-09-01` onwards; earlier versions receive `invalid_request_error` for the three codes that predate that cut (`payment_method_required`, `employee_seat_payment_method_required` and `employee_seat_charge_failed`; every other 402 code, such as `addon_required`, `plan_limit_exceeded` or the additional tax ID codes, is newer and always carries `payment_required_error`). `error.code` is stable across every version.
