post.description:
Create an invoice. It is created in `draft` by default; pass `options.issue_directly: true` to issue it immediately (assigning the correlative number and freezing the document per AEAT), or issue it later. VeriFactu *alta* is transmitted to AEAT asynchronously — a `201` does not mean AEAT has accepted the invoice yet, so poll it for the AEAT status.

```json
{
  "client_id": "0190a1b2-c3d4-7e5f-8a90-1b2c3d4e5f60",
  "lines": [{ "description": "Consulting", "quantity": 1, "unit_price": 1000, "tax_rate": 21 }],
  "options": { "issue_directly": true }
}
```

Limits: at least one line is required; send an `Idempotency-Key` (≤255 chars, remembered 24 h) for safe retries; a duplicate `external_id` upserts the existing invoice instead of creating a new one. A line with no `tax_rate`, no referenced tax and no product with a tax takes the DEFAULT TAX your company has set for invoices, as if you had chosen that tax (its rate, indirect-tax regime and AEAT qualification); if there is none the request is rejected with 422 `missing_required_param` (`error.param` `lines.N.tax_rate` and `error.line_index` N, the zero-based index of the line). `options.send_automatically` emails the invoice once issued to `options.send_to` or, when omitted, to the client; with no possible recipient the request is rejected BEFORE anything is created —no draft, no number consumed— with 422 `missing_required_param` and `error.param` `options.send_to`.

**Unattended checkout (self-service terminals and vending machines).** A terminal can issue an already-paid simplified invoice in ONE idempotent call. A request is a checkout when it carries `type: F2`, a `payment` block or `options.register_verifactu`; only those get the extra response blocks below, any other request behaves as described above.

- `type: F2` is the simplified invoice. Without `client_id` it is an anonymous ticket; with one it is a qualified simplified invoice (the client must belong to your company). `F1` (the default) still requires a client with a complete tax ID. The company needs simplified invoices enabled (422 `simplified_invoices_disabled`) and the amount cannot exceed the absolute cap of 3,000 € VAT included (422 `simplified_invoice_not_allowed`).
- `series_id` is optional. Invoice series have a fixed purpose (`invoice_kind`: `complete`, `simplified`, `corrective`, `simplified_corrective`) and a document is only numbered in a series of its own purpose. Without `series_id`, a `F1` goes to your default complete series (`F`) and a `F2` to your default simplified series (`S`), created automatically if you have none. If you DO send a `series_id` of another `invoice_kind`, issuing is rejected with 422 `series_invoice_kind_mismatch` (it is never changed silently); `GET /v1/companies/{company}/series/default?document_type=invoice&invoice_kind=simplified` returns the series to use.
- `prices_include_tax: true` makes every `unit_price` the FINAL price with taxes. The system computes the net base to the cent so that the invoice total equals the sum of the amounts you sent; if no distribution reaches it, 422 `amount_reconciliation_failed` and nothing is issued. Catalog lines (`product_id`) are not accepted in this mode.
- `payment` (`method` required, `paid_at` and `reference` optional) records the payment for the whole amount due after issuing. It implies issuing.
- `operation_on` is the date the operation took place when it differs from `issued_on`; it cannot be later than `issued_on` (422 `operation_date_after_issue_date`) unless the first line that declares a `regime_key` uses 14 or 15.
- `options.register_verifactu: true` generates the VERI*FACTU alta synchronously, BEFORE responding, and implies issuing. Its transmission to AEAT follows its course in batches.

The response is the invoice plus `verifactu` (alta `status` `registered` or `failed` with its `error_code`, `aeat_status`, `huella`, `qr_url`, `qr_png_base64`, `legend` and `csv`), `pdf` (`status`, signed `url` and `expires_at`) and `public_url`. `pdf.status` is `ready` only when the A4 PDF is already materialized and `pdf.url` serves it at once (use `options.wait_for_pdf`, which waits up to about 15 s); otherwise it is `pending` and the URL answers 404 for a few seconds — never an error. If the alta cannot be generated, the invoice stays issued and the response says so (`status: failed`).

**Late retries.** Identify the operation by its `external_id`: it has no expiry, unlike an `Idempotency-Key`. A checkout that repeats the `external_id` of an invoice already issued in your company returns that invoice with `200` and `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, completing the alta and the payment if they were missing, without creating or changing anything else and without emailing again an invoice whose email is already queued or delivered. If the type or the total differ from the issued invoice, it returns `409` `unattended_replay_mismatch` (also in `subcode`) with `param: external_id`: the `external_id` identifies ONE operation, so use a new one for a new operation. Two simultaneous requests with the same `external_id` produce ONE invoice, ONE number and ONE payment: the second waits for the first (up to 20 seconds) and then replays it, and if the first has still not finished it returns `409` `resource_locked` with `param: external_id` — nothing was written by the waiting request, so sending the same request again is harmless. Requests that are not checkouts keep the `external_id` upsert.

**Signing certificate (NO VERI*FACTU).** Only when the company has VeriFactu enabled in NO VERI*FACTU mode, the alta billing record of this operation is signed with the company's electronic certificate (art. 6.c and 14 of Order HAC/1177/2024), and a certificate that is missing, expired, revoked, issued for another tax id or unreadable is rejected **before** the invoice is issued: 422 `verifactu_not_eligible` with `error.subcode: signing_certificate_unavailable`; `error.param` says what is missing (`certificate`: the company certificate; `representation`: the representation that lets Factuarea sign on its behalf is not active; `system_certificate`: the Factuarea certificate is unavailable, nothing for you to fix). The invoice stays exactly as it was (a draft without a number) and nothing is consumed: upload a valid certificate in Settings → Digital certificate (or register the representation in the third-party remission modes) and repeat the same call. Companies that have not enabled VeriFactu, and companies in VERI*FACTU mode (whose records are not signed), are never blocked by this rule.

409.description: The request conflicts with data that already exists or with a request running at the same time. `resource_locked`: another request with the same `external_id` is still being processed (up to 20 seconds). Nothing was written by this request; send the same request again, which will return the invoice already issued. `unattended_replay_mismatch`: the `external_id` already belongs to an issued invoice with a different type or total. It identifies ONE operation: use a new `external_id` for a new operation. Nothing was changed. `resource_locked` with `subcode` `chain_position_conflict`: another process was generating VeriFactu billing records for the company at the same time and this one could not take its place in the chain after several attempts. Nothing was written; send the request again. `resource_conflict`: another request was reserving identifiers for the same kind of record at that moment and this one could not complete its reservation. Nothing was written; send the request again after a few seconds.

402.description: The operation requires a payment that could not be completed: either no payment method is on file (`error.details.payment_setup_url` links to the Billing Portal where it can be set up), the immediate charge was declined by the payment provider, the account lacks the plan or add-on this operation bills against, the annual document limit is reached (`plan_limit_exceeded`, with `error.details.period_end` indicating the end of the period — wait until it has ended or upgrade the plan to continue now), or the account has reached its maximum usage (`storage_quota_exceeded`, raised by upload operations such as signing a delivery note or attaching a file to an expense — contact support before retrying). Nothing was created or modified — resolve the cause and retry the same request. Version note: `error.type` is `payment_required_error` from `Factuarea-Version: 2026-09-01` onwards; earlier versions receive `invalid_request_error` for the three codes that predate that cut (`payment_method_required`, `employee_seat_payment_method_required` and `employee_seat_charge_failed`; every other 402 code, such as `addon_required`, `plan_limit_exceeded` or the additional tax ID codes, is newer and always carries `payment_required_error`). `error.code` is stable across every version.

get.description: List your invoices with cursor-based pagination. Supports filtering by `status[in]`, `client_id`, `series_id`, `issued_on[gte|lte]`, and `total[gte|lte]`.

parameters.name: company
parameters.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of the company. Get it from `GET /v1/me` (`data.scope[].id`).

parameters.name: original_invoice_id
parameters.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of an original invoice, to list its corrective invoices.

parameters.name: verifactu_status
parameters.description: VeriFactu status: `no_verifactu`, `pending`, `accepted` or `rejected`.

parameters.name: is_sent
parameters.description: Delivery filter, independent of the fiscal status: `true` returns only invoices delivered to the customer and `false` only the rest.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of objects to return, between 1 and 100 (default 25).

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor for forward pagination: pass the `id` of the last object on the previous page (the `next_cursor` of the previous response).

parameters.name: ending_before
parameters.description: Cursor for backward pagination: pass the `id` of the first object on the current page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Invoice status: `draft`, `scheduled`, `issued`, `paid`, `partially_paid`, `cancelled`, `overdue` or `annulled` (`sent` is an alias of `issued`).

parameters.name: status[in]
parameters.description: Invoice status. Comma-separated list; any of the values matches. `sent` is accepted as an alias of `issued` in every API version.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Client ID (UUID v7). Exact match on `client_id`.

parameters.name: client_id[in]
parameters.description: Client ID (UUID v7). Comma-separated list. Any of the values matches.

parameters.name: series_id
parameters.description: Series ID (UUID v7). Exact match on `series_id`.

parameters.name: series_id[in]
parameters.description: Series ID (UUID v7). Comma-separated list. Any of the values matches.

parameters.name: created[gte]
parameters.description: Creation date (ISO 8601). Greater than or equal to the given value.

parameters.name: created[lte]
parameters.description: Creation date (ISO 8601). Less than or equal to the given value.

parameters.name: created[gt]
parameters.description: Creation date (ISO 8601). Strictly greater than the given value.

parameters.name: created[lt]
parameters.description: Creation date (ISO 8601). Strictly less than the given value.

parameters.name: due_on[gte]
parameters.description: Due date. Greater than or equal to the given value.

parameters.name: due_on[lte]
parameters.description: Due date. Less than or equal to the given value.

parameters.name: due_on[gt]
parameters.description: Due date. Strictly greater than the given value.

parameters.name: due_on[lt]
parameters.description: Due date. Strictly less than the given value.

parameters.name: total[gte]
parameters.description: Total amount. Greater than or equal to the given value.

parameters.name: total[lte]
parameters.description: Total amount. Less than or equal to the given value.

parameters.name: total[gt]
parameters.description: Total amount. Strictly greater than the given value.

parameters.name: total[lt]
parameters.description: Total amount. Strictly less than the given value.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. EUR). Exact match on `currency`.

parameters.name: currency[in]
parameters.description: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. EUR). Comma-separated list. Any of the values matches.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Invoice number. Exact match on `number`.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Classification tag (lowercase slug); `tags[in]=a,b` matches invoices carrying ANY of the tags. Exact match on `tags`.

parameters.name: tags[in]
parameters.description: Classification tag (lowercase slug); `tags[in]=a,b` matches invoices carrying ANY of the tags. Comma-separated list. Any of the values matches.

parameters.name: paid_on[gte]
parameters.description: Payment date. INPUT parameter that keeps its name; the equivalent OUTPUT key is `paid_date`. Greater than or equal to the given value.

parameters.name: paid_on[lte]
parameters.description: Payment date. INPUT parameter that keeps its name; the equivalent OUTPUT key is `paid_date`. Less than or equal to the given value.

parameters.name: paid_on[gt]
parameters.description: Payment date. INPUT parameter that keeps its name; the equivalent OUTPUT key is `paid_date`. Strictly greater than the given value.

parameters.name: paid_on[lt]
parameters.description: Payment date. INPUT parameter that keeps its name; the equivalent OUTPUT key is `paid_date`. Strictly less than the given value.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order: `created`, `total`, `number` ascending, or with a `-` prefix for descending (default `-created`).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search. Escaped `LIKE %term%` (case-insensitive, max 80 chars) across the resource's key text columns, combined with the other filters (AND) and compatible with the cursor.

parameters.name: metadata
parameters.description: Metadata filter as `metadata[key]=value` (deepObject): pairs combine with AND, up to 50, keys matching `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}`.

post.description: Issue a TAX ID TRANSFER over ONE tax ID of your account, named explicitly in `company_id`, and receive **201 Created** with the transfer and its plaintext `secret`. This is the only way a tax ID can move from this account to another one, and the initiative is always the giving side: no operation lets an account ask for someone else's tax ID. The secret is returned EXACTLY ONCE and never persisted — only its irreversible fingerprint is stored, so no later read can return it, today or ever; hand it to the receiving account through a channel you trust. An idempotent replay of this call returns the same transfer with `secret: null`: the secret is never stored, not even in the idempotency cache. `recipient_account_id` is OPTIONAL and closes the transfer to a single account: only that account can accept it, and anyone else presenting the secret gets `nif_transfer_invalid`; without it, whoever holds the secret can accept it. The OWNER company of your account cannot be given away. `expires_at` is OPTIONAL: omit it for the product default (24 hours), or pass an ISO 8601 instant that is in the future and within the product ceiling (7 days). If the secret leaks, revoke the transfer with the revoke operation. No `Location` header is returned, deliberately: a transfer has no individual read operation. Returns 403 `forbidden_action` when the credential holder does not administer that tax ID, 403 `company_read_only` when the effective access of the credential to that tax ID is read-only (`view`), without issuing anything, 404 `profile_not_found` when the tax ID does not exist, belongs to another account, is outside your scope or the credential has no access to it (all with the same body), 422 `business_rule_violation` on a past, too-distant or uninterpretable `expires_at`, on the owner company of the account (`error.param` `company_id`) or on a recipient that does not exist or is your own account (`error.param` `recipient_account_id`, both with the same body), 422 `idempotency_key_required` because issuing is irreversible — once out, the secret is out — and 404 `account_not_found` when `{account}` is not the credential account. Requires the `nif_transfers:write` scope, which `*` does not cover: the API key must list it explicitly.

get.description: List the tax ID transfers your account has ISSUED over the tax IDs your credential reaches — the inventory of open cessions — with cursor-based pagination (`limit` 1-100, default 25, plus `starting_after`, or `ending_before` for the previous page) and an optional `status` filter (`active`, `expired`, `revoked`, `consumed`). Transfers RECEIVED from other accounts are never listed: a transfer someone handed you is not yours — you only hold a secret — and publishing them would tell you which other accounts are giving away which tax IDs. Like its member and invitation siblings this listing is narrowed by the tax-ID scope of the credential: a transfer over a tax ID the credential does not reach is not listed — once a transfer is accepted its tax ID leaves your account, so it stops being listed too. It does not go through the administration guard: the `nif_transfers:read` scope is what authorises it. The `status` of each item is DERIVED against a single clock instant for the whole page — the table has no status column — and the `secret` never travels through this read: publishing it would turn a read permission into an effective tax-ID transfer permission. Returns 422 `invalid_param_value` for a `status` outside the closed vocabulary, 400 for an unknown query parameter or a malformed `limit`/`starting_after`, and 404 `account_not_found` when `{account}` is not the credential account. Requires the `nif_transfers:read` scope, which `*` does not cover: the API key must list it explicitly.

get.description: List products in your catalog with cursor-based pagination.

parameters.name: company
parameters.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of the company. Get it from `GET /v1/me` (`data.scope[].id`).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of objects to return, between 1 and 100 (default 25).

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor for forward pagination: pass the `id` of the last object on the previous page (the `next_cursor` of the previous response).

parameters.name: ending_before
parameters.description: Cursor for backward pagination: pass the `id` of the first object on the current page.

parameters.name: sku
parameters.description: Product SKU. Exact match on `sku`.

parameters.name: sku[in]
parameters.description: Product SKU. Comma-separated list. Any of the values matches.

parameters.name: sku[contains]
parameters.description: Product SKU. Partial case-insensitive match (`LIKE %term%`) on `sku`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Product name. Exact match on `name`.

parameters.name: name[contains]
parameters.description: Product name. Partial case-insensitive match (`LIKE %term%`) on `name`.

parameters.name: is_active
parameters.description: Filter by active / inactive products. Exact match on `is_active`.

parameters.name: created[gte]
parameters.description: Creation date (ISO 8601). Greater than or equal to the given value.

parameters.name: created[lte]
parameters.description: Creation date (ISO 8601). Less than or equal to the given value.

parameters.name: created[gt]
parameters.description: Creation date (ISO 8601). Strictly greater than the given value.

parameters.name: created[lt]
parameters.description: Creation date (ISO 8601). Strictly less than the given value.

parameters.name: price[gte]
parameters.description: Unit price. Greater than or equal to the given value.

parameters.name: price[lte]
parameters.description: Unit price. Less than or equal to the given value.

parameters.name: price[gt]
parameters.description: Unit price. Strictly greater than the given value.

parameters.name: price[lt]
parameters.description: Unit price. Strictly less than the given value.

parameters.name: in_stock
parameters.description: Filter by products with available stock (`true` → stock > 0) or out of stock (`false` → stock = 0). Exact match on `in_stock`.

parameters.name: low_stock
parameters.description: Filter by products with low stock (`true` → 0 < stock ≤ configured threshold) or with ample stock (`false` → stock > threshold). Exact match on `low_stock`.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Filter by classification tag. Supports multiple values with `tag[in]`. Exact match on `tag`.

parameters.name: tag[in]
parameters.description: Filter by classification tag. Supports multiple values with `tag[in]`. Comma-separated list. Any of the values matches.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search. Escaped `LIKE %term%` (case-insensitive, max 80 chars) across the resource's key text columns, combined with the other filters (AND) and compatible with the cursor.

parameters.name: metadata
parameters.description: Metadata filter as `metadata[key]=value` (deepObject): pairs combine with AND, up to 50, keys matching `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}`.

post.description: Create a purchase order in `draft` status with its supplier, the warehouse where the goods are expected, the date you expect them and its lines; at least one line is required. `supplier_order_reference` is the reference the supplier or your own system uses for that order and it is unique per company: sending one that already exists returns 409 naming `supplier_reference`, instead of creating a second order. Two orders without that reference can coexist, and the same reference in two different companies creates two independent orders. The response is the order that was created, with its lines and, per line, the quantity in the purchase unit, its conversion factor to the base unit and the quantity received so far. Unlike a sales order, a purchase order carries its number from the very first moment: the number is stamped when the order is created, not when you confirm it. It is unique per company and not dense — an order that does not complete leaves a permanent gap, because a purchase order is not a fiscal document.

post.description: Request a return of goods against a document you already issued: the kind of the origin and its public id, and at least one line, each one naming the line of the origin with the reference the returnable-lines read gives you, the quantity with four decimal places and a reason from the closed catalog of reasons. A line of a variable-weight origin line sold by count may also carry `counted_quantity` (the pieces coming back, informational, in the unit the origin line counted); pieces sent for any other line are rejected with 422 `business_rule_violation` and subcode `return_line_pieces_not_allowed`. Optionally a header reason — derived from the lines when you omit it —, the destination warehouse and a note. The unit price and the tax rate are NOT accepted from you: both are INHERITED from the line of the origin, because the amount that will eventually be corrected is not decided by whoever asks for the return, and a corrective invoice hangs from it. The article and the variant come from the origin too, and so does the moment of the request. Two rules of admission are checked before anything is written and both answer 422: the return window of the origin has to still be open, and a line cannot return more than what was delivered and is not already covered by another live return — a return that was rejected frees its share again. The return is created as REQUESTED and with no number yet, and it can be edited and deleted while it stays in that status. Ask the returnable lines of the origin first if you want to know the ceiling instead of discovering it through successive rejections. Returns the return that was created, with its public id and its lines, and a location header pointing at it.

get.description: List the returns of your company with cursor-based pagination. Filter by status, by the kind of document the goods came from, by reason, by destination warehouse, by business contact, by number and by the dates of the cycle; search free text; and sort by creation, by number or by the date the return was requested. The filters that take a public id — the warehouse, the contact, the origin document — are resolved inside your company, so an id that belongs to another company returns an empty page and never a row. A return that is still requested has NO number: the number is stamped when it is approved, so do not key your own records on it before then. The `id` is stable from the moment the return is created.

post.description: Hold stock for a holder — a cart, an order, whatever your system commits against — so that nobody else sells it. The body carries the holder as a pair of type and id, the lines to hold with the article, its variant and its warehouse when you want to pin them, the quantity with four decimal places, and optionally the number of SECONDS the hold should last, which is a duration and never a date. It is ATOMIC: if a single line has less available than you ask for, nothing at all is held and the call returns 422 with the shortage detailed line by line — the quantity asked for and the quantity available — so you can rebuild the basket without a second call. And it is idempotent PER HOLDER: holding the same list twice for the same holder does not duplicate anything, because only the difference over what that holder already holds is set aside. The response is the collection of reservations that were created, with their public ids and their count, and the location header points at the first of them.

post.description: Issue a publishable storefront key for the company in the path and return its plaintext secret EXACTLY ONCE — store it now, no later call returns it. It takes a name, at least one ALLOWED ORIGIN and at least one scope of the shopper lane, plus an optional expiry. The origins are the heart of this credential and not a formality: the key is meant to travel in the browser of a custom-built storefront, so every request it makes is checked against the origins declared here, and an origin with a wildcard, with a path, with a query string or without a scheme is rejected with 422 naming the field. Scopes outside the shopper lane are rejected as well, the ones that manage these very keys included: a key that travels in a browser must not be able to mint another one. When the company already holds as many ACTIVE keys as its quota tier allows, the call is rejected with the business-rule error that says so — revoke one you no longer serve, or raise the tier. Returns the key with its plaintext secret and a location header pointing at it.

post.description: Turn a cart into a real sales order. It is authenticated with the publishable storefront key that travels in the browser of an anonymous shopper, and it is the operation of the lane to read whole before integrating. It is IDEMPOTENT BY TWO INDEPENDENT AXES, and the contract keeps them apart on purpose: the `Idempotency-Key` header, which is REQUIRED here and identifies the REQUEST — the same key with the same body returns the same order and leaves one single row, and a call without it is rejected —, and the optional external id, which identifies the ORDER in your own system and is unique PER COMPANY, so two creations with the same external id return the same order even from different requests and days apart, while two different companies may each use the same one. Neither axis is derived from the other. THE PRICE IS THE SERVER'S: every line is priced again at creation and any amount in the body is ignored, so a manipulated browser cannot change what is charged, and neither the previewed price nor the one stored in the cart session is taken as the price of the line without resolving it again. Availability is checked line by line and a single line without enough units rejects the WHOLE order naming that line: no partial order is ever created. The identity of the shopper needs a name, an email and a shipping address; the tax id is OPTIONAL and a shopper without one completes the order, which then creates no business contact at all, because a business contact requires a fiscal identity and a private individual does not have one. The consent to commercial communications travels as an explicit field instead of being presumed, and neither the IP address of the shopper nor any browser tracking identifier is stored. The order is born with the storefront channel, so its origin is distinguishable from a manual entry, from a connected store and from an integrator API call. When the company that owns the key is in TEST MODE the lane keeps working and what is neutralized is the EFFECT and never the access: the check happens as the LAST step before any effect, so what is simulated is exactly what would have been produced. Returns the created order with its public id, its number, its status, its channel, its lines with the amounts of the server, its totals and the session it came from.

post.description: Open a cart session that holds the shopping of a shopper between visits and that the order creation later converts. It is authenticated with the publishable storefront key that travels in the browser of an anonymous shopper, and it REQUIRES an `Idempotency-Key` header: retrying with the same key returns the same session instead of opening a second one. The session stores, line by line, the COMPLETE selection — article, variant, presentation, configuration, option values and quantity — and the amounts LAST RESOLVED BY THE SERVER together with the moment they were resolved; any amount present in the body is ignored and resolved again, because the browser of a shopper does not get to set a price. It is born with an expiry computed from the lifetime configured for the storefront, 24 hours by default, and its public id is an unguessable UUID that is the ONLY secret separating the cart of one shopper from the cart of another, so treat it as a secret and never as a number you can walk. Returns the session with its lines, its buyer identity when it already carries one, its totals, the moment its prices were resolved, its expiry and whether it is already expired. No stock is held by opening a cart: units are checked when the order is created.

get.description: Search the tasks of your company across projects. Filters: `q` (free text; a value shaped like a task key such as `DEV-12` also matches that key), `project_id`, `status` (`planned`, `active`, `archived`), `column_id`, `priority`, `assignee_id` (a member UUID or `me`), `label_id`, `due_before`, `due_after` and `completed`. `sort` accepts `created_at`, `updated_at`, `due_on`, `priority` or `number`, with a `-` prefix for descending (default `-created_at`); ties are broken by `id` so the order is stable. Cursor-paginated: pass the `next_cursor` of a page as `starting_after` to get the next one; `has_more` tells whether there are more.

parameters.name: company
parameters.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of the company. Get it from `GET /v1/me` (`data.scope[].id`).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text matched against the task title and description. A value shaped like a task key (`DEV-12`) also matches that task by its key or a previous alias. Maximum 512 characters.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: UUID of a project of your company: only its tasks are returned.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Board status: `planned` (backlog), `active` (in a column of the board) or `archived`.

parameters.name: column_id
parameters.description: UUID of a board column: only tasks in that column are returned.

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: Task priority: `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high` or `urgent`.

parameters.name: assignee_id
parameters.description: UUID of the assigned member, or `me` for the member who owns the API key.

parameters.name: label_id
parameters.description: UUID of a task label: only tasks carrying that label are returned.

parameters.name: due_before
parameters.description: Only tasks due on or before this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

parameters.name: due_after
parameters.description: Only tasks due on or after this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

parameters.name: completed
parameters.description: `true` returns only completed tasks; `false` only open ones. Omit it to return both.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order: `created_at` (default is `-created_at`), `updated_at`, `due_on`, `priority` or `number`; prefix it with `-` for descending.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of tasks to return. Integer between 1 and 100. Defaults to 25.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor for forward pagination: the `id` of the last task of the previous page (the `next_cursor` you received). An `id` that is not a task of your company returns 422 `invalid_param_value`.

post.description: Create a transport document (DeCA) in `draft`. `company_role` says whether your company acts as contractual shipper (`shipper`) or effective carrier (`carrier`); your party is filled with your company data and the other one from `contact_id` or from the fields you send. Pass `delivery_note_ids` (1 to 50 of your delivery notes) to pre-fill one shipment per delivery note with its destination, date and goods (services excluded, frozen weights); a cancelled delivery note is rejected with 422 `delivery_note_cancelled`. A shipment that omits `origin` gets your default loading place or, if you have none, your registered address (an explicit `origin: null` leaves it without origin). The `id` is generated by the server; `shipments[].id` is optional and an identifier already in use returns 422 on `shipments.N.id`. A goods line whose `quantity × gross_weight_kg` exceeds 9,999,999,999.9999 kg or rounds to 0 returns 422 `invalid_gross_weight` on `shipments.N.goods.M.gross_weight_kg`. A draft admits incomplete data; the minimum data is only required to issue. A concurrent write that collides on an identifier returns 409 `resource_conflict`: nothing was saved and the request can be retried. Returns 201 with the resource and a `Location` header.

get.description: List the transport control documents (DeCA, Spanish electronic administrative control document for road freight) of your company with cursor-based pagination. Filters: `status` (also `status[in]`), `transport_date[gte]`/`transport_date[lte]` (a document matches when the date range of its shipments overlaps the period), `company_role` (`shipper` or `carrier`), `carrier_tax_id`, `delivery_note_id` (documents with a shipment from that delivery note) and `q` (number, parties or plates). Sort with `sort` (`transport_date`, `number`, `created`, `updated`; prefix `-` for descending; default `-transport_date`). `q` takes 1 to 255 characters. Any other query parameter returns 400. The MCP tool `search_transport_documents` accepts the same `sort` and `q`.

post.description: Create a warehouse with its code, its name, its type — own, external, store or transit —, its full address and, optionally, the mark that makes it the default one of the company. The code is the integration key: required, up to 20 characters and unique per company among the warehouses that are still active, so repeating one that is in use returns 422 naming `code`, never 409. Two different companies can each have their own `MAD-01`, and archiving a warehouse frees its code for a later creation. Marking the new warehouse as the default one unmarks the previous default in the same transaction, so the company never has two. The response is the warehouse that was created, with its public id, its address broken down field by field and the number of locations it has active — none at this point.

post.description: Add a location to a warehouse: its code, its name and, optionally, the location it hangs from. The hierarchy is ONE level deep — a location may have a parent, and that parent may not have one in turn —, so a third level is rejected as a business rule violation with 422. The code is up to 20 characters and unique per WAREHOUSE among the active locations, so two warehouses of the same company can each have their own `A-01`, and repeating one that is in use returns 422 naming `code`. The parent has to belong to the same warehouse. Returns the location that was created, with its public id and its parent when it has one.

post.description: Deactivate a tax ID of the account, moving it from `active` to `inactive`: it becomes non-operational but its data is preserved and the change is reversible (reactivate it later through the additional tax ID gate). No charge is applied: the additional tax ID is released without credit, and it can be reactivated for free within the paid period. The account must keep at least one active tax ID (422 `business_rule_violation` with subcode `account_must_keep_one_nif`). A tax ID that is not part of the account returns 404. Deactivating is not billed: it never returns 402. The person who issued the credential must be an owner or admin of the account, with the `user_management` section available: otherwise 403 `forbidden_action`, before anything is charged or changed. A credential whose effective access to that tax ID is read-only (`view`) returns 403 `company_read_only`, and one with no access returns the same 404 as a tax ID outside the account.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

delete.description: Delete a contact. It is a soft delete: the contact disappears from every read surface — list, search, options and selectors, stats, export, activities and its own detail, which answers 404 `contact_not_found` from then on — while nothing is physically removed. Its identity, roles, directional profiles, bank accounts, legacy aliases and every invoice, quote, delivery note or expense that references it are preserved exactly as they were, and those documents keep showing their customer or supplier data. Deleting releases the fiscal identity and the `external_id`, so the same tax ID or external ID can be registered again as a different contact. A deleted contact can no longer be used in new documents, not even through its legacy alias. The operation is irreversible through the API — `POST /companies/{company}/contacts/{contact}/restore` only unarchives — and deleting an unknown, foreign or already deleted UUID returns 404 `contact_not_found`. For a reversible removal that keeps the contact readable, use `POST /companies/{company}/contacts/{contact}/archive` instead. It emits the `contact.deleted` webhook event.

delete.description: Delete a carrier from the master of your company. It returns no content. Deleting one that is assigned to delivery notes is a VALID operation and destroys nothing of those notes: the free-text carrier they already carried is preserved — the text travels alongside the reference and not instead of it — so they keep reading and keep showing the carrier the goods went with. What is lost is the entry of the master, its code, its contact and the template that was deriving the tracking URL of the notes that pointed at it, which stop publishing that link. If what you want is to stop assigning it while keeping all of that, deactivate it instead: that is what the partial update is for. A carrier of another company answers exactly like one that does not exist. Irreversible: this API publishes no operation that brings a deleted carrier back, and creating it again with the same code produces a different entry with a different id, so it requires an `Idempotency-Key` when the policy of your credential demands it.

patch.description: Partially update a carrier: only the fields present in the body change, the ones you omit keep their value, and a field sent explicitly as null is cleared — that is how a tracking template or a contact is removed, never with an empty string, which is rejected. The name, the code, the tracking kind, the template, the contact and the active flag are all editable. The code keeps being unique per company, so moving it onto one that is already in use is rejected with 422 naming `code`. The template keeps its two rules: the placeholder for the tracking number and the scheme of the web. Changing the template changes the tracking URL of EVERY delivery note this carrier carries, because that URL is derived on each read and stored nowhere — which is the point of having a template, and also the reason to change it deliberately. Deactivating a carrier keeps it readable and keeps resolving the tracking of the notes that already reference it, but it can no longer be assigned to a shipment.

parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

patch.description: Update a draft invoice. Once an invoice has been issued (status `issued`), most fields become immutable per AEAT compliance. `operation_on` (the date the operation took place, when it differs from `issued_on`) can only be changed while the invoice is a draft; it cannot be later than `issued_on` (422 `operation_date_after_issue_date`) unless the first line that declares a `regime_key` uses 14 or 15. Sending `lines` replaces the whole set: a line with no `tax_rate`, no referenced tax and no product with a tax takes the DEFAULT TAX your company has set for invoices, as if you had chosen that tax (its rate, indirect-tax regime and AEAT qualification), and if there is none it is rejected with 422 `missing_required_param` (`error.param` `lines.N.tax_rate`, `error.line_index` N). A line that sends both a tax (`tax_rate_id`) and a `tax_rate` that contradicts it is rejected with 422 `parameter_invalid_value` (subcode `tax_rate_mismatch`, `error.param` `lines.N.tax_rate`): the chosen tax qualifies the line. `type` switches a draft between a complete (`F1`) and a simplified (`F2`) invoice, never a corrective one: `F2` requires simplified invoices enabled (422 `simplified_invoices_disabled`) and a total eligible for a simplified invoice (422 `simplified_invoice_not_allowed`), and `F1` requires a client (422 `business_rule_violation`, subcode `invoice_type_change_not_allowed`, `error.param` `client_id`). Changing `type` without `series_id` detaches the draft from its series, so it will be numbered in the default series of its new purpose when issued; `series_id: null` detaches it explicitly, and a series of another purpose (`invoice_kind`) is rejected right away with 422 `series_invoice_kind_mismatch`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. delete.description: Permanently delete a board column. The optional query `move_to_column_id` is the UUID of another column of the same project that receives its tasks: if the column has tasks and it is not sent, the call returns 409 `column_has_tasks`; a target that does not exist, belongs to another project or is the column being deleted returns 422 `invalid_move_target_column`. With a valid target, the tasks are appended to the end of that column in their order, each one emits its status-change event, and the column is deleted in the same transaction. Irreversible: there is no trash or restore, so send an `Idempotency-Key` header (required) to retry safely.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

get.description: Retrieve a return by its `id`, with its status and its localized label, its number once it has been approved, the document it came from by kind, public id and number, its reason, the destination warehouse, the business contact, the amount that can be refunded and the amount that was refunded, the moments of every step of its cycle, and its lines with the quantity, the reason, the inherited unit price and tax rate and the line amount. When it has been rejected it also carries the rejection reason and its note, and when it has been refunded, the corrective invoice by its public id and its number. The detail publishes no internal identifier of any kind, and it does not expose the reference of the origin line either: that reference belongs to the pre-flight read and to the body of the request. A return of another company answers exactly like one that does not exist.

patch.description: Partially update a return: the header reason, the destination warehouse, the invoice to be corrected and the notes. Only the fields present in the body change, the ones you omit keep their value, and a field sent explicitly as null unsets it — that is how a destination warehouse or a chosen invoice is cleared. An empty body is accepted and does nothing, which is what a partial update means. The body does NOT accept lines: the lines of a return are fixed at the moment it is requested, and correcting them means deleting the return and requesting it again while it is still in that status. Only a return that is still REQUESTED can be edited; on any other status the call is rejected as a business rule violation with 422 naming the status, never with 403. The warehouse and the invoice are resolved inside your company, so a reference of another company is rejected without revealing that it exists.

delete.description: Delete one package from the shipment of a delivery note. It returns no content. The total weight of the shipment drops by the weight of that package, because the total is the sum of the packages and is recalculated on each read. The positions of the remaining packages are NOT renumbered, so a gap in the sequence is expected and means nothing is missing: the order is what the position preserves, not the count. The package is resolved by the double key company and delivery note, so one of another company and one that hangs from a different note of yours both answer as not found. Irreversible: this API publishes no operation that brings a deleted package back — declaring it again creates a new one, with a new id and a new position at the end — so it requires an `Idempotency-Key` when the policy of your credential demands it.

patch.description: Partially update one package of a delivery note: only the fields present in the body change, the ones you omit keep their value, and a field sent explicitly as null is cleared. The reference, the weight, the three dimensions and the notes are editable; the POSITION is not, because it is what keeps the packages in the order they were declared. Weight and dimensions keep the ceiling and the two decimal places of their columns, so a value above the ceiling is rejected with 422 and nothing is written. Editing a weight changes the total weight of the shipment, which is the sum of the packages and is recalculated on each read. The package is resolved by the DOUBLE key company and delivery note: one of another company, and one that exists but hangs from a different note of yours, both answer exactly like one that does not exist.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. delete.description: Disconnect a store: the link is closed and its credential destroyed, so reconnecting it means authorising again at the provider. The invoices it already produced are kept — under VeriFactu a document is never deleted — and later deliveries from that store are recorded without being processed. Because the operation is irreversible, it requires an `Idempotency-Key` header. Responds 204 with no body; a missing store or one from another company returns 404.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. post.description: Dispatch a stock transfer: the goods leave the ORIGIN warehouse and stay in transit until they are received. It takes no body and it dispatches the lines as they stand, so a transfer with no lines is rejected with 422, and dispatching one that is already dispatched returns 422 with the code that names that condition. This call DOES move stock, and it is the part to read before building your own reconciliation: dispatching records, for every line, the OUTGOING movement in the origin warehouse, so the balance of that article in that warehouse goes down by the quantity dispatched. That ledger entry is written only for articles whose stock you track and while stock management is active for your company; when it is not, the transfer still advances but no balance changes. Irreversible: no published operation takes that movement back, so it requires an `Idempotency-Key` when the policy of your credential demands it. Returns the transfer as it is left.

get.description: Download the PDF representation of an invoice. Returns the binary PDF stream (`application/pdf`). The optional `format` query chooses the paper: `a4` (default, with the company template), `ticket_80` (80 mm thermal roll) or `ticket_58` (58 mm roll); any other value returns 422 with a `parameter_invalid_enum` entry (and its `allowed_values`) in `error.errors[]`. Tickets are laid out for a receipt printer — QR of 30 mm, no header band or footer — and each format is rendered and cached separately, so asking for a ticket never changes the company template of the A4. The response carries an `ETag` that changes with the invoice, with its VeriFactu alta (so a PDF downloaded before the alta, without QR, never revalidates as current) and with the `format`; send it back in `If-None-Match` to get `304 Not Modified` when nothing changed.

get.description: Download the CSV template of the bulk import of managed accounts: `text/csv` in UTF-8 with a BOM, separated by semicolons, with the closed set of columns (`mode`, `external_ref`, `plan`, `tax_id`, `legal_name`, `address`, `postal_code`, `city`, `province`, `country_code`, `owner_email`, `display_name`, `language`, `access_level`) and an example row marked `# ejemplo`, which the import ignores. `mode` is required on every row (`own_nif` or `managed_account`); a `managed_account` row requires `external_ref`, and `plan` is only allowed in `managed_account` rows (an `own_nif` row inherits the plan of your account). The import also reads comma- and tab-separated files and skips up to 20 lines of preamble before the header row. The template is the same for every provider and reads no data of your account. Requires the privileged `accounts:read` scope, which `*` does not cover: 403 `privileged_scope_required` without the account provider privilege granted by Factuarea.

200.description: CSV template of the accounts file of the bulk import of managed accounts: UTF-8 with BOM, `;` separator and CRLF line endings, the closed header row (`mode`, `external_ref`, `plan`, `tax_id`, `legal_name`, `address`, `postal_code`, `city`, `province`, `country_code`, `owner_email`, `display_name`, `language`, `access_level`) and one example row whose first cell starts with `# ejemplo`, which the import always ignores. Without that marker, the example row is a valid `managed_account` row.

get.description: Download the PDF representation of a packing list. Returns the binary PDF stream (`application/pdf`). Pass `?download=1` for `Content-Disposition: attachment` (file download); otherwise it is served `inline`. It is the document that travels WITH the goods: the shipment identified by the number of the delivery note and its packages reference, the packages ordered by position with their weight and dimensions, the derived total weight, and the contents. It carries no amounts, so it can be handed to the carrier and to the recipient without disclosing what was charged.

post.description:
Simulate what a rule would do against a sample event: whether its condition would match, why it could not be evaluated when it cannot, and what each of its actions would resolve to. It executes NOTHING — no email is sent, no document changes, no third party is called, no quota is consumed and neither a run nor a step is recorded — which is why it takes the read scope even though it is a POST (the sample event has to travel in the body).

IMPORTANT — if the rule acts on documents (send a document by email, send a payment reminder, change a status, tag an entity), pass `event_aggregate_id` with the id of a real document of yours. Without it the dry run reports that no step would run, and a perfectly correct rule looks broken.

A condition that cannot be evaluated is not an HTTP error: it comes back as `condition_error` with 200, because seeing exactly that is what the dry run is for. A step a guardrail would cut short in production comes back as non-executable with its typed reason, never as a success.

Nothing was created or modified — resolve the cause and retry the same request. Version note: `error.type` is `payment_required_error` from `Factuarea-Version: 2026-09-01` onwards; earlier versions receive `invalid_request_error` for the three codes that predate that cut (`payment_method_required`, `employee_seat_payment_method_required` and `employee_seat_charge_failed`; every other 402 code, such as `addon_required`, `plan_limit_exceeded` or the additional tax ID codes, is newer and always carries `payment_required_error`). `error.code` is stable across every version.

delete.description: End the management of one of your managed accounts: from the next request your account loses access to it and to its tax IDs. If the holder already claimed it and your account paid it, the payment moves to the holder; when the holder has no payment method the management still ends, your account stops paying and the tax IDs of the account are suspended until the holder takes over the payment. An account whose management ends before being claimed stays non-operable until it is claimed. Returns 200 with the managed account and `management.status: ended`. Returns 422 `enterprise_contract_transition_required` for an enterprise account by contract without a destination plan, and 422 `idempotency_key_required` because ending the management is irreversible. The account axis admits only a managed account provisioned by the credential account, with the management in force and in the same environment as the key; your own account, a foreign or non-existent one, one of the other environment and one whose management ended all return the same 404 `account_not_found`. Requires the privileged `accounts:write` scope, which `*` does not cover: without the account provider privilege granted by Factuarea, or when the person who issued the key is no longer an owner or admin of your account, it returns 403 `privileged_scope_required`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

post.description:
Export a selection of invoices to a spreadsheet (`xlsx` or `csv`) and stream it back as an attachment. Narrow it with the filters of the body (`invoice_ids`, `client_id`, `series_id`, `status`, `date_from`, `date_to`, `search`) or omit them to export everything. `format` picks the layout: `SUMMARY` (one row per invoice) or `ITEMS` (one row per line).

```http
POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/export/excel
Content-Type: application/json

{"format": "SUMMARY", "status": "paid", "date_from": "2026-01-01", "date_to": "2026-03-31"}
```

Limits: the selection is capped at 5,000 invoices; a wider one returns 422 `export_limit_exceeded`.

Two catalog codes carry this status, both with `error.type: invalid_request_error`: `export_document_cap_exceeded` (the request covers more documents than the cap for that artifact allows — narrow the date range or export in batches) and `export_byte_cap_exceeded` (the artifact would weigh more than the byte cap; `error.subcode` says whether it was rejected up front from the size estimate, `before_writing`, or aborted mid-packaging, `while_writing`, in which case the partial file was deleted and nothing is served). Retrying the same request unchanged returns the same error — ask for less, do not wait. A third, unrelated code shares this status on every write operation: `payload_too_large`, raised when the REQUEST body exceeds the 1 MB limit, which is about what you send and not about the size of what you asked to build.

post.description: Look up a carrier by the code it was created with, so your own system can reconcile its carrier master against ours without storing our ids. It is a read that travels as a POST because the code goes in the body: nothing is created, nothing is modified and no idempotency key is needed. The match is EXACT, after normalizing the code exactly as the creation does — trimmed and upper-cased —, and that is the point of the operation: searching `SEUR` over the listing would also match `SEUR-EXP` and leave you to disambiguate, while a code identifies one carrier and only one. A carrier that is no longer active is still found, because retiring one does not free its code. A code that does not exist and a code that belongs to another company answer exactly the same way, so probing codes tells you nothing about them.

post.description: Looks up a single invoice by its number. parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

get.description: Retrieve the module access level of an account member (`{member}` is the account member `id`) in the tax ID passed in the required `company_id` query parameter. `restrictions` is a DENY list — section to withdrawn capabilities out of `access`, `create`, `edit`, `delete`, `send` and `export` — so an empty object means no restriction at all, never no access; it applies on top of the member grant on that tax ID. `grants` is the opposite list: the administrator-only sections (never the four Administrator keys) that were GRANTED to the member in that tax ID; it is empty for most members and always empty for an `owner` or `admin`, who hold every permission of their plan. A member that does not exist, belongs to another account or has no access to that tax ID, and a tax ID outside the account or outside what your credential reads, all return the same 404 `member_not_found`. Requires the `members:read` scope, which `*` does not cover: the API key must list it explicitly.

patch.description: Replace the FULL set of module restrictions of an account member (`{member}` is the account member `id`) in the tax ID named by `company_id`, and optionally the set of administrator-only sections GRANTED to that member there. The body substitutes every previous restriction, so repeating the call leaves the same state and an empty `restrictions` object lifts them all; lifting restrictions never grants more than the member grant on that tax ID. `grants` is optional: when omitted the member grants of sections are left as they are, and when sent — even empty — it replaces them entirely, in the same transaction as the restrictions. Returns 404 `member_not_found` when the member or the tax ID is outside the account or your credential scope, and 422 `business_rule_violation` when restricting yourself, the account owner or a section that cannot be restricted; with subcode `permissions_not_applicable_to_administrator` (`param` `restrictions`) when the member is an `owner` or `admin` of the account, who take neither restrictions nor grants; with subcode `administrator_key_not_grantable` (`param` `grants`) when a granted section is one of the four Administrator keys; and with subcode `module_not_grantable` (`param` `grants`) when a granted section is not administrator-only or the company does not have it. Requires the `members:write` scope, which `*` does not cover: the API key must list it explicitly.

get.description: Return one `company_stats` row per company (tax ID) of the account that your credential reads: the number of issued invoices in the period (`invoices_count`, sent, paid and overdue ones), what they invoice (`total_invoiced`, a 2-decimal string) and the last issued invoice of the company regardless of the period (`last_invoice`, or `null` when it has not issued any). The rows cover the same companies as `GET /v1/accounts/{account}/companies`, archived ones hidden. The period is `date_from`/`date_to` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, both optional and inclusive); without them it is the current calendar year, and with only one the other end stays within the same year. The list is not paginated, because an account holds a bounded set of companies: `has_more` is always `false` and `next_cursor` always `null`. An `{account}` that is not the account of your credential returns 404 `account_not_found` (anti-enumeration), and a malformed date or an end before the start returns 422 `invalid_param_value`.

get.description: Retrieve the API usage of your account for the CURRENT period: total requests, total documents, and the per-tax-ID breakdown over every tax ID the credential reaches. The subject is the ACCOUNT, never the tax ID acting on the request, so the answer is the same whichever one is effective — narrowing it by the effective company would turn an account read into a company read and the breakdown would stop adding up to its own total. This is a different counter from automation run usage, which lives on the company axis and IS scoped to the credential company; the two coexist and neither replaces the other. The period is not a parameter: it is resolved server-side, so this is not a historical report. An account identifier that is not yours returns 404 `account_not_found`, indistinguishable from one that does not exist.

get.description: Return a combined agenda between `from` and `to` (at most 93 days, both included): due tasks and, from other modules, invoice and purchase invoice due dates, quote and pro forma expiries, recurring invoice runs, tax deadlines, absences and holidays. `sources` chooses the layers. Every layer also needs the read scope of its own resource and its module (for example `invoices:read` for invoice due dates, `absences:read` for absences); layers the key cannot read are left out without an error, and `sources` in the response lists the layers actually served. `assignee_id` (`me` or a member id) filters the task layer. The whole window is returned in one page.

parameters.name: company
parameters.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of the company. Get it from `GET /v1/me` (`data.scope[].id`).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day of the window (`YYYY-MM-DD`, included). Required.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day of the window (`YYYY-MM-DD`, included). Required. The window spans at most 93 days: a longer or inverted window returns 400 `parameter_invalid_range` on `to`.

parameters.name: sources
parameters.description: Comma-separated agenda layers: `tasks`, `invoice_due`, `purchase_invoice_due`, `quote_expiry`, `proforma_expiry`, `recurring_invoice_run`, `fiscal_deadline`, `absence`, `holiday`; default all.

parameters.name: assignee_id
parameters.description: Only filters the `tasks` layer: `me` for the member who owns the API key, or the UUID of a member of your company. Any other value returns 422 `invalid_param_value`.

get.description: Read how many automation runs the company has consumed in the current period, the quota of its plan (`limit: null` means no automatic ceiling; Enterprise capacity is agreed by contract), the instant the counter resets and the consumption percentage at which the account is warned. Use it to anticipate running out of budget — activating a rule deliberately does not pre-check the quota. get.description: Return the CURRENT representation with which your company authorizes Factuarea to remit its VeriFactu records to AEAT on its behalf (social collaboration, annex I, or a power of attorney registered with AEAT): kind, signer, grant date, last day of validity (`valid_until`) and whether it has expired (`is_expired`), and whether the signed document is custodied. A representation that has expired is still returned (`is_active: true`, `is_expired: true`) but no longer enables third-party remission: register a new one. The document itself is never returned. Returns 404 `resource_not_found` only when there is no current (not revoked) representation.

post.description: Register the representation that lets Factuarea remit your VeriFactu records to AEAT with its own certificate. Send `multipart/form-data` with `kind` (`social_collaboration_annex_i` or `aeat_power_of_attorney`), `signer_name`, `signer_tax_id`, `granted_on` and the evidence: the signed annex I as `document` (PDF, up to 5 MB, validated by magic bytes) for social collaboration, and the proof of the power of attorney as `document` or its reference in `power_of_attorney_reference` for a power of attorney. The document is custodied encrypted and counts against your storage quota (402 `storage_quota_exceeded`). If a representation was already active it is revoked and kept in the history, and the new one becomes the active one. The optional `valid_until` sets the last day of validity (not before `granted_on`, at most 5 years after it); without it the representation does not expire, and once the day has passed it stops enabling third-party remission (you are warned 30 and 7 days ahead and when it expires). If your company already remits through a third-party mode, registering a representation of the OTHER kind moves the mode to the one that kind asks for (annex I → `social_collaborator`, power of attorney → `power_of_attorney`) — or back to `own_certificate` when that mode cannot be used, because this instance does not offer the social collaborator or the new representation is already expired — and the records that were blocked waiting for it are reactivated. With `own_certificate` nothing changes: switch explicitly with `PATCH /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/settings`, which requires this representation. Returns 201 with `data` (the new representation) and `remission_mode`, the remission mode that results, plus a `Location` header; an invalid payload returns 422 (`param` names the field; the evidence that is missing or not a valid PDF is `business_rule_violation` / `invalid_representation`).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

remission_mode.description: Remission mode of the company AFTER registering: registering a representation moves a company that remits through a third-party mode to the mode of the new kind (or back to `own_certificate` when that mode cannot be used); with `own_certificate` it does not change.

402.description: The operation requires a payment that could not be completed: either no payment method is on file (`error.details.payment_setup_url` links to the Billing Portal where it can be set up), the immediate charge was declined by the payment provider, the account lacks the plan or add-on this operation bills against, the annual document limit is reached (`plan_limit_exceeded`, with `error.details.period_end` indicating the end of the period — wait until it has ended or upgrade the plan to continue now), or the account has reached its maximum usage (`storage_quota_exceeded`, raised by upload operations such as signing a delivery note or attaching a file to an expense — contact support before retrying). Nothing was created or modified — resolve the cause and retry the same request. Version note: `error.type` is `payment_required_error` from `Factuarea-Version: 2026-09-01` onwards; earlier versions receive `invalid_request_error` for the three codes that predate that cut (`payment_method_required`, `employee_seat_payment_method_required` and `employee_seat_charge_failed`; every other 402 code, such as `addon_required`, `plan_limit_exceeded` or the additional tax ID codes, is newer and always carries `payment_required_error`). `error.code` is stable across every version.

delete.description: Revoke the active representation: Factuarea stops remitting your records on your behalf and `remission_mode` goes back to `own_certificate`, so from then on the remission uses your own certificate. Revoking is TERMINAL — a revoked representation is never reactivated; register another one to authorize again — and the custodied document is kept in the history. `reason` is optional, 3 to 500 characters, in the JSON body or in the query (a text outside that range returns 422 with `param=reason` instead of being trimmed); without it «Revocada vía API v1.» is recorded. Returns 204; with no current representation it returns 422 `business_rule_violation` / `invalid_representation`.

get.description: Return the consolidated time-tracking compliance panel for your portfolio: one row per `active` company within your credential scope (the owner company of the account excluded), each projected from that company's latest monthly close without recomputation — whether the current (last closable) period is closed, its status (`closed`/`reopened`), the last closed period (`last_closed_year`/`last_closed_month`), and the aggregated `total_balance_minutes`, `total_overtime_minutes` and `employee_count`. Scope-bound: the rows are resolved from the tax IDs your credential reaches, never from the payload, so a credential scoped to one tax ID sees that tax ID and no other company. Unlike the per-company endpoints, which name a single company in the `{company}` path segment, this aggregates across the scope in one call. Returned as `{ "data": [ConsolidatedWorkforce, ...] }`.

get.description:
Answer "did the email for these documents go out?" for a whole batch at once, instead of paging through the deliveries of each one: per document, how many emails were sent, the last status, the last hand-off and how many failed. Ideal to paint a "sent / not sent" column over a page of invoices in a single call.

get.description: Return the billing status of the per-employee add-on for your company: whether the `employee-seats` subscription is active, how many seats are billed (`quantity`), how many employees are active, and the recurring per-seat cost with VAT. Amounts are euros as 2-decimal strings and are `null` when the cost is not resolvable (not subscribed, no active plan, enterprise outside Stripe, sandbox) — never a misleading 0. `seats_billable` tells whether your plan MUST be paying per seat, independently of `subscribed`: `subscribed: false` with `seats_billable: true` and active employees is a billing anomaly, while `seats_billable: false` is a legitimate no-charge state (enterprise by contract, trial or sandbox). Employees never count towards the plan `users` seat limit. Returns 403 `billing_managed_by_provider` when the billing of the account is managed by its provider.

get.description: Return the time balance of an arbitrary period of an employee: expected vs worked minutes, the balance and overtime per day, and the period totals. The employee is the `{employee}` (UUID v7) in the path; `from` and `to` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) are required. This is the same contract the monthly close reuses over closed periods. Each day carries `is_unscheduled` (within the employment period but with no schedule in effect) and `is_outside_employment` (before `hire_date` or after `termination_date`); on both, expected, balance and overtime are 0 and worked minutes are the minutes actually clocked, so the period balance is the sum of the daily balances. A range where `to` is before `from` returns 422. Totals are in minutes. A computed resource: it exposes `employee_id`, never an `id`.

get.description: Returns a temporary signed URL to the invoice PDF instead of streaming the bytes. The optional `format` query chooses the paper: `a4` (default), `ticket_80` or `ticket_58` (80 mm / 58 mm thermal rolls); any other value returns 422 with a `parameter_invalid_enum` entry (and its `allowed_values`) in `error.errors[]`, and each format is rendered and cached separately. Convenient for embedding in emails or messaging apps. The URL is signed, needs no API key, only opens this invoice and stops working at `expires_at` (24 h) with 403 — or earlier with 404 if the invoice or the company branding changes after the PDF was generated: request a new link instead of storing it. Dual contract: 200 with the URL when the PDF is already materialized; 202 with `status: pendiente` when generation was enqueued (the PDF renders on the `pdf` queue) — retry until you get the 200. The `pdf_url` of the 202 is also signed and answers 404 until the PDF is ready.
