get.description: Check whether one of the NIFs within your credential scope is ready to ISSUE invoices, as a FISCAL and module state: a `can_issue` verdict, a closed list of `blockers`, and the signals it was composed from (census status, default series, fiscal profile, operability, missing modules). This is a NEUTRAL read: it never inspects or reports subscription, plan, tier, quota, usage or price, and it never answers with a payment-required state. `{company}` names the NIF being CHECKED, not the company that owns the data, and membership is decided by the credential scope alone. A test credential of a live account reads, like the equivalent live credential, the live NIFs its sandbox scope mirrors (the whole portfolio when its scope holds the sandbox of the account owner). A NIF that does not exist, belongs to another account, falls outside what your credential reads (including a live NIF for a test credential of a legacy test account owned by a sandbox), or carries a malformed identifier all return the SAME 404 `resource_not_found` (`param: company`) — never a 403 — so the answer cannot be used to census NIFs by difference.

get.description: Introspect the credential authenticating the request: its public identity, the account it belongs to, its environment (`live`/`test`), its rate-limit tier, its EFFECTIVE scopes (a scope trimmed by the plan of the scoped tax IDs is not listed) and the tax IDs it reaches, each with its opaque identifier and its fiscal identifier. Use it to validate a credential and discover its scope in a single call — including the single-tax-ID case, where it is how you learn your own opaque identifier. `account` also carries its `name`, its `environment`, whether it is an account provider (`is_provider`) and the privileged scopes Factuarea granted it (`privileged_scopes`), and `client_accounts[]` lists the accounts of your clients the credential account reaches through a relation (granted or provisioned), with their access level, status, whether your account pays them and their environment. `client_accounts[]` is filled only when the credential has the privileged `accounts:read` scope in effect (otherwise it is empty and `client_accounts_visible` is `false`) and holds at most 100 accounts (`client_accounts_has_more` tells whether there are more; `GET /v1/accounts` lists them all). It never returns per-tax-ID settings (personalization, plan, add-ons): those belong to the company axis.

get.description: Return the live monthly time sheet of an employee for the open (in-progress) period: expected vs worked minutes, the balance and overtime per day, and the monthly totals. `employee_id` (UUID v7) is required; `month` (`YYYY-MM`) defaults to the current month. The sheet is recomputed on every request from the immutable ledger, so a just-recorded clock entry is reflected without closing the month. Expected minutes discount public holidays and approved absences. Each day carries `is_unscheduled` (within the employment period but with no schedule in effect: the minutes actually clocked count as worked, while expected, balance and overtime are 0) and `is_outside_employment` (before `hire_date` or after `termination_date`: expected 0 even if a schedule covers the day). The `total_*` fields cover the whole month, so in the current month they are a projection that already subtracts the expected minutes of today and of the remaining days; `to_date` holds the actual accumulation of the closed days (every day before today) with `through_date`, and is `through_date: null` with zeros when no day has closed yet. Totals are in minutes. A computed resource: it exposes `employee_id`, never an `id`.
get.summary: Retrieve an employee’s monthly time sheet

parameters.name: company
parameters.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of the company. Get it from `GET /v1/me` (`data.scope[].id`).

parameters.name: employee_id
parameters.description: Employee ID (UUID v7) whose monthly sheet to retrieve.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Sheet month in YYYY-MM format; defaults to the current month.

It only answers for your own account: `{account}` is the credential account, and any other returns 404 `account_not_found`. Requires the privileged `accounts:read` scope, which `*` does not cover (403 `privileged_scope_required` otherwise).

get.description: Read the three-way match of a purchase order: per line, how much was ordered, how much arrived in posted goods receipts and how much the supplier invoices linked to the order have billed — the three in the base unit —, plus the list of those invoices with their public id, their number, their match status and their total. An order with no invoice linked is not an error: it answers with an empty list and the match status that means it does not apply. This read is anchored to the ORDER and does not break the deviation down line by line; that detail comes back in the response of the three match writes, which are anchored to the invoice.

get.description: Preview the prorated amount the account would be charged for registering or activating ADDITIONAL tax IDs, decided by the same gate as those writes and computed from the Stripe upcoming invoice of the account titular, without charging. Use `count` (≥1) to preview a batch, or `company_ids` for a coverage-aware preview: tax IDs still covered for the current period cost `0` (`already_covered: true`). `amount` is the taxable base in euros as a 2-decimal string (`tax_amount` and `total` too; only `recurring_base_cents` and `recurring_total_cents` are in cents); `requires_payment_method` is `true` when no payment method is on file. A tax ID that is not additional, a test account, and an account without a current plan or whose plan does not allow additional tax IDs preview `0`: this read never returns 402 nor the plan or cap rejections of the writes. It returns 403 `billing_managed_by_provider` when the billing of the account is managed by its provider, and 404 when a `company_ids` value is not a tax ID of the account.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

get.description:
Return, in a single document, the Spanish tax knowledge you need to build a compliant invoicing form: indirect tax regimes (IVA, IGIC, IPSI) with their legal rates and their VeriFactu L1 code, header-level operation regimes with the legal wording each one requires, exemption causes with their AEAT code, legal wording and article of the Spanish VAT Act, the system IRPF withholding rates and the closed matrix of legal VAT/equivalence-surcharge pairs. It replaces the hardcoded table every integration ends up maintaining by hand.

The catalog carries no data of the authenticated company: two different companies receive byte-identical bodies for the same language, and `retention_rates` never includes the custom taxes a company creates in the application, which `GET /v1/companies/{company}/taxes` lists. Withholding rates are published in POSITIVE, so apply them as a deduction from the taxable base.

This is the catalog of what the platform supports, NOT an exhaustive normative list of every regime, exemption or withholding rate Spanish law defines. Use it to know what you can send to this API; do not read it as tax advice or as a substitute for the legislation.

Every entry carries its `label` (and, in the two normative blocks, its `description`) in Spanish, English and Catalan at once. `Accept-Language` only picks the language reported in `primary_language`; it never filters the payload, so one cached document is enough to render a multilingual selector. The response is cacheable: it ships `ETag` and a public `Cache-Control`, and sending the validator back in `If-None-Match` returns 304 with no body. Two languages produce two different `ETag`s, because the negotiated language travels inside the body.

get.description: List the issuance evidence of a transport document in chronological order: versions issued or modified, manual closes (`closed`) and automatic closes (`auto_closed`), reopenings, cancellation, supersession, email deliveries with their recipients and public downloads with truncated IP (/24 IPv4, /48 IPv6) and user agent. Public downloads are recorded once per hour for the same network and version (the user agent is stored but does not count as a different download), and only the first 100 are listed: `meta.downloads_total` is the number recorded and `meta.downloads_listed` how many are in `data`. Each entry names its actor in `actor_name` (user, API key or MCP client, with the name it had then; `null` for automatic closes and public downloads) and `occurred_at` carries its UTC offset. It is the proof of issuance of art. 7.1 of Orden FOM/2861/2012. A draft returns 422.

It also reports the pending-remission alert: `pending_incident_count` — the records still waiting to be remitted to AEAT: pending (or without a state yet), in error of ANY kind, submitted and rejected records that were already subsanados; accepted records and rejected ones still waiting for your correction are not counted, nor are sandbox companies —, `blocked_incident_count` — of those, the blocked ones: errors with no automatic retry that need your action (see `POST /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/records/retry-blocked`) — and `oldest_pending_at`, the generation time of the oldest pending record. Those three fields are never affected by the filters: they are the figure art. 16 of Order HAC/1177/2024 asks you to show the taxpayer. Returned as `{ "data": VeriFactuStats }`.

post.description:
Import canonical contacts from CSV with target roles, explicit field mapping, conflict strategy and optional `dry_run`. Returns per-row classifications and a stable import_uuid for synchronous 200 and queued 202 results. Dry-run is always synchronous and does not reserve or consume quota. New admissions share bulk_import_rows_per_month; imports admitted under the previous contact exemption retain it. Applied create/update/add_role rows consume quota; admission rejects with 429 import_row_quota_exceeded before writing or queueing when the allowance is exhausted.

Fill in the downloaded template before applying the import. A file with no data rows returns 422 with code `business_rule_violation`, subcode `empty_import` and param `file`, before creating an import record or queueing work. Preview and `dry_run=true` accept a file containing only column headers and preserve `source_headers` with total 0.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.factuarea.com/v1/companies/{company}/contacts/import \
  -F file=@contacts.csv \
  -F 'target_roles[]=customer' \
  -F 'target_roles[]=supplier' \
  -F conflict_strategy=reject \
  -F dry_run=true
```

Limits: the file accepts CSV, TXT, XLSX or XLS up to 10 MB; `target_roles` accepts at most three distinct roles. Use the preview endpoint before importing. A queued import returns `202`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

post.description: Import tasks into a project from a JSON document (`factuarea.tasks.v1`, or an export of other task tools in a supported format). The import is synchronous only and accepts up to 200 tasks per call: more than 200 returns 422, so split the file. The report lists, per task, its `index` in the document, the created `id` and `key` or the `error` that prevented it; it has no `mode` or `run_id` because the API does not create background import runs. At most the first 200 warnings are listed; `warnings_total` counts them all and `warnings_truncated` tells whether some were left out. Requires `projects:write` only: it creates tasks and comments even if the key has no `tasks:write`. Requires an `Idempotency-Key`: repeating the call with the same key and the same body returns the same report without creating tasks again, and reusing the key with a different body returns 422 `idempotency_key_reused`. Importing again with a new key creates a new copy of the tasks. The key is mandatory over REST (a request without it is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required`); only the MCP tool `import_project_tasks` can be called without one, and then every call creates a copy.

post.description: Invite a person by email to join the ACCOUNT with an account `role` (`admin` or `member`) and the required `grants` list (it may be empty; only a `member` carries grants, each one a tax ID of the account by its `company_id` UUID and a `level`). This is how a person who already exists on the platform joins an account. Set `send_email: false` to skip the email and deliver the link yourself. Returns 201 with the invitation and a `Location` header; only a copy-link invitation (`send_email: false`) carries its acceptance `secret` and `accept_url`, exactly once. With `send_email: true` the secret travels only in the email and both fields are `null`, so the invitee proves control of the mailbox. An idempotent replay returns them as `null`. Inviting an `admin` requires a credential scope that covers every tax ID of the account. Returns 400 `parameter_missing` when `grants` is absent, 422 `grants_only_for_member`, 422 `grant_company_not_in_account`, and 422 `business_rule_violation` when a pending invitation already exists for that address, the person is already a member, a tax ID repeats or the account reached its plan user limit. The external advisor invitation is only available in the web app. Requires the `invitations:write` scope, which `*` does not cover: the API key must list it explicitly.

post.description: Turn the selected billable time into a DRAFT invoice for the project billing contact, grouped by `grouping`, and mark those entries as invoiced. Requires the `invoices:write` scope (it creates an invoice), not a projects scope. The draft is numbered when issued from the invoice API. Entries already invoiced return 422 `task_time_entry_invoiced`; if the plan has used up its invoices or yearly documents, 402 `limit_exceeded` and nothing is created. Sending the same `batch_id` again with the same request returns the same invoice; reusing a `batch_id` with a different project selection, grouping or entries (or after its invoice was deleted) returns 422 `idempotency_key_reused`. Deleting the draft invoice releases the entries.

post.description:
Issues a draft invoice without sending it: assigns its definitive series number, freezes the issuer and customer snapshots, sets `issued_at`, registers the VeriFactu record when applicable and emits the `invoice.issued` event. No email is sent and the delivery mark is not set (`is_sent` stays `false`); to deliver it use `POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/send`, or `POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/mark-sent` with `Factuarea-Version: 2026-10-01` when you delivered it through another channel. Only a `draft` can be issued: any other status returns 422 `invalid_status_transition`. Issuing is irreversible and consumes a series number, so send an `Idempotency-Key` to retry safely. Available in every API version; the response follows the effective version (before `2026-10-01` the issued invoice is published as `status: sent`).

**Signing certificate (NO VERI*FACTU).** Only when the company has VeriFactu enabled in NO VERI*FACTU mode, the alta billing record of this operation is signed with the company's electronic certificate (art. 6.c and 14 of Order HAC/1177/2024), and a certificate that is missing, expired, revoked, issued for another tax id or unreadable is rejected **before** the invoice is issued: 422 `verifactu_not_eligible` with `error.subcode: signing_certificate_unavailable`; `error.param` says what is missing (`certificate`: the company certificate; `representation`: the representation that lets Factuarea sign on its behalf is not active; `system_certificate`: the Factuarea certificate is unavailable, nothing for you to fix). The invoice stays exactly as it was (a draft without a number) and nothing is consumed: upload a valid certificate in Settings → Digital certificate (or register the representation in the third-party remission modes) and repeat the same call. post.description: Issue a draft transport document. It checks the minimum data (shipper name, tax ID and full address; carrier name and tax ID; at least one shipment with origin, destination, goods and declared measure; tractor plate; transport date), that every origin and destination is in Spain and that every transport date is today or later (Europe/Madrid). In a single atomic operation it assigns the next number of the `DC` series and the permanent public URL, renders and stores version 1 of the PDF with its sha256, and moves the document to `issued`. Missing data returns 422 `transport_document_not_issuable` with the list in `error.details.missing`, using this closed vocabulary: `shipper.name`, `shipper.tax_id`, `shipper.address`, `carrier.name`, `carrier.tax_id`, `vehicle.tractor_plate`, `transport_date`, `shipments` (no shipment) and `shipments.N.origin|destination|goods|measure` with `N` counting from 1. A PDF over 5 MB returns 422 `transport_document_pdf_too_large` and nothing is issued. Irreversible: requires `Idempotency-Key`. Hand the PDF, link or QR to the driver before the transport starts.

post.description: Link a supplier invoice to a purchase order so the three-way match can be evaluated: what was ordered, what arrived in posted goods receipts and what the invoice bills. The body carries the purchase order by its public id. The response is the match of that invoice with the deviation broken down line by line — the typed reason and its magnitude — so the outcome of the decision is read without a second call, and the invoice does not move forward on its own. The scope is not the one the path suggests: this operation needs the WRITE scope of the PURCHASE ORDER, because matching is a capability of the order and it is the module of the order that a company may not have contracted; a credential holding only the write scope of purchase invoices is rejected. Linking against an order of another company returns 404, identical to an order that does not exist. Not irreversible: the link is undone from the application. Be aware of what this version publishes and what it does not — unlinking is not published, so you can link through the API and you cannot undo that link through the API.

get.description: Inspect the requests made with ANY API key of your account, newest first, in the environment of the credential (a `live` key sees the live traffic and a `test` key the test traffic), so you can debug your integrations without opening a support ticket: what was called, what came back, how long it took and, when a call failed, the error it returned. It takes the same filters as the company listing (`method`, `status_range`, `only_errors`, `api_key_prefix`, `path_search` and `created_at[gte|lte]`) and `starting_after` is its only cursor: `environment` and `ending_before` are not accepted (400 `parameter_unknown`). Rows are purged after 30 days, so this is a debugging window, not an audit trail. The credential must reach every tax ID of the account and the person who issued it must be an owner or admin of the account (403 `forbidden_action` otherwise).

get.description: List the delivery attempts of one account webhook endpoint, cursor-paginated with `limit` (1-100, default 25) and `starting_after`, optionally filtered by `status` (`pending`, `delivered`, `failed`, `failed_permanently` or `cancelled`). Deliveries come OLDEST FIRST (ascending by `id`, a time-ordered UUID v7), so to look for recent failures filter by `status=failed` (or `failed_permanently`) and keep paginating with `starting_after` until `has_more` is `false`. Deliveries of an endpoint of the `test` environment are recorded but never sent: they stay `pending` with `attempt` 0. Each delivery carries the event it delivers, the tax ID it is about (`company_id`, `null` in `account.*` events that are not about a tax ID), its relationship with your account (`own` or `managed`), the attempt counters, the HTTP response of your server and the signed `payload`. An endpoint the account does not see (unknown, deleted, or of another account or environment) returns 404 `webhook_endpoint_not_found`, never an empty page. `ending_before` is not accepted (400 `parameter_unknown`).

get.description:
Browse the sealed versions of the definition of a rule, from the most recent to the oldest. Every edit seals a version and every run keeps a pointer to the one it executed, so this is how you reconstruct what a rule looked like when it ran.

IMPORTANT — the cursor of THIS listing is not a UUID. It is the only listing of the automation surface whose read path still paginates by offset, so `next_cursor` carries an opaque token of a different shape (a page number as a string). Treat it as strictly opaque: pass back verbatim the value you received and never build, parse or validate one yourself. The envelope is the canonical one, `limit` behaves as everywhere else, and `ending_before` steps one page back.

A rule of another company returns 200 with an empty list instead of 404 — an empty page tells an attacker nothing about whether the rule exists.
get.summary: List the versions of an automation rule

post.description: Register a new tax ID (company) in the account of the path, which is the credential account. `name` and `tax_id` are required, and `tax_id` must be unique within the account (a duplicate returns 409); a tax ID that already belongs to another account returns 422 `business_rule_violation` and is moved with a tax ID transfer instead. When the account already has an active tax ID, the new one is an ADDITIONAL tax ID and goes through the additional tax ID gate before anything is created: the credential must reach the titular company of the account, which pays it (403 `forbidden_action` otherwise), the account must be billed by itself (403 `billing_managed_by_provider` otherwise), hold a current plan (402 `additional_nif_plan_required` otherwise) that allows additional tax IDs — `empresario` or `enterprise`, trial included (403 `additional_nif_not_in_plan` otherwise) — and stay within its cap of active additional tax IDs (422 `business_rule_violation` with subcode `additional_nif_limit_reached`). In live mode with a paid subscription the additional tax ID is charged immediately: with no payment method on file it returns 402 `payment_method_required` (`error.details.payment_setup_url` links to where to set it up) and a declined charge returns 402 `additional_nif_charge_failed`; in every rejection nothing is created and nothing is charged. Trial and enterprise without a paid subscription are not charged. Use `GET /v1/accounts/{account}/companies/seat-charge-preview` to anticipate the cost. The person who issued the credential must be an owner or admin of the account, with the `user_management` section available: otherwise 403 `forbidden_action`, before anything is charged or changed.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

get.description: Returns the closed catalog of the PHYSICAL axis of a delivery note — how the goods progress through the warehouse and the carrier — with the public `value` of each status, its localized `label` and its UI color. Use it to populate filters and status pickers instead of hard-coding values. There are seven: pending, picking, prepared, handed over to the carrier, in transit, delivered to the recipient and failed delivery. This axis is NOT the commercial status of the document, and the distinction matters because BOTH have a status called `delivered`: the one in THIS catalog is the physical one and means the goods reached the recipient, while the commercial `delivered` — published as `sent` in the status catalog of the delivery note itself — means the note was issued to the customer. The two axes are orthogonal by design: moving one never moves the other, and neither catalog contains a single value of the other. The catalog enumerates STATUSES and not transition targets: a delivery note is born pending and no transition leads back to it, but it stays here because the filter and the badge need it.

get.description: List your goods receipts with cursor-based pagination. Filter by `status`, `purchase_order_id`, `supplier_id`, `warehouse_id`, `number` and `received_on`, and sort by reception date or by number. Each receipt comes back with the purchase order it belongs to, its warehouse and its lines.

parameters.name: company
parameters.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of the company. Get it from `GET /v1/me` (`data.scope[].id`).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of objects to return, between 1 and 100 (default 25).

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor for forward pagination: pass the `id` of the last object on the previous page (the `next_cursor` of the previous response).

parameters.name: ending_before
parameters.description: Cursor for backward pagination: pass the `id` of the first object on the current page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Goods receipt status: `created`, `posted` (the only one that consumes pending quantity) or `cancelled`. Exact match on `status`.

parameters.name: status[in]
parameters.description: Goods receipt status: `created`, `posted` (the only one that consumes pending quantity) or `cancelled`. Comma-separated list. Any of the values matches.

parameters.name: purchase_order_id
parameters.description: Purchase order ID (UUID v7) the goods were received against. An order that does not belong to the company in the path yields an EMPTY page, never a rejection. Exact match on `purchase_order_id`.

parameters.name: supplier_id
parameters.description: Business contact ID (UUID v7) of the supplier. It travels on the purchase order the receipt belongs to: the receipt does not repeat the supplier. Exact match on `supplier_id`.

parameters.name: warehouse_id
parameters.description: Receiving warehouse ID (UUID v7). A receipt registered with no warehouse never matches this filter. Exact match on `warehouse_id`.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Goods receipt number. It is stamped when the receipt is registered. Exact match on `number`.

parameters.name: number[in]
parameters.description: Goods receipt number. It is stamped when the receipt is registered. Comma-separated list. Any of the values matches.

parameters.name: number[contains]
parameters.description: Goods receipt number. It is stamped when the receipt is registered. Partial case-insensitive match (`LIKE %term%`) on `number`.

parameters.name: received_on
parameters.description: Delivery date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), chosen by whoever receives the goods and not by the server clock. Exact match on `received_on`.

parameters.name: received_on[gte]
parameters.description: Delivery date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), chosen by whoever receives the goods and not by the server clock. Greater than or equal to the given value.

parameters.name: received_on[lte]
parameters.description: Delivery date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), chosen by whoever receives the goods and not by the server clock. Less than or equal to the given value.

parameters.name: received_on[gt]
parameters.description: Delivery date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), chosen by whoever receives the goods and not by the server clock. Strictly greater than the given value.

parameters.name: received_on[lt]
parameters.description: Delivery date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), chosen by whoever receives the goods and not by the server clock. Strictly less than the given value.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order: `received_on`, `number` ascending, or with a `-` prefix for descending (default `-created`).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search. Escaped `LIKE %term%` (case-insensitive, max 80 chars) across the resource's key text columns, combined with the other filters (AND) and compatible with the cursor.

post.description: Register the arrival of goods against a purchase order: the order, the date, the warehouse the goods enter — optional —, a note and the lines that arrived, each one naming a line of the order and the quantity received in the PURCHASE unit. At least one line is required: an empty receipt is not a document, it is a mistake of whoever sends it. Quantities are converted to the base unit with the conversion factor the ORDER stored, never with the one the catalog has today. Receiving more than a line has pending returns 422 with the code that names it, before anything is created; what is pending counts POSTED receipts only, so a cancelled one gives its quantity back. The receipt is created in `created` status: nothing has moved and no quantity is consumed until you post it, which is why the creation itself is not irreversible.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

get.description: List the accounts your account provisioned, ONLY in the environment of the key: a `fact_test_` key lists your test managed accounts and a live key the live ones. Without `status` it lists only the managements in force. Filter by `status` (`provisioned`, `claimed` or `active` filter by the status of the account; `ended` returns the ones whose management ended, each with ONLY its `id`, your `external_ref` and the `management` block: your account no longer sees the current name, status, plan or tax IDs of an account it stopped managing) and by `external_ref` (zero or one result), cursor-paginated with `limit` (1-100, default 25) and `starting_after`. No item carries a claim voucher. Requires the privileged `accounts:read` scope, which `*` does not cover (403 `privileged_scope_required` otherwise). Returns 422 for a `status` outside the vocabulary or an `external_ref` longer than 128 characters, and 400 for an unknown query parameter or a malformed `limit`/`starting_after`.

post.description: Provision a SEPARATE account for one of your clients, with its tax ID (`tax_id`, `legal_name`), its plan (`emprendedor`, `empresario` or `integral`) and the `access_level` your account keeps on it (`none` by default, `view` or `operate`). Your account pays it: in live mode the account is charged on the `managed-accounts` subscription of your account. `external_ref` is YOUR reference and makes the call idempotent by itself: provisioning an `external_ref` you already provisioned returns 200 with that same account, creates nothing and issues no claim voucher (use the claim-token operation to issue a new one). A new account returns **201 Created** with the claim voucher the holder uses to take the account: with `send_email: false` (the default) `claim_token` and `claim_url` are returned EXACTLY ONCE, for you to deliver; with `send_email: true` the link travels only in the email to `owner_email` and both fields are `null`. An idempotent replay returns them as `null` too: the voucher is never stored in the clear, not even in the idempotency cache. `owner_email` is required with a live key and whenever `send_email` is `true`. The environment is the one of the key: a `fact_test_` key creates a TEST account, with no charge, no voucher (`claim_token` and `claim_url` are `null`) and outside your managed account limit. Requires the privileged `accounts:write` scope, which `*` does not cover: without the account provider privilege granted by Factuarea, or when the person who issued the key is no longer an owner or admin of your account, it returns 403 `privileged_scope_required`. Returns 402 `payment_method_required` when your account has no payment method to pay a live managed account, 409 `provisioning_account_claimed` when the `external_ref` names an account its holder already claimed, 409 `managed_account_external_ref_in_other_environment` when it names a managed account of the other environment, 422 `managed_account_plan_not_self_serve` for `enterprise` (it is only assigned by Factuarea by contract), 422 `managed_account_provider_in_trial` for a paid plan while your account is in trial (only test accounts), 422 `managed_accounts_limit_reached` at the managed account limit of your account, and 422 `idempotency_key_required` because provisioning is irreversible. The response also carries `claim_expires_at` (returned also when the link is emailed), `reactivated` (`true` when the call reactivated a management that had ended before the holder claimed the account) and, as in every read of the account, `claim` (the pending voucher without its secret), `payment_assumed_at` and `plan_renews_at`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

409.description: The request conflicts with data that already exists or with a request running at the same time. `provisioning_account_claimed`: the holder already claimed this managed account, so its voucher can no longer be reissued and its `external_ref` can no longer be provisioned again. The account belongs to its holder; read it with the retrieve operation while the management is in force. `managed_account_external_ref_in_other_environment`: a managed account of the other environment (live or test) already uses this `external_ref`. References are unique per provider across both environments: use another one. `resource_conflict`: another request was reserving identifiers for the same kind of record at that moment and this one could not complete its reservation. Nothing was written; send the request again after a few seconds.

402.description: The operation requires a payment that could not be completed: either no payment method is on file (`error.details.payment_setup_url` links to the Billing Portal where it can be set up), the immediate charge was declined by the payment provider, the account lacks the plan or add-on this operation bills against, the annual document limit is reached (`plan_limit_exceeded`, with `error.details.period_end` indicating the end of the period — wait until it has ended or upgrade the plan to continue now), or the account has reached its maximum usage (`storage_quota_exceeded`, raised by upload operations such as signing a delivery note or attaching a file to an expense — contact support before retrying). Nothing was created or modified — resolve the cause and retry the same request. Version note: `error.type` is `payment_required_error` from `Factuarea-Version: 2026-09-01` onwards; earlier versions receive `invalid_request_error` for the three codes that predate that cut (`payment_method_required`, `employee_seat_payment_method_required` and `employee_seat_charge_failed`; every other 402 code, such as `addon_required`, `plan_limit_exceeded` or the additional tax ID codes, is newer and always carries `payment_required_error`). `error.code` is stable across every version.

get.description: List the charges of a connected Stripe account that were deliberately not invoiced because a charge treatment rule excluded them. Each item exposes `id`, `connected_account_id`, `transaction_id`, `amount`, `refunded_amount` (cumulative amount Stripe has refunded, `0` if none), `net_amount` (`amount` minus `refunded_amount`), `currency`, `reason`, `charge_rule_id` (`null` if the rule was deleted), `description`, `occurred_at` and `refunded_at` (date of the latest refund, `null` if none); the three monetary fields use the same format. Filter by period with `occurred_from` and `occurred_to` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, both included, by the date the charge happened); a malformed date or an `occurred_to` earlier than `occurred_from` returns 422. Cursor paginated (`limit` 1-100, `starting_after`, `ending_before`), newest first.

get.description: List the work queue of the warehouse — the delivery notes that still have work pending on their physical axis — with cursor-based pagination. Filter by fulfilment status, by carrier, by origin warehouse and by the sales order the note came from; the last three take the public id of the resource and are resolved inside your company, so an id that belongs to another company returns an empty page and never a row. Sort by the date of the note or by its expected delivery date. Each item carries only what a work queue needs: the delivery note by its public id and its number, its fulfilment status with its label, and the origin warehouse and the source sales order as OPAQUE ids when it has them. It deliberately carries neither the carrier, nor the two dates you can sort by, nor the picking lines: resolving the name of a warehouse or the number of an order for every row would turn one listing into an extra read per row, and the lines belong to the picking list of each note, which has its own operation.

get.description: List the commercial combinations (variant × presentation × option values) declared by a product, each with its canonical `signature`, its optional own price and its activation state. An EMPTY list does not mean the product cannot be sold: it means the product is in LEGACY mode and accepts any cross of its active variants and presentations. As soon as one active combination exists the list becomes an allow-list and every cross not enumerated stops being accepted. Without the `active` filter both active and inactive combinations come back — a deactivated combination still names historical lines, and hiding it would leave already issued documents without a label. Cursor-paginated (`limit`, `starting_after`); a cursor that matches no combination of this product returns 422. A product of another company returns 404 `product_not_found`.

get.description: Read the append-only stock ledger of a product, from the most recently applied movement to the oldest, so an integration can audit where a balance came from and reconcile inventory against its own system. Each row carries the signed `delta` and the `stock_after` balance in BASE units as decimal strings, the reason, the source document, the acting user and the managing variant. `stock_after` is the balance at the instant the movement was applied and is derived from the COMPLETE ledger, so it does not change when `direction` hides the interleaved rows. Paginated by cursor (`limit` + `starting_after`); optional `direction=in|out` narrows it to stock in or stock out.

post.description: Record a partial (or total) payment against an expense and append it to its ledger. Body: `amount`, `paid_on`, `payment_method`, plus the optional `bank_account_id`, `reference` and `notes`. Three invariants are enforced and return `422`: the amount must be greater than zero and no larger than the outstanding balance, `paid_on` cannot be later than today (an earlier date than the supplier document issue date is accepted as an advance payment), and a cancelled expense accepts no payments. Once the accumulated payments cover the total, the expense settles on its own — you do not need to call `mark_paid` as well. Returns `201` with the payment just created and a `Location` header pointing at the ledger.

get.description: Read which articles of the company are below their declared stock threshold and what to buy to bring them back up: per article, the current quantity and the threshold in the base unit, the suggested quantity in the PURCHASE unit of the preferred supplier offer, the supplier, the code of that unit, the conversion factor, the unit cost and the lead time when the offer declares one. An article below its threshold with no active supplier offer is never hidden: it comes back marked as not actionable with its reason written, and the envelope adds how many are actionable and how many are not. It can be narrowed to a single supplier. This is a report calculated over the whole catalog and not a stored collection with a stable order, so it does NOT paginate by cursor: it is returned complete, and its size grows with your catalog — something to keep in mind before polling it.

get.description: List the invoices that this return could correct, each one with its public id, its number, its total and its issue date. It is the question to ask right before refunding: when the origin of a return resolves to more than one invoice, the refund cannot choose for you and is rejected asking you to name one, and this read is what gives you the identifiers to choose from. The internal identifier of a candidate is never published. A return with no candidates answers with an empty list and not with an error — the empty collection is the correct answer to a legitimate question, and the rejection belongs to the refund. A return of another company answers as not found.

get.description: Returns the closed catalog of return statuses with their public `value` and their localized `label`: requested, approved, received, refunded and rejected. Use it to populate filters and status pickers instead of hard-coding values. The cycle runs requested, approved, received and refunded; a return can be rejected from requested and from approved; and refunded and rejected are both TERMINAL. Only a return that is still requested can be edited. The catalog enumerates STATUSES and not transition targets: a return is born requested and nothing transitions back to it.

get.description: Ask what is still returnable of a document BEFORE requesting anything. The kind of the origin and its public id travel as query parameters, and the answer carries, line by line, the reference of the origin line — the one a request quotes —, the article and its variant, the description, how much was delivered, how much is already returned and how much is STILL returnable, plus the unit price and the tax rate that a request would inherit. Quantities carry four decimal places. Returns that were rejected do not count as returned, so their share is available again. This is the read that keeps you from discovering the ceiling through successive rejections. A document of another company answers as not found, and a document with nothing left to return answers with an empty list, which is the correct answer to a legitimate question and never an error.
get.summary: List the returnable lines of a document

get.description: List the availability of your articles with cursor-based pagination: per article, the physical balance, the quantity committed by live reservations and the available balance that results from the two, plus the breakdown per warehouse. Filter by warehouse, by variant and by an availability threshold to ask which articles are running low, and sort by available quantity or by article code. An article that does not manage stock travels marked as such and WITHOUT an availability figure: treating its zero as sold out would stop you from selling a service that has no stock to run out of. Availability can be negative when the physical balance is, and it is not clipped to zero. Expired reservations commit nothing and do not reduce what is returned.

parameters.name: company
parameters.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of the company. Get it from `GET /v1/me` (`data.scope[].id`).

parameters.name: warehouse_id
parameters.description: Public ID of the warehouse the figures are narrowed to. A foreign warehouse is rejected like one that does not exist. Exact match on `warehouse_id`.

parameters.name: variant_id

get.description: List the articles your company publishes to its storefront, with cursor-based pagination and the same envelope as the rest of the API: the data, whether there is more and the cursor for the next page. It is authenticated with the PUBLISHABLE storefront key, the credential that travels in the browser of an anonymous shopper, so it returns only what a shopper may see: the public id, the reference, the name, the description, the categories, the base unit, the kind of item, the applicable tax, the primary image and the three flags that say whether the article has variants, presentations or options. Cost, margin, supplier, supplier offer, reorder point, per-warehouse balance and internal notes are never published here, and the list of fields is an INCLUSION list, so a new field of the article does not reach the storefront by omission. Filter by category, by reference and by whether the article has units available, sort by name, by reference or by creation date, and page with the cursor the previous page returns; a filter the contract does not declare is rejected with a validation error. An article that is not publishable is not listed, and a company in the path that is not the one that owns the key answers exactly like a company that does not exist.

parameters.description: Cursor for forward pagination: pass the `id` of the last object on the previous page (the `next_cursor` of the previous response).

parameters.name: ending_before
parameters.description: Cursor for backward pagination: pass the `id` of the first object on the current page.

parameters.name: category

parameters.description: Commercial reference of the article. Exact match only; use the search operation for fragments. Exact match on `sku`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

402.description: The operation requires a payment that could not be completed: either no payment method is on file (`error.details.payment_setup_url` links to the Billing Portal where it can be set up), the immediate charge was declined by the payment provider, the account lacks the plan or add-on this operation bills against, the annual document limit is reached (`plan_limit_exceeded`, with `error.details.period_end` indicating the end of the period — wait until it has ended or upgrade the plan to continue now), or the account has reached its maximum usage (`storage_quota_exceeded`, raised by upload operations such as signing a delivery note or attaching a file to an expense — contact support before retrying). Nothing was created or modified — resolve the cause and retry the same request. Version note: `error.type` is `payment_required_error` from `Factuarea-Version: 2026-09-01` onwards; earlier versions receive `invalid_request_error` for the three codes that predate that cut (`payment_method_required`, `employee_seat_payment_method_required` and `employee_seat_charge_failed`; every other 402 code, such as `addon_required`, `plan_limit_exceeded` or the additional tax ID codes, is newer and always carries `payment_required_error`). `error.code` is stable across every version.

413.description: The packaged download you asked for is too large to build, so nothing was generated and no file was left on the server. Two catalog codes carry this status, both with `error.type: invalid_request_error`: `export_document_cap_exceeded` (the request covers more documents than the cap for that artifact allows — narrow the date range or export in batches) and `export_byte_cap_exceeded` (the artifact would weigh more than the byte cap; `error.subcode` says whether it was rejected up front from the size estimate, `before_writing`, or aborted mid-packaging, `while_writing`, in which case the partial file was deleted and nothing is served). Retrying the same request unchanged returns the same error — ask for less, do not wait. A third, unrelated code shares this status on every write operation: `payload_too_large`, raised when the REQUEST body exceeds the 1 MB limit, which is about what you send and not about the size of what you asked to build.

post.description: Request the correction of a time entry (RD-ley 8/2019). `time_entry_id` (UUID v7 of the entry to correct), `kind` (`add_missing_entry`/`adjust_time`/`remove_entry`), a `reason` and the `proposed` values are required. A correction is a new append-only entry that references the original entry without mutating it (analogous to a corrective invoice); the workflow stays `pending` until a manager approves or rejects it. An `add_missing_entry` or `adjust_time` correction whose proposed time falls outside the employee’s employment period (before `hire_date` or after `termination_date`) returns 422 `business_rule_violation` with subcode `clocking_outside_employment_period` and no request is created; `remove_entry` is never blocked by this rule. Returns 201 with the created request and a `Location` header.

parameters.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of the company. Get it from `GET /v1/me` (`data.scope[].id`).

post.description: Transition a delivery note to the `delivered` state (public `sent`). Canonical REST replacement for the deprecated `POST /change_status`. Returns 409 `invalid_status_transition` if the note cannot transition. Supports `Idempotency-Key` for safe retries. This `delivered` is the COMMERCIAL status of the document — the note has been issued to the customer — and it is not the physical one: a delivery note also has a FULFILMENT axis, whose own `delivered` means the goods reached the recipient and which is moved by the fulfilment-status transition and never by this operation. The two axes are orthogonal: this call changes neither the fulfilment status nor anything the fulfilment catalog publishes.

post.description:
Its meaning depends on the effective API version. **Before `2026-10-01`** (including the default version) it ISSUES a draft invoice without dispatching any email, exactly as it always did: the response publishes the invoice as `status: sent`. **From `2026-10-01`** it only records that you delivered an issued invoice to the customer through a channel of your own (WhatsApp, paper, a portal…): it sets `is_sent: true`, `sent_via: manual` and `sent_at`, and never changes the fiscal status, the number or the VeriFactu record. In that version it is only accepted on `issued` or `overdue` invoices — on a draft it returns 422 `invoice_cannot_be_marked_as_sent` (issue it first with `POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/issue`) — and it is idempotent: an invoice already marked as sent keeps its original date and channel. Because in the default version it issues the invoice, the operation stays classified as irreversible and accepts an `Idempotency-Key`.

**Signing certificate (NO VERI*FACTU).** Only when the company has VeriFactu enabled in NO VERI*FACTU mode, the alta billing record of this operation is signed with the company's electronic certificate (art. 6.c and 14 of Order HAC/1177/2024), and a certificate that is missing, expired, revoked, issued for another tax id or unreadable is rejected **before** the invoice is issued: 422 `verifactu_not_eligible` with `error.subcode: signing_certificate_unavailable`; `error.param` says what is missing (`certificate`: the company certificate; `representation`: the representation that lets Factuarea sign on its behalf is not active; `system_certificate`: the Factuarea certificate is unavailable, nothing for you to fix). The invoice stays exactly as it was (a draft without a number) and nothing is consumed: upload a valid certificate in Settings → Digital certificate (or register the representation in the third-party remission modes) and repeat the same call. Companies that have not enabled VeriFactu, and companies in VERI*FACTU mode (whose records are not signed), are never blocked by this rule.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

post.description: Record how much of one picking line has been picked, naming the delivery note and the line in the path. The quantity travels as a decimal string with four decimal places, so articles that are picked by weight travel whole, and it cannot exceed what the line asks for: more than that is rejected with 422 and nothing is recorded. Marking again OVERWRITES the value and marking zero undoes it, which is why this operation is not published as irreversible; the moment of the marking is kept even when the quantity goes back to zero. A picking line id that is valid but belongs to ANOTHER delivery note is rejected with 422 and touches nothing: the note in the path bounds the operation even though the line resolves on its own. And if the list is stale — the note was edited after the list was opened — the call is rejected with 422 and the message names the remedy: open the list again.

patch.description: Partially update a series: only the fields you send change (`name`, `code`, `counter_reset`, `number_format`, `initial_number`, `invoice_kind`; `year_reset` is the deprecated alias of `counter_reset`). The same fiscal guards as the web app apply, each one as a 422 `business_rule_violation` with its own `subcode` and nothing changed: `code` and `number_format` only while the series has no documents (`series_code_immutable_with_documents`, `series_format_immutable_with_documents`); once AEAT has accepted a record of one of its invoices, `code`, `number_format` and `initial_number` are locked (`series_locked_by_verifactu`); `initial_number` cannot open a gap (`series_initial_number_creates_gap`); `invoice_kind` is fixed with the first invoice (`series_invoice_kind_locked`) and the default series of a purpose cannot change purpose (`series_default_kind_change`). A `code` already used by another series of the same document type returns 422 with `param=code`; `document_type` cannot be changed. Returns 200 with the updated series, and 404 `series_not_found` if it does not belong to your company.

post.description: Modify an `issued` transport document during the service (method 1 of the Resolution of 5 June 2026): same number, same URL and same QR. Send the changed data plus `reason` (3–500 characters) and `data_origin` (`company` or `carrier_reported`). The parties cannot change (422 `transport_document_parties_immutable`: cancel and issue a new one) and a request that changes nothing returns 422 `transport_document_no_changes`. A document has at most 50 versions and the last one is reserved for cancelling or superseding, so the 49th modification returns 422 `transport_document_version_limit_reached` (issue a new document and mark this one as superseded); a PDF over 5 MB returns 422 `transport_document_pdf_too_large`; a goods line with an impossible weight, 422 `invalid_gross_weight`; a `shipments[].id` of another document, 422 on `shipments.N.id`; and a concurrent write that collides on an identifier, 409 `resource_conflict` (retryable, nothing saved). If the result lacks minimum data it returns 422 `transport_document_cannot_be_modified` with `error.details.missing` (same vocabulary as issuing). It stores a new full PDF version that keeps the original creation date and lists the data that is no longer valid. Irreversible: requires `Idempotency-Key`. Send the modified PDF to the driver.

post.description: Open — or re-open — the picking list of a delivery note. It takes no body: the list is BUILT from the lines the note has at this moment, one picking line per line of the note, and it comes back COMPLETE with the public id of every line, so you can start marking without a second read. Opening it on a note that ALREADY has one replaces the previous list entirely and the marking recorded on it is lost: re-opening is the operation and not an edge case of it, and it is how a stale list is refreshed after the note has been edited. Nothing replaces the list on its own, not even when it is stale — it is always somebody asking for it. Opening does NOT move the fulfilment status: the physical axis advances only through its own transition operation. A cancelled delivery note does not enter fulfilment, so the call is rejected as a business rule violation with 422 — never 403 — and no list is created. Irreversible, because the previous list and the work recorded on it are not recoverable: it requires an `Idempotency-Key` when the policy of your credential demands it.
post.summary: Open the picking list of a delivery note

get.description: Retrieve the picking list of a delivery note: its header — the note by its public id and its number, its fulfilment status with its label, the origin warehouse and the source sales order as opaque ids when it has them, how many lines it has and how many are still pending — and its lines. Each line carries its own public id, which is the one the marking operation takes, its position, the description and the article as they were WHEN THE LIST WAS OPENED, the quantity to pick, the quantity picked so far and the moment it was marked. A line that has never been marked carries NO picked quantity, which is not the same as a quantity of zero: zero is somebody recording that the goods were not there. The operator who marked it is not published. The header says whether the list is STALE: stale means the delivery note was edited after the list was opened, so the snapshot no longer describes the lines of the note — while it is stale both the marking and the step to prepared are rejected, and the way out is to open the list again. A note that never entered fulfilment has no list and answers as not found, and a note of another company answers exactly like one that does not exist.
get.summary: Retrieve the picking list of a delivery note

parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

post.description: Post a goods receipt: this is the call in which the goods actually come in. It takes no body. It consumes received quantity on the lines of the purchase order, triggers the stock entry in the warehouse and, in the same operation, leaves the order in the status derived from what has arrived — partially received while something is still pending, received when nothing is. A receipt that is already posted returns 422 with the code that names it, and a cancelled one cannot be posted. Irreversible: no published operation takes the entry back, because cancelling the receipt is a new movement and not an undo. It requires an `Idempotency-Key` when the policy of your credential demands it, and repeating it with the same key returns the result of the first call without consuming the quantity twice.

post.description: Compute what would be lost if the commercial combinations of a product were replaced by the proposed ones, and mint the `impact_token` that confirms THAT exact change. It is a READ and persists nothing — asking twice over the same catalog returns the same token — but it requires `products:write`, because the only thing its answer does is authorise a destructive write. Send `configurations` as the COMPLETE list of combinations that would remain ACTIVE (an empty list means "retire the allow-list", which returns the product to the cartesian cross), plus `variant_ids`/`presentation_ids` enumerating what SURVIVES on each axis — omitting a key means "that axis is untouched", which is not the same as an empty list. The answer says whether the change needs confirmation at all (`requires_confirmation`), which crosses stop being sellable, and which negotiated prices would be retired and from which price lists. The token is a fingerprint of the current catalog AND of the set of prices at stake, not a credential: if either changes before you confirm, the confirmation is rejected and you ask for a fresh preview. Send it back as `impact_token` when emptying `configurations` on `PATCH /v1/companies/{company}/products/{product}`, or when deleting the variant or presentation whose removal would leave the product with no declared combination.

422.description: Validation failed, or the invoice cannot undergo the requested state transition (e.g. marking an already-paid invoice as paid, or editing an issued invoice — use a corrective instead). The `error.param` field identifies which input is invalid, if any. Issuing or annulling an invoice can also be rejected with `verifactu_not_eligible`: either a field of the invoice does not fit its billing record, or — only when the company has VeriFactu enabled in NO VERI*FACTU mode — it has no usable signing certificate (`error.subcode: signing_certificate_unavailable`; `error.param` is `certificate`, `representation` or `system_certificate`, depending on what is missing); in both cases the invoice stays exactly as it was.

post.description: Preview, with NO effect, a bulk import of managed accounts and own tax IDs from a file: upload the same `multipart/form-data` body you would apply (`accounts_file`, optional `customers_file` and `options`) and receive every row with its `status`, its column `errors`, its `plan` and its monthly and prorated amounts, the totals by status and the `cost` by mode (`managed_account`, `own_nif` and `total`). Nothing is written, no account is provisioned and nothing is charged: it is a query sent by POST because it uploads files, so it needs no `Idempotency-Key`. To price the rows it only QUERIES Stripe (the end of the billing period and, for every confirmed plan change, the prorated amount of that change), so it has its own per-route rate limit. Each row declares its `mode`: `managed_account` provisions a SEPARATE account for a client, identified by your `external_ref`, with its `plan` (`emprendedor`, `empresario` or `integral`) and the `access_level` your account keeps on it (`operate` by default); `own_nif` registers the tax ID as an additional tax ID of YOUR account, with the plan of your account. Row statuses: `VALID` and `WARNING` rows would be applied, `ALREADY_EXISTS` rows would be reconciled (a new import of the same file never duplicates nor charges twice), `BLOCKED` rows break a business rule (reason in `code`: plan not self-serve, trial, managed account limit, billing not current, no payment method, tax ID held by another account, additional tax IDs not in your plan or at their limit, `external_ref` in the other environment or no longer managed) and `ERROR` rows are wrong (column `errors`). The environment is the one of the key: with a `fact_test_` key the `managed_account` rows would create TEST accounts, with no charge and no voucher, and the `own_nif` rows are `ERROR` `live_credential_required`. `own_nif` rows also require `companies:write` on the key (`ERROR` `insufficient_scope` otherwise) and a key that reaches the titular company of your account, which pays them (`BLOCKED` `forbidden_action` otherwise). The prorated total announced here is what applying the same files charges: new accounts and tax IDs, and the confirmed plan upgrades of existing accounts (`options.confirm_plan_changes`), priced with the same preview as a single plan change (a downgrade takes effect at the end of the period and adds 0 now). Limits: 5 MB per file, 100 rows in `accounts_file` and 1,000 in `customers_file`. Requires the privileged `accounts:write` scope, which `*` does not cover. Returns 403 `privileged_scope_required` without the account provider privilege granted by Factuarea or when the person who issued the key is no longer an owner or admin of your account, 413 `import_file_too_large` for a file over 5 MB (`error.param` names the file), 422 `import_row_limit_exceeded` for too many rows, 422 `import_file_invalid` for an unreadable file or a missing column, and 422 on an unknown option.

get.description: Preview, with no effect, changing the plan of a managed account your account pays to the `plan` in the query (`emprendedor`, `empresario` or `integral`): `effective` is `immediate` for an upgrade (charged at once, `prorated_amount_cents`) and `period_end` for a downgrade, which stays pending until `effective_at`; `next_invoice_amount_cents` is the monthly fee of the requested plan on the next periodic invoice. `renews_at` is the end of the current billing period (also for an upgrade) and, for a downgrade, `deactivates` lists the active additional tax IDs (`id`, `name`, `tax_id`) that the change would deactivate. Amounts are integer cents, taxable base without VAT. A managed account that is not charged to your account (a test one, or one blocked by its payer) has no real charge: both amounts are 0 and the change is immediate. Returns 422 `managed_account_plan_not_self_serve` for `enterprise`. Unlike retrieving the managed account, it requires your `access_level` on it to be `operate`: with `view` or `none` it returns 403 `forbidden_action` (raise the level first). The account axis admits only a managed account provisioned by the credential account, with the management in force and in the same environment as the key; your own account, a foreign or non-existent one, one of the other environment and one whose management ended all return the same 404 `account_not_found`. A managed account whose holder took over the payment also returns 404 `account_not_found`. Requires the privileged `accounts:read` scope, which `*` does not cover (403 `privileged_scope_required` otherwise).

get.description: Preview, with no effect, provisioning a NEW managed account of the `plan` in the query (`emprendedor`, `empresario` or `integral`) for the account of the credential: what would be charged to your account today (`amount_cents`, `tax_amount_cents` and `total_cents`, with `tax_rate`; when something is charged but the payment gateway returns no VAT rate, `tax_rate`, `tax_amount_cents` and `total_cents` are `null` and the base is never published as the total), the date of the next invoice and the joint monthly fee that follows (`recurring_*`). Amounts are integer cents. Nothing is written, nothing is charged and no account is created, so it needs no `Idempotency-Key`; it is a read-only counterpart of the provisioning operation and applies its same business rules. With a test key (`fact_test_`) every amount is 0. When the charge is real and your account has no payment method, `requires_payment_method` is `true` and the amounts are 0. Returns 400 `parameter_unknown` for a query parameter other than `plan`, 403 `forbidden_action` when the person who issued the key cannot administer your account, 403 `privileged_scope_required` without the account provider privilege granted by Factuarea, 403 `insufficient_scope` without `accounts:read`, 422 on a missing or unknown `plan`, 422 `managed_account_plan_not_self_serve` for `enterprise`, 422 `managed_account_provider_in_trial` while your account is in trial and 422 `managed_accounts_limit_reached` when your account already provisioned its maximum number of managed accounts, and 503 when the payment gateway cannot resolve the unit price (retry later). Requires the privileged `accounts:read` scope, which `*` does not cover.

post.description: Compute, without writing anything, what happens when a product is replaced by a new one with a different base unit, and mint the `impact_token` that confirms THAT exact change. The base unit of a product with history (stock, movements, presentations, supplier offers or variants with stock) cannot be edited in place: its `base_unit_change.mode` is `replacement` and the way to change it is to replace the product. It is a READ — asking twice over the same catalog returns the same token — but it requires `products:write`, because the only thing its answer does is authorise an irreversible write. Send `target_base_unit` (one of the nine measure units; a packaging unit such as `XPK` or `XBX` can only be a presentation), `equivalence` (how many units of the CURRENT base equal ONE unit of the NEW base, e.g. `0.001` when moving from kg to g because 1 g = 0.001 kg; required between a count unit and a measure unit, in either direction; calculated by itself inside the same measure family; there is none between two different measure families), an optional `base_price` to confirm, and `presentations` with a `keep` or `retire` decision per presentation of the old product (the ones you omit get the proposed decision). The answer lists every element of the plan in `items`, each with its `before`, its `after`, its `group` (`review`, `converted` or `carried`) and its `flags` (`precision_loss`, `no_equivalence`, `fraction`); `items[].ref` is the public id of the affected element, and `null` for the product itself and for price-list entries and pack components, which have no public id. `pending_documents` lists the unissued sales documents that will keep pointing at the old product, and `warehouse_stock` shows how the stock is split by warehouse when it moves to the new product (one stock-out and one stock-in per warehouse; the rounding remainder goes to the largest portion so the portions add up exactly). The preview is rejected with 422 `business_rule_violation` and subcode `base_unit_replacement_blocked_by_open_operations` or `base_unit_replacement_warehouse_balance_mismatch` when the replacement cannot proceed. The token is a fingerprint of the plan, not a credential: if the catalog, the price lists or the packs change before you confirm, the confirmation is rejected with 422 `base_unit_replacement_preview_stale` and you ask for a fresh preview. A product of another company returns 404 `product_not_found`.

parameters.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the values of secret fields (`password`, `secret`…) count as part of the body, so retrying with a corrected secret under the same key is a different request, never the replay of the earlier answer. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency). **Required on this operation**: repeating it delivers an effect that cannot be taken back (an email sent, a file generated, a third-party call, a charge), so a request without this header is rejected with `422 idempotency_key_required` before any business logic runs.

When the company has charges left out of invoicing in that quarter (from any of its connected Stripe accounts) and `include_non_invoiced_charges` is not `false` (default `true`), the ZIP also includes the CSV `cobros_sin_factura_Q{quarter}_{year}.csv` with the charges of the quarter and the refunds that happen in the quarter (date, type, description, origin, reason, reference, currency, amount, refunded amount and net amount; a refund of a charge from an earlier quarter is a negative line) and totals per currency; without such charges the file is not added. If the quarter has no invoices but has such charges, the ZIP contains only the CSV. Returns ZIP metadata (path, processed counts, errors).

413.description: The packaged download you asked for is too large to build, so nothing was generated and no file was left on the server. Two catalog codes carry this status, both with `error.type: invalid_request_error`: `export_document_cap_exceeded` (the request covers more documents than the cap for that artifact allows — narrow the date range or export in batches) and `export_byte_cap_exceeded` (the artifact would weigh more than the byte cap; `error.subcode` says whether it was rejected up front from the size estimate, `before_writing`, or aborted mid-packaging, `while_writing`, in which case the partial file was deleted and nothing is served). Retrying the same request unchanged returns the same error — ask for less, do not wait. A third, unrelated code shares this status on every write operation: `payload_too_large`, raised when the REQUEST body exceeds the 1 MB limit, which is about what you send and not about the size of what you asked to build.
