post.description:
Withdraw an issued invoice. The invoice moves to `annulled`, `voided_at` starts reporting when that happened and the status is terminal: voiding is **irreversible** and there is no way back to `sent` or `draft`.

**Void or correct?** Void when the whole document should never have existed and has not been paid — the invoice is withdrawn as a whole and no amending document is produced. Issue a corrective (`POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/corrective`) when the invoice was already paid, or when only part of it is wrong (amount, recipient, partial return): a `paid` invoice can never be voided, and voiding never fixes a figure.

What voiding does **not** do: the correlative number of the series is neither released nor reused (the series counter only moves forward), the original invoice is not deleted, and its VeriFactu *alta* record is not withdrawn. When the company is enrolled in VeriFactu, an AEAT cancellation (*anulación*) record is queued **asynchronously** with your `reason` as its `motivo` — a `200` means the invoice is annulled on our side, not that AEAT has already processed the cancellation. With VeriFactu inactive the annulment is purely internal.

Limits: only an invoice in `sent` or `overdue` can be voided. A `draft` is not voidable (delete it instead), and `paid`, `cancelled` and `annulled` return 422. An invoice that **is** a corrective can never be voided — to undo a wrong corrective, issue a new corrective of the original. Note the inverse is allowed: having correctives does not block voiding the original. Call `GET /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/can-annul` first if you need to check eligibility without attempting the change.

`reason` is optional here and a placeholder is persisted when you omit it. `POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/annul` is the very same operation with `reason` required — prefer it whenever the reason must be documented.

**Signing certificate (NO VERI*FACTU).** Only when the company has VeriFactu enabled in NO VERI*FACTU mode, the annulment billing record of this operation is signed with the company's electronic certificate (art. 6.c and 14 of Order HAC/1177/2024), and a certificate that is missing, expired, revoked, issued for another tax id or unreadable is rejected **before** the invoice is annulled: 422 `verifactu_not_eligible` with `error.subcode: signing_certificate_unavailable`; `error.param` says what is missing (`certificate`: the company certificate; `representation`: the representation that lets Factuarea sign on its behalf is not active; `system_certificate`: the Factuarea certificate is unavailable, nothing for you to fix). The invoice stays exactly as it was (issued and not annulled) and nothing is consumed: upload a valid certificate in Settings → Digital certificate (or register the representation in the third-party remission modes) and repeat the same call. Companies that have not enabled VeriFactu, and companies in VERI*FACTU mode (whose records are not signed), are never blocked by this rule.

OAuth2.description:
OAuth 2.1 authorization-code flow with PKCE (`code_challenge_method=S256`).
Discovery metadata (RFC 8414) is published at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`.

The access tokens of this flow authorize the Factuarea MCP server; the REST operations of this API accept only API keys (`fact_live_` / `fact_test_`), which is why no operation lists this scheme in `security`.

The scopes of this flow use the dotted vocabulary of the consent screen (`invoices.read`, `factuarea.full`): a request that names a fine-grained scope such as `invoices:read`, which is how API keys are scoped, is rejected with `invalid_scope`. The consent grants business data of one tax ID and never the administration of the account.

## API key rotation policy

API keys and OAuth client secrets are long-lived credentials and MUST be rotated periodically and immediately after any suspected leak.

- **Prefixes**: every key carries an unambiguous environment prefix — `fact_live_` (production) and `fact_test_` (sandbox). The prefix is the source of truth for the environment; never mix them across environments.
- **How to rotate**: rotate an API key from the Factuarea portal (or via the self-service `account:write` endpoints). Rotation issues a brand-new secret and returns it **once** — store it immediately, it is never shown again.
- **Grace window (dual-secret)**: after a rotation the previous secret keeps working for a **24-hour grace window**, so you can roll out the new secret with zero downtime. During that window both the new and the previous secret are accepted; once the window expires the previous secret is rejected and purged.
- **When to rotate**: on a regular schedule (e.g. every 90 days), whenever a teammate with access leaves, and **immediately** if a secret is ever exposed in logs, source control or a public client. Rotation leaves the previous secret valid for the 24-hour grace window, so to cut an exposed secret off at once, **revoke** the key instead (revocation is immediate) and issue a new one.
- **What a key reaches**: an API key belongs to one account and operates only on the companies (tax IDs) in its scope, fixed when the key is issued; `GET /v1/me` returns the account (`data.account.id`) and that scope (`data.scope[]`). The company each request acts on travels in the path, `/v1/companies/{company}/…`, and must be in the scope.
- Secrets MUST NEVER be embedded in browsers, mobile apps or any public client — keep them server-side only.

AbsenceBalance.description: An absence balance for the Control Horario (time tracking) module: the accrued, carried-over, consumed and available days of one employee for one absence type in a given year. Day amounts are decimal strings. `accrued_days`, `carried_over_days` and `consumed_days` are the exact ledger figures; `available_days` is the usable balance (accrued + non-expired carried-over − consumed) **rounded up to a whole day**, because absences are requested in whole working days. As a result `available_days` can exceed the exact arithmetic by up to one day — that fraction is granted by the company — so do not expect it to reconcile to the cent with the other three fields.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the balance, a UUID v7.

employee_id.description: UUID v7 of the employee the balance belongs to.

absence_type_id.description: UUID v7 of the absence type the balance tracks.

absence_policy_id.description: UUID v7 of the absence policy the balance accrues under.

year.description: Accrual year the balance belongs to (e.g. `2026`).

accrued_days.description: Days accrued so far this year, as an exact decimal string.

carried_over_days.description: Days carried over from the previous year (capped by the policy), as an exact decimal string.

carryover_expires_on.description: Date on which the carried-over days expire (`YYYY-MM-DD`), or `null` when they do not expire or there is no carryover.

consumed_days.description: Days already consumed against this balance, as an exact decimal string.

available_days.description: Usable balance (accrued + non-expired carried-over − consumed), rounded up to a whole day. Always an integer value, serialised as a decimal string.

measurement_unit.description: Unit in which the balance is measured: `days` or `hours`.

updated_at.description: Last-update timestamp (ISO 8601).

carryover.description: How much unused balance carries over at year-end under this policy.

max_days.description: Maximum days that carry over when `type` is `capped`; `null` otherwise.

AcceptNifTransferV1Request.description: Body of the tax ID transfer acceptance. It carries the plaintext `secret` exactly as the issuance response returned it, and nothing else. There is NO `company_id` here and it is not an omission: the tax ID is named by the TRANSFER, not by whoever presents it, so accepting one would allow aiming a transfer at a tax ID it does not cover — the request rejects it explicitly instead of ignoring it in silence. The secret travels from the body to the command and dies there: it is never logged, never recorded in any audit metadata, and never returned in the response, not even in the one that spends it.

secret.description: Plaintext secret of the tax ID transfer, exactly as its issuance response returned it.

AcceptPurchaseReorderSuggestionRequest.description: Turn a reorder suggestion into purchase orders. `items[]` holds between 1 and 100 articles you accept to reorder; each entry names the article (`product_id`, plus `product_variant_id` when a specific variant is reordered), the `quantity` IN THE PURCHASE UNIT of the offer it is bought under, and optionally the `offer_id` of that offer — omitting it takes the preferred active offer of the article. The result is one purchase order in DRAFT per supplier, each with a line per accepted article, returned with its public id and its number, plus the articles left out with their reason. Read this before retrying: a suggestion is not a document and has no identity of its own, so accepting the same one twice creates a SECOND set of drafts instead of returning the first. Send an `Idempotency-Key` if you may retry — it is not mandatory here, but it is honoured when it travels. Articles, variants and offers of another company are rejected exactly like non-existent ones, and the orders always belong to the company of the path.

items.description: Articles you accept to reorder: between 1 and 100. Each entry names the article, the quantity in the PURCHASE unit of the offer it is bought under, and optionally that offer. The result is one purchase order in draft per SUPPLIER, so the number of orders created depends on how many suppliers the selection brings along.

product_id.description: Public ID of the article being reordered, of the company in the path. Required on every entry.

product_variant_id.description: Public ID of the variant, when a specific one is reordered.

offer_id.description: Public ID of the ACTIVE supplier offer the article is bought under. Omitting it takes the preferred active offer, which is the one the report suggests.

quantity.description: Quantity to order IN THE PURCHASE UNIT of that offer: greater than zero, at most four decimals, up to 9999999999.9999. The cost is not sent — it comes from the offer —, so the amount of the resulting line is checked against its own limit inside the order and an entry that overflows it is rejected.

AcceptPurchaseReorderSuggestionRequest.title: AcceptPurchaseReorderSuggestionRequest

Account.description: Snapshot of the company, plan, Developer API entitlement, personalization and metadata of the API key used to make the request. To introspect the calling credential and its scope of tax IDs, use `GET /v1/me` instead, which returns the `Me` resource.

object.description: Stripe-like discriminator. Always `account` for this resource.

tax_id.description: Spanish fiscal identifier (NIF, CIF, NIE). Structural format: NIF `^\d{8}[A-Z]$`, NIE `^[XYZ]\d{7}[A-Z]$`, CIF `^[A-Z]\d{7}[A-Z0-9]$`. AEAT control-digit (checksum) validation is enforced when the request opts in via the `Factuarea-Version` header on or after the activation version; without that opt-in the legacy permissive behaviour is preserved.

addon.description: Developer API entitlement derived from the company plan. The `addon` property name is retained for backwards compatibility.

active.description: true when the company plan includes Developer API access.

in_grace.description: Legacy compatibility field. The plan-based entitlement does not grant an add-on grace period.

expires_at.description: Legacy compatibility field. Always null for the canonical plan-based entitlement.

api_key.description: Metadata of the API key used to authenticate the request. The secret is never returned (it is only shown once at creation time).

name.description: Human-friendly label assigned at creation time.

prefix.description: First chars of the key (e.g. `fact_live_1N0Fnyhh`) — safe to log.

scopes.description: Authorized scopes. `*` means super scope (full access).

tier.description: Rate-limit tier (`free`, `starter`, `pro`, `scale`). Derived from the company plan (or preserved by historical grandfathering).

environment.description: Environment of the authenticated key: `live` (`fact_live_` prefix, real side effects) or `test` (`fact_test_` prefix, sandbox company, no real-world effects).

personalization.description: Account personalization: invoice-emission language and PDF template/accent color. Mutable via `PATCH /v1/companies/{company}/personalization`.

language.description: Invoice-emission language of the account. One of `es`, `en`, `ca`.

pdf_template.description: Slug of the invoice PDF template (closed `PdfTemplate` catalog).

accent_color.description: Accent color of the PDF in `#RRGGBB` hex, or null when not configured.

Account.title: Account

AccountBilling.description: Billing snapshot of the authenticated company: current plan (trial, grace period, pending change), additional NIF subscription in `gestoria_seats` (when the account has additional tax IDs) and payment method. A tax ID whose billing is paid by another account returns `managed: true` with plan `gestionada`, no additional NIF subscription and no payment method: what the payer pays is never shown to it.

object.description: Stripe-like discriminator. Always `account_billing` for this resource.

managed.description: true when the effective tax ID is paid by another account: it has no plan billing of its own, so `gestoria_seats` and `payment_method` are null.

plan.description: Current plan subscription of the account.

status.description: Subscription status (e.g. `active`, `trialing`, `blocked`).

billing_interval.description: Billing interval of the plan, or null when there is no paid subscription.

is_on_grace_period.description: true when the plan was cancelled but remains usable until `ends_at`.

current_period_end.description: End of the current billing period (ISO 8601), or null.

ends_at.description: Scheduled end of the subscription (ISO 8601) when cancelled, or null.

pending_change.description: Scheduled plan change taking effect at the end of the current period, or null.

gestoria_seats.description: Additional NIF subscription of the account (one seat per active additional tax ID; the field keeps its original public name `gestoria_seats` for compatibility), or null when the account has no additional tax IDs. Amounts are in euros as 2-decimal strings and are null when the recurring cost is not resolvable (enterprise outside Stripe, sandbox, no active plan) — never a misleading 0.

status.description: Status of the additional NIF subscription (`active`, `past_due`, …), or `none` when there is no subscription yet (e.g. trial: additional tax IDs are free).

quantity.description: Number of billed seats (one per active additional tax ID) in the additional NIF subscription.

active_companies.description: Number of ACTIVE additional tax IDs of the account.

unit_amount.description: Taxable base of one seat per billing cycle, in euros as a 2-decimal string.

tax_rate.description: Applied VAT rate (e.g. 21), or null when not resolved.

tax_amount.description: VAT amount of one seat, in euros as a 2-decimal string.

total_per_seat.description: Base + VAT of one seat, in euros as a 2-decimal string.

recurring_total.description: Projected recurring total (`total_per_seat` × `quantity`), in euros as a 2-decimal string. Null when VAT is not resolved.

billing_interval.description: The seat is always billed monthly, regardless of the plan interval.

next_invoice_at.description: Next invoice date of the additional NIF subscription (ISO 8601), or null.

ends_at.description: Scheduled end of the additional NIF subscription (ISO 8601) when cancelled at period end, or null.

payment_method.description: Default payment method on file, or null when none is configured.

last_four.description: Last four digits of the card.

AccountEventEnvelope.description: The signed body an account webhook endpoint receives on every delivery: the envelope of a company event plus `account`, `account_relationship` and `company_id`. The same event carries the same `id` in its company envelope and in this one, so a receiver can deduplicate. Requests are signed with the `Factuarea-Signature` header, as for company endpoints.

id.description: Identifier (UUID v7) of the event. It is also sent in the `Factuarea-Event-Id` header and is the `Idempotency-Key` of the delivery.

anyOf.description: A company event type of the public catalog, for the events of a tax ID forwarded to the account.

type.description: Type of the event: an account-level type of `AccountEventType`, or a company event type when the event is about a tax ID.

api_version.description: Payload version (`YYYY-MM-DD`) the `data` is shaped in.

created.description: When the event happened, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

livemode.description: `true` for an event of the live environment, `false` for the test environment.

test.description: `true` on a synthetic event sent by the test operation of the endpoint; it is not related to `livemode`.

correlation_id.description: Correlation identifier of the request or process that caused the event, or `null`.

account.description: The account the endpoint belongs to.

id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of your account.

account_relationship.description: Relationship of the event with your account: `own` (about your account or one of its tax IDs) or `managed` (about an account your account manages).

company_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the tax ID the event is about. Always present: `null` in the account-level events that are not about a tax ID.

data.description: The content of the event, in the version of `api_version`.

type.description: Type of the event, the same as the envelope `type`.

object.description: Snapshot of what the event is about. In an account-level event it is the member, owner, grant, relation, tax ID or import concerned, always with opaque identifiers (UUID v7) and never with internal ones; in a company event it is the same snapshot the company webhook carries.

AccountEventEnvelope.title: AccountEventEnvelope

AccountEventType.description: Type of an account-level event (the `account.*` catalog). Only account webhook endpoints can subscribe to them: they are not part of the company event catalog (`GET /v1/event-catalog`). Members: `account.member_added`, `account.member_removed`, `account.member_role_changed`, `account.owner_transferred` and `account.member_grant_changed`. Relations between accounts: `account.access_granted`, `account.access_revoked` and `account.access_level_changed`. Managed accounts: `account.managed_account_provisioned`, `account.managed_account_claimed` and `account.management_ended`. Tax IDs of the account: `account.nif_added`, `account.nif_transferred` and `account.nif_archived`. Bulk imports: `account.import_completed`.

external_advisor.description: Whether this is the invitation of the external advisor of the account (only created from the web app).

invited_by.description: The person who created the invitation. `null` when that person no longer belongs to the account.

name.description: Full name of the person.

AddPurchaseOrderLineRequest.description: Add ONE line to a purchase order that still accepts changes. The line is a COPY of the supplier offer as it stands when you add it: the supplier reference, the purchase unit, the factor that converts that unit to the base unit, the agreed cost, the minimum quantity and the lead time all come from the offer and are frozen on the line, so a later catalog change does not rewrite an order already placed and a later goods receipt converts with the agreed factor. Required: `product_id` and `quantity`. Optional: `product_variant_id`, `offer_id` (an ACTIVE offer; omitting it takes the preferred active offer of the product) and `warehouse_id` (an ACTIVE warehouse of your company; omitting it inherits the one on the order). `quantity` is in PURCHASE UNIT — the one the offer publishes, which need not be the base unit of the product — greater than zero, with at most four decimals and up to 9999999999.9999. What this body REJECTS naming the field instead of ignoring it: the unit cost (both spellings, `unit_cost` and `unit_price`) and the `tax_rate`, `retention_rate` and `surcharge_rate` percentages, which come from the chosen offer — to buy on other terms pick another offer, or send the lines with their amounts when you create the order, which is the only operation that accepts them; the `description`, which is composed from the product; the `received_quantity`, which is never writable on any route and moves on its own when a goods receipt is posted or cancelled; and the line `id`, which the order assigns and returns in the response. The line amount and the taxes derived from it have their own, narrower limit, checked against the agreed cost of the offer before the line is created. Every reference — product, variant, offer and warehouse — must belong to the company in the path: one from another company is rejected exactly like a non-existent one. An order that no longer accepts changes by its status rejects the creation of lines as a business-rule violation, not as a validation error.

id.description: Not accepted. The line is identified by the URL and its identity is assigned by the order.

product_id.description: Public ID of the product being ordered, of the company in the path. Required.

product_variant_id.description: Public ID of the variant, when the line orders a specific one.

offer_id.description: Public ID of the ACTIVE supplier offer the terms are copied from. Omitting it takes the preferred active offer of the product.

description.description: Not accepted: the description is composed from the product being ordered.

quantity.description: Ordered quantity in PURCHASE UNIT — the one the offer publishes, which need not be the base unit of the product. Required, greater than zero, at most four decimals, up to 9999999999.9999. Its equivalent in base units is derived with the conversion factor the order froze from the offer, which is not sent.

warehouse_id.description: Public ID of the ACTIVE warehouse of your company this line enters through. Omitting it inherits the warehouse of the order.

unit_cost.description: Not accepted: the unit cost is copied from the supplier offer. Pick another offer, or send the lines with their cost when you create the order.

unit_price.description: Not accepted: the unit cost is copied from the supplier offer. Pick another offer, or send the lines with their cost when you create the order.

tax_rate.description: Not accepted: the tax, withholding and surcharge percentages of the line are taken from the product and the supplier offer.

retention_rate.description: Not accepted: the tax, withholding and surcharge percentages of the line are taken from the product and the supplier offer.

surcharge_rate.description: Not accepted: the tax, withholding and surcharge percentages of the line are taken from the product and the supplier offer.

received_quantity.description: Not accepted on any route: the received quantity is DERIVED from posted goods receipts and moves on its own when one is posted or cancelled.

AddPurchaseOrderLineRequest.title: AddPurchaseOrderLineRequest

AddSalesOrderLineRequest.description: Add ONE line to a sales order that still accepts changes. The line is born with its ordered quantity; the served, invoiced and returned quantities are never sent here or by any other route — they move on their own when a delivery note, an invoice or a return consumes quantity from this line. The subject of the line is either a catalog product (`product_id`) or free text: with no `product_id`, `description` and `unit_price` become required, and with one, a price you send WINS over the catalog price while omitting it lets the catalog resolve it with the rate that applies to the buyer. `quantity` is required, greater than zero and with at most four decimals. `discount`, `vat_rate`, `retention_rate` and `surcharge_rate` are percentages between 0 and 100, and `vat_id`, `retention_id` and `surcharge_id` point at the tax catalog. `warehouse_id` is the warehouse this line ships from; omitting it inherits the one on the order. The field names are the SAME ones each element of `lines` uses when creating or updating an order, and the same ones the lines sub-resource returns: a line is written the same way by both routes. Beyond the ceiling of each field, the line amount and the taxes derived from it have their own, narrower limit: a combination of price, quantity and percentage whose result overflows it is rejected naming the amount that does not fit and its value, even when price and quantity are legitimate on their own. An order that no longer accepts changes rejects the creation of lines as a business-rule violation, not as a validation error.

product_id.description: Public ID of the catalog product of the line, of the same company as the order.

description.description: Concept of the line, up to 255 characters. Required when the line names no product.

additional_description.description: Extended detail of the line, up to 5000 characters.

quantity.description: ORDERED quantity: required, greater than zero and with at most four decimals. The served, invoiced and returned quantities are never sent.

unit_price.description: Unit price, with at most four decimals. Required when the line names no catalog product; with a product, the price you send wins over the catalog one, and omitting it lets the catalog resolve it with the rate that applies to the buyer.

discount.description: Discount percentage of the line, between 0 and 100.

vat_rate.description: VAT percentage of the line, between 0 and 100.

retention_rate.description: Withholding percentage of the line, between 0 and 100. The sign the tax catalog publishes is accepted and the magnitude is what gets stored.

surcharge_rate.description: Equivalence surcharge percentage of the line, between 0 and 100.

vat_id.description: Public ID of the VAT tax of the line, from the GLOBAL tax catalog (shared by every company).

retention_id.description: Public ID of the withholding tax of the line, from the GLOBAL tax catalog.

surcharge_id.description: Public ID of the equivalence surcharge of the line, from the GLOBAL tax catalog.

warehouse_id.description: Public ID of the ACTIVE warehouse of your company this line ships from. Omitting it inherits the warehouse of the order.

AddShipmentPackageRequest.description:
Adds one package to the shipment of a delivery note.

## A package with nothing filled in is a legitimate package

All six properties are optional and none of them is required: a warehouse
counts boxes before weighing and measuring them, and demanding a weight would
turn "there are three boxes" into a form that cannot be sent. Not weighed is
NOT weighing zero, and not measured is NOT measuring zero by zero by zero, so
there are no default values either: what you leave out stays empty.

## Weight and the three sides

`weight_kg` is in kilograms and `length_cm`, `width_cm` and `height_cm` are in
centimetres. The four of them accept at most eight whole digits and two
decimals, which is exactly what their storage holds. A value above that
ceiling, or one carrying a third decimal, is rejected as a validation error
naming the property at fault, and it is rejected BEFORE the shipment is
touched: the alternative is the write being refused further down and the
request answering with a server error that names nothing.

Send the four of them as numeric STRINGS, which is also how they are read
back. Two decimals do not survive a binary floating point number, and the
weight that was declared would stop being the weight somebody typed.

Zero is accepted and a negative value is not. A box that weighs nothing makes
no physical sense, but a zero typed by mistake is still what the user wrote,
and rejecting it honestly for being negative is more useful than rejecting it
for having to weigh something.

## The position is not sent

The position of the package inside the shipment is assigned as the next one of
the delivery note, so that two packages added at the same time from two places
cannot claim the same position. It is what a warehouse reads out loud ("box 2
 * of 3") and never an identifier.

## The two text properties

`reference` is the label the carrier prints for THIS package, up to 60
characters, and it is the same kind of value as the reference of the shipment
as a whole. `notes` is free internal text.

reference.description: Label the carrier prints for THIS package, up to 60 characters. It is the number on the sticker, not the reference of the whole shipment, which belongs to the shipment itself.

weight_kg.description: Weight of the package in kilograms, with at most two decimals and up to 99999999.99. The total weight of the shipment is the sum of its packages and is calculated for you: it is never sent.

length_cm.description: Length of the package in centimetres, with at most two decimals and up to 99999999.99.

width_cm.description: Width of the package in centimetres, with the same limits as the length.

height_cm.description: Height of the package in centimetres, with the same limits as the length.

notes.description: Free text about the package, for whoever handles it. It is not printed on the label and does not reach the carrier.

AddShipmentPackageRequest.title: AddShipmentPackageRequest

AddStockTransferLineRequest.description: Add ONE line to a stock transfer that is still a draft. Required: `product_id` and `quantity`, greater than zero, with at most four decimals and up to 9999999999.9999. Optional: `product_variant_id` when one specific variant travels, and `origin_location_id` / `destination_location_id`, the locations inside the origin and the destination warehouse of the transfer; each one is checked against your company by this body and against its own warehouse by the transfer, which is what has both warehouses in front of it. The RECEIVED quantity is rejected naming the field instead of being silently dropped: a line is born with zero received and only the reception moves that number. A transfer whose status no longer admits changes rejects the creation of lines as a business-rule violation, not as a validation error.

product_id.description: Public ID of the article that travels, of the company in the path.

product_variant_id.description: Public ID of the variant, when the line moves one specific variant of the article.

quantity.description: Quantity to dispatch: greater than zero, with at most four decimals and up to 9999999999.9999.

origin_location_id.description: Public ID of the location inside the ORIGIN warehouse the goods leave from. Optional; the transfer itself checks that it belongs to its origin warehouse.

destination_location_id.description: Public ID of the location inside the DESTINATION warehouse the goods are placed at, with the same criterion.

quantity_received.description: Never writable, here or on any other route: a line is born with zero received and only the reception moves that number, adding to what was received before. Sending it is rejected naming the field instead of being silently dropped.

name.description: Human-friendly label assigned at creation time.

prefix.description: First chars of the key (e.g. `fact_live_1N0Fnyhh`) — safe to log. Does NOT authenticate.

ApiRequestLog.description: A single request your integration made against this API. Read-only, scoped to your own company, and retained for 30 days before being purged. Request headers, bodies and query strings are never stored, so they are never returned.

request_id.description: Opaque identifier of the request (`req_` + ULID), the same value returned in the `X-Request-Id` response header of that call. It is the identity of this resource — quote it in support requests and use it in `GET /v1/companies/{company}/request-logs/{request_id}`. Deliberately NOT a UUID v7: request logs are ephemeral rows, not domain resources.

api_key_prefix.description: First 8 characters of the identifier of the API key that authenticated the request — enough to attribute the call to one of your keys without exposing the full identifier. `null` when the request was not authenticated. The plaintext secret is never involved.

path.description: Request path, without the query string (which is never stored).

status_code.description: HTTP status code of the response.

ip.description: Source IP address of the request.

user_agent.description: `User-Agent` header sent by the client, or `null` when absent.

error_type.description: Error family of the response envelope (e.g. `invalid_request_error`, `not_found_error`). `null` for 2xx and 3xx responses.

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code of the response envelope (e.g. `invalid_param_value`, `resource_not_found`). `null` for 2xx and 3xx responses.

factuarea_version.description: API version (date-based) the request was resolved under, as reported in the `Factuarea-Version` response header. `null` for requests logged before versions were sealed.

environment.description: Environment of the key that issued the request: `live` (`fact_live_`) or `test` (`fact_test_`). Test keys operate on the sandbox company, so their logs belong to a different tenant and a live key never sees them; the filter is what lets a test key inspect its own traffic.

company.description: The company (tax ID) the request acted on, or `null` when the request did not act on one (for example an account-level call) or the company no longer exists.

id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the company.

tax_id.description: Spanish fiscal identifier (NIF, CIF, NIE). Structural format: NIF `^\d{8}[A-Z]$`, NIE `^[XYZ]\d{7}[A-Z]$`, CIF `^[A-Z]\d{7}[A-Z0-9]$`. AEAT control-digit (checksum) validation is enforced when the request opts in via the `Factuarea-Version` header on or after the activation version; without that opt-in the legacy permissive behaviour is preserved.

axis.description: Axis the request was made on, derived from the path prefix: `company` for `/v1/companies/{company}/…` and `account` for `/v1/accounts/{account}/…`. `null` when the path belongs to neither.

AutomationActionInput.description: One action of an automation rule: what to run when an event matches the condition tree.

type.description: Kind of action to run. Must be one of the action types `GET /v1/companies/{company}/automations/catalog` reports as registered.

order.description: Position of the action within the sequence, starting at 0. Omit it (or send `null`) and the action takes position 0.

parameters.description: Parameters of the action, whose accepted keys depend on `type`. The schema of each action type is published by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/automations/catalog`.

AutomationActionInput.title: AutomationActionInput

AutomationCatalog.description: Everything you need to build a valid automation rule without guessing: the triggers your company can listen to, the operators and combinators its conditions accept, and the actions it can run with their parameter schemas. Deterministic: two consecutive calls with no configuration change return exactly the same body, so it is safe to cache and diff. It deliberately does NOT include the evaluable fields of every trigger (that would be hundreds of kilobytes) — ask `GET /v1/companies/{company}/automations/catalog/triggers/{trigger}/fields` for the one you picked.

triggers.description: Events your company can subscribe an automation to, already filtered by the modules your plan includes: a trigger governed by a module you have not contracted is not offered at all. Returned in catalogue order.

key.description: Name of the event, in `resource.action` form. This is the value you send as `trigger_type` when creating a rule.

label.description: Human-readable name of the trigger, already translated to the language negotiated for the request via `Accept-Language`.

category.description: Prefix of the event name (the part before the first dot). It is part of the name itself, so it is not translated — use it to group triggers in a picker.

module.description: Key of the module that governs the visibility of this trigger, or `null` when the trigger is transversal. Informational: a trigger you cannot use never reaches this list.

operators.description: The closed set of comparison operators a condition can use, with the field types each one applies to.

key.description: Raw value of the operator, as sent inside a condition tree.

label.description: Human-readable name of the operator, already translated.

applies_to.description: Field types this operator accepts. It is the same operator-by-type matrix the write validation applies, so an operator you pick from here for a matching field type will never be rejected with a 422.

value_shape.description: Shape the comparison value must have: `scalar` for a single value, `list` for a non-empty array of values (`in`, `not_in`), `none` for an operator that takes no value at all (`is_null`).

combinators.description: The closed set of logical combinators a condition tree can nest.

key.description: Raw value of the combinator, as sent inside a condition tree.

label.description: Human-readable name of the combinator, already translated.

actions.description: Actions an automation can run, derived from the adapters actually WIRED in this deployment — never from the declared type catalogue. A type without a registered adapter is not announced, because picking it would produce a rule whose step is skipped at run time.

key.description: Raw value of the action type, as sent in the `actions` of a rule.

label.description: Human-readable name of the action, already translated.

parameters.description: Parameter schema declared by the adapter, in the order it declared it. Serialised deterministically: the same configuration always yields the same array.

name.description: Key of the parameter inside the `parameters` object of the action.

required.description: Whether the action refuses to be created without this parameter.

allowed_values.description: Closed set of accepted values, or an empty array when the parameter is free-form.

label.description: Human-readable name of the parameter, already translated.

description.description: What the parameter is for, already translated.

supports_portfolio_scope.description: Whether this action can be used in a rule whose `scope` is `cartera`. Actions that notify you —or that touch no record at all— can; actions whose subject would be a record of another tax ID cannot, because a portfolio rule never operates on behalf of another tax ID. Creating a portfolio rule with an action marked `false` is rejected with `automation_portfolio_scope_forbids_action`.

module.description: Key of the module that governs this action, or `null` when the action is transversal. Informational: an action of a module you have not contracted never reaches this list.

AutomationDryRun.description: What an automation rule WOULD do against a sample event, without materialising a single effect: no e-mail is sent, no webhook delivery is created, no target entity is mutated, no run or step row is written, and neither the monthly budget nor the rate limit is consumed. That is why the operation only requires the read scope even though it is a POST.

automation_rule_id.description: UUID v7 of the automation rule that was tested.

trigger_type.description: Trigger declared by the rule, in `resource.action` form. It is the only event type the rule can be tested against.

matched.description: Whether the condition of the rule would be satisfied by the sample payload. When `false`, no step would fire.

condition_trace.description: One entry per LEAF node that was evaluated, in evaluation order — which is the order the condition was written in. An empty array with `matched: true` means the rule has no condition and always acts. Same shape the real execution path produces.

path.description: Path of the evaluated field inside the `data.object` of the sample event.

expected.description: Comparison value declared by the condition. Its shape follows the `value_shape` of the operator: a scalar, an array of scalars, or `null` for operators that take no value.

observed.description: Value actually found at `path` in the sample payload, or `null` when the field was absent.

condition_error.description: Why the condition could not be evaluated, in Spanish, or `null` when it evaluated fine. It travels in the DOCUMENT with a 200, not as an HTTP failure: seeing why a rule cannot be evaluated BEFORE activating it is exactly what the dry run is for. Not redundant with `matched`: a non-null error implies `matched: false`, but the common case is a condition that evaluates perfectly and simply is not satisfied.

steps.description: One entry per action, in the order they would run.

index.description: Position the step WOULD have in the real run — the one that results from ordering the actions by their `order`, not the position in the stored array. It matches the `step_index` you would later replay.

action_type.description: Raw value of the action type, exactly as stored in the definition. Returned verbatim and NOT as a closed enum: a type retired from the catalogue must still be countable in a dry run instead of breaking it.

executable.description: Whether the code path reached the edge of the effect without anything discarding it. It never promises the effect would SUCCEED. It is `false` in three cases: the condition of the rule is not satisfied, the action type has no registered adapter, or the adapter refused the action because of some state of the world.

resolved_parameters.description: Parameters that would be frozen into the step — those of the current rule definition. `{}` when the action takes none.

effects.description: Traces of the effects that would fire, in order. Same shape the real execution path records.

kind.description: Family of the effect (sending an e-mail, mutating a document, …).

target.description: What the effect would act on.

summary.description: What the adapter derived from the parameters — recipient, subject, document — which is where the detail of the effect is readable. `{}` when there is none.

simulated.description: Always `true` here: the trace comes from the simulator, never from a materialised effect.

reason.description: Why the step would NOT run, in Spanish, or `null` when it would. A guardrail that would also cut the real execution shows up here as a non-executable step instead of faking success.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the automation rule, a UUID v7 (e.g. `01931b3e-7c4a-7f2e-9a8b-3c5d6e7f8a9b`).

name.description: Name the account owner gave the automation.

description.description: Free-form description of what the automation is for, or `null`.

trigger_type.description: Event the automation listens to, in `resource.action` form (e.g. `invoice.paid`). It is one of the event types returned by `GET /v1/event-catalog`.

scope.description: Which tax IDs the automation watches: `empresa` (the default, and the scope of every rule created before portfolio automations existed) watches only the events of the company that owns it, while `cartera` is reserved for the titular company of an account with the gestoría module and watches the events of the other tax IDs the account operates (its own and those another account lets it operate), delivering the notices to the titular itself. It is fixed when the rule is created and cannot be changed afterwards, so a run stays attributable to the scope it executed under.

conditions.description: Condition tree of the current version that decides whether an incoming event triggers the actions. An empty object `{}` means the automation has no condition and always acts. Its shape is defined by the account owner (nested combinators over the fields of the trigger payload), so it is returned verbatim.

actions.description: Actions of the current version, in the order the account owner declared them. Each element carries its action type and its frozen parameters. An empty array means the version declares no action.

AutomationRun.description: One execution of an automation rule, with its steps. Delivered as the `data.object` of the `automation_run.*` webhook events, captured at emission time and frozen there: a run snapshotted while `running` keeps showing `running` even after it completes. It carries the frozen definition it executed (`rule_version` + `rule_snapshot`) and the frozen payload of the event that triggered it (`event_payload`), so an execution stays readable weeks later, when the rule has moved on to a newer version.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the run, a UUID v7 (e.g. `01931b3e-7c4a-7f2e-9a8b-3c5d6e7f8a9b`).

automation_rule_id.description: UUID v7 of the automation rule that produced this run.

rule_version.description: Version number of the rule definition this run executed. It can lag behind the rule’s `current_version`: editing a rule never rewrites past runs.

rule_snapshot.description: The rule definition of `rule_version`, frozen at execution time (its condition tree and its actions with their parameters). Returned verbatim, because its shape is defined by the account owner.

trigger_type.description: Event the rule listens to, in `resource.action` form. It is the trigger of the rule, not necessarily identical to `event_name` in future versions of the matcher.

subject_company.description: The tax ID this run acted upon, when it comes from a rule of scope `cartera`. It is `null` for runs of scope `empresa`, which act on the company that owns the rule and have no subject. `id` and `name` are themselves `null` when the company cannot be read at that moment: the block is still emitted, so a portfolio run stays distinguishable from a company-scoped one. When the tax ID is deleted, the run is kept but its link to the company is cleared, so `subject_company` becomes `null`, as in a run of scope `empresa`.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the tax ID, a UUID v7, or `null` when it can no longer be read.

name.description: Name of the tax ID, or `null` when it can no longer be read.

event_name.description: Public name of the event that triggered this run (e.g. `invoice.paid`), one of the types returned by `GET /v1/event-catalog`.

event_aggregate_id.description: UUID v7 of the resource the triggering event happened on (the invoice that was paid, the quote that was accepted, …).

event_occurred_on.description: When the triggering event happened (ISO 8601), or `null` when the emitter did not record it.

event_payload.description: The `data.object` of the triggering event, frozen at execution time. Its keys are those of the resource of `event_name`, so the shape varies with the trigger and it is returned verbatim.

correlation_id.description: Identifier shared by everything that descends from the same originating event, so a chain of automations can be followed end to end. `null` when the emitter did not propagate one.

chain_depth.description: How deep this run sits in a chain of automations triggering one another (`0` for a run triggered directly by a business event). The platform caps the depth to stop runaway chains: a run over the cap is blocked with reason `chain_depth_exceeded`.

status.description: State of the run: `pending` (queued), `running`, `completed`, `failed` (finished without producing its effect and not reprocessable), `dead_lettered` (parked awaiting a manual replay) or `blocked` (stopped by a guardrail such as the chain-depth cap, the rate limit or the monthly budget).

discard_reason.description: Classified reason why the run did not produce its effect, or `null` while it has not finished in the red. It is what tells apart a run stopped by a guardrail (`chain_depth_exceeded`, `rate_limit_exceeded`, `monthly_budget_exhausted`) from one that exhausted its attempts (`step_attempts_exhausted`) or timed out (`run_execution_timeout`) — a guardrail cut-off has no step carrying a reason, so this is the only place it shows. Returned VERBATIM as stored: the current engine writes values of a closed catalogue, but rows written before that catalogue existed still hold free-form text, so do not model this as a fixed enum.

discard_reason_label.description: Human-readable label of `discard_reason`, in Spanish. `null` when there is no reason, or when the stored value predates the closed catalogue and therefore cannot be interpreted — in that case `discard_reason` still carries the raw value. The label is always Spanish: it is part of the vocabulary of the automation engine and does not follow `Accept-Language`.

last_error.description: Technical message of the last failure, or `null`. Free-form text meant for debugging: the classified reason of the outcome is `discard_reason` (and the `discard_reason` of each step), an orthogonal axis.

started_at.description: When the run started (ISO 8601), or `null` while it is still queued.

finished_at.description: When the run reached its outcome (ISO 8601), or `null` while it has not finished.

created_at.description: When the run row was created (ISO 8601).

updated_at.description: When the run row was last modified (ISO 8601).

steps.description: Steps of the run, ALWAYS in execution order — the order is part of the contract, because `step_index` is the identity of a step. The `automation_run.step_dead_lettered` event publishes the index of the parked step as the extra key `data.step_index`: resolve it here, against the element whose `step_index` matches.

items.description: One step of a run: an action of the frozen rule definition together with its outcome. It is the same document that `GET /v1/companies/{company}/automations/runs/{run}/steps` returns as `AutomationStepRun`, inlined here so a run is readable in one call.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the step, a UUID v7.

step_index.description: Zero-based position of the step inside its run, unique within the run. It is the identity of the step: it is what `automation_run.step_dead_lettered` publishes as `data.step_index`, and what `POST /v1/companies/{company}/automations/runs/{run}/steps/{step_index}/replay` takes.

action_type.description: Type of action of the step, as frozen in the rule version snapshot.

status.description: State of the step: `pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `skipped`, `dead_lettered` (parked awaiting a manual replay) or `blocked` (stopped by a guardrail).

parameters.description: Parameters of the action, frozen from the rule version snapshot. `{}` when the action takes none.

result.description: Trace the action adapter returned. `{}` while the step has not finished, or when the adapter produced no trace.

discard_reason.description: Classified reason of the step outcome, or `null` when there is none. Returned VERBATIM as stored: the current engine writes values of a closed catalogue (`condition_not_matched`, `chain_depth_exceeded`, `step_attempts_exhausted`, …), but rows written before that catalogue existed still hold free-form text, so do not model this as a fixed enum. The catalogue value IS guaranteed on the `data.discard_reason` extra of `automation_run.step_dead_lettered`.

discard_reason_label.description: Human-readable label of `discard_reason`, in Spanish. `null` when there is no reason, or when the stored value predates the closed catalogue and therefore cannot be interpreted — in that case `discard_reason` still carries the raw value. The label is always Spanish: it is part of the vocabulary of the automation engine and does not follow `Accept-Language`.

replayable.description: Whether replaying this step can produce a different outcome. `true` only for reasons caused by an external state you can change (a disconnected channel, a client without an e-mail address, exhausted attempts): those park the step in `dead_lettered`, the only state that allows re-entry. `false` for reasons frozen into the rule snapshot (an unregistered action type, invalid parameters) and for guardrail cut-offs, where a replay would take exactly the same branch. Also `false` when the reason is unknown to the catalogue.

last_error.description: Technical message of the last failure of the step, or `null`. Orthogonal axis to `discard_reason`: this one is the raw message, that one is the classification.

next_retry_at.description: When the step is scheduled to be retried (ISO 8601), or `null` when no retry is pending.

claimed_at.description: When a worker claimed the step (ISO 8601), or `null` while unclaimed.

finished_at.description: When the step reached its outcome (ISO 8601), or `null` while it has not finished.

AutomationTriggerFields.description: The fields of ONE trigger that an automation condition can evaluate, with the operators each field accepts. Served per trigger, not inside the catalogue: with around a hundred visible triggers and dozens of properties each, a single document would be hundreds of kilobytes to end up using the fields of one.

trigger.description: Trigger these fields belong to, in `resource.action` form. It travels in the body as well as in the URL so a cached response stays interpretable on its own.

fields.description: Evaluable fields, in the order the payload contract declares them. This list is never empty: a trigger without a declared payload contract is rejected as such instead of degrading to an empty list.

path.description: Path of the field relative to the `data.object` of the event. This is the value you put in the `field` of a condition.

type_label.description: Human-readable name of the type, already translated.

operators.description: Operators this field accepts — the row of the operator-by-type matrix that the write validation applies. Pick from here and your condition will not be rejected with a 422.

AutomationUsage.description: Current active automation rules and automation runs consumed this period, with the limits of the plan. Activating a rule checks the active-rule cap; the execution budget is checked only when admitting a run. Read both counters to anticipate reaching either limit. The figure comes from the same counter the engine applies when admitting a run, so it advances by exactly N after N admitted runs and does NOT change when run history is purged.

consumed.description: Automation runs already consumed in the current period.

limit.description: Cap of the plan for the period, or `null` when there is no automatic ceiling. Enterprise capacity is agreed by contract. `null` is not an unknown value or zero: omit the progress bar.

reset_at.description: When the counter resets — the first instant of the next period (ISO 8601). Returned already resolved so no client has to derive it.

threshold_percent.description: Consumption percentage at which the platform starts warning the account owner. It travels so your own warning and ours cannot drift apart.

active_rules.description: Current active rules and the cap enforced when activating a rule. Draft, paused and deleted rules do not consume this cap.

count.description: Active, non-deleted rules belonging to this company.

limit.description: Active-rule cap of the plan. Zero permits no activations; null means no automatic ceiling. Enterprise capacity is agreed by contract.

BaseUnitChange.description: Whether the base unit of the product can be edited in place. `mode` is `direct` exactly when there are no blockers; with blockers it is `replacement` and the base unit is changed by replacing the product (`POST /v1/companies/{company}/products/{product}/base-unit-replacement`); an already replaced product is `unavailable` with no blockers. Attempting to edit `base_unit` with blockers is rejected with 422 `business_rule_violation`, subcode `product_base_unit_locked`, and the same `blockers` in `details`. Only calculated on single-product reads (show, create, update, replacement): list responses omit the key.

blockers.description: What fixes the base unit, in a stable order.

code.description: Closed catalog of blockers.

quantity.description: Decimal string without trailing zeros: the stock in `unit` for `stock`, a count of elements for the rest.

unit.description: UN/ECE code of the unit of `quantity`. Only informed for `stock`; `null` for the rest.

BaseUnitChange.title: BaseUnitChange

BaseUnitReplacementPreview.description: What replacing a product by another with a different base unit would do, with the `impact_token` that confirms THAT exact plan. Nothing is written. `impact_token` is a fingerprint of the plan, not a credential: it is rejected with 422 `base_unit_replacement_preview_stale` if the catalog, the price lists or the packs change before the replacement runs.

product_id.description: Id of the product that would be replaced.

equivalence.description: Units of the CURRENT base per ONE unit of the NEW base, decimal string with scale 6 (`"0.001000"` when moving from kg to g). `null` between measure families with no declared equivalence.

equivalence_calculated.description: True when the equivalence was derived from the units (same measure family) instead of sent.

price_confirmation_required.description: True when the conversion loses precision or there is no equivalence: the execution then needs `base_price` confirmed.

group.description: `review` needs the user to look at it before confirming, `converted` is converted automatically and `carried` moves to the new product unchanged.

ref.description: Public id (UUID v7) of the affected element. `null` for the product itself and for `price_list_item` and `pack_component`, which have no public id and are told apart by `kind` and `name`.

before.description: Relevant values as strings (`quantity`, `unit_code`, `price`, `conversion_factor`, …). `null` when the element did not exist before or is not transferred.

after.description: Relevant values as strings (`quantity`, `unit_code`, `price`, `conversion_factor`, …). `null` when the element did not exist before or is not transferred.

proposed_decision.description: Decision the planner proposes for a presentation.

pending_documents.description: Unissued sales documents that will keep pointing at the old product.

warehouse_stock.description: How the stock of the product is split by warehouse when it moves to the new product: one portion per warehouse (and per old variant), with one stock-out and one stock-in per warehouse. The remainder of the rounding goes to the largest portion so the portions add up exactly to the converted total. Empty when the product holds no stock.

ref.description: Public id (UUID v7) of the OLD variant this portion belongs to, or `null` for the stock of the product itself.

warehouse_id.description: Public id (UUID v7) of the warehouse where the stock of the new product enters, or `null` when the stock is not assigned to any warehouse.

warehouse_name.description: Name of that warehouse, ready to display.

allocated.description: True when the portion is assigned to a warehouse; false for unassigned stock.

before.description: Quantity in the old base unit.

after.description: Quantity in the new base unit.

flags.description: Warnings of the conversion of this portion (for example `rounded`).

impact_token.description: Send it back as `impact_token` to execute THIS plan.

BatchStockAvailabilityRequest.description: Ask for the availability of several articles in ONE call. `references` is required and holds between 1 and 100 entries; each one is the public ID of an article or its catalog code, up to 255 characters. The same reference may not be sent twice, not even written in a different case, because two rows for one article would be indistinguishable in the answer. The response carries ONE row per reference SENT and in the order you sent them, each echoing its `reference`: a reference that resolves to nothing is reported as not found INSIDE a 200 response instead of failing the whole batch, so one typo never costs you the other ninety-nine answers. It reads and changes nothing, so it consumes no idempotency key.

references.description: Articles asked about: between 1 and 100 entries, each the public ID of an article or its catalog code, up to 255 characters. The same reference may not be sent twice, not even in a different case. The answer carries one row per reference SENT, in the order you sent them, and a reference that resolves to nothing is reported as not found inside a successful response instead of failing the batch.

BulkCreatePurchaseOrdersRequest.description: Create purchase orders in bulk. `purchase_orders[]` holds up to 100 payloads, each with the same shape as the single-create body. That reference is unique per COMPANY, so two rows of the SAME batch that repeat it collide with each other too, and the second one is rejected rather than updating the order the first one created. failed.description: Number of rows that were invalid or could not be created. Equals `failures` length in create mode.

results.description: Per-row classification of validate-only mode (`dry_run=true`). Empty in create mode.

index.description: 0-based position of the row within the batch.

status.description: Row status: `valid` (would be created without error) or `invalid` (has blocking errors).

errors.description: Per-field blocking issues of the row. Empty when the row is valid.

warnings.description: Per-field non-blocking warnings of the row (e.g. recipient not found in the AEAT census). Empty when there are none.

failures.description: Rows that could not be created (create mode, `dry_run=false`). Each item carries the 0-based `index`, an `error_code`, a Spanish `error_message` and the per-field `errors[]`. Empty in validate-only mode.

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code from the v1 error catalog (stable across languages).

BulkPartialSuccessResult.description: Result of a bulk or import operation that reports per-resource status. `total` is how many rows/resources were processed (`successful + failed`), `successful` how many were applied (deleted, created or validated) and `failed` how many could not be processed. `failures[]` carries one item per failed row. Shape shared by every bulk endpoint of the public API (the bulk-delete endpoints emit it today). Anchored integrators before `2026-09-01` keep receiving the previous `{object, deleted, failed[{id, reason}]}` shape via `Factuarea-Version`.

total.description: Number of rows/resources processed (`successful + failed`).

successful.description: Number of rows/resources processed successfully (deleted, created or validated).

failed.description: Number of rows/resources that could not be processed. Equals `failures` length.

failures.description: One item per failed row/resource. Always a list (empty, never `null`, when there are no failures).

items.description: A failed row/resource. Identity is polymorphic: `id` for an existing resource (bulk-delete/bulk-send/bulk-pdf), or `index` for a new row without a resource yet (bulk-create with `dry_run`, import CSV). Exactly one of `id`/`index` is present.

id.description: UUID v7 of the existing resource that could not be processed. Present for bulk operations over existing resources (e.g. bulk-delete).

index.description: 0-based position of the row within the batch. Present for new rows without a resource yet (bulk-create with `dry_run`, import CSV).

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code from the v1 error catalog (stable across languages). For bulk-delete: `resource_not_found` or `resource_not_deletable`.

error_message.description: Human-readable reason for the failure, in Spanish (internal messages are not exposed).

errors.description: Per-field blocking issues (validate-only / bulk-create flows). Empty or absent for bulk-delete.

warnings.description: Per-field non-blocking warnings (validate-only / bulk-create flows). Empty or absent for bulk-delete.
