BulkResolveStorefrontAvailabilityRequest.description: Ask, for a whole cart and in ONE request, how many units of each line a shopper can still buy: the PHYSICAL quantity minus the quantity COMMITTED by live reservations, never the physical balance. `selections` is required, needs at least one entry and is capped at the declared ceiling of 50. Each entry takes the SAME selection shape as the price resolution — `product_id` required, plus the variant, the presentation, the configuration, the signature, `options` and `quantity` — so a storefront can send the same cart to both operations without rewriting it. And, written here rather than left to be discovered: the units are counted on the ARTICLE and its VARIANT, so the presentation, the configuration, the chosen options and the quantity are accepted to let the cart travel whole and do NOT change the answer. `quantity` is optional here, because what is published is what is available and not whether what you asked for fits. The answer carries one entry per index of the input, in the same order, and a line pointing at an article of another shop is reported as not found with its index while the rest answer normally. No cost, no supplier, no reorder point, no committed quantity, no physical balance and no per-warehouse breakdown ever travel in the answer.

selections.description: Selections whose availability is asked for: at least one and at most 50, the declared ceiling of the lane. The answer carries one entry per INDEX of this list and in the same order, so a line pointing at an article of another shop is reported as not found with its index while the rest answer normally.

product_id.description: Public id of the article asked about, of the shop that owns the key. Required in every entry, and together with the variant it is what DETERMINES the figure.

variant_id.description: Public id of the variant asked about. With it the figure is the one of that variant; without it, the one of the article as a whole.

presentation_id.description: Public id of the presentation chosen. It is accepted so the cart can travel whole and it does NOT change the figure: one stock is not split by how what is sold happens to be packed.

configuration_id.description: Public id of the configuration chosen. Accepted so the cart can travel whole, and it does not change the figure.

selection_signature.description: Fingerprint of the configuration chosen: 64 hexadecimal characters. Accepted so the cart can travel whole, and it does not change the figure.

options.description: Option values chosen, as a list of pairs of `group_id` and `value_id`. Accepted so the cart can travel whole, and they do not change the figure.

items.description: Each chosen option, with its group and its value

group_id.description: Public id of the option group the choice belongs to.

value_id.description: Public id of the value chosen inside that group.

quantity.description: Units asked for. OPTIONAL here, unlike in the price resolution, and it does not change the answer: what is published is what is AVAILABLE, not whether what you asked for fits.

BulkResolveStorefrontAvailabilityRequest.title: BulkResolveStorefrontAvailabilityRequest

BulkResolveStorefrontPricesRequest.description: Resolve the price of a WHOLE cart in one request, which is the operation to build a storefront on: resolving line by line would be one request per line from the browser of EVERY shopper, and the admission budget of the lane counts them all. `selections` is required, needs at least one entry and is capped at the declared ceiling of 50 — sending more is rejected and resolves nothing. Each entry has the same shape as the single resolution: `product_id` required, then `variant_id`, `presentation_id`, `configuration_id`, `selection_signature`, `options` as pairs of `group_id` and `value_id`, and `quantity`. The answer carries one entry PER INDEX of the input and in the same order, so an entry that cannot be resolved comes back with its index and its reason and does not invalidate the rest of the cart. As in the single resolution the price list is not chosen from the browser, the amounts are a preview the order resolves again, and nothing is stored.

selections.description: Selections whose price is asked for: at least one and at most 50, the declared ceiling of the lane. The answer carries one entry per INDEX of this list and in the same order, so a selection that cannot be resolved does not invalidate the rest of the cart.

product_id.description: Public id of the article priced, of the shop that owns the key. Required in every entry.

variant_id.description: Public id of the variant chosen, when the article has variants.

presentation_id.description: Public id of the presentation chosen. It changes the unit the price refers to.

configuration_id.description: Public id of the configuration chosen, when there is one.

selection_signature.description: Fingerprint of the configuration chosen: 64 hexadecimal characters.

options.description: Option values chosen for that entry, as a list of pairs of `group_id` and `value_id`: one value per group and at most 50.

items.description: Each chosen option, with its group and its value

group_id.description: Public id of the option group the choice belongs to.

value_id.description: Public id of the value chosen inside that group.

quantity.description: Units asked for in that entry: required, greater than zero, with at most four decimals and up to 9999999999.9999.

BulkResolveStorefrontPricesRequest.title: BulkResolveStorefrontPricesRequest

BulkSendDeliveryNotesV1Request.description: Email several delivery notes in one request (queued), up to 200 per batch. `ids` is an array of delivery-note UUIDs; the optional `to`/`cc` arrays and `subject`/`message`/`language` overrides apply to the whole batch (when `to` is omitted, each delivery note uses its client email).
BulkSendDeliveryNotesV1Request.title: BulkSendDeliveryNotesV1Request

BulkSendInvoicesV1Request.description: Email several invoices in one request (queued), up to 200 per batch. `ids` is an array of invoice UUIDs; the optional `to`/`cc` arrays and `subject`/`message`/`language` overrides apply to the whole batch (when `to` is omitted, each invoice uses its client email).
BulkSendInvoicesV1Request.title: BulkSendInvoicesV1Request

BulkSendProformasV1Request.description: Email several proformas in one request (queued), up to 200 per batch. `ids` is an array of proforma UUIDs; the optional `to`/`cc` arrays and `subject`/`message`/`language` overrides apply to the whole batch (when `to` is omitted, each proforma uses its client email).
BulkSendProformasV1Request.title: BulkSendProformasV1Request

BulkSendQuotesV1Request.description: Email several quotes in one request (queued), up to 200 per batch. `ids` is an array of quote UUIDs; the optional `to`/`cc` arrays and `subject`/`message`/`language` overrides apply to the whole batch (when `to` is omitted, each quote uses its client email).
BulkSendQuotesV1Request.title: BulkSendQuotesV1Request

BulkStatusDeliveryNotesV1Request.description: Transition several delivery notes to `new_status` (`delivered` or `cancelled`) in one request, up to 50 per batch. `ids` is an array of delivery-note UUIDs; every transition passes the document state guard, and notes that cannot transition are returned under `failures[]`.
BulkStatusDeliveryNotesV1Request.title: BulkStatusDeliveryNotesV1Request

BulkStatusGoodsReceiptsRequest.description: Move several goods receipts to the same target status in one request. `new_status` admits exactly `posted` and `cancelled`: `created` is the initial status and has no incoming transition. The batch is applied item by item and returns a partial result — a receipt that does not admit the requested transition is reported as a failed item with its reason while the rest are applied — and it is capped at 100 items per request.

ids.description: Public IDs (UUID v7) of the goods receipts to transition, between one and one hundred per request. An unknown ID — or one from another company — is reported as a failed item, never as a rejection of the whole batch.

new_status.description: Target status: `posted` (accounting for the goods, which consumes ordered quantity) or `cancelled` (undoing a receipt, which gives that quantity back). Both are irreversible. `created` is the status a receipt is born in and is never a target.

BulkStatusGoodsReceiptsRequest.title: BulkStatusGoodsReceiptsRequest

BulkStatusInvoicesV1Request.description: Transition several invoices to `new_status` (`issued` or `paid`) in one request, up to 50 per batch. `issued` issues each draft without sending any email; `sent` is still accepted as an alias of `issued` in every API version and never marks the invoice as delivered. `ids` is an array of invoice UUIDs; `payment_date` is required and cannot be in the future when `new_status` is `paid`. Every transition passes the document state guard, and invoices that cannot transition are returned under `failures[]`.

new_status.description: Target status: `issued` issues each draft (definitive number, VeriFactu record) without sending any email; `paid` records a payment for the outstanding amount of each issued invoice. `sent` is accepted as an alias of `issued` in every API version and never sets the delivery mark (`is_sent`).

BulkStatusInvoicesV1Request.title: BulkStatusInvoicesV1Request

BulkStatusProductsV1Request.description: Transition several products to `new_status` (`active` or `inactive`) in one request, up to 50 per batch. `ids` is an array of product UUIDs; the change is idempotent (a product already in the target status counts as successful). Products that do not exist are returned under `failures[]`.
BulkStatusProductsV1Request.title: BulkStatusProductsV1Request

BulkStatusProformasV1Request.description: Transition several proformas to `new_status` (`accepted` or `rejected`) in one request, up to 50 per batch. `ids` is an array of proforma UUIDs; every transition passes the document state guard, and proformas that cannot transition are returned under `failures[]`.
BulkStatusProformasV1Request.title: BulkStatusProformasV1Request

BulkStatusPurchaseInvoicesV1Request.description: Transition several expenses to `new_status` (`paid`) in one request, up to 50 per batch. `ids` is an array of expense UUIDs; `payment_date` is required and cannot be in the future. Every transition passes the document state guard, and expenses that cannot transition are returned under `failures[]`.
BulkStatusPurchaseInvoicesV1Request.title: BulkStatusPurchaseInvoicesV1Request

BulkStatusPurchaseOrdersRequest.description: Move several purchase orders to the same target status in one request, up to 100 per batch. `ids` is an array of purchase-order UUIDs and `new_status` admits exactly `sent`, `confirmed` and `cancelled`. Those three are the only targets: `draft` is the initial status and has no incoming transition; the three consumption values (`partially_received`, `received` and `billed`) are derived from posted goods receipts and from the supplier-invoice match, and are never requested; and CLOSING an order is not a status at all, it is a separate operation on a single order. Every transition passes the document state guard, and orders that cannot make it are returned under `failures[]` while the rest are applied.

ids.description: Public IDs of the purchase orders to transition: between 1 and 100. Unknown identifiers, identifiers of another company and orders that cannot make the transition are reported as failed, one by one.

new_status.description: Target status of the transition: `sent` (the supplier has the document), `confirmed` (the supplier accepted it) or `cancelled`. Those three are the only ones that can be requested. `draft` is the status an order is born in and has no incoming transition; `partially_received`, `received` and `billed` are DERIVED — the first two from posted goods receipts, the third from the supplier-invoice match — so they are never a target; and closing an order is not a status, it is a separate operation on a single order.

BulkStatusPurchaseOrdersRequest.title: BulkStatusPurchaseOrdersRequest

BulkStatusQuotesV1Request.description: Transition several quotes to `new_status` (`approved` or `rejected`) in one request, up to 50 per batch. `ids` is an array of quote UUIDs; every transition passes the document state guard, and quotes that cannot transition are returned under `failures[]`.
BulkStatusQuotesV1Request.title: BulkStatusQuotesV1Request

BulkStatusSalesOrdersRequest.description: Transition several sales orders to `new_status` (`confirmed`, `cancelled` or `closed`) in one request, up to 100 per batch. `ids` is an array of sales-order UUIDs. Only those three are valid targets: the four consumption states (`partially_served`, `served`, `partially_invoiced`, `invoiced`) are derived from delivery notes and invoices against the order lines and are never requested, and `draft` is never a target because confirming stamps a series number. Every transition passes the document state guard, and orders that cannot transition are returned under `failures[]`. Confirming consumes one series number per confirmed order.

ids.description: Public IDs of the sales orders to transition: between 1 and 100. Unknown identifiers, identifiers of another company and orders that cannot make the transition are reported as failed, one by one.

new_status.description: Target status of the transition: `confirmed`, `cancelled` or `closed`. Those three are the only ones that can be requested — the four consumption states are derived from delivery notes and invoices, and `draft` is never a target.

BulkStatusSalesOrdersRequest.title: BulkStatusSalesOrdersRequest

BulkUpdateProductStockRequest.description: Update the stock of up to 500 products in a single operation. `updates[]` holds the entries, each with `product_id`, `stock` (numeric string), an optional `operation` (`set`, `add` or `subtract`) and an optional `variant_id` that targets the own balance of a variant of that product. A product or variant that is unknown (or does not belong to the product) is skipped. `items` is accepted as an alias of `updates`.

updates.description: Up to 500 entries `{product_id, stock, operation?, variant_id?, warehouse_id?}`. `variant_id` targets the own balance of a variant of that product; entries whose product, variant or warehouse is unknown are skipped silently.

product_id.description: UUID v7 of the product. A product that does not exist or does not belong to your company is skipped, without revealing whether it exists.

warehouse_id.description: Optional UUID of the warehouse each adjustment is booked to. When omitted, it is resolved from the product default and then from the company default warehouse.

BulkUpdateProductStockRequest.title: BulkUpdateProductStockRequest

assignee_id.description: `id` of the new assignee, a member of the company; `null` removes the assignee.

BusinessContact.description: A canonical business contact with cumulative customer, supplier and fiscal lead roles, or no assigned role. The fiscal lead role requires the same fiscal identity as other contacts; pre-fiscal opportunities belong to the separately planned CRM.

id.description: Public UUID v7. Internal numeric keys are never exposed.

coordinates.description: Geographic coordinates. Each axis is nullable independently; the object is null only when neither axis is recorded.

financial_summary.description: Directional sales and purchases totals for this contact, as 2-decimal strings. Amounts use the currency declared in each direction.

latest_activity.description: Most recent sales or purchases movement, or `null` when the contact has no financial activity.

BusinessContact.title: BusinessContact

BusinessContactActivity.description: An item in the canonical contact timeline. It combines sales, purchases and relationship changes in reverse chronological order.

amount.description: Amount of the movement in EUR as a 2-decimal string, or `null` when the activity carries no amount.

metadata.description: Sanitized event metadata. Internal numeric identifiers are removed.

BusinessContactActivity.title: BusinessContactActivity

BusinessContactImport.description: Tracking of a contact import. `outcomes` lists at most 500 rows (`outcomes_truncated`); `skip_reasons` counts the skipped rows by reason.

outcome_kind.description: `nothing_changed` means the import finished without creating or updating anything; do not present it as a success.

severity.description: Only present on warnings; errors omit it.

received_value.description: Received cell value, truncated to 120 characters.

errors.description: Errors and warnings of the row.

BusinessContactImport.title: BusinessContactImport

reason.description: Why the row is skipped, failed or leaves the contact unchanged; null when the row is applied.

result.description: Present for confirmed execution rows; omitted from planned preview rows.

merge_candidate.description: Rows matching an existing contact under the `merge` strategy: nothing is applied and they are flagged for manual review (`reason=merge_review_required`).

skip.description: Rows that change nothing: identical to the existing contact (`no_changes`) or targeting an archived contact (`update_not_allowed`).

import_uuid.description: Persisted import reference for synchronous and queued execution; null for dry-run.

outcome_kind.description: Business reading of a finished execution, same as the tracking resource; null for preview, dry-run and queued imports. `nothing_changed` means nothing was created or updated; do not present it as a success.

status.description: Persisted execution status; null for preview and dry-run. Synchronous responses can be failed with unprocessed rows after a concurrent closure.

BusinessContactStats.description: Aggregated counters for canonical identities and their cumulative customer, supplier and fiscal lead roles. A contact with multiple roles is counted once in `total` and in each applicable role counter.
BusinessContactStats.title: BusinessContactStats

CalculateTaxRequest.description: Calculate a tax on a base amount. Body: `base` (number) and `taxes_id`, the public identifier (UUID v7) of the tax, never the tax ID of a company. Returns `base`, `tax_rate`, `tax_amount`, `total_amount` and `tax`.

taxes_id.description: Identifier (UUID v7) of the tax to apply, from the Factuarea catalog plus your company's own taxes. A well-formed but non-existent value returns 404 `tax_not_found`.

CalculateTaxRequest.title: CalculateTaxRequest

CalculateTotalsRequest.description: Calculate the totals of a set of lines. Body: `lines[]`, each with `quantity`, `unit_price` and the optional `discount`, `vat_rate`, `retention_rate` and `surcharge_rate`. Returns the subtotal, VAT, surcharge, withholding and total. `price` is accepted as a legacy alias of `unit_price`.
CalculateTotalsRequest.title: CalculateTotalsRequest

CanAnnulInvoice.description: Result of the pre-cancellation validator of an invoice: whether it can be cancelled, the blocking reasons (when it cannot), whether the cancellation will create an additional VeriFactu record and whether its live payments are the only obstacle (`requires_collection_reversal`). `can_annul` is the verdict of `POST .../annul` WITHOUT `revert_collections`.

can_annul.description: Whether the invoice can be annulled in its current status.

reasons.description: Blocking reasons when `can_annul` is `false`. Empty `[]` when the invoice can be cancelled.
example: La factura está en estado Borrador y no puede ser anulada
examples: La factura está en estado Borrador y no puede ser anulada

will_create_verifactu.description: Indicates whether the cancellation will generate a cancellation record in VeriFactu.

info.description: Additional informational messages about the cancellation (non-blocking warnings). Empty `[]` when there are none.
example: La factura no tiene registro VeriFactu de alta. Se anulará sin registro VeriFactu.
examples: La factura no tiene registro VeriFactu de alta. Se anulará sin registro VeriFactu.

requires_collection_reversal.description: `true` when the live payments of the invoice are the ONLY obstacle to annulling it: `POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/annul` with `revert_collections: true` would succeed. `can_annul` stays `false` in that case, because it is the verdict without `revert_collections`. `false` when there are no live payments or when something else also blocks the annulment.

active_collections_amount.description: Amount, in euros, of the live payments of the invoice — what `revert_collections` would revert. `0` when there are none.

CanAnnulInvoice.title: CanAnnulInvoice

CancelFaceSubmissionV1Request.description: Cancel a FACe submission. `reason` is required: it travels to the FACe web service alongside the cancellation request (code 4200).
CancelFaceSubmissionV1Request.title: CancelFaceSubmissionV1Request

CancelTransportDocumentRequest.description: Cancel an issued transport document. Required: `reason` (3-500 characters).
CancelTransportDocumentRequest.title: CancelTransportDocumentRequest

Carrier.description: A carrier: the company that physically moves the goods of a delivery note. It is a MASTER record and not a document — no number, no series and no lifecycle beyond being active or withdrawn. It is what turns the free-text transport company that used to be typed on every delivery note into a referenced entity, and what makes the tracking URL of a shipment DERIVABLE instead of stored.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the carrier, a UUID v7. Every reference to it travels the same way: no internal numeric key is ever published.

name.description: Name of the carrier, ready to display.

code.description: Code of the carrier: the INTEGRATION key, unique per company. It is the value `POST /carriers/find-by-code` resolves, so a system that already knows its own carrier by code does not have to store our identifier. It is normalised to upper case on write, and withdrawing a carrier does NOT release its code.

tracking_kind.description: How the tracking of this carrier is resolved: `url_template` (we build the tracking URL out of `tracking_url_template` and the tracking number of the shipment), `manual` (the number is recorded but there is no address to send the customer to) and `store_provided` (the online store supplies the link). Only `url_template` carries a template, which is why the template key is optional.

tracking_url_template.description: Template the tracking URL is built from, with the `{tracking_number}` placeholder where the number goes. This key is ABSENT — not `null` — when the carrier has none, which is the case of every `manual` and `store_provided` carrier by definition. The tracking URL is composed on EVERY read and never stored: changing this template changes the published URL of every shipment of this carrier without rewriting a single row.

contact.description: Contact details of the carrier. The whole OBJECT is ABSENT — not `null` — when none of its three fields is recorded, because the object is the unit: with three flat fields, "no contact" would be three loose nulls. When it does travel, its three keys always travel, `null` on the ones that are not recorded. It is NOT a reference to a business contact: a business contact is a billable entity with a life of its own, and publishing it as a reference would force you to create one just to register a carrier.

name.description: Name of the person or desk to talk to at the carrier, or `null`.

email.description: Contact email address of the carrier, or `null`.

phone.description: Contact phone number of the carrier, or `null`.

is_active.description: Whether the carrier is in operation. A withdrawn carrier keeps serving the shipments that already point at it —that is why `POST /carriers/find-by-code` resolves it too— but assigning it to a shipment is rejected as a business rule violation.

Carrier.title: Carrier

CatalogConfigurationImpact.description: What a proposed restriction of a product configurable catalog would invalidate, plus the token that confirms THAT exact change. `impact_token` is not a credential: it carries no secret and does not expire in time, it is the proof of "you were shown the impact over THIS catalog". On confirmation the backend recomputes the fingerprint with the product freshly loaded under lock; if the catalog or the set of prices to retire changed meanwhile, the fingerprints differ and the confirmation is refused asking for a new preview.

currently_legacy.description: True when the product declares no active combination and any cross of active variants and presentations is still sellable.

requires_confirmation.description: False when the change widens or does not touch what is sellable, and can be applied with no token.

impact_token.description: Fingerprint to send back as `impact_token` when applying the change. Null when `requires_confirmation` is false.

CatalogConfigurationImpact.title: CatalogConfigurationImpact

CensusVerification.description: Result of verifying the account's persisted company name + tax ID pair against the AEAT census (VNifV2). Use it to anticipate VeriFactu 4104 rejections before invoicing. Fail-open: returns `unavailable` when AEAT cannot be reached.

object.description: Stripe-like discriminator. Always `census_verification` for this resource.

status.description: Census result. `identified`: name + tax ID match an active taxpayer. `not_identified`: the pair is not in the census. `not_identified_similar`: a similar individual exists (natural persons only). `identified_inactive` / `identified_revoked`: the taxpayer is deregistered or revoked. `unavailable`: AEAT could not answer (timeout, fault, no platform certificate) — verification is informational and never blocks.

verified_name.description: The company name that was checked against the census (the persisted account name). `null` when the account has never been verified.

checked_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last verification. `null` when never verified.

CensusVerification.title: CensusVerification

ChainValidation.description: Result of recomputing and verifying the VeriFactu hash chain (`huella`) of your company without mutating data. Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/chain/validate`.

is_valid.description: Indicates whether the hash chain is intact.

first_invalid_record_id.description: UUID v7 of the first invalid record, or `null` if the chain is intact.

ChainValidation.title: ChainValidation

role.description: New account role: `admin` or `member`. Required when `external_advisor` is not sent.

external_advisor.description: Mark or unmark the member as the external advisor of the account (only a `member`, one per account). Required when `role` is not sent.

ChangeManagedAccountAccessLevelV1Request.description: Change the access level your account keeps on the managed account of the path: `level` is `none`, `view` or `operate`. After the holder claims the account it can only be lowered.

level.description: New access level of your account: `none`, `view` (read-only) or `operate`.

ChangeManagedAccountAccessLevelV1Request.title: ChangeManagedAccountAccessLevelV1Request

ChangeManagedAccountPlanV1Request.description: Change the plan of the managed account of the path, which your account pays: `plan` is `emprendedor`, `empresario` or `integral` (`enterprise` is only assigned by Factuarea by contract). An upgrade is charged at once; a downgrade takes effect at the end of the period.
ChangeManagedAccountPlanV1Request.title: ChangeManagedAccountPlanV1Request

ChargeRule.description: A charge treatment rule of a connected Stripe account. Rules are evaluated in `position` order and the first one that matches decides whether the charge is invoiced or left out. The public `id` is the rule UUID v7.

id.description: UUID v7 of the rule. Public identity (KEY `id`).

position.description: Evaluation order within the account, starting at 1. Change it with `PUT /v1/companies/{company}/connected-accounts/{account}/charge-rules/order`.

condition.description: Condition a charge must meet for the rule to apply.

type.description: Kind of condition: the charge metadata `key` equals `value`, the charge description contains `value`, or the charge comes from the payment link `value`.

key.description: Metadata key. Only used (and required) with `metadata_equals`; `null` otherwise.

value.description: Value to compare against.

outcome.description: `invoice` issues the invoice (optionally with `concept` and `vat_rate`); `do_not_invoice` leaves the charge out and records it with `non_invoice_reason`.

non_invoice_reason.description: Reason recorded for charges left out. Only with `do_not_invoice`; `null` with `invoice`.

concept.description: Concept of the invoice line. Only with `invoice`; `null` otherwise.

vat_rate.description: VAT rate in percent applied to the line. Only with `invoice`; `null` otherwise.

updated_at.description: When the rule was last updated (ISO 8601).

ChargeRule.title: ChargeRule

commercial_name.description: Optional trade name (DBA), distinct from the legal name.

tax_id.description: Spanish fiscal identifier (NIF, CIF, NIE). Structural format: NIF `^\d{8}[A-Z]$`, NIE `^[XYZ]\d{7}[A-Z]$`, CIF `^[A-Z]\d{7}[A-Z0-9]$`. AEAT control-digit (checksum) validation is enforced when the request opts in via the `Factuarea-Version` header on or after the activation version; without that opt-in the legacy permissive behaviour is preserved.

billing_emails.description: Additional emails for invoice delivery (administration, accounting). Maximum 5.

coordinates.description: Geographic coordinates of the client. `null` when not recorded.

default_discount.description: Default discount applied to the client (percentage).

default_vat_rate.description: Default VAT rate applied to the client (percentage).

is_surcharge_subject.description: Whether the equivalence surcharge (*recargo de equivalencia*, the Spanish special VAT regime for retailers) applies to the client.

bank_accounts.description: Bank accounts associated with the client. Empty `[]` when there are none.

preferred_operation_regime.description: Preferred operation regime of the client for VAT / VeriFactu purposes.

accumulate_347.description: Whether this client accumulates towards the annual Modelo 347 report (operations with third parties above the legal threshold).

dir3_accounting_office.description: DIR3 code of the public-administration accounting office (Oficina Contable). FACe/Facturae directory code, not a foreign key. `null` for non-AAPP clients.

dir3_managing_body.description: DIR3 code of the public-administration managing body (Órgano Gestor). FACe/Facturae directory code, not a foreign key. `null` for non-AAPP clients.

dir3_processing_unit.description: DIR3 code of the public-administration processing unit (Unidad Tramitadora). FACe/Facturae directory code, not a foreign key. `null` for non-AAPP clients.

external_id.description: External integration key (ERP/CRM/e-commerce) mapping this client to a record in a third-party system. Free-format, unique per company, distinct from the fiscal `tax_id`.

default_price_list_id.description: UUID v7 of the default price list assigned to the client.

default_price_list_name.description: Snapshot of the assigned default price-list name.

employee_id.description: Employee ID (UUID v7) clocking in or out.

source.description: Origin of the clock entry: `web` or `mobile`.

occurred_at.description: Clock entry timestamp in ISO 8601 (defaults to the server instant).

year.description: Year of the period to close (YYYY).

month.description: Month of the period to close (1-12).

Company.description: A company (tax ID) of your account, registered and operated through the `/v1/accounts/{account}/companies` endpoints. `readiness` (whether it can issue right now, with the same contract as `GET /v1/accounts/{account}/companies/{company}/issuing-readiness`) is present only when the list is requested with `include=readiness`; otherwise the key is absent.

id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the tax ID.

name.description: Commercial name of the tax ID.

business_name.description: Legal/registered business name (razón social), or `null` if not set.

tax_id.description: Spanish fiscal identifier (NIF/CIF/NIE). Unique within your account.

status.description: Status of the tax ID in the account: `active` (operational), `inactive` (deactivated, data preserved, can be reactivated) or `archived` (no longer accepts operations).

status_since.description: When the tax ID entered its current `inactive` or `archived` status (ISO 8601). `null` for an `active` tax ID and for one whose change predates the lifecycle events: the date is never invented.

address.description: Street address of the fiscal domicile, or `null`.

city.description: City of the fiscal domicile, or `null`.

postal_code.description: Postal code of the fiscal domicile, or `null`.

province.description: Province of the fiscal domicile, or `null`.

country_aeat_zone.description: AEAT territorial zone of the company (`peninsula`, `canarias`, `ceuta`, `melilla`), or `null`.

country.description: Country of the fiscal domicile as recorded in the company profile (free text, up to 100 characters), or `null` when it was not set.

logo_url.description: Absolute URL of the company logo, or `null` if not set.

paid_until.description: Paid coverage of this company as an additional tax ID of the account (ISO 8601): reactivating it before this date is free. `null` when it was never charged or the coverage expired.

suspension_reason.description: Why the system suspended this `inactive` tax ID, or `null` when it is not suspended by the system (active, archived, or deactivated by the account itself). `payer_blocked`: the account paying for this managed account has its billing blocked; it resumes when the payer settles. `management_ended`: the management of this managed account ended before anyone took over the payment; it resumes when the holder of the account takes over the payment.

created_at.description: When the tax ID was registered in the account (ISO 8601).

updated_at.description: When the tax ID was last updated (ISO 8601), or `null`.

Company.title: Company

CompanyCertificate.description: Metadata of an FNMT (PKCS#12) certificate used to sign VeriFactu transmissions. The certificate password and binary are never exposed — only X.509 metadata.

id.description: UUID v7 of the certificate.

subject_nif.description: Tax ID (NIF) of the X.509 certificate holder.

subject_kind.description: Type of holder (individual / legal entity / representative).

is_active.description: Whether this is the active certificate used to sign transmissions.

revoked_at.description: Revocation date, or `null` if not revoked.

CompanyCertificate.title: CompanyCertificate

CompanyCreationStatus.description: Provisioning lifecycle status of a tax ID (company) of the account. Poll it after registering the tax ID to know when it becomes operational.

id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the tax ID.

payment_setup_url.description: URL to set up the payment method of the account titular; when it is saved the person returns to the Companies page of the app (`/companies`). Only present while `awaiting_payment` and for a production credential that reaches the titular company; `null` otherwise.

failed_reason.description: Human-readable reason the provisioning failed. Only present when `provisioning_status` is `failed`; `null` otherwise.

started_at.description: When provisioning started (ISO 8601), or `null` if not started yet.

completed_at.description: When provisioning completed (ISO 8601), or `null` if not completed yet.

CompanyCreationStatus.title: CompanyCreationStatus

CompanyList.description: Cursor-paginated list of the tax IDs of your account (`{ data, has_more, next_cursor }`).

data.description: Page of tax IDs.

has_more.description: `true` when more companies exist beyond this page.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or `null` when `has_more` is `false`.

CompanyList.title: CompanyList

CompanyRepresentation.description: The representation with which your company authorizes Factuarea to remit its VeriFactu records to AEAT on its behalf: social collaboration (annex I of the Resolution of 18-12-2024) or a power of attorney registered with AEAT. There is at most ONE active representation per company; a revoked one is kept in the history and never reactivated. The custodied document is never returned.

id.description: UUID v7 of the representation.

kind.description: `social_collaboration_annex_i`: the signed annex I (social collaboration). `aeat_power_of_attorney`: a power of attorney registered with AEAT.

signer_name.description: Name of the person who signed the authorization.

granted_on.description: Date on which the authorization was granted.

has_document.description: Whether the signed document (annex I or power-of-attorney proof) is custodied. The document itself never leaves the system.

power_of_attorney_reference.description: Reference of the power of attorney in the AEAT register, or `null`.

valid_until.description: Last day of validity (YYYY-MM-DD, Europe/Madrid), or `null` when the representation does not expire.

is_expired.description: `true` once the last day of validity has passed. An expired representation does NOT enable third-party remission any more, so register a new one before it expires (you are warned 30 and 7 days ahead and when it expires).

is_active.description: `true` while the representation has not been revoked, that is, it is the CURRENT one — even when it has expired. It only enables third-party remission when `is_active` is `true` AND `is_expired` is `false`.

revoked_at.description: Instant of the revocation, or `null` while it is active.

revocation_reason.description: Reason recorded on revocation, or `null` while it is active.

ConfirmStorefrontCheckoutRequest.description: Confirm, right after the shopper comes back from the gateway, that the payment session was really paid — and get the state of the order and its invoice. `session_id` is REQUIRED: it is the identifier the gateway itself puts in the return address, it starts with `cs_` and is at most 255 characters long. Nothing else travels in the body: neither the amount, nor the currency, nor the account, because what is being confirmed is read from the gateway and never taken from the browser. A session that cannot be verified, or one that belongs to a DIFFERENT order, changes nothing and answers with the current state of the order rather than with an error, so probing identifiers tells the caller nothing. The `Idempotency-Key` HEADER IS REQUIRED here, because a confirmation issues the invoice of the order — a fiscal document with a sequential number that can only be undone with a corrective one: the same key with the same body replays the SAME answer and leaves ONE single invoice. Confirming an order that is already paid is not an error either: it answers what it already knows.

session_id.description: Identifier of the payment session the gateway returns in the address the shopper comes back to. REQUIRED, starts with `cs_` and is at most 255 characters long. It is checked against the order being confirmed: a session of ANOTHER order changes nothing and the answer publishes the current state of this one, so it never confirms that some other session exists or was paid.

ConnectStoreV1Request.description:
Public REST API v1 — POST /v1/companies/{company}/stores.

Connect an e-commerce store to your company. Required: `integration_id` (the
provider connection that backs the store), `provider`, `external_store_id`
(the identifier the provider gives to the shop) and `name`. The eight
settings are optional and each one falls back to its declared default, so a
store connected without any of them is created with automatic invoicing OFF
and in the `test` environment. `simplified_threshold` is expressed in EUROS
and capped at the legal maximum for a simplified invoice. `series_id` is a
series of type invoice; omit it to follow the default series of your company,
which is never frozen into the store. A company may connect several stores of
the same provider, but not the same remote shop twice.

integration_id.description: Identifier (UUID v7) of the provider connection that backs the store.

provider.description: E-commerce provider of the store: `woocommerce`, `shopify` or `prestashop`.

external_store_id.description: Identifier the provider gives to the shop; unique per provider within your company.

name.description: Display name of the store, editable at any time.

series_id.description: Series (UUID v7, type invoice) the store numbers into; omit to follow the default series of your company.

simplified_threshold.description: Order total, in euros, up to which the store issues a simplified invoice. Maximum 3000.00.

require_tax_id.description: Whether the buyer tax ID is required for the order to be invoiced.

prices_include_tax.description: Whether the prices of the store already include taxes.

autoinvoicing_enabled.description: Whether paid orders are invoiced automatically. Off unless you turn it on.

autosend_enabled.description: Whether the invoice is emailed to the buyer automatically. Off unless you turn it on.

remote_base_url.description: Base address of the remote shop, checked against the outbound policy of your company.

environment.description: Environment the store reports as: `live` invoices for real, `test` discards with a typed reason.

authorize_remote_host.description: Authorize the host of `remote_base_url` as an outbound destination in the same call.

ConnectStoreV1Request.title: ConnectStoreV1Request

ConvertProformaRequest.title: ConvertProformaRequest

ConvertProformaToSalesOrderV1Request.description: Convert a proforma into a sales order. The body publishes ONE optional property, `target_series_id`: the public identifier of a live SALES-ORDER series of your company, which the order will be numbered with when it is confirmed; omitting it leaves the confirmation to resolve the default series of that type. There is NO partial selection of lines, and that is not an omission: the pending-per-line quantities belong to the sales order — which is what delivery notes and invoices consume from — and a proforma has no pending quantities of its own, so the conversion always carries the whole document across. The operation needs TWO scopes: write on sales orders (`sales_orders:write`), which is what the route enforces, and read on proformas (`proformas:read`), which the operation enforces on top of it. It consumes its origin: the proforma is left as converted and no published operation returns it to its previous state. Creating an order consumes monthly plan quota, and an exhausted monthly allowance answers payment required. The response is the created SALES ORDER, not the proforma.

target_series_id.description: Public ID of the SALES-ORDER series the created order will be numbered with when it is confirmed: live and of the same company. Omitting it leaves the confirmation to resolve the default series of that type. It is the ONLY property of this body: the conversion carries the whole proforma across and admits no partial selection of lines, because the pending-per-line quantities belong to the sales order and not to the document it came from.

ConvertSalesOrderToDeliveryNoteRequest.description: Serve a sales order with a delivery note, in full or in part. The line selection travels as a MAP of line identifier to quantity, for example `{"lines": {"0199aa00-0000-7000-8000-000000000001": "4.0000"}}`. The key of each entry is the PUBLIC IDENTIFIER of the order line — the same `id` the lines sub-resource returns — never its position in the list and never an internal identifier; it is a map and not a list of objects so that two entries for the same line are impossible by construction. `lines` is OPTIONAL: omitting it, or sending it empty, serves EVERYTHING the order has pending delivery. An order with nothing pending is rejected as a business-rule violation and creates no delivery note. `target_series_id` is optional and drives the numbering of the delivery note created: it must be a live DELIVERY-NOTE series of the same company, and omitting it numbers with the default delivery-note series. `warehouse_id` is optional and is the warehouse the goods of this delivery note leave from: active and of the same company, and omitting it inherits the one on the order. Each quantity is a positive number with at most four decimals; zero and negative are rejected, because serving zero is not serving. The delivery note INHERITS the price, the discount and the taxes of the order line, which is why this body does not declare them and they cannot be changed while serving: changing them means editing the order line, before serving it. What this body does not decide is checked afterwards against the order and rejected as a business-rule violation before any delivery note is created and before any series number is consumed: that the line belongs to THIS order, that the order may be served, and that the quantity does not exceed what is pending delivery on that line. An order accepts SEVERAL delivery notes over its life and its status is derived from the resulting quantities. The operation is irreversible.

lines.description: Selection of what to serve, as a MAP of line identifier to quantity (`{"<line id>": "4.0000"}`). Each key is the PUBLIC identifier of the order line — the same `id` the lines sub-resource returns — never its position in the list. Each quantity is positive, with at most four decimals, and may not exceed what is pending delivery on that line. OPTIONAL: omitting it, or sending it empty, serves EVERYTHING the order has pending delivery.

additionalProperties.description: Quantity to deliver for that line: positive, at most four decimals, and never above what is still pending delivery on it.

target_series_id.description: Public ID of the DELIVERY-NOTE series the created delivery note is numbered with: live and of the same company. Omitting it numbers with the default delivery-note series.

warehouse_id.description: Public ID of the ACTIVE warehouse of your company the goods of this delivery note leave from. Omitting it inherits the warehouse of the order.

ConvertSalesOrderToDeliveryNoteRequest.title: ConvertSalesOrderToDeliveryNoteRequest

ConvertSalesOrderToInvoiceRequest.description: Invoice a sales order, in full or in part. The line selection travels as a MAP of line identifier to quantity, for example `{"lines": {"0199aa00-0000-7000-8000-000000000001": "3.0000"}}`. The key of each entry is the PUBLIC IDENTIFIER of the order line — the same `id` the lines sub-resource returns — never its position in the list and never an internal identifier; it is a map and not a list of objects so that two entries for the same line are impossible by construction. `lines` is OPTIONAL: omitting it, or sending it empty, invoices EVERYTHING the order has pending invoicing, which is what has already been served and not yet invoiced, because an order is served before it is invoiced. An order with nothing pending invoicing is rejected as a business-rule violation and creates no invoice. `target_series_id` is optional and drives the numbering of the invoice created: it must be a live INVOICE series of the same company, and omitting it numbers with the default invoice series. `mode` is optional and says how far the invoice goes: `draft` (the default) leaves it as a draft; `issue` issues it on creation (sequential number, VeriFactu registration and stock output, never sends it); `issue_and_send` issues it and queues the delivery email, to `send_to` or, without it, to the customer email. Issuing additionally requires the `invoices:write` scope and sending the `invoices:send` scope, and both are irreversible. Each quantity is a positive number with at most four decimals; zero and negative are rejected, because invoicing zero is not invoicing. What this body does not decide is checked afterwards against the order and rejected as a business-rule violation before any invoice is created and before any series number is consumed: that the line belongs to THIS order, that the order may be invoiced, that the quantity does not exceed what is pending invoicing on that line, and that the buyer carries a tax ID when the amount requires one. An order accepts SEVERAL invoices over its life and its status is derived from the resulting quantities. The operation is irreversible.

lines.description: Selection of what to invoice, as a MAP of line identifier to quantity (`{"<line id>": "3.0000"}`). Each key is the PUBLIC identifier of the order line — the same `id` the lines sub-resource returns — never its position in the list. Each quantity is positive, with at most four decimals, and may not exceed what is pending invoicing on that line. OPTIONAL: omitting it, or sending it empty, invoices EVERYTHING the order has pending invoicing, which is what has been served and not yet invoiced.

additionalProperties.description: Quantity to invoice for that line: positive, at most four decimals, and never above what is still pending invoicing on it.

target_series_id.description: Public ID of the INVOICE series the created invoice is numbered with: live and of the same company. Omitting it numbers with the default invoice series.

mode.description: How far the created invoice goes: `draft` (the default) leaves it as a draft; `issue` issues it on creation (sequential number, VeriFactu registration and stock output) without sending it; `issue_and_send` issues it and queues the delivery email. Issuing requires the `invoices:write` scope and sending, additionally, `invoices:send`. Issuing and sending are irreversible.

send_to.description: Recipient of the delivery email with `issue_and_send`: a valid email address. Omitting it sends to the customer email of the order. Ignored with `draft` and `issue`.

ConvertSalesOrderToInvoiceRequest.title: ConvertSalesOrderToInvoiceRequest

CreateCarrierRequest.description:
Create a carrier in the company master data.

`name`, `code` and `tracking_kind` are required. The code is the integration
key of the carrier: up to 40 characters of letters, digits, hyphens and
underscores, held trimmed and upper-cased, and unique within the company, so
`seur`, `SEUR` and ` SEUR ` all name the same carrier. Reusing the code of
another carrier of the same company is rejected as a business rule violation
pointing at `code`, never as a creation conflict; two different companies may
each hold the same code without interfering, because the scope of uniqueness
is the company and never the installation.

`tracking_kind` states where the tracking link of a shipment comes from and
takes one of three values. With `url_template` the tracking address is built
on every read from `tracking_url_template` plus the tracking number of the
delivery note, so the template is REQUIRED for that kind; with `manual` the
recipient types the number on the carrier website, and with `store_provided`
the online store hands the link over. For those two the template is optional.

A template has to carry the `{tracking_number}` placeholder, since a template
without it is a fixed address that would lead to the same page for every
shipment while reading as the tracking of that one. Its scheme has to be
`http` or `https`, and any other scheme, executable ones included, is
rejected: that check is what makes sure no executable address ever reaches a
browser. The template is a link for the browser and is never resolved or
visited by the server, so it needs no outbound allowance of any kind.

`contact` is optional and travels as one block, with `name`, `email` and
`phone`, the very keys the carrier is published with. It holds the people you
call when a shipment goes missing and it is master data of the carrier, not a
reference to a commercial contact: no contact has to exist beforehand in order
to create a carrier.

Optional text is either sent with a value or left out. An empty string is
rejected instead of being read as `no value`, so that what you send and what
you read back always agree.

The body takes neither the company, which comes from the path, nor the
identifier of the carrier, which the operation assigns, nor the active flag: a
carrier is born active and withdrawing it is a partial update. Internal notes
are not part of the published carrier and are not accepted here either.

name.description: Human-readable name of the carrier, up to 120 characters

code.description: Short code that identifies the carrier within your company: up to 40 characters of letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, stored trimmed and upper-cased. It is the key an integration names the carrier by, and it stays taken even after the carrier is withdrawn, so a withdrawn carrier and a live one never share it.

tracking_kind.description: Where the tracking link of a shipment comes from: `url_template` (you publish an address with a placeholder and each shipment fills it in with its own tracking number), `manual` (there is a tracking number but no address to build a link with, so no link is published) or `store_provided` (the link travels from the shop the order came from). It is a closed set and the value is taken literally: a different casing or a surrounding space is rejected rather than corrected, so the same kind is never stored two ways.

tracking_url_template.description: Address the tracking link is built from, REQUIRED when the tracking kind is `url_template` and optional otherwise. It must carry the `{tracking_number}` placeholder exactly once — without it every shipment would link to the same page and none would be tracked — and its scheme must be `http` or `https`: anything else is rejected, including schemes that would run code in the browser of whoever clicks the link. Example: `https://tracking.example.com/parcel/{tracking_number}`.

contact.description: Operational contact of the carrier — who to call about a shipment — published back under the same keys it is sent with. It travels as ONE block: sending it replaces the three fields at once, so a field you leave out inside the block ends up empty rather than keeping its previous value.

name.description: Person to call about a shipment

email.description: Email address of the person to call about a shipment.

The new company joins your account and is adopted into the scope of the calling key, so you can operate on it right away. A tax ID already registered in another account is rejected: the account that holds it has to hand it over to yours with a tax ID transfer instead.

name.description: Trade name of the company registered under this tax ID (1-255 characters).

CreateCorrectiveInvoiceRequest.description: Generate a corrective (rectificativa) invoice for a previously issued invoice. `correction_reason` (required) maps to a VeriFactu R-code; `correction_type` is `full` or `partial`; the optional `correction_nature` is `I` (by differences: void the whole invoice with `full` and no `lines`, or correct amounts with `partial` and the adjustment `lines`) or `S` (substitution: `full` with the final `lines`, no negative quantity) — omitted, `full` with `lines` is `S` and the rest `I`; `unit_price` is never negative (a negative `quantity` subtracts); the optional `correction_code` (`R1`..`R5`) forces the explicit R-code and is validated against the AEAT legal matrix for the original invoice type. Optional `justification`, `notes`, and `lines[]` (none to void the whole invoice; required for a partial correction and for a substitution). Each line may also declare the fiscal nature of the line it corrects — `unit`, `regime_key`, `exemption_reason` and `exemption_reason_text` — with the same rules as `POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices`: a key you OMIT inherits the value of the original line at the same index, a key you SEND (even `null`) replaces it, and `null` means explicitly none.

correction_nature.description: Nature of the correction (art. 15.5 Royal Decree 1619/2012; VeriFactu `TipoRectificativa`). Optional: OMIT it and `full` with `lines` is a substitution (`S`), while `full` without `lines` and `partial` are by differences (`I`). `I`, by differences: the corrective carries the amount of the rectification, whatever its sign — void the whole invoice with `correction_type: full` and no `lines`, or correct some amounts with `partial` and the adjustment `lines` (`full` with `lines` and an explicit `I` is rejected). `S`, substitution: `correction_type: full` with the FINAL `lines` of the correct invoice (no negative quantity); registered with `ImporteRectificacion` (base and tax of the original). An incoherent combination is rejected with 422 before anything is created.

line_type.description: Kind of line: `NORMAL` (default) for an ordinary line, or `SUPLIDO` for a DISBURSEMENT — an amount paid in the name and on behalf of the client (an official fee, duty or registry charge) re-invoiced at cost, which stays out of the taxable base (art. 78.Tres.3 LIVA) and is aggregated into `total_disbursements`. A `SUPLIDO` line must carry no VAT, withholding, surcharge, discount or product, and requires `source_invoice_reference`. Only meaningful when `lines[]` is sent (a partial correction or a substitution); a value outside the catalog is rejected with 422.

unit.description: Unit of measure printed next to the quantity on the corrected line (`hours`, `kg`, `units`, …), up to 20 characters. Presentation only. OMIT it and the line inherits the unit of the original line at the same index; SEND it (even `null`) and it replaces it, `null` meaning no unit.

regime_key.description: VeriFactu special-regime key of the corrected line (the closed AEAT catalog, e.g. `01` general regime, `14` or `15` for operations whose VAT accrues later than the issue date). OMIT it and the line inherits the key of the original line at the same index; SEND it (even `null`) and it replaces it, `null` meaning no special regime.

exemption_reason.description: Cause of VAT exemption of the corrected line (the closed catalog of `POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices`). OMIT it and the line inherits the exemption of the original line at the same index; SEND it and it replaces it; send `null` for explicitly none — for example, `exemption_reason: null` turns an exempt original line into a taxed one.

exemption_reason_text.description: Free-text wording of the exemption provision of the corrected line (up to 255 characters), printed under the line description (art. 6.1.j of Royal Decree 1619/2012). OMIT it and the line inherits the text of the original line at the same index; SEND it (even `null`) and it replaces it, `null` meaning no text.

vehicle_plate.description: Licence plate of the vehicle used for the delivery (up to 20 characters).

unit_price.description: Unit price. Send a JSON number or a decimal string with up to 4 decimals (`"0.0125"`, `"100.0000"`): the string is the exact form the response returns, so a line read from the API can be sent back unchanged. Derived amounts are computed from it and keep 2 decimals.

tax_rate.description: VAT rate of the line (0–100). Optional: when you omit it (or send `null`) the line takes, in this order, the tax it references or the tax assigned to its product, and otherwise the DEFAULT TAX of your company for this kind of document (tax settings), inherited as a whole: its rate, its indirect-tax regime (IVA, IGIC or IPSI) and its AEAT qualification; an exempt or not-subject default also declares its cause (`exemption_reason`) on the line unless the line sends its own. The line ends up exactly as if you had chosen that tax. If none of them exists the request is rejected with 422 `missing_required_param`, with `error.param` = `lines.N.tax_rate` and `error.line_index` = N (the zero-based index of the line): the API never guesses a rate. A `0` you send is honoured as a real 0 % rate, never confused with «not stated».

contract_hours.description: Weekly contracted hours (greater than 0 and up to 168).

ccaa.description: Spanish autonomous community or city (ISO 3166-2:ES) used to localise public holidays.

CreateInvoiceRequest.description: Create an invoice. Required: `series_id`, `issued_on`, `due_on`, `lines[]` (at least one) and `client_id` — except on a simplified invoice (`type: F2`), where the client is optional. A terminal can issue an already-paid simplified invoice in ONE idempotent call (unattended checkout): send `type: F2`, `prices_include_tax`, a `payment` block and `options.register_verifactu`, and identify the operation with `external_id`. Optional: `notes`, `metadata`, `tags`, `custom_fields`, and an `options` object to atomically create, issue, send and wait for the PDF in a single call. Without `options` the invoice is created as a draft. A line may also be a DISBURSEMENT (`line_type: "SUPLIDO"`): an amount paid in the name and on behalf of the client (an official fee, duty or registry charge) that is re-invoiced at cost and, under art. 78.Tres.3 of the Spanish VAT Act (LIVA), stays out of the taxable base — it carries no VAT, withholding, surcharge, discount or product, requires `source_invoice_reference`, and is not allowed on a simplified (`F2`) invoice. Worked example: a 1,000.00 service line at 21% plus a 150.00 `SUPLIDO` line returns `subtotal` 1000.00, `taxes_total` 210.00, `total` 1210.00, `total_disbursements` 150.00 and `total_to_pay` 1360.00.

type.description: Invoice type: `F1` (complete invoice, the default) or `F2` (simplified invoice, the ticket of a terminal). A simplified invoice needs simplified invoices enabled for the company (422 `simplified_invoices_disabled`) and cannot exceed the absolute cap of 3,000 € VAT included (422 `simplified_invoice_not_allowed`).

client_id.description: Id of the client (UUID v7). Required with `type: F1` (or without `type`), and the client must have a complete tax ID. Optional with `type: F2`: without it the invoice is an anonymous ticket; with it, a qualified simplified invoice (the client must belong to your company).

prices_include_tax.description: When `true`, the `unit_price` of every line is the FINAL price with taxes (VAT included) and the system computes the net base to the cent, so the invoice total equals the sum of the amounts you sent. If no distribution of the cents reaches that total the request is rejected with 422 `amount_reconciliation_failed` and nothing is issued. Catalog lines (`product_id`) are not accepted in this mode. Defaults to `false`.

operation_on.description: Date the operation took place (YYYY-MM-DD) when it differs from the issue date (arts. 6.1.f and 7.1.c of Royal Decree 1619/2012). It cannot be later than `issued_on` (422 `operation_date_after_issue_date`) unless the first line that declares a `regime_key` uses 14 or 15. It is printed on the PDF and reported in the VeriFactu record.

payment.description: Payment recorded in the same call: after issuing, a payment is registered for the whole amount due and the invoice ends up paid. It implies issuing. Its presence makes the request an unattended checkout.

method.description: Payment method, from the catalog of `GET /v1/payment-methods`. Required when `payment` is sent.

paid_at.description: Date of the payment (ISO 8601); only its date is used. Defaults to the issue date.

reference.description: Reference of the payment, for example the transaction id of the card terminal (up to 100 characters).

unit_price.description: Unit price. Send a JSON number or a decimal string with up to 4 decimals (`"0.0125"`, `"100.0000"`): the string is the exact form the response returns, so a line read from the API can be sent back unchanged. Derived amounts are computed from it and keep 2 decimals.

tax_rate.description: VAT rate of the line (0–100). Optional: when you omit it (or send `null`) the line takes, in this order, the tax it references or the tax assigned to its product, and otherwise the DEFAULT TAX of your company for this kind of document (tax settings), inherited as a whole: its rate, its indirect-tax regime (IVA, IGIC or IPSI) and its AEAT qualification; an exempt or not-subject default also declares its cause (`exemption_reason`) on the line unless the line sends its own. The line ends up exactly as if you had chosen that tax. If none of them exists the request is rejected with 422 `missing_required_param`, with `error.param` = `lines.N.tax_rate` and `error.line_index` = N (the zero-based index of the line): the API never guesses a rate. A `0` you send is honoured as a real 0 % rate, never confused with «not stated».

line_type.description: Kind of line: `NORMAL` (default) for an ordinary line of your own operation, or `SUPLIDO` for a DISBURSEMENT — an amount you paid in the name and on behalf of the client (an official fee, duty or registry charge) and now re-invoice at cost. A disbursement is not part of your taxable base (art. 78.Tres.3 LIVA): it stays out of `subtotal`/`taxes_total`/`total`, is aggregated into `total_disbursements`, and is never declared in the AEAT VeriFactu record. A `SUPLIDO` line must carry no VAT, withholding, surcharge, discount, regime key, exemption cause or product, and is rejected on a simplified (`F2`) invoice.

source_invoice_reference.description: Reference of the supporting document that originated the disbursement — the receipt or fee number issued by the public body (up to 100 characters). REQUIRED when `line_type` is `SUPLIDO`; leave it out on a normal line. Free text on purpose: the receipt of a public body is rarely a supplier invoice.

source_invoice_ids.description: Optional traceability of a disbursement: list of IDs (UUID v7) of your own expenses that back it. An expense of another company is rejected with 422. Omit it (or send `null`) when there is nothing to link.

unit.description: Unit of measure printed next to the quantity on the document (`hours`, `kg`, `units`, …), up to 20 characters. Presentation only: free text, no closed catalog and no fiscal effect.

exemption_reason_text.description: Free-text wording of the exemption provision of this line (up to 255 characters), printed under the line description to satisfy the mention required by art. 6.1.j of Royal Decree 1619/2012 when the catalogued cause does not cover it. Orthogonal to `exemption_reason` and to the document-level exemption cause; no coherence is enforced between them.

line_total.description: Optional CHECKSUM of the line total. When sent, it is compared against the total this API computes and the request is rejected with 422 (`line_total_checksum_mismatch`, with the expected and received values in `error.details`) when they differ by more than one cent. Never stored and never returned: the invoiced amount is always the computed one, so this field only reports a rounding mismatch with your own ERP. Omit it and no checksum runs.

issue_directly.description: When `true`, the invoice is issued right after it is created (definitive number, frozen document) instead of staying as a draft.

send_automatically.description: When `true`, the invoice is emailed once issued; it implies issuing. The recipient is `options.send_to` or, when you omit it, the email of the client. If there is no possible recipient (no client, or a client with no email, and no `send_to`) the request is rejected with 422 `missing_required_param` and `param` = `options.send_to` BEFORE anything is created: no draft is left behind and no number is consumed. Repeating the request of an `external_id` that is already issued does not email it again while that email is queued or delivered.

send_to.description: Recipient email for `options.send_automatically`. Optional when the client has an email; required (422 `missing_required_param`) when you ask for the sending with no client or with a client that has no email. An empty value is rejected as well.

wait_for_pdf.description: When `true`, the response waits up to about 15 seconds for the A4 PDF to be materialized (`pdf.status: ready`); if it is not ready by then `pdf.status` is `pending`. It implies issuing.

register_verifactu.description: When `true`, the VeriFactu alta is generated synchronously, BEFORE responding, and the response carries its huella and QR in the `verifactu` block. It implies issuing. If the alta cannot be generated the invoice stays issued and the block reports `status: failed` with its `error_code`. Its transmission to AEAT follows its course in batches.

CreateNifTransferV1Request.description: Body of the tax ID transfer issuance. `company_id` is the opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the tax ID of your account that this transfer gives away; it must be within your credential scope and cannot be the owner company of the account. `recipient_account_id` is OPTIONAL and names the only account that will be able to accept the transfer. `expires_at` is OPTIONAL and is a REQUEST, not a command: pass an ISO 8601 instant in the future and within the product ceiling, or omit it and the product default applies. Nothing else is accepted — the issuing account and the acting person come from the authenticated credential, never from the body, because issuing a transfer is giving away control of a tax ID and the giver is always the account that holds it.

recipient_account_id.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of the ONLY account that will be able to accept this transfer. Optional: without it, whoever holds the secret can accept it.

sku.description: Stock keeping unit (your own product code), unique per company. Optional; up to 100 characters.

stock.description: Initial stock. Absent → defaults to 0. Later you can set it absolutely with `stock` on `PATCH /v1/companies/{company}/products/{product}`, or move it with `PATCH /v1/companies/{company}/products/{product}/stock` (`set`/`increase`/`decrease`).

Public identifier (UUID v7) of the option value. A new value sent with another UUID version is rejected with 422.

custom_fields.description: Typed custom fields as `[{field, value}]`. `field` up to 60 characters (non-empty), `value` up to 500 characters, up to 50 entries.

operation_class.description: Classifies the origin of the expense for the input VAT of Modelo 303 (boxes [28]-[39]). Closed set; nullable → defaults to `corriente`.

exclude_347.description: Whether to exclude this expense from the annual Modelo 347 declaration.

unit_price.description: Unit price. Send a JSON number or a decimal string with up to 4 decimals (`"0.0125"`, `"100.0000"`): the string is the exact form the response returns, so a line read from the API can be sent back unchanged. Derived amounts are computed from it and keep 2 decimals.

tax_rate.description: Per-line VAT rate (0–100). REQUIRED. There is no silent default: a purchase with no VAT is declared explicitly as `tax_rate: 0`, so that "not stated" and "stated as zero" never collapse into the same document.

retention_rate.description: Per-line IRPF retention and deductible VAT. `retention_rate` is the percentage withheld from the supplier (0–100); `vat_deductible` flags VAT deductibility — it does not change the amount paid, but a `false` line is excluded from the deductible input VAT of Modelo 303 (boxes [28]-[37]).

surcharge_rate.description: Per-line equivalence surcharge (the legal VAT↔surcharge pair is validated) and LIVA exemption reason (closed catalog).

indirect_tax_regime.description: Per-line indirect tax regime of the supplier. Passthrough only (purchase lines have no `tax_id`): the incoming override is the sole regime channel; the real invariant lives in the domain.

CreatePurchaseOrderRequest.description: Create a purchase order with its supplier and its lines. It is born in draft AND ALREADY NUMBERED: unlike a sales order, a purchase order is stamped with its number when it is created and not when it is confirmed, so a draft already carries one; it is unique per company and not dense, because a purchase order is not a fiscal document. Required: `supplier_id` and `lines[]`, with at least one line — an order with no lines is not a document. Optional: `supplier_order_reference`, `warehouse_id` (an ACTIVE warehouse the goods are expected at), `expected_date` and `notes`. `supplier_order_reference` is the reference the supplier uses for this order in its own system, and it is THE UNIQUENESS KEY OF THE CREATION, scoped to YOUR COMPANY: sending one that is already taken is rejected with a conflict naming `supplier_reference` and creates NO second order. It is never an upsert — the existing order is not updated and nothing of it is overwritten —, so after a conflict you read that order instead of resending the body. Two orders with no reference coexist without colliding, and the same reference in two different companies is two independent orders. Neither the order date nor a numbering series is accepted from the body: the date is the moment the order is registered, and a purchase order is not numbered by series. Each line names a catalog product of your company and the `quantity` IN THE PURCHASE UNIT of the supplier offer it is bought under, and may carry the variant, the offer, a description, the unit cost and the tax, withholding and surcharge percentages; omitting the offer takes the preferred active one of that product, and omitting the cost takes the cost of that offer. Every reference — supplier, warehouse, product, variant and offer — must belong to the company in the path: one from another company is rejected exactly like a non-existent one.

supplier_id.description: Public ID of the business contact the order is placed with, of the company in the path. Required.

supplier_order_reference.description: Reference the supplier uses for this order in its own system, up to 120 characters. Unique PER COMPANY and the key of the creation: one that is already taken is rejected with a conflict naming it, and no second order is created — it is never an upsert of the existing one. Two orders with no reference coexist without colliding, and the same reference in two different companies is two independent orders.

warehouse_id.description: Public ID of an ACTIVE warehouse of your company. On the order it is the warehouse the goods are expected at; on a line it overrides that choice for that line alone, and omitting it on a line inherits the one on the order.

expected_date.description: Date the goods are expected (`YYYY-MM-DD`). The date of the ORDER is not a field of this body: it is the moment the order is registered.

notes.description: Free text attached to the order, up to 1000 characters.

lines.description: Lines of the order: at least one, because an order with no lines is not a document. Each entry names the product bought and the quantity in the PURCHASE unit of the supplier offer it is bought under, and may carry the variant, the offer, a description, the unit cost and the three percentages.

product_id.description: Public ID of the catalog product being ordered, of the company in the path. Required on every line.

product_variant_id.description: Public ID of the variant, when the line orders a specific one.

offer_id.description: Public ID of the ACTIVE supplier offer the terms of the line are copied from: purchase unit, factor that converts it to the base unit, agreed cost, minimum quantity and lead time. Omitting it takes the preferred active offer of the product.

description.description: Concept of the line, up to 255 characters. Omitting it composes it from the product being ordered.

quantity.description: Ordered quantity IN THE PURCHASE UNIT of the offer the line is bought under — boxes, pallets or whatever that offer publishes, which need not be the base unit of the product. Greater than zero, at most four decimals, up to 9999999999.9999. The equivalent in base units is DERIVED with the conversion factor the order freezes from that offer, and that factor is not a field of any body on this surface: it is copied with the rest of the agreed terms, so a later catalog change cannot rewrite an order already placed and a goods receipt converts with the factor that was agreed.

unit_price.description: Agreed unit cost, per PURCHASE unit, with at most four decimals. Omitting it takes the cost of the chosen offer. The line amount and the taxes derived from it have their own, narrower limit than the one of this field.

tax_rate.description: VAT percentage of the line, between 0 and 100 with at most two decimals. Omitting it takes the one that applies to the product.

retention_rate.description: Withholding percentage of the line, between 0 and 100. The sign the tax catalog publishes is accepted and the magnitude is what gets stored.

surcharge_rate.description: Equivalence surcharge percentage of the line, between 0 and 100.

warehouse_id.description: Public ID of an ACTIVE warehouse of your company. On the order it is the warehouse the goods are expected at; on a line it overrides that choice for that line alone, and omitting it on a line inherits the one on the order.

CreateRecurringFromInvoiceRequest.description: Create a recurring invoice from an existing invoice, reusing its lines, client and series. The body supplies only the recurrence configuration: `frequency` and `start_on` are required; `end_on`, `name`, `description`, `notes`, `metadata`, `holiday_handling`, `days_before_due`, `max_occurrences`, `generation_mode` (`draft`, `issue` or `issue_and_send`) and an `auto_delivery` object are optional.

generation_mode.description: What each run of the recurrence does with the invoice it generates: `draft` leaves it as a draft; `issue` issues it (definitive number, VeriFactu record, stock movements) without emailing it; `issue_and_send` issues it and emails it to the `auto_delivery` recipients. Any other value is rejected with 422. Optional and nullable: when omitted (or `null`) the mode is derived from `send_automatically` (`true` → `issue_and_send`, `false` or absent → `draft`). When sent, it takes precedence and `send_automatically` becomes a derived field (`true` only with `issue_and_send`); sending a `send_automatically` (top-level or inside `auto_delivery`) that contradicts it is rejected with 422. Recipients are only required with `issue_and_send`: if an `auto_delivery` object is configured, `auto_delivery.recipients` must then contain at least one address (422 `auto_delivery_recipients_required` otherwise); `draft` and `issue` send no email and need none. Available in every API version.

send_automatically.description: Compatibility flag derived from `generation_mode`. Without `generation_mode`, `true` selects `issue_and_send` and `false` selects `draft`. Together with `generation_mode` it must agree with it (`true` only with `issue_and_send`), otherwise the request is rejected with 422. Prefer sending `generation_mode`.
