CreateRecurringInvoiceRequest.description: Create a recurring invoice template that auto-generates invoices on a fixed cadence. Required: `client_id`, `series_id`, `frequency`, `start_on` and `lines[]` (at least one). Optional: `end_on`, `name`, `description`, `notes`, `metadata`, `holiday_handling`, `days_before_due`, `max_occurrences`, `email_to`, `send_automatically`, `generation_mode`, `auto_delivery`, `tags` and `custom_fields`. `generation_mode` (`draft`, `issue` or `issue_and_send`) decides what each run does with the generated invoice; `send_automatically` is its derived compatibility field. `frequency` accepts `daily`, `weekly`, `biweekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `semiannual` or `yearly`.

send_automatically.description: Compatibility flag derived from `generation_mode`. Without `generation_mode`, `true` selects `issue_and_send` and `false` selects `draft`. Together with `generation_mode` it must agree with it (`true` only with `issue_and_send`), otherwise the request is rejected with 422. Prefer sending `generation_mode`.

generation_mode.description: What each run of the recurrence does with the invoice it generates: `draft` leaves it as a draft; `issue` issues it (definitive number, VeriFactu record, stock movements) without emailing it; `issue_and_send` issues it and emails it to the `auto_delivery` recipients. Any other value is rejected with 422. Optional and nullable: when omitted (or `null`) the mode is derived from `send_automatically` (`true` → `issue_and_send`, `false` or absent → `draft`). When sent, it takes precedence and `send_automatically` becomes a derived field (`true` only with `issue_and_send`); sending a `send_automatically` (top-level or inside `auto_delivery`) that contradicts it is rejected with 422. Recipients are only required with `issue_and_send`: if an `auto_delivery` object is configured, `auto_delivery.recipients` must then contain at least one address (422 `auto_delivery_recipients_required` otherwise); `draft` and `issue` send no email and need none. Available in every API version.

send_automatically.description: Compatibility flag derived from `generation_mode`. Without `generation_mode`, `true` selects `issue_and_send` and `false` selects `draft`. Together with `generation_mode` it must agree with it (`true` only with `issue_and_send`), otherwise the request is rejected with 422. Prefer sending `generation_mode`.

unit_price.description: Unit price. Send a JSON number or a decimal string with up to 4 decimals (`"0.0125"`, `"100.0000"`): the string is the exact form the response returns, so a line read from the API can be sent back unchanged. Derived amounts are computed from it and keep 2 decimals.

tax_rate.description: VAT rate of the line (0–100). Optional: when you omit it (or send `null`) the line takes, in this order, the tax it references or the tax assigned to its product, and otherwise the DEFAULT TAX of your company for this kind of document (tax settings), inherited as a whole: its rate, its indirect-tax regime (IVA, IGIC or IPSI) and its AEAT qualification; an exempt or not-subject default also declares its cause (`exemption_reason`) on the line unless the line sends its own. The line ends up exactly as if you had chosen that tax. If none of them exists the request is rejected with 422 `missing_required_param`, with `error.param` = `lines.N.tax_rate` and `error.line_index` = N (the zero-based index of the line): the API never guesses a rate. A `0` you send is honoured as a real 0 % rate, never confused with «not stated».

CreateReturnRequest.description:
Request the return of one or more lines of a delivery note, an invoice or a
sales order.

The return is born in the requested state, which is the only state where it
can still be edited or deleted. Asking for it consumes no numbering and moves
no stock: goods come back when the return is received, and money goes back
when it is refunded.

## The origin

 - `origin_type` (required) — where the return comes from: `delivery_note`,
   `invoice` or `sales_order`, and nothing else. The value travels as written:
   `Invoice` or a value padded with blanks is rejected instead of being
   silently fixed, so the same origin is never stored under two spellings.
 - `origin_id` (required) — public identifier of that document, which has to
   belong to the company in the path.

The origin cannot be changed afterwards: returning against another document
means rejecting this return, which frees the quantity, and asking for a new
one.

## The lines

`lines` is required and needs at least one entry. Each entry carries:

 - `origin_line_id` (required) — which line of the origin document comes back.
   It is the reference handed out by the returnable lines reading of that same
   document, and it is bounded by the origin: the return is checked again
   against that document within that company before anything is inherited from
   it.
 - `quantity` (required) — how much comes back, greater than zero, with up to
   ten integer digits and four decimals. It travels as a decimal number and is
   compared as a decimal: in floating point, four decimals lose scale before
   anyone compares them against what was delivered.
 - `reason` (required) — why that line comes back, out of the closed set of
   four values.

## What this body does not accept, stated so it does not read as an oversight

 - **Unit price and tax rate of a line.** Both are inherited from the origin
   line. The amount to be corrected is not decided by whoever asks for the
   return: it is decided by the document being returned, and the refund step
   issues a corrective invoice that cannot be deleted afterwards, only voided
   with another fiscal document. Both keys are dropped from the validated body
   and never reach the created line.
 - **Product and variant of a line.** Inherited from the origin line too, for
   the same reason, so there is no product reference in this body.
 - **Request date.** The return window is measured between the reference date
   of the origin and the moment of asking, so letting the caller choose that
   moment would let the caller choose whether the window has expired.
 - **Series, number and state.** The provisional number is stamped when the
   return is requested and the definitive one when it is approved, out of the
   live return series of the company. A return is always born requested and
   every step forward has an operation of its own.
 - **Target invoice.** The invoice to be corrected is resolved from the origin
   when the refund happens, and can be fixed beforehand through the partial
   update.
 - **Company and actor.** Both come from the path and from the credential.

## Optional fields and how to leave them out

 - `reason` — header reason out of the same closed set of four values. Left
   out, it is derived from the lines when they all share one.
 - `warehouse_id` — public identifier of the warehouse that will take the
   goods in, active and of the company in the path.
 - `notes` — free text, up to 1000 characters.

An optional text field left blank is rejected rather than read as absence:
omit the field instead of sending empty text, so the contract never depends on
whether someone typed a space.

## Company

Every reference in this body is checked against the company in the path, so a
document or a warehouse of another company is rejected exactly like one that
does not exist, without revealing that it exists.

## What comes back

A created return with its public identifier, its requested state and its lines
carrying the price and the tax rate inherited from the origin, plus the
location header of the new resource.

origin_type.description: Kind of document the goods came out on: `delivery_note`, `invoice` or `sales_order`. It says where the returnable quantities are read from, and it is not redundant with the identifier: the three kinds are numbered independently.

origin_id.description: Public ID of the origin document of that kind, of the company in the path. A document of another company is rejected exactly like one that does not exist.

reason.description: Header reason of the return; left out, it is derived from the lines

warehouse_id.description: Public ID of the warehouse that takes the goods back in: an ACTIVE warehouse of the company in the path. Omitting it leaves the destination to be decided when the goods are received. An archived one is rejected, because goods cannot come back into a site that is out of service.

notes.description: Free text of the return, up to 1000 characters.

lines.description: Lines that come back: at least one. Each entry names the origin line, how much of it comes back and why. Neither the unit price nor the tax rate travels here: both are inherited from the origin document, so a return can never restate the amount of what it gives back.

origin_line_id.description: Reference of the origin line that comes back, exactly as the returnable-lines reading hands it out. It is a whole number and not a public ID, which is the one place in this API where that happens: the lines of a delivery note and of an invoice carry no public identifier of their own yet. Read the returnable lines of the origin first and send back the reference you are given there.

quantity.description: Quantity of that line that comes back: greater than zero, with at most four decimals and up to 9999999999.9999. More than what is still returnable on that line is rejected as a business-rule violation naming what is left.

counted_quantity.description: Pieces that come back from a variable-weight line sold by count: greater than zero, with at most four decimals. Optional and informational (it never drives stock or amounts); the unit is inherited from the origin line. It is only accepted when the origin line carries pieces (see `counted_unit` in the returnable lines reading): otherwise the request is rejected with `return_line_pieces_not_allowed`.

reason.description: Reason of the line, out of the closed set of four values

CreateSalesOrderRequest.description: Create a sales order. It is always born as a draft with no number: the number is stamped when the order is confirmed, with the sales-order series of your company. Required: `channel`, `order_date`, `buyer_name` and `lines[]` (at least one line). Optional: `expected_delivery_date`, `series_id`, `warehouse_id`, `business_contact_id`, `external_id`, `notes`, the rest of the buyer identity (`buyer_email`, `buyer_phone`, `buyer_tax_id` — at least one contact channel is needed, and the tax ID is optional because a private individual may not have one) and the two addresses, sent as flat `billing_*` and `shipping_*` fields, which the response groups under `buyer`, `billing_address` and `shipping_address`. `external_id` is the reference the system that created the order uses to identify it, and it is the key of the creation: its uniqueness scope is THE COMPANY, so sending one that is already taken is rejected naming the order that holds it, creates no second order and consumes no series number, while the same reference in two different companies is two different orders. The status, the number and the order ID are never accepted from the body, and the served, invoiced and returned quantities are never sent: they move on their own as delivery notes, invoices and returns consume the order lines. Every reference — business contact, series, warehouse, product — must belong to the company in the path: one from another company is rejected exactly like a non-existent one. Creating an order consumes monthly plan quota, and an exhausted monthly allowance answers payment required.

channel.description: Origin channel of the order, fixed on creation and changed by no later operation: `manual` (entered by a person), `store` (a connected e-commerce store), `storefront` (your own public storefront), `api` (this API), `quote` and `proforma` (converted from one of those documents) or `assistant` (created through the conversational assistant).

expected_delivery_date.description: Date the order is expected to be delivered (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

series_id.description: Public ID of the numbering series the order will be confirmed with: a live sales-order series of your company. Omitted, the confirmation resolves the default series of that type.

warehouse_id.description: Public ID of an ACTIVE warehouse of your company. On the order it is the warehouse the goods ship from; on a line it overrides that choice for that line alone, and omitting it on a line inherits the one on the order.

business_contact_id.description: Public ID of the business contact the order is linked to. Optional: an order may exist with no contact.

external_id.description: Reference the system that created the order uses to identify it, up to 100 characters. Unique PER COMPANY: one that is already taken is rejected naming the order that holds it, and the same reference in two different companies is two different orders.

notes.description: Free text attached to the order, up to 1000 characters.

buyer_name.description: Name or registered business name of the buyer. Always required.

buyer_email.description: Email of the buyer. At least one of the two contact channels, email or phone, is needed.

buyer_phone.description: Phone number of the buyer. At least one of the two contact channels, email or phone, is needed.

buyer_tax_id.description: Tax identifier of the buyer. OPTIONAL: a private individual may not have one and the order is registered all the same.

billing_address_line.description: Street and number of the billing address.

billing_city.description: Town or city of the billing address.

billing_province.description: Province or region of the billing address.

billing_postal_code.description: Postal code of the billing address.

billing_country.description: Country of the billing address as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Required as soon as any other field of the billing block is sent.

shipping_address_line.description: Street and number of the shipping address.

shipping_city.description: Town or city of the shipping address.

shipping_province.description: Province or region of the shipping address.

shipping_postal_code.description: Postal code of the shipping address.

shipping_country.description: Country of the shipping address as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Required as soon as any other field of the shipping block is sent.

lines.description: Lines of the order: at least one. Each entry carries its subject (`product_id`, or `description` and `unit_price` without it), the ordered `quantity`, the `discount` and the three tax percentages, and may ship from its own warehouse.

product_id.description: Public ID of the catalog product of the line, of the same company as the order.

description.description: Concept of the line. Required when the line names no product.

quantity.description: ORDERED quantity: greater than zero and with at most four decimals. The served, invoiced and returned quantities are never sent — they move on their own as the documents of the order consume it.

unit_price.description: Unit price, with at most four decimals. Required when the line names no catalog product; with a product, the price you send wins over the catalog one, and omitting it lets the catalog resolve it.

discount.description: Discount percentage of the line, between 0 and 100.

vat_rate.description: VAT percentage of the line, between 0 and 100.

retention_rate.description: Withholding percentage of the line, between 0 and 100. The sign the tax catalog publishes is accepted and the magnitude is what gets stored.

surcharge_rate.description: Equivalence surcharge percentage of the line, between 0 and 100.

vat_id.description: Public ID of the VAT tax of the line, from the GLOBAL tax catalog (shared by every company).

retention_id.description: Public ID of the withholding tax of the line, from the GLOBAL tax catalog.

surcharge_id.description: Public ID of the equivalence surcharge of the line, from the GLOBAL tax catalog.

warehouse_id.description: Public ID of an ACTIVE warehouse of your company. On the order it is the warehouse the goods ship from; on a line it overrides that choice for that line alone, and omitting it on a line inherits the one on the order.

CreateStockReservationRequest.description: Hold stock for a holder so it stops counting as available while a checkout completes. Required: `holder_type` (a lowercase short name you choose for the kind of holder — letters, digits and underscores, up to 40 characters, e.g. `storefront_cart`), `holder_id` (the public ID of that holder, UUID) and `lines[]` (1 to 100 entries). Each line requires `product_id` and a `quantity` greater than zero, with up to 10 integer digits and 4 decimals; it may also carry `product_variant_id`, `warehouse_id` (an active warehouse of the company in the path — omitted, the warehouse planned for that product is used) and `holder_line_id` to match the hold back to a line of your own cart. `expires_in_seconds` is optional and is a DURATION counted from the moment the server handles the request, between 1 and 86400; omit it for a hold that never expires. An absolute expiry date is not accepted, so a clock skew on your side can never decide the hold lifetime. The origin of the hold is never taken from the body: it is stamped by the platform. The creation is all-or-nothing — if a single line asks for more than the available quantity, nothing is held and the response reports the requested and the available amount per line.

holder_type.description: Kind of holder that keeps the goods on hold. You pick the value: a lowercase short name (letters, digits and underscores, up to 40 characters) identifying the owner of the hold in your own system. It is not a closed catalog, and it is half of the key used later to query or release what that holder keeps on hold.

holder_id.description: Public ID (UUID v7) of the holder in your own system. It is not checked against any table — which table it points at depends on the holder type — and everything is scoped to the company in the path, so a holder of another company reaches nothing.

expires_in_seconds.description: How long the hold lasts, in SECONDS counted from the moment the server handles the request (1 to 86400). Omit it for a hold that never expires. It is a duration and not an absolute date on purpose: with a date, a clock skew on the client would hold stock longer than intended — or expire it at birth — with nothing to show for it.

lines.description: Articles put on hold: between 1 and 100 entries. The hold is all-or-nothing, so one line asking for more than there is available rejects the whole request and holds nothing.

product_id.description: Public ID of the article put on hold, of the company in the path.

product_variant_id.description: Public ID of the variant, when the hold is on one specific variant of the article.

warehouse_id.description: Public ID of the active warehouse the stock is held from. Omitted, the warehouse planned for that product is used; when none can be resolved the line holds nothing and the whole creation is rejected.

holder_line_id.description: Public ID of the line of your own holder (a cart line, an order line) this hold belongs to, so you can match each reservation back to it later.

quantity.description: Units to put on hold: greater than zero, with at most four decimals and up to 9999999999.9999.

CreateStockReservationRequest.title: CreateStockReservationRequest

CreateStockTransferRequest.description: Create a stock transfer between two warehouses of your company. It is born as a DRAFT and moves no stock: the goods leave the origin when the transfer is dispatched and enter the destination when it is received. Required: `origin_warehouse_id` and `destination_warehouse_id`, two warehouses of the company in the path — one from another company answers not found, exactly like one that does not exist, and sending the same warehouse twice is rejected as a business-rule violation, because a transfer to the same place moves nothing. Optional: `notes` (up to 1000 characters) and `lines[]`, up to 100 entries. A transfer with NO lines is a legitimate draft you add lines to afterwards; what gets rejected is dispatching an empty one. Each line names the article (`product_id`, plus `product_variant_id` when one specific variant travels) and the `quantity` to dispatch, greater than zero and with at most four decimals, and may carry the location the goods leave from and the one they are placed at. The number of the transfer is stamped when it is created and is never accepted from the body; neither is the status, which the three transitions move, nor the received quantity, which only the reception moves.

origin_warehouse_id.description: Public ID of the warehouse the goods LEAVE from, of the company in the path. One of another company answers not found, exactly like one that does not exist.

destination_warehouse_id.description: Public ID of the warehouse that RECEIVES the goods, with the same rules as the origin one. Origin and destination equal is rejected as a business-rule violation: a transfer to the same place moves nothing.

notes.description: Free notes of the transfer, up to 1000 characters. The free-text search of the listing reads them as well as the number.

lines.description: Lines of the transfer: optional and up to 100. A transfer with no lines is a legitimate draft you add lines to afterwards; dispatching an empty one is what gets rejected.

product_id.description: Public ID of the article that travels, of the company in the path.

product_variant_id.description: Public ID of the variant, when the line moves one specific variant of the article.

quantity.description: Quantity to dispatch: greater than zero, with at most four decimals and up to 9999999999.9999. It is what LEAVES the origin; the received quantity is never sent and moves on its own when the transfer is received.

origin_location_id.description: Public ID of the location inside the ORIGIN warehouse the goods leave from. Optional: this body checks it against your company, and that it also belongs to the origin warehouse of this transfer is checked by the transfer, which is what has both warehouses in front of it.

destination_location_id.description: Public ID of the location inside the DESTINATION warehouse the goods are placed at, with the same criterion.

CreateStockTransferRequest.title: CreateStockTransferRequest

CreateStorefrontKeyRequest.description: Issue a publishable storefront credential. `name` is a label to tell your credentials apart (1-120 chars). `allowed_origins` is the list of web origins the browser may use it from (1 to 10 entries, each `scheme://host[:port]`, no path, no query string, no fragment and NO WILDCARDS: neither `*` nor `https://*.example.com`) — that list is the whole access control of this credential, so every domain and subdomain is written in full. `scopes` must belong to the buyer lane (`storefront:read`, `storefront:write`); credential-management and integrator scopes are rejected. `expires_at` is optional and must be in the future. The plaintext secret is returned once in this response and never again; the prefix, the secret, its hash, the status and the company are never accepted from the body. Reaching the active-credential cap of your tier returns 422.

name.description: Label that tells your publishable credentials apart, from 1 to 120 characters. It is never published to shoppers: it is what you recognize the credential by in the listing.

allowed_origins.description: Web origins the browser may use this credential from: between 1 and 10 entries, each one `scheme://host[:port]`, with no path, no query string, no fragment and NO WILDCARDS, neither `*` nor `https://*.example.com`. This list IS the access control of a credential that lives in a browser, so every domain and subdomain is written in full, and an entry that breaks any of those rules is rejected naming the entry that does.

scopes.description: Scopes granted to the credential: at least one and only from the shopper lane (`storefront:read`, `storefront:write`). The ones that manage these very credentials and the integrator ones are rejected, because a credential that travels in a browser must not be able to mint another one. The assignable catalog is published by the scopes operation of this resource, so it does not have to be hard-coded.

expires_at.description: Moment from which the credential stops authenticating, in ISO 8601 and strictly in the future. Optional: without it the credential lasts until it is revoked. It is fixed at issuance and no later update changes it.

CreateStorefrontKeyRequest.title: CreateStorefrontKeyRequest

CreateStorefrontOrderRequest.description: Turn what a shopper has in the cart into a real sales order. THE PRICE IS ALWAYS THE SERVER: every line is priced again at creation, ANY AMOUNT PRESENT IN THE BODY IS IGNORED, and neither the amount previewed nor the one stored in the cart session is taken as the price of the line without resolving it again — it is the only real defence against a manipulated browser. The `Idempotency-Key` HEADER IS REQUIRED here and identifies the REQUEST: the same key with the same body returns the SAME order and leaves one single row, and a call without it is rejected. `external_id` is the OTHER axis and the contract keeps the two apart on purpose: it identifies the ORDER in the system that originates it and it is the key of an UPSERT whose uniqueness scope is THE COMPANY — two creations with the same external id inside the same shop return the same order, even from different requests and days apart, while two different companies may each use the same one —, and neither axis is derived from the other. The lines come from one of two mutually exclusive paths: `session_id`, the public id of a cart session, whose lines are the ones the server has stored and are NOT repeated in the body; or `lines`, required when no session is given, with at least one entry and the ceiling of 50. Availability is checked line by line and a single line without enough units rejects the WHOLE order naming that line: no partial order is ever created. The shopper needs `buyer_name`, `buyer_email` and the shipping address (`shipping_address_line`, `shipping_city` and `shipping_country`); `buyer_tax_id` is OPTIONAL, and a shopper without one completes the order, which then creates no business contact at all, because a business contact requires a fiscal identity and a private individual does not have one. `marketing_consent` is REQUIRED and says whether the shopper accepts commercial communications: it is declared instead of presumed in either direction, because silence leaves no record of what the shopper was asked. Neither the IP address of the shopper nor any browser tracking identifier is stored. A session that does not exist, that belongs to another shop, that has expired, that was already turned into an order or that was abandoned rejects the creation saying which of those happened, because the remedy of each one is different. The order is born with the storefront channel, so its origin is distinguishable from a manual entry, from a connected store and from an integrator call.

session_id.description: Public id of the cart session being confirmed. With it, the lines are the ones the server has stored for that cart and the body does NOT repeat them, which is why it cannot travel together with `lines`. A session that does not exist, that belongs to another shop, that has expired, that was already turned into an order or that was abandoned rejects the creation saying which of those happened, because the remedy of each one is different.

external_id.description: Reference the system that originates the order uses to identify it, up to 100 characters. It is the key of an UPSERT and its uniqueness scope is THE COMPANY: sending one a previous order already holds returns THAT order instead of creating a second one, and the same reference in two different companies is two different orders. It is NOT the idempotency key and is not derived from it — this one identifies the ORDER, the header identifies the REQUEST.

marketing_consent.description: Whether the shopper accepts commercial communications. REQUIRED: it is declared instead of presumed in either direction, because silence would leave no record of what the shopper was asked. It is a field of the order and it is not kept in the cart.

buyer_name.description: Name of the shopper. REQUIRED, up to 255 characters.

buyer_email.description: Email of the shopper. REQUIRED, up to 191 characters: it is where the order is notified.

buyer_phone.description: Phone of the shopper, up to 40 characters. Optional.

buyer_tax_id.description: Fiscal identification of the shopper, up to 20 characters. OPTIONAL: a shopper without one completes the order, which is then created with the buyer identity and linked to no business contact at all, because a business contact requires a fiscal identity and a private individual does not have one.

shipping_address_line.description: Street and number the order is delivered to. REQUIRED, up to 255 characters.

shipping_city.description: Town or city of delivery. REQUIRED, up to 120 characters.

shipping_province.description: Province of delivery, up to 120 characters. Optional.

shipping_postal_code.description: Postal code of delivery, up to 20 characters. Optional.

shipping_country.description: Country of delivery as a two-letter code. REQUIRED: an address with no country can neither be delivered nor validated.

billing_address_line.description: Street and number of the billing address, up to 255 characters. The whole billing block is optional.

billing_city.description: Town or city of the billing address, up to 120 characters.

billing_province.description: Province of the billing address, up to 120 characters.

billing_postal_code.description: Postal code of the billing address, up to 20 characters.

billing_country.description: Country of the billing address as a two-letter code. It becomes required as soon as any other field of the billing block is sent.

lines.description: Lines of the order, REQUIRED when no cart session is confirmed and forbidden together with one: at least one entry and at most 50. No amount is accepted inside a line — every line is priced again on the server at creation — and the availability of each one is checked before anything is created.

product_id.description: Public id of the article of the line, of the shop that owns the key. Required in every line.

variant_id.description: Public id of the variant chosen, when the article has variants.

presentation_id.description: Public id of the presentation chosen, when the article has presentations.

configuration_id.description: Public id of the configuration chosen, when there is one.

selection_signature.description: Fingerprint of the configuration chosen: 64 hexadecimal characters.

options.description: Option values chosen for the line, as a list of pairs of `group_id` and `value_id`: one value per group and at most 50.

items.description: Each chosen option, with its group and its value

group_id.description: Public id of the option group the choice belongs to.

value_id.description: Public id of the value chosen inside that group.

quantity.description: Units of the line: required, greater than zero, with at most four decimals and up to 9999999999.9999. A line without enough available units rejects the WHOLE order naming that line.

CreateStorefrontOrderRequest.title: CreateStorefrontOrderRequest

CreateStorefrontSessionRequest.description: Open a cart session for a shopper and get back its public id, which is the ONLY key to that cart: whoever holds it can read it and change it, so it is unguessable and has to be treated as a secret. The cart may be born EMPTY — `lines` is optional and an empty list is valid, because opening a cart and filling it are two different moments — and the number of lines is capped at the declared ceiling of 50. Each line carries `product_id` (required), the variant, the presentation, the configuration and the signature when there are any, the `options` chosen as pairs of `group_id` and `value_id`, and the `quantity`, greater than zero and with at most four decimals. THE PRICE IS NOT SENT: this body accepts no amount field and any amount that arrives is IGNORED, because the line stores the CHOICE and the server resolves the amount of every line and keeps it with the moment it was resolved. The price list is not chosen from the browser either. The buyer is optional but is given WHOLE: as soon as any of its fields travels, the minimum to serve and to notify becomes required — `buyer_name`, `buyer_email` and the shipping address (`shipping_address_line`, `shipping_city` and `shipping_country`) —, because half an identity serves neither to deliver nor to warn. The tax id is OPTIONAL, since a private individual may not have one. The consent to commercial communications does not travel here: it is a field of the ORDER, declared when it is confirmed. Neither the IP address of the shopper nor any browser tracking identifier is stored. The cart expires after the lifetime configured for the storefront, 24 hours by default, and once expired it admits no changes and cannot be confirmed.

lines.description: Lines of the cart. Optional, because a cart just opened may be empty, and capped at 50 lines. No amount is accepted inside a line: the server resolves the price of every one of them and keeps it with the moment it was resolved.

product_id.description: Public id of the article of the line, of the shop that owns the key. Required in every line.

variant_id.description: Public id of the variant chosen, when the article has variants.

presentation_id.description: Public id of the presentation chosen, when the article has presentations.

configuration_id.description: Public id of the configuration chosen, when there is one.

selection_signature.description: Fingerprint of the configuration chosen: 64 hexadecimal characters.

options.description: Option values chosen for the line, as a list of pairs of `group_id` and `value_id`: one value per group and at most 50.

items.description: Each chosen option, with its group and its value

group_id.description: Public id of the option group the choice belongs to.

value_id.description: Public id of the value chosen inside that group.

quantity.description: Units of the line: required, greater than zero, with at most four decimals and up to 9999999999.9999.

buyer_name.description: Name of the shopper, up to 255 characters. It becomes REQUIRED as soon as any other field of the buyer travels, because the identity is stored whole or not at all.

buyer_email.description: Email of the shopper, up to 191 characters. It is where the order is notified, so it becomes required as soon as any other field of the buyer travels.

buyer_phone.description: Phone of the shopper, up to 40 characters. Optional.

buyer_tax_id.description: Fiscal identification of the shopper, up to 20 characters. OPTIONAL: a private individual may not have one, and buying without it is legitimate.

shipping_address_line.description: Street and number the order is delivered to, up to 255 characters. Required as soon as any other field of the buyer travels.

shipping_city.description: Town or city of delivery, up to 120 characters. Required as soon as any other field of the buyer travels.

shipping_province.description: Province of delivery, up to 120 characters. Optional.

shipping_postal_code.description: Postal code of delivery, up to 20 characters. Optional.

shipping_country.description: Country of delivery as a two-letter code. Required as soon as any other field of the buyer travels: an address with no country can neither be delivered nor validated.

billing_address_line.description: Street and number of the billing address, up to 255 characters. The whole billing block is optional.

billing_city.description: Town or city of the billing address, up to 120 characters.

billing_province.description: Province of the billing address, up to 120 characters.

billing_postal_code.description: Postal code of the billing address, up to 20 characters.

billing_country.description: Country of the billing address as a two-letter code. It becomes required as soon as any other field of the billing block is sent.

required.description: Whether the field is required; a required field needs a non-empty default value.

default_value.description: Default value, applied to the existing tasks that have no value for the field: text, number, boolean, a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, an option or a list of options (`multiselect`).

options.description: Options of a `dropdown` (at least 1) or `multiselect` (at least 2, all different) field, up to 100.

name.description: Label name, unique within the company ignoring case (1-60 characters).

color.description: Palette key or hexadecimal `#RGB`/`#RRGGBB`.

target_task_id.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of the target task of the relation, from the same company.

target.description: Where the uploads received through the link are delivered: `comment` (default) or `description`.

note.description: Note for whoever uploads the files.

project_id.description: `id` of the project the task belongs to.

custom_fields.description: Values of the project's custom fields, as a map from the custom field public identifier (UUID v7) to its value: text, number, boolean, or a list of options for a `multiselect` field. `null` leaves the field empty.

linked_surcharge_taxes_id.description: FK to the linked equivalence-surcharge tax. UUID v7 value referencing the Factuarea catalog plus your company's own taxes.

default_for_documents.description: Sets this tax as the default per document type. Object with optional booleans: `invoice`, `quote`, `delivery_note`, `proforma`, `purchase_invoice`, `recurring_invoice`.

CreateTransportDocumentRequest.description: Create a transport control document (DeCA) in `draft`. Only `company_role` (`shipper` or `carrier`) is required: a draft admits incomplete data and the minimum data is enforced when issuing. Your own party is filled with your company data; the other one comes from `contact_id` or from the fields you send. `delivery_note_ids` (1 to 50 of your delivery notes, without repetition) pre-fills one shipment per delivery note. Every reference is a UUID of your company (`*_id`); `shipments[].loading_place_id` is not accepted in the public API. A shipment that omits `origin` gets your default loading place or, without one, your registered address (role `shipper`) or the address of the shipper contact (role `carrier`); an explicit `origin: null` leaves the shipment without origin. `shipments[].id` is optional: an identifier already in use, in this or any other company, returns 422 on `shipments.N.id`. Every UUID is normalised to lower case before validating.

CreateWarehouseLocationRequest.description: Create a location inside the warehouse in the path. `code` (required, up to 20 chars, letters, digits and hyphens, stored uppercase) is unique within its warehouse among the active locations; a duplicate is rejected with 422 naming the field, and archiving a location frees its code. `name` (required, up to 120 chars) is the human-readable label. `parent_id` (optional) is the public ID of the parent location, which must belong to the same warehouse; omit it for a top-level location. The hierarchy is one level deep: naming a parent that already has a parent is rejected with 422 as a business rule violation, not as a malformed body. The warehouse comes from the path and the location ID is assigned by the operation; neither is accepted in the body.

code.description: Short code used to label the location within its warehouse; unique among the active ones. Up to 20 characters of letters, digits and hyphens, stored uppercase, and freed for reuse when the location is archived.

name.description: Human-readable label of the location, up to 120 characters.

parent_id.description: Public ID of the parent location, which must belong to the same warehouse; omit for a top-level location. The hierarchy is ONE level deep, so naming a parent that already has a parent is rejected as a business-rule violation.

id.description: The public ID of the location is assigned by the operation and is not accepted in the body.

warehouse_id.description: The warehouse is the one in the path; sending it in the body could contradict it.

status.description: A location is born active; withdrawing it has its own operation.

CreateWarehouseLocationRequest.title: CreateWarehouseLocationRequest

CreateWarehouseRequest.description: Create a warehouse in the company master data. Required: `code`, `name`, `type` (`own`, `external`, `store` or `transit`) and the `address` object (`line1`, `city`, `province`, `postal_code`; `line2` and `country` are optional and `country` defaults to `ES`). The `code` is the integration key: up to 20 characters of letters, digits and hyphens, stored upper-cased and trimmed, and unique among the LIVE warehouses of the same company — a duplicate returns 422 pointing at `code`, never a 409 creation conflict. Two different companies may each use the same code, and archiving a warehouse frees its code for reuse. The optional `is_default` flag marks the new warehouse as the company default, unmarking the previous one in the same write.

code.description: Short code of the warehouse, up to 20 characters of letters, digits and hyphens, stored trimmed and upper-cased. It is the key an integration identifies the warehouse by: unique among the LIVE warehouses of your company, freed for reuse when the warehouse is archived, and free to repeat in a different company. A duplicate is rejected naming this field, never as a creation conflict.

name.description: Human-readable label of the warehouse, up to 120 characters.

type.description: Operational nature of the warehouse: `own` (a site of your own company), `external` (a third-party site, such as a logistics operator), `store` (a point of sale) or `transit` (goods on their way between two warehouses). It describes what the warehouse IS, and no operation derives from it: a transfer may run between any two of them.

address.description: Postal address of the warehouse, under the same keys the response publishes it with.

line2.description: Second address line: unit, floor or door. Optional.

country.description: Country as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Defaults to `ES` when omitted.

is_default.description: Marks the new warehouse as the DEFAULT one of the company, unmarking the previous one in the SAME write, so a company never has two. The default warehouse is the last step of the chain that decides which warehouse a document ships from, which is why a company with none answers the default-warehouse lookup with a rejection instead of an empty body.

CreateWarehouseRequest.title: CreateWarehouseRequest

api_version.description: Payload version (date-based, `YYYY-MM-DD`) to pin for the events delivered to this endpoint. Supported values: `2026-05-22`, `2026-10-01` and `2026-10-05`. Omitted or `null`, the endpoint is pinned at creation to the payload version that matches the effective REST version of the request: `2026-10-05` (the latest) when that version is `2026-10-01` or later (`Factuarea-Version` header, or the version pinned on the API key), and `2026-05-22` otherwise, including requests without a version header. So nobody receives the new vocabulary without opting in. With `2026-10-01` amounts are JSON numbers and the payment keys are `paid_at`/`paid_on`; with `2026-10-05` amounts are decimal strings and the payment keys are `paid_recorded_at`/`paid_date`. With `2026-05-22`, invoices keep the previous vocabulary (`status: sent` for an issued invoice, `sent_at` equal to the issuance instant). A value that is not a `YYYY-MM-DD` date returns 422 (subcode `api_version_invalid_format`), and an unsupported one 422 (subcode `api_version_unsupported`).

name.description: Weekly schedule name.

mode.description: Schedule mode: `validated` (assumed fulfilled) or `real_clocking` (computed from real clock entries).

week_pattern.description: Weekly pattern: list of days with their time ranges.

day.description: Day of the week in ISO 8601 format (1 Monday .. 7 Sunday).

ranges.description: Time ranges for the day (empty = rest day).

end.description: Range end time (HH:MM; 24:00 is allowed as end of workday).

CustomField.description: A typed custom field as an ordered `{field, value}` pair. Distinct from `metadata` (a free key→value map): use `custom_fields` for structured, display-oriented integration metadata.

value.description: Field value (≤ 500 chars).

CustomHeaders.description: Custom HTTP headers (string → string) added to every delivery request for a webhook endpoint. Max 20 entries, each value ≤ 1024 chars. Header names are normalized to Title-Case. Reserved names (`Host`, `Content-Type`, `Factuarea-Signature`, `X-Forwarded-*`, …) are rejected. Empty object when none are set. Never put secrets here — values are returned verbatim by the API.

summary.description: Safe owner counts and identifiers only. No profiles, code or Stripe IDs.

result.description: Safe owner UUID/result receipt; no profile or financial evidence.

DailyPresence.description: An office/remote presence declaration for the Control Horario (time tracking) module: an employee’s declared work location for a single day (one row per company + employee + day). Read-only over the public API — the declaration itself is made from the Factuarea app.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the presence record, a UUID v7.

employee_id.description: UUID v7 of the employee the declaration belongs to.

declared_at.description: Timestamp of the declaration (ISO 8601), or `null` when not retained.

DailyPresence.title: DailyPresence

DayBalance.description: The balance of a single day of the period for the Control Horario (time tracking) module: expected vs worked minutes, the resulting balance (worked − expected) and the day’s overtime minutes, plus the flags that explain why the expected minutes are zero (holiday, approved absence, rest day, no schedule in effect, outside the employment period). The live monthly sheet and the period balance always include `is_unscheduled` and `is_outside_employment`; the frozen daily detail of a monthly close report does not.

expected_minutes.description: Expected working minutes of the day derived from the schedule (0 on holidays, approved absences, rest days, days without a schedule in effect and days outside the employment period).

worked_minutes.description: Worked minutes of the day. Always the minutes actually clocked, also on days without a schedule in effect or outside the employment period, except under a `validated` schedule, where a scheduled day counts its expected minutes.

balance_minutes.description: Day balance in minutes (worked − expected); negative when the employee worked less than expected. 0 on days without a schedule in effect or outside the employment period (no reference to compare against).

overtime_minutes.description: Overtime minutes of the day (worked above the configured threshold, with the tolerance applied). 0 on days without a schedule in effect or outside the employment period: minutes clocked on those days never count as overtime.

is_holiday.description: Whether the day is a public holiday for the employee.

is_approved_absence.description: Whether the day is covered by an approved absence.

is_rest_day.description: Whether the day is a rest day (no shift in the schedule).

is_unscheduled.description: Whether the day falls within the employment period but no work schedule is in effect for it. Expected, balance and overtime minutes are 0; worked minutes are the minutes actually clocked. Never `true` together with `is_outside_employment`. Absent from the daily detail of a monthly close report.

is_outside_employment.description: Whether the day is before the employee’s `hire_date` or after their `termination_date`. Expected, balance and overtime minutes are 0 even if a schedule assignment covers the day; clock entries recorded before this rule existed still show as worked minutes. Absent from the daily detail of a monthly close report.

DayBalance.title: DayBalance

termination_date.description: Effective termination date, in `Y-m-d`. Defaults to today when omitted.

DeclaracionResponsable.description: The producer-level VeriFactu Declaración Responsable (SIF compliance declaration issued by the system producer, Factuarea). Global per `version`, read-only — not per-company.

id.description: UUID v7 of the declaration.

system_id.description: Identifier of the invoicing software system (SIF).

system_name.description: Name of the invoicing software system (not its code: that is `system_id`).

components.description: Components of the system (art. 15.d of Order HAC/1177/2024). An empty string in declarations that predate the full art. 15 content.
components.example: Aplicación web de facturación y su API REST pública; servicio de remisión de registros a la AEAT.
examples: Aplicación web de facturación y su API REST pública; servicio de remisión de registros a la AEAT.

producer_tax_id.description: Tax ID (NIF) of the SIF producer.

producer_address.description: Postal address of the SIF producer (art. 15.j). An empty string in declarations that predate the full art. 15 content.

verifactu_only.description: Whether the system can ONLY operate as VERI*FACTU (art. 15.e, `TipoUsoPosibleSoloVerifactu`). It declares a possibility of the system, not the mode of a company.

multi_ot.description: Whether the system can serve several obliged taxpayers (art. 15.f, `TipoUsoPosibleMultiOT`). It declares a possibility of the system; the per-customer `IndicadorMultiplesOT` reported on each record is computed separately and is not part of art. 15.

signature_types.description: Signature types the system uses when it also works outside VERI*FACTU (art. 15.g). `null` when the system only works as VERI*FACTU and in declarations that predate the full art. 15 content.
signature_types.example: XAdES Enveloped Signature, clase EPES (ETSI EN 319 132), con la política de firma de la Administración General del Estado (OID 2.16.724.1.3.1.1.2.1.9), huella SHA-256 de las referencias y del certificado firmante, algoritmo de firma RSA-SHA256 y canonicalización XML 1.0, generada con la clave privada de un certificado electrónico en vigor.

signing_place.description: Place where the declaration is signed.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of the declaration content for integrity verification (the full content is not exposed).
