PublicLink.description: Represents the state of the shareable public link of a document (quote/invoice/proforma/delivery_note). `url` is the absolute URL ready to send to the client; `enabled` indicates whether it is active; `expires_at` the deadline (`null` = unlimited); `max_days` the maximum allowed when extending it.

url.description: Absolute URL of the public link to share with the client.

id.description: UUID v7 of the document the link points to.

enabled.description: Indicates whether the public link is currently active.

expires_at.description: Expiration date/time of the link, or `null` if it does not expire.

max_days.description: Maximum number of days allowed when extending the link validity (business limit).

PublicLink.title: PublicLink

PurchaseInvoice.description: An invoice received from a supplier.

external_invoice_number.description: The number assigned by the supplier on their invoice. `null` for a simplified expense ticket (`is_simplified`) with no supplier number.

is_simplified.description: Whether this is a simplified supplier invoice (expense ticket). When `true`, `supplier` and `external_invoice_number` may be `null`.

external_id.description: External integration key (ERP/CRM/e-commerce) mapping this document to a record in a third-party system. Free-format, unique per company, filterable via `?external_id=`. `null` when not set. Persistent synchronization key, independent of the request-level `Idempotency-Key`.

internal_code.description: Optional internal code assigned by the company for its own classification.

received_on.description: Reception date of the invoice, or `null`.

taxes_total.description: VAT BORNE (IVA soportado) of this expense, WITHOUT surcharge and WITHOUT withholding. Careful: on the sales-side documents (invoice, delivery note, quote, proforma) the SAME field name carries the NET aggregate `total_vat + total_surcharge − total_retention` instead. Header invariant here: `total === subtotal + taxes_total + total_surcharge − total_retention`. Read `total_vat` for a VAT figure whose meaning does not depend on the document family.

total_vat.description: Same VAT amount as `taxes_total`, published under the name the concept carries in the other four document families, so that the explicit identity `total === subtotal + total_vat + total_surcharge − total_retention` holds across all five without knowing which resource produced the body.

total_retention.description: Aggregated IRPF withholding of the lines (Σ retention_amount). Header invariant: `total === subtotal + taxes_total + total_surcharge − total_retention`.

total_surcharge.description: Aggregated equivalence surcharge of the lines (Σ surcharge_amount). It adds to the total exactly like VAT does, so it is part of the header invariant above.

total.description: Total of the expense. Two equivalent ways to reconstruct it from the published amounts, and only these two: the EXPLICIT one, identical in the five document families - `total = subtotal + total_vat + total_surcharge - total_retention` - or the one specific to this family, where `taxes_total` is the VAT alone - `total = subtotal + taxes_total + total_surcharge - total_retention`. Note that the aggregate shortcut of the sales-side families (`subtotal + taxes_total`) does NOT apply here: the same field name carries a different meaning on each side.

paid_amount.description: Amount already paid against this expense (derived from the payment ledger). Satisfies the invariant `paid_amount + pending_amount === total`.

pending_amount.description: Outstanding balance pending payment for this expense (derived from the payment ledger).

payment_status.description: Derived payment status, NOT a persisted domain state (the model keeps 4 statuses). `overdue` derives from `pending` + `due_date < today` and prevails in presentation.

paid_recorded_at.description: Instant (ISO 8601 with offset) at which the payment that settled the purchase invoice was RECORDED in the ledger. `null` while it is not paid. Not the declared date: see `paid_date`.

paid_date.description: Declared payment date (YYYY-MM-DD). `null` while the purchase invoice is not paid. The input field of `mark-paid` and `payments` keeps the name `paid_on`.

payment_terms_days.description: Payment term days agreed with the supplier, or `null`.

bank_account.description: Supplier bank account. Always `null` in this version (accounts live embedded as JSON in `suppliers` without a stable identity). Follow-up `bridge-bank-account-cross-bc-supplier` will expose it as an object once Supplier promotes a read port.

expense_category_id.description: UUID v7 of the associated expense category, or `null`.

deductible_percentage.description: Deductible percentage of the input VAT (0–100), or `null` when not set.

operation_class.description: Operation class for the input VAT of Modelo 303. Defaults to `corriente`. `isp` (domestic reverse charge, Art. 84.Uno.2 LIVA) and `intracomunitaria` are self-assessed: the buyer declares both the output VAT and the deductible input VAT.

exclude_347.description: Declarative per-document flag: whether this expense is excluded from the annual Modelo 347 report.

is_reverse_charge.description: Indicates whether the invoice is subject to reverse charge.

tags.description: Free classification tags (lowercase slugs `[a-z0-9-]`, ≤ 40 chars each, ≤ 30 tags). Filterable via `?tags[in]=tag1,tag2` (JSON_CONTAINS, OR semantics). Empty `[]` when there are none.

custom_fields.description: Ordered list of typed custom fields `[{field, value}]` (≤ 50). Distinct from `metadata` (a free key→value map): use `custom_fields` for structured, display-oriented integration metadata. Empty `[]` when there are none.

internal_notes.description: Internal notes not visible to the supplier, or `null`.
internal_notes.example: Revisar con contabilidad antes del cierre trimestral.
examples: Revisar con contabilidad antes del cierre trimestral.

PurchaseInvoice.title: PurchaseInvoice

PurchaseInvoiceAttachment.description: File attached to the expense (PDF or image). `null` when there is no attachment.

filename.description: Original name of the uploaded file.

download_url.description: Relative download URL of the attachment (`/v1/companies/{company}/purchase-invoices/{purchase_invoice}/file`).

PurchaseInvoiceAttachment.title: PurchaseInvoiceAttachment

PurchaseInvoiceLine.description: A line item on an expense.

source_line_index.description: Zero-based ordinal of the line within this expense, in the stable read order. Send it back on create/update to keep a line matched to its historical counterpart (measures, units and frozen cost are preserved when the physical selection and the supplier do not change). It is NOT a primary key and it grants no access to any other document.

additional_description.description: Optional secondary description rendered below the line concept on document PDFs.

quantity.description: Billed quantity. A measured purchase line (one carrying `purchase_measurement`) returns it as a 4-decimal STRING so no precision is lost; a legacy line keeps the numeric type it has always published.

unit_price.description: Cost per billed unit, always a decimal STRING with the 4-decimal scale of its column (e.g. `"7.4000"`, `"100.0000"`), on measured (carrying `purchase_measurement`), legacy and manual lines alike: it is returned exactly as it was accepted and stored, so reading a line and sending it back never changes its cost. Derived amounts keep 2 decimals.

discount_percent.description: Discount percentage applied to the line (0-100) BEFORE any tax. `subtotal` is already net of it, so `unit_price` multiplied by `quantity` does NOT equal `subtotal` on a discounted line. Default 0.

confirmed_base_quantity.description: Real measured quantity in the base unit, as a decimal string, for a variable-measure presentation (weighed goods). `null` when the line does not require one. It is reconstructed from the stored base quantity, never recomputed against the live catalog.

purchase_measurement.description: Measured-purchase block. `null` on a legacy or manual line, which keeps its previous `quantity` × `unit_price` semantics. On write only `package_quantity` and `cost_basis` are accepted; the remaining fields are DERIVED by the server and are never taken from the client.

package_quantity.description: Physical number of packages/presentations received, as a decimal string (e.g. `"3.0000"` boxes). `null` when the purchase is not counted in packages — it means neither one nor zero.

billing_quantity.description: Derived. Billed quantity expressed in `billing_unit_code` (e.g. `"6.0000"` kg for three 2 kg boxes).

billing_unit_code.description: Derived. UN/ECE code of the unit the cost applies to (`KGM`, `LTR`, `C62`, …).

billing_conversion_factor.description: Derived. Factor, at scale 6, between the billing unit and the base unit of the product.

unit_cost.description: Derived. Cost per billing unit, as a decimal string (e.g. `"7.4000"` per kg). A confirmed `"0.0000"` is a free line, not an unknown cost.

cost_basis.description: Which unit the cost is quoted in: the supplier offer unit (requires an applicable offer), the product base unit (factor 1, manual cost) or a fixed presentation (manual cost per presentation).

retention_rate.description: IRPF withholding percentage applied to the supplier (0–100). Default 0.

surcharge_rate.description: Equivalence surcharge (recargo de equivalencia) percentage paid to the retail supplier (0–100). Default 0. Only the legal VAT-surcharge pairs are accepted (21→5.2, 10→1.4, 4→0.5).

retention_amount.description: Withholding amount of the line (`subtotal * retention_rate / 100`). The line total follows `subtotal + taxes − retention_amount + surcharge_amount`.

surcharge_amount.description: Equivalence surcharge amount of the line (`subtotal * surcharge_rate / 100`). Default 0.

vat_deductible.description: Whether the line VAT is deductible. It does not change the amount paid, but a `false` line is excluded from the deductible input VAT of Modelo 303 (boxes [28]-[37]).

exemption_reason.description: LIVA exemption cause (E1–E6) or non-subjection cause (N1/N2) declared for this line, or null when the line does not declare one.

indirect_tax_regime.description: Indirect tax regime override of the supplier line: `iva`/`igic`/`ipsi` when set per-document (precedence override>zone), otherwise `null`. Writable on create/update; the document must be homogeneous (a single non-null regime across all lines, 422 otherwise).

configuration.description: Commercial combination frozen on the line, or `null` when the line was not sold or bought through one (legacy product, manual line).

options.description: Configurable options frozen on the line, in printing order. Always an array, `[]` included.

price_adjustment.description: Adjustment of the chosen value per commercial unit. `null` means the value does not change the price — NOT the same as adjusting by `0`.

applied.description: Whether that amount was actually ADDED to the unit price. `false` when an exact price (price-list entry, combination price or a manually typed unit price) already absorbed it.

price_semantics.description: Monetary semantics of the frozen price: `per_base_unit` (converted once by the presentation factor) or `per_commercial_unit` (never converted). `null` when the line carries no catalog price context.

price_adjustment_total.description: Sum of the adjustments of the chosen option values, as a decimal string.

option_adjustments_absorbed.description: TRI-STATE, and `null` is NOT `false`. `true`: the frozen price already includes the option adjustments. `false`: they were added on top. `null`: it could not be determined.

PurchaseInvoiceLine.title: PurchaseInvoiceLine

PurchaseInvoiceMatch.description: The three-way match of a supplier invoice, read from the INVOICE: the resulting status, the purchase order it is linked to, and line by line what was ordered, what was received and what is being invoiced, with the typed reason of every deviation and the figure that justifies it. It is what the three match write operations return, so the integrator sees the resulting state without a second call.

match_status.description: Match status of the invoice: `not_applicable` when it is not linked to any order, `pending` while it has not been evaluated, `matched` when everything adds up, `deviation` when it does not, and `rejected` when the deviation was rejected. Accepting a deviation resolves it to `matched`, and that leaves the ORDER invoiced — a terminal status no operation of this API reopens.

purchase_order_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the linked purchase order, or `null` when the invoice is not linked to one.

purchase_order_number.description: Number of that order, or `null` when there is none.

has_deviation.description: Whether any line carries a deviation reason. It is the question the decision hangs on, published as a boolean so a client does not have to walk the lines to ask it.

lines.description: One entry per matched line, with the three quantities in BASE units, the two costs per base unit, and the deviation reasons of that line. A line with no reason is a line that adds up.

deviations.label: Cantidad facturada por encima de la recibida
Precio facturado por encima de lo pactado
Cantidad facturada por encima de la recibida
Precio facturado por encima de lo pactado

excluded_line_count.description: How many lines of the invoice were left OUT of the match because they carry no catalog identity (shipping, a free-text concept). They are not deviations and they are not invented a counterpart: they are declared here so that a total that does not add up has a visible explanation instead of a silent one.

PurchaseInvoiceMatch.title: PurchaseInvoiceMatch

PurchaseInvoiceMatchDeviation.description: ONE reason why a line does not match, with the figure that justifies it. The classification alone is not actionable — "there is a price deviation" can neither be accepted nor argued — so every reason always carries the three magnitudes: the expected one, the invoiced one and the signed difference between them. Tolerance is applied BEFORE classifying, so a reason with a zero difference never travels.

reason.description: Typed reason. Four compare a line against its counterpart on the order (`price_*` against the agreed cost per base unit, `quantity_*` against what was actually received); the other two exist because a line may have NO counterpart, which is a deviation just as real: `line_not_ordered` (the invoice brings an item the order does not contain) and `line_not_invoiced` (the order has a received line the invoice does not cover).

expected.description: Expected magnitude — what was agreed with the supplier or what actually arrived at the warehouse, depending on the reason — as a decimal string. Quantities carry four decimal places and costs per base unit six: the scale is chosen by the FAMILY of the reason, so both sides of a comparison always share it.

invoiced.description: Magnitude the supplier is claiming, as a decimal string with the same scale as `expected`.

difference.description: Signed difference, always `invoiced - expected`: POSITIVE on the `*_above` reasons and on `line_not_ordered`, NEGATIVE on the `*_below` ones and on `line_not_invoiced`. Never zero.

PurchaseInvoiceMatchDeviation.title: PurchaseInvoiceMatchDeviation

PurchaseInvoiceMatchLine.description: One line of the supplier invoice seen from the three-way match, against its counterpart on the order. Quantities are in BASE units with four decimal places and costs per base unit with six, which is what lets buying in boxes of twelve and invoicing in units NOT read as a price deviation.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the catalog item of the line.

product_variant_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the variant, or `null` when the item has none.

base_unit_code.description: Code of the BASE unit every quantity of this entry is expressed in.

ordered_base_quantity.description: Quantity ordered, in base units, as a decimal string with FOUR decimal places.

received_base_quantity.description: Quantity received in POSTED goods receipts, in base units, with the same scale. It is what the invoiced quantity is compared against: what is invoiced is what arrived, and comparing against what was ordered would flag every legitimate partial delivery.

invoiced_base_quantity.description: Quantity the supplier is invoicing, in base units, with the same scale.

agreed_cost_per_base_unit.description: Cost of one BASE unit agreed on the order (`unit_cost / conversion_factor`), as a decimal string with SIX decimal places.

invoiced_cost_per_base_unit.description: Cost of one BASE unit the supplier is invoicing, with the same six-decimal scale.

deviations.description: Typed reasons why this line does not add up, each with its figures. Empty when the line matches within tolerance.

PurchaseInvoiceMatchLine.title: PurchaseInvoiceMatchLine

PurchaseInvoicePayment.description: A single payment recorded against a purchase invoice (payment ledger entry). Listed by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/purchase-invoices/{purchase_invoice}/payments` and returned by `POST` on the same path.

id.description: Opaque UUID v7 of the payment.

object.description: String identifying the object type. Always `purchase_invoice_payment`.

amount.description: Payment amount as a string with two decimal places (Stripe-style).

paid_date.description: Payment date (YYYY-MM-DD). Renamed from `paid_on`, which is no longer emitted; the INPUT field of `POST` keeps the old name on purpose.

payment_method.description: Payment method (backing value of the Shared enum `PaymentMethod`, e.g. `bank_transfer`).

bank_account_id.description: Internal bank account the payment was settled into, or `null`.

reference.description: Payment reference/operation number. `null` if not provided.

notes.description: Internal notes for the payment. `null` if not provided.

is_reversed.description: Whether the payment has been reverted. A reverted payment stays in the ledger but stops counting towards `paid_amount`/`pending_amount` — read this flag, do not infer the state from absence.

reversed_at.description: When the payment was reverted (ISO 8601), or `null` while it is in force.

reversal_reason.description: Reason the payment was reverted, from the closed catalog. `null` while the payment is in force.

reversal_reason_text.description: Human-readable label of the reversal reason (Spanish), or `null`.

reversal_note.description: Free-text remark recorded with the reversal, or `null`.

PurchaseInvoicePayment.title: PurchaseInvoicePayment

PurchaseInvoiceStats.description: Aggregated metrics (KPIs) of the expenses of the authenticated company: total, count by status and accumulated amounts. `overdue` is a derived condition (`pending` + past due date), not a persisted status.

by_status.description: Invoice count by status (key = status, value = number of invoices). Keys: `draft`, `pending`, `paid`, `cancelled` (persisted statuses) plus `overdue` (derived KPI: overdue subset of `pending`).

overdue.description: Number of overdue and unpaid invoices (subset of `pending` with a past due date).

total_amount.description: Total aggregate amount of all expenses.

PurchaseInvoiceStats.title: PurchaseInvoiceStats

PurchaseOrder.description: A purchase order: the commitment to buy goods from a supplier, and the document the goods receipts and the supplier invoices that fulfil it are matched against. It is NOT a fiscal document, but unlike a sales order it takes its number when it is CREATED, so `number` is always present — even on a draft. Amounts are decimal strings with two decimal places; line quantities are decimal strings with four.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the purchase order, a UUID v7. Every reference of this document travels the same way: no internal numeric key is ever published.

number.description: Number of the order (`PC-YYYY-N`), stamped inside the transaction that CREATES it. It is never `null`, not even while the order is a draft: this family numbers on creation, unlike the sales order, which numbers on confirmation. The sequence guarantees uniqueness and not density, so a creation that rolls back leaves a permanent gap.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the order: `draft` (editable), `sent` (issued to the supplier), `confirmed` (accepted by the supplier), `partially_received` and `received` (goods arrived in part or in full), `billed` (the supplier invoice matched it) and `cancelled`. The two reception states are DERIVED from posting a goods receipt and are not destinations you can ask for, and `billed` is stamped by the three-way match from the supplier invoice. Both `billed` and `cancelled` are terminal and no operation reopens them.

status_label.description: Label of the status in Spanish, ready to display.

supplier_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the commercial contact acting as the supplier of this order.

supplier_name.description: Name of the supplier as it was recorded on the order.

supplier_order_reference.description: Reference the SUPPLIER uses for this order, or `null` when none was given. It is OPTIONAL and UNIQUE per company: creating a second order with a reference that already exists is REJECTED with `409`, it does not update the first one. Two orders without a reference coexist, because two `NULL` values do not collide in a unique index.

warehouse_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the warehouse the goods are expected at, or `null` when the order is not tied to one. Each line may override it.

warehouse_name.description: Name of that warehouse, or `null` when there is none.

order_date.description: Date of the order, as a plain calendar date.

expected_date.description: Date the goods are expected to arrive, as a plain calendar date, or `null` when none was agreed.

notes.description: Free-text notes of the order, or `null` when there are none.
notes.example: Entrega en muelle 2; avisar 24 h antes por teléfono.
examples: Entrega en muelle 2; avisar 24 h antes por teléfono.

subtotal.description: Amount of the order before taxes, as a decimal string with two decimal places.

tax_amount.description: Input VAT (IVA soportado) of the order: sum of the VAT of its lines.

retention_amount.description: Withholding (retencion de IRPF) of the order: sum of the withholding of its lines, as a POSITIVE amount that SUBTRACTS from the total.

surcharge_amount.description: Equivalence surcharge (recargo de equivalencia) of the order: sum of the surcharge of its lines. It ADDS to the total exactly like VAT does.

total.description: Total of the order, reconstructed with the identity shared by every document family: `total = subtotal + tax_amount + surcharge_amount - retention_amount`.

fully_received.description: Whether every line has already received the whole quantity that was ordered. It is DERIVED from the posted goods receipts: no operation writes it.

lines.description: Lines of the order, each with the quantity in its PURCHASE unit, the conversion factor to the base unit, the received and pending quantities derived from the posted receipts, and the ledger of the receipts that consumed it.

receipts.description: Goods receipts registered against this order, including the cancelled ones: what an order received is history and a cancelled receipt is part of it. Empty while nothing has arrived.

updated_at.description: When the order was last modified (ISO 8601).

PurchaseOrder.title: PurchaseOrder

PurchaseOrderEmailDelivery.description: Acknowledgement that the purchase order was accepted and queued for delivery to the supplier by email.

purchase_order_id.description: Opaque identifier of the purchase order that was queued for sending, a UUID v7. It is also the key with which the delivery is located afterwards on the email deliveries surface.

status.description: Always `queued`: the acknowledgement states that the email was accepted and queued, never that it was delivered. Delivery is observed afterwards through the email deliveries surface.

PurchaseOrderEmailDelivery.title: PurchaseOrderEmailDelivery

PurchaseOrderLine.description: A line of a purchase order. It is the only line of the API that carries TWO units at once: the PURCHASE unit that was agreed with the supplier (a box, a pallet) and the BASE unit of the catalog item, joined by the conversion factor frozen on the line. Everything that later enters the warehouse is measured in the base unit, and everything the supplier invoices is measured in the purchase unit, so both travel side by side instead of being recomputed on each screen.

id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the line. The line sub-resource edits and deletes it by this identifier, and a goods receipt names the lines it receives with it.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the catalog item bought on this line. A purchase order line always names a catalog item: free-text lines do not exist in this family, because what arrives at the warehouse has to be something the warehouse knows.

product_variant_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the variant, or `null` when the item has none.

description.description: Concept of the line, frozen when the line was added.

supplier_sku.description: Code the SUPPLIER uses for this item, copied from its offer, or `null` when the offer declares none. It is what lets the supplier read the order without translating the catalog.

purchase_unit_code.description: Code of the unit the item is BOUGHT in (the one of the supplier offer): the unit `quantity` is expressed in.

conversion_factor.description: How many BASE units one purchase unit holds, as a decimal string with SIX decimal places. It is FROZEN on the line when the line is added: a later change of the supplier offer does not move what was already agreed, which is what makes the receipt of an old order convert with the factor that was pacted and not with the current one.

quantity.description: Quantity ordered, in the PURCHASE unit, as a decimal string with FOUR decimal places. Quantities travel as strings and not as numbers because they are the figures a partial receipt and the three-way match use to decide what is left, and a binary float turns that arithmetic into a line nobody can close.

base_quantity.description: The same quantity expressed in the BASE unit of the item (`quantity * conversion_factor`), with the same four-decimal scale.

received_quantity.description: Quantity already received, accumulated, in the PURCHASE unit, with the same four-decimal scale. No public operation writes it: it moves when a goods receipt is POSTED, and a cancelled receipt does not count.

pending_quantity.description: Quantity still to receive, DERIVED as `quantity - received_quantity` with a floor of zero, in the PURCHASE unit. It is the figure a new receipt is checked against: no receipt may exceed it.

received_base_quantity.description: The received quantity expressed in the BASE unit, with the same four-decimal scale. It is the figure the warehouse ledger moves and the one the three-way match compares against the invoice.

pending_base_quantity.description: The pending quantity expressed in the BASE unit, with the same four-decimal scale.

unit_cost.description: Cost agreed for ONE purchase unit, as a decimal string with FOUR decimal places — not two. Its column is `decimal(14,4)` and it is the figure margins are computed from, so it is published with the scale it is stored in; truncating it to two decimals would change the published cost. It is copied from the supplier offer when the line is added.

tax_rate.description: VAT percentage applied to the line (0-100). A percentage is not money, so it travels as a number.

retention_rate.description: IRPF withholding percentage applied to the line (0-100). Its amount subtracts from the total.

surcharge_rate.description: Equivalence surcharge percentage applied to the line (0-100). Its amount adds to the total.

subtotal.description: Amount of the line before taxes, as a decimal string with two decimal places.

retention_amount.description: Withholding amount of the line, as a POSITIVE amount that subtracts from the line total.

surcharge_amount.description: Equivalence surcharge amount of the line.

total.description: Total of the line: `subtotal + tax_amount + surcharge_amount - retention_amount`.

warehouse_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the warehouse this line is expected at; it inherits the one of the order when it is not set.

receipts.description: Ledger of the POSTED goods receipts that took quantity away from this line. The accumulated figures above are a number; this is the list of receipts behind them, so `received 7 of 10` stops being a figure without an author. It is populated by the line sub-resource (`GET .../purchase-orders/{purchase_order}/lines`), which is the operation that exists to answer that question, and arrives EMPTY on the order detail: resolving it costs one extra query per order and only the operation that needs it pays for it.

PurchaseOrderLine.title: PurchaseOrderLine

PurchaseOrderLineReceipt.description: One reception of a purchase order line: the goods receipt that took a quantity away from it, and how much. Only POSTED receipts appear here — a cancelled one gave the quantity back and counting it would say the goods are in the warehouse when they are not. The sum of these quantities matches EXACTLY the `received_quantity` of the line.

goods_receipt_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the goods receipt that took the quantity, so the line can be reconciled against it.

goods_receipt_number.description: Number of that goods receipt, so the reconciliation does not need a second call to become readable.

received_on.description: Date the goods were received, as a plain calendar date.

quantity.description: Quantity of this reception in the PURCHASE unit of the line, as a decimal string with FOUR decimal places.

base_quantity.description: The same quantity in the BASE unit of the item, converted with the factor FROZEN on the line, with the same four-decimal scale.

PurchaseOrderLineReceipt.title: PurchaseOrderLineReceipt

PurchaseOrderMatch.description: The three-way match of a purchase order, read from the ORDER: what was ordered, what was actually received and what the supplier has invoiced, line by line, plus the supplier invoices linked to it. Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/purchase-orders/{purchase_order}/match`. An order with no linked invoice is not an error: it answers `not_applicable` with an empty list of invoices. The line-by-line DETAIL of a deviation lives on the surface anchored to the INVOICE, which is where it is resolved.

purchase_order_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the order this match belongs to.

match_status.description: Match status of the SET of linked invoices: `not_applicable` when there is none, `deviation` as soon as ONE of them deviates (a deviation is not compensated by an invoice that adds up), the shared status when all of them agree, and `pending` on any other mix — the match of the order is not settled while one of its invoices is not.

has_deviation.description: Whether the set is in deviation. It is `match_status === "deviation"` seen as a boolean, published so a client does not have to compare tokens to decide whether to raise an alert.

lines.description: One entry per line of the ORDER, with the three quantities that describe the match. Always in the BASE unit of the item: ordering in boxes of twelve and invoicing in units must not read as a deviation.

invoices.description: Supplier invoices linked to this order. Empty when none has been linked yet.

PurchaseOrderMatch.title: PurchaseOrderMatch

PurchaseOrderMatchInvoice.description: A supplier invoice linked to the purchase order, with its own match status: the order-level status is derived from these, so they are published rather than summarised away.

purchase_invoice_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the supplier invoice.

number.description: Number of the supplier invoice.

match_status.description: Match status of THIS invoice against the order.

total.description: Total of the supplier invoice, as a decimal string with two decimal places.

PurchaseOrderMatchInvoice.title: PurchaseOrderMatchInvoice

PurchaseOrderMatchLine.description: One line of the order seen from the three-way match: how much was ordered, how much actually arrived and how much the supplier has invoiced. The three quantities are in the BASE unit of the item and share the same four-decimal scale, so they can be subtracted from one another without converting anything.

purchase_order_line_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the order line this entry reports on.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the catalog item of the line.

product_variant_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the variant, or `null` when the item has none.

description.description: Concept of the line, as it was frozen on the order.

base_unit_code.description: Code of the BASE unit the three quantities are expressed in.

ordered_base_quantity.description: Quantity ordered, in the base unit, as a decimal string with FOUR decimal places.

received_base_quantity.description: Quantity received in POSTED goods receipts, in the base unit, with the same scale. A cancelled receipt does not count.

invoiced_base_quantity.description: Quantity invoiced by the linked supplier invoices, in the base unit, with the same scale. Zero while nothing has been invoiced.

PurchaseOrderMatchLine.title: PurchaseOrderMatchLine

PurchaseOrderStats.description: Aggregated headline figures of the purchase orders of the authenticated company. Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/purchase-orders/stats`, wrapped in `{ "data": PurchaseOrderStats }`.

total_count.description: Number of purchase orders of the company. It is a COUNT, not money: it does not travel with the two decimals of an amount, unlike `total_amount` of this very object.

count_by_status.description: Number of orders per status, keyed by the token of the closed catalog. It carries one entry per status INCLUDING the ones at zero, so a client never has to tell `zero` apart from `did not come`.

total_amount.description: Accumulated total of every purchase order of the company, as a decimal string with two decimal places.

pending_to_receive_amount.description: Amount already committed to suppliers whose goods have not arrived in full: orders from `sent` onwards that are not fully received. A draft does not count, because it commits nothing.

pending_to_bill_amount.description: Amount of goods already received that the supplier has not invoiced yet. It is the other half of the picture: what is owed but not yet claimed.

PurchaseOrderStats.title: PurchaseOrderStats

PurchaseOrderStatusItem.description: A purchase order status from the closed catalog, with its label, its colour and what it allows. Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/purchase-orders/statuses` as a flat list. The three permissions are the contract that spares the integrator a round of trial and error: they say, BEFORE trying, which statuses admit editing the order or deleting it.

value.description: Status token. It is the identity of the status: a token of a closed catalog, not a row of any table.

label.description: Label of the status in Spanish, ready to display.

color.description: Suggested colour token for rendering the status.

can_edit.description: Whether the status admits editing the contents of the order. Only a draft does.

can_delete.description: Whether the status admits deleting the order. Only a draft does: an order already sent to the supplier is cancelled, not deleted, so the trace survives.

can_convert.description: Whether the status admits converting the order into another document. It is `false` in every status today, and that is the answer of the domain and not a gap: what closes a purchase order is the three-way match against the supplier invoice, which is not a conversion. The field is published anyway so the catalog has one single shape across the six document families.

PurchaseOrderStatusItem.title: PurchaseOrderStatusItem

issue_count.description: Number of issues still pending review: one per field, supplier identity counted once, 0 before the first extraction.

deferred_until.description: When set, the scan is waiting for the company daily OCR quota to reset; it will be retried automatically.

attempts.description: The 50 most recent processing attempts, newest first. `attempts_total` holds how many there are in all.

attempts_total.description: Total number of processing attempts, including those not listed in `attempts`.

audit.description: The 50 most recent audit events, newest first. `audit_total` holds how many there are in all.

audit_total.description: Total number of audit events, including those not listed in `audit`.

source_retained.description: Whether the original file is still retained. It does not depend on the API key permissions: `download_source` can be missing from `available_actions` while this is true.

operation_classes.description: Accepted values of the `operation_class` review field.

rejection_code.description: Business rule that stopped the automatic conversion and sent the scan back to review, or null.

options.description: Chosen option values, at most one per option group.

package_quantity.description: Decimal string greater than zero when provided.

confirmed_base_quantity.description: Decimal string greater than zero when provided.

PurchaseScanCatalogSelection.description: Catalog selection made by a person during review, never by OCR. In the review request, omit it to keep the current selection and send null to unlink the line. Company ownership is verified when the review is saved; the combination is resolved when the scan is converted.
PurchaseScanCatalogSelection.title: PurchaseScanCatalogSelection

result.description: pending while the attachments are still being ingested; parked when the sender is not allowlisted or fails SPF/DKIM/DMARC authentication (no scan is created).

reason.description: Why the email was parked, rejected or failed; null for any other result.

sender_authentication.description: SPF/DKIM/DMARC verdict computed by the receiving server, or null when it was never evaluated.

issue_count.description: Number of issues still pending review: one per field, supplier identity counted once, 0 before the first extraction.

deferred_until.description: When set, the scan is waiting for the company daily OCR quota to reset; it will be retried automatically.

by_supplier.description: Suppliers with at least one linked scan in scope, ordered by count desc then name asc, capped at 100.

QuarterlyDownloadV1Request.description:
Public REST API v1 — POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/quarterly/download-zip
and POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/quarterly/send-email (shared fields).

The canonical recipient field is `email`. We accept
`to_email` as a deprecated alias for compatibility with older clients.
QuarterlyDownloadV1Request.title: QuarterlyDownloadV1Request

Quote.description: A sales quote that can be converted to an invoice.

status.description: Quote lifecycle status (draft, sent, accepted, rejected, expired, converted, cancelled).

price_list_id.description: UUID of the price list selected for this document.

price_list_name.description: Price-list name snapshot frozen on the document.

converted_to_id.description: UUID v7 of the invoice this quote was converted into, if any.

converted_invoice_number.description: Human-readable number of the invoice this quote was converted into (e.g. "F-2026-00042"). null if not converted.

taxes_total.description: NET aggregate of the header taxes: `total_vat + total_surcharge − total_retention`. It is the amount that, added to `subtotal`, yields `total` (`total === subtotal + taxes_total`), so it must NOT be combined with `total_retention`: subtracting the withholding again on top of the aggregate produces a false total (4,320.00 + 259.20 − 648.00 = 3,931.20 against a real total of 4,579.20). It is NOT the VAT figure of the Spanish Modelo 303 — read `total_vat` for that. Beware that on an expense the same field name carries a DIFFERENT meaning (VAT only), which is why the identity that holds across all five document families is the explicit one: `total === subtotal + total_vat + total_surcharge − total_retention`.

total_vat.description: Sum of VAT (IVA) across all lines.

total_retention.description: Sum of withholding (IRPF/retention) across all lines.

total_surcharge.description: Sum of equivalence surcharge (recargo de equivalencia) across all lines.

total.description: Total of the document. Two equivalent ways to reconstruct it from the published amounts, and only these two: the EXPLICIT one, identical in the five document families - `total = subtotal + total_vat + total_surcharge - total_retention` - or the AGGREGATE one, specific to the sales-side families - `total = subtotal + taxes_total`. NEVER reconstruct it as `subtotal + taxes_total - total_retention`: `taxes_total` ALREADY has the withholding netted out, so that combination subtracts it twice and yields a false total (4,320.00 + 259.20 - 648.00 = 3,931.20 against a real 4,579.20).

terms.description: Free-text terms and conditions rendered on the quote PDF.
terms.example: Presupuesto valido durante 30 dias desde la fecha de emision.
examples: Presupuesto valido durante 30 dias desde la fecha de emision.

reference.description: Origin number of the document (e.g. the number it had in a previous system when imported). `null` if not set.

operation_regime.description: VAT operation regime of the quote (`general`, `intracomunitaria`, `importacion_exportacion`, `isp`).

external_id.description: External integration key (ERP/CRM/e-commerce) mapping this document to a record in a third-party system. Free-format, unique per company, filterable via `?external_id=`. `null` when not set. Persistent synchronization key, independent of the request-level `Idempotency-Key`.

tags.description: Free classification tags (lowercase slugs `[a-z0-9-]`, ≤ 40 chars each, ≤ 30 tags). Filterable via `?tags[in]=tag1,tag2` (JSON_CONTAINS, OR semantics). Empty `[]` when there are none.

custom_fields.description: Ordered list of typed custom fields `[{field, value}]` (≤ 50). Distinct from `metadata` (a free key→value map): use `custom_fields` for structured, display-oriented integration metadata. Empty `[]` when there are none.

link_expires_at.description: Expiry date of the public share link, or null if unlimited.

link_is_active.description: Whether the public share link is currently active.

Quote.title: Quote

QuoteLine.description: A line item on a quote.

additional_description.description: Optional secondary description rendered below the line concept on document PDFs.
additional_description.example: Auditoría inicial e informe de mejoras

unit_price.description: Unit price as a decimal STRING with the 4-decimal scale of its column (e.g. `"0.0125"`, `"100.0000"`): it is returned exactly as it was accepted and stored, so reading a line and sending it back never changes its price. Derived amounts (`subtotal`, `taxes`, `total`) keep 2 decimals.

retention_rate.description: IRPF withholding percentage applied to the line (0–100). Default 0. Its amount is already aggregated into `taxes`.

surcharge_rate.description: Equivalence surcharge (recargo de equivalencia) percentage applied to the line (0–100). Default 0. Its amount is already aggregated into `taxes`.

indirect_tax_regime.description: Indirect tax regime of the line: the per-document override (`iva`/`igic`/`ipsi`) when the user set it (precedence override>zone), otherwise `null` (derived from the establishment AEAT zone). Writable per-document input on create/update; the document must be homogeneous (a single non-null regime across all lines, 422 otherwise).

counted_quantity.description: Pieces the customer asked for on a variable-weight line sold by count (decimal string, scale 4, greater than 0), e.g. `"4.0000"` for four pieces weighing `quantity` kg in total. Informational: the line is charged and the stock is discounted by `quantity` (the real weight), never by the pieces. `null` on any other line. Only accepted on a `variable_measure` presentation whose unit is a count unit.

counted_unit.description: UN/ECE code of the count unit of `counted_quantity` (`H87` piece, `XPK` pack…). `null` exactly when `counted_quantity` is `null`.

configuration.description: Commercial combination frozen on the line, or `null` when the line was not sold or bought through one (legacy product, manual line).

options.description: Configurable options frozen on the line, in printing order. Always an array, `[]` included.

price_adjustment.description: Adjustment of the chosen value per commercial unit. `null` means the value does not change the price — NOT the same as adjusting by `0`.

applied.description: Whether that amount was actually ADDED to the unit price. `false` when an exact price (price-list entry, combination price or a manually typed unit price) already absorbed it.

price_semantics.description: Monetary semantics of the resolved price: `per_base_unit` (product/variant own price, converted once by the presentation factor) or `per_commercial_unit` (presentation, combination or price-list entry, never converted). `null` on a line with no catalog price context.

price_adjustment_total.description: Sum of the adjustments of the chosen option values, as a decimal string. Informational when an exact price already absorbed them.

option_adjustments_absorbed.description: TRI-STATE, and `null` is NOT `false`. `true`: the resolved price already includes the option adjustments. `false`: they were added on top. `null`: it could not be determined — the assembler refuses such a line with 422 rather than risking charging the adjustments twice, so `null` only ever reaches a reader on a legacy line with no configurable options at all.

QuoteLine.title: QuoteLine

QuoteStats.description: Aggregated summary of the quotes of the authenticated company: total, accumulated amount, count by status, expired and converted to invoice. Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/quotes/stats`.

total_amount.description: Aggregate amount of the quotes (EUR), as a 2-decimal string.

expired_count.description: Quotes whose `valid_until` date has already passed.

QuoteStats.title: QuoteStats

ReceiveReturnRequest.description:
Receiving the goods of an approved return.

This is the step that puts the merchandise back into the warehouse: the stock
entry is written inside the same transaction that moves the return to
received, so a failure never leaves a received return without goods, nor
goods without a return behind them.

## The destination warehouse is optional, and leaving it out is not "none"

When the body does not name a warehouse, the destination is INHERITED from
the stock ledger: the goods go back to the warehouse they left from. Forcing
a choice here would invite receiving into a warehouse other than the one that
shipped, which leaves the shipping one permanently negative while the global
balance still adds up — a mismatch nobody sees until the physical count.

When the body does name one, it has to be an ACTIVE warehouse of the same
company as the path. An archived warehouse is refused because goods cannot
enter a warehouse that is out of service, and a warehouse held by another
company is refused exactly like one that does not exist, with no way to tell
the two apart.

## The reception date is optional and cannot be in the future

Leaving it out means now. It is accepted because goods can arrive on a Friday
and be registered on Monday, and this date is the one that dates the stock
movement. A future date is refused: a movement dated tomorrow brings forward
goods that are not in the warehouse yet, and every stock report cut at a date
would read them as already there. The date is a plain calendar date,
`YYYY-MM-DD`, with no time part.

## No quantity travels in this body

What is received is what was approved. There is no property for quantities,
neither for the return as a whole nor per line: accepting one would let the
caller put into stock something different from what the approval authorised,
and each returned quantity is already fixed when the return is requested.
A property this body does not declare is ignored, and what enters the ledger
is always the approved quantity.

## Idempotency key

Receiving is declared irreversible — it writes the entry of goods into the
ledger and no operation of this API reverses it — so this operation asks for
an idempotency key header whenever the policy of the credential in use
requires one. Send a unique key per operation and repeat exactly the same key
when you retry, so an answer lost on the wire never turns into a second entry
of the same goods.

warehouse_id.description: Public ID of the warehouse the goods physically come back into: an ACTIVE warehouse of the company in the path. Omitting it takes the destination already recorded on the return. A warehouse of another company, an archived one and one that does not exist are all rejected the same way, naming the field, so the three cannot be told apart.

received_at.description: Date the goods physically arrived, as a calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD` with no time of day. Omitting it records the moment of the call. A date in the future is rejected: goods that have not arrived cannot have been received. No quantity travels here — receiving takes in what the return declares, in full.

ReceiveReturnRequest.title: ReceiveReturnRequest

ReceiveStockTransferRequest.description: Receive the goods of a dispatched stock transfer, in full or in part. `lines` is required and needs at least one entry: each one names the transfer line being received (`stock_transfer_line_id`, the public ID the lines sub-resource returns) and the `quantity` received NOW — not the running total —, greater than zero and with at most four decimals. The same line may not be declared twice in one call, not even written in a different case: the second entry would overwrite the first and the goods declared in it would vanish with nothing to show for it. Receiving ADDS to what that line had already received, so the operation may be repeated until everything dispatched has arrived, and a quantity that takes a line above what was dispatched is rejected as a business-rule violation. That is also why the operation is irreversible and honours an idempotency key: a second identical call without one would advance the received quantity twice.

lines.description: Lines received now. Required and never empty: a reception that declares no line declares nothing.

additionalProperties.description: Quantity received NOW for that line, which is added to what was already received.

ReceiveStockTransferRequest.title: ReceiveStockTransferRequest

employee_id.description: Employee ID (UUID v7) the retroactive workday is recorded for.

started_at.description: Start of the retroactive workday in ISO 8601.

ended_at.description: End of the retroactive workday in ISO 8601 (after the start).

reason.description: Required reason for the retroactive entry.

pauses.description: Optional breaks within the retroactive workday.

start.description: Start of a break in ISO 8601.

end.description: End of a break in ISO 8601 (after its start).

RecurringInvoice.description: A recurring invoice template that auto-generates invoices on a fixed cadence.

status.description: Recurring schedule status (active, paused, completed, cancelled).

price_list_id.description: UUID of the price list selected for generated invoices.

price_list_name.description: Price-list name snapshot stored by the recurrence.

name.description: Descriptive name of the recurrence.

description.description: Free-text description of the recurrence.
description.example: Contrato de soporte y mantenimiento Plan Pro
examples: Contrato de soporte y mantenimiento Plan Pro

notes.description: Internal notes carried over to the generated invoices.
notes.example: Renovación automática. Facturar el día 1 de cada mes.
examples: Renovación automática. Facturar el día 1 de cada mes.

email_to.description: Recipient of the automatic dispatch of generated invoices. `null` if not configured.

send_automatically.description: Compatibility field DERIVED from `generation_mode`: `true` if and only if `generation_mode` is `issue_and_send` (each generated invoice is issued and emailed to `email_to`). On write, without an explicit `generation_mode`, `true` still means `issue_and_send` and `false` means `draft`; when both are sent and contradict each other the request is rejected with 422.

generation_mode.description: What each run of the recurrence does with the invoice it generates: `draft` leaves it as a draft (no definitive number); `issue` issues it (definitive number, VeriFactu record, stock movements) without emailing it, so it stays `is_sent = false`; `issue_and_send` issues it and emails it to the configured recipients, and it is marked as sent once the mail server accepts the email (if the delivery fails the invoice stays issued and not sent). Available in every API version. `send_automatically` is derived from it.

days_before_due.description: Payment term days (Net X) applied to the due date of each generated invoice.

max_occurrences.description: Maximum number of invoices to generate before completing the recurrence. `null` = no limit.

occurrences_count.description: Number of invoices already generated by this recurrence.

remaining_occurrences.description: Invoices remaining until `max_occurrences` is reached. `null` when there is no limit.

holiday_handling.description: Adjustment policy when the run date falls on a holiday/weekend (e.g. `none`, `next_business_day`, `previous_business_day`).

next_run_at.description: When the next invoice will be generated.

last_run_at.description: When the last invoice was generated, if any.

cancelled_at.description: When the recurrence was cancelled (irreversible terminal state). `null` if not cancelled.

taxes_total.description: NET aggregate of the header taxes: `total_vat + total_surcharge - total_retention`. It is the amount that, added to `subtotal`, yields `total` (`total === subtotal + taxes_total`), so it must NOT be combined with `total_retention`: subtracting the withholding again on top of the aggregate produces a false total. It is NOT the VAT figure of the Spanish Modelo 303 - read `total_vat` for that. These amounts are a PREVIEW aggregated from the template lines (the recurrence persists no header totals), rounded per line exactly as the invoice it will issue stores them.

total_vat.description: Output VAT (IVA repercutido) the recurrence will accrue: sum of the VAT of its template lines. This is the figure a Spanish Modelo 303 declares, and it is NOT recoverable from `taxes_total`, which nets the withholding out.

total_retention.description: Withholding (retencion de IRPF) the recurrence will apply: sum of the withholding of its template lines, as a POSITIVE amount that SUBTRACTS from the total. This is the figure a Spanish Modelo 130/111 declares. It is ALREADY netted out inside `taxes_total`, so do not subtract it again.

total_surcharge.description: Equivalence surcharge (recargo de equivalencia) of the template lines. It ADDS to the total exactly like VAT does, and is ALREADY included inside `taxes_total`.

total.description: Total the recurrence will invoice. Two equivalent ways to reconstruct it from the published amounts, and only these two: the EXPLICIT one, identical in the six document families - `total = subtotal + total_vat + total_surcharge - total_retention` - or the AGGREGATE one, specific to the sales-side families - `total = subtotal + taxes_total`. NEVER reconstruct it as `subtotal + taxes_total - total_retention`: `taxes_total` ALREADY has the withholding netted out, so that combination subtracts it twice.

external_id.description: External integration key (ERP/CRM/e-commerce) mapping this document to a record in a third-party system. Free-format, unique per company, filterable via `?external_id=`. `null` when not set. Persistent synchronization key, independent of the request-level `Idempotency-Key`.

tags.description: Free classification tags (lowercase slugs `[a-z0-9-]`, ≤ 40 chars each, ≤ 30 tags). Filterable via `?tags[in]=tag1,tag2` (JSON_CONTAINS, OR semantics). Empty `[]` when there are none.

custom_fields.description: Ordered list of typed custom fields `[{field, value}]` (≤ 50). Distinct from `metadata` (a free key→value map): use `custom_fields` for structured, display-oriented integration metadata. Empty `[]` when there are none.

auto_delivery.description: Rich auto-delivery configuration (superset of the scalar `email_to`): the generated invoices are emailed to `recipients` (with optional `cc`) using `subject`/`body`. `recipients`/`cc` are empty lists and `subject`/`body` are `null` when nothing is configured.

send_automatically.description: Compatibility field DERIVED from `generation_mode`: `true` if and only if `generation_mode` is `issue_and_send`, in which case each generated invoice is emailed to `recipients`.

recipients.description: Primary recipients of the automatic dispatch. Empty list if not configured.

cc.description: Carbon-copy recipients. Empty list if not configured.

subject.description: Custom email subject. `null` to use the default.

RecurringInvoiceLine.description: A line item on a recurring invoice template.

additional_description.description: Optional secondary description rendered below the line concept on generated invoice PDFs.

unit_price.description: Unit price as a decimal STRING with 4 decimals (e.g. `"100.0000"`), the scale the template accepts: reading a line and sending it back never changes its price.

retention.description: IRPF withholding percentage applied to the line (0–100). Default 0. Its amount is already aggregated into `taxes`.

surcharge.description: Equivalence surcharge (recargo de equivalencia) percentage applied to the line (0–100). Default 0. Its amount is already aggregated into `taxes`.

discount_percent.description: Discount percentage applied to the line (0-100) BEFORE any tax, exactly as the domain and the invoice this recurrence will issue apply it. `subtotal` is already net of it, so `unit_price` multiplied by `quantity` does NOT equal `subtotal` on a discounted line. Default 0.

exemption_reason.description: LIVA exemption / non-subjection cause of the line (subset of the E and N codes). `null` if not informed.

regime_key.description: VeriFactu regime key (`ClaveRegimen`, AEAT list L8.1) of the line. `null` if not informed.

retention_rate_id.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of the catalog tax applied as IRPF withholding to the line. Opaque: it does not take part in the `taxes`/`total` computation (the formula uses the flat `retention` percentage). `null` if not informed.

surcharge_rate_id.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of the catalog tax applied as equivalence surcharge to the line. Opaque: it does not take part in the `taxes`/`total` computation (the formula uses the flat `surcharge` percentage). `null` if not informed.

indirect_tax_regime.description: Indirect tax regime override of the recurring template line: `iva`/`igic`/`ipsi` when set per-document (precedence override>zone), otherwise `null`. Writable on create/update; propagated to each generated invoice. The template must be homogeneous (a single non-null regime across all lines, 422 otherwise).

counted_quantity.description: Pieces the customer asked for on a variable-weight line sold by count (decimal string, scale 4, greater than 0), e.g. `"4.0000"` for four pieces weighing `quantity` kg in total. Informational: the line is charged and the stock is discounted by `quantity` (the real weight), never by the pieces. `null` on any other line. Only accepted on a `variable_measure` presentation whose unit is a count unit.

counted_unit.description: UN/ECE code of the count unit of `counted_quantity` (`H87` piece, `XPK` pack…). `null` exactly when `counted_quantity` is `null`.

configuration.description: Commercial combination frozen on the line, or `null` when the line was not sold or bought through one (legacy product, manual line).

options.description: Configurable options frozen on the line, in printing order. Always an array, `[]` included.

price_adjustment.description: Adjustment of the chosen value per commercial unit. `null` means the value does not change the price — NOT the same as adjusting by `0`.

applied.description: Whether that amount was actually ADDED to the unit price. `false` when an exact price (price-list entry, combination price or a manually typed unit price) already absorbed it.

price_semantics.description: Monetary semantics of the frozen price: `per_base_unit` (converted once by the presentation factor) or `per_commercial_unit` (never converted). `null` when the line carries no catalog price context.

price_adjustment_total.description: Sum of the adjustments of the chosen option values, as a decimal string.

option_adjustments_absorbed.description: TRI-STATE, and `null` is NOT `false`. `true`: the frozen price already includes the option adjustments. `false`: they were added on top. `null`: it could not be determined.

RefundReturnRequest.description:
Refunding a received return: the step that issues the corrective invoice.

## The target invoice is optional, and the three outcomes are all legitimate

The invoices of the origin document that can still be corrected are resolved
on the server, and there are three outcomes. With exactly ONE candidate it is
taken and this body can be empty. With NONE the request is refused as a
business rule violation saying there is no invoice to correct, and the return
stays received with its goods already back in stock. With SEVERAL — the case
of an order invoiced in two batches — the choice is required, and without it
the request is refused naming the candidates by their number.

Omitting the property therefore succeeds only when the origin resolves to
exactly one candidate. Making it required instead would force the ordinary
case — a delivery note with a single invoice behind it — to read the
candidates first only to send back the only one there is. The reading of
corrective candidates published for the same return answers that question
before you send anything, so the choice is made with the numbers in front of
you and never by trial and error.

## What the check on this body covers, and what it does not

Here it is settled that the invoice EXISTS in the same company as the path;
an invoice held by another company is refused exactly like one that does not
exist. What is checked afterwards, on the server, is that the invoice is also
AMONG THE CANDIDATES of the origin: an invoice that is perfectly yours but
unrelated to what was returned would correct a document with no link to the
goods, and a corrective invoice cannot be deleted — it can only be undone by
issuing another fiscal document.

## What this body never accepts

Neither the amount to refund, nor the scope of the correction, nor the tax
authority code of the correction. All three are derived from what was
actually returned and from the total of the chosen invoice, and the type of
the original document decides the rest. Accepting any of them would let the
caller declare a fiscal effect different from the one the return produced.

## Idempotency, twice over

Refunding is declared irreversible, so this operation asks for an idempotency
key header whenever the policy of the credential in use requires one: send a
unique key per operation and repeat exactly the same key when you retry.

Independently of that header, the refund is idempotent by the identity of the
return itself: refunding the same return twice never issues a second
corrective invoice, whichever surface asks for it and however much time goes
by. The header protects an immediate retry of the same request, including one
whose answer you never saw; the identity of the return protects everything
else.

target_invoice_id.description: Public ID of the invoice to correct, of the company in the path. Omitting it works only when the origin resolves to EXACTLY ONE candidate invoice; with several, the request is rejected and the candidates are listed so you can pick one, and with none there is nothing to correct. An invoice of another company is rejected exactly like one that does not exist.

RefundReturnRequest.title: RefundReturnRequest

RegisterCompanyRepresentationV1Request.description: Register the representation that authorizes Factuarea to remit your VeriFactu records to AEAT on your behalf. Send `multipart/form-data`: `kind`, `signer_name`, `signer_tax_id` and `granted_on` are required, plus the evidence — `document` (PDF, up to 5 MB) for the signed annex I, and `document` or `power_of_attorney_reference` for a power of attorney. The optional `valid_until` sets the last day of validity: without it the representation does not expire. An active representation that already exists is revoked and kept in the history.

kind.description: Kind of representation: `social_collaboration_annex_i` (social collaboration, with the signed annex I of the Resolution of 18-12-2024) or `aeat_power_of_attorney` (a power of attorney registered with AEAT).

signer_name.description: Name of the person who signed the authorization.

granted_on.description: Date on which the authorization was granted (YYYY-MM-DD). It cannot be in the future.

valid_until.description: Last day of validity of the representation (YYYY-MM-DD), optional: without it the representation does not expire. It cannot be earlier than `granted_on` nor more than 5 years after it (power of attorney registered in the AEAT register, art. 6.4 of Law 39/2015); otherwise 422 with `param=valid_until`. Once the day has passed the representation is reported with `is_expired: true` and stops enabling third-party remission.

power_of_attorney_reference.description: Reference of the power of attorney in the AEAT register. For a power of attorney, send this or the `document`.

document.description: Signed evidence as a PDF (up to 5 MB, validated by magic bytes): required for the annex I, and for a power of attorney when no `power_of_attorney_reference` is sent. It is custodied encrypted, counts against your storage quota and is never returned.

RegisterGoodsReceiptRequest.description: Register a goods receipt against a purchase order. A receipt is born as `created`: it is a written declaration with no effect yet — it consumes no pending quantity and does not move the order status; posting it is a separate operation. `purchase_order_id` is required when registering through the goods receipt resource and must be omitted — or repeated identically — when registering under the purchase order, where the order comes from the path. `lines` is required and needs at least one entry: an empty receipt is not a document. Each line names the purchase order line it consumes and the quantity received IN THE PURCHASE UNIT of that line; its base-unit equivalent is derived with the conversion factor the ORDER froze when the line was added, never with the one the catalogue holds today.

purchase_order_id.description: Purchase order ID (UUID v7) the goods are received against. Required through the goods receipt resource; under the purchase order the path carries it and the body must either omit it or repeat the SAME value — any other one is rejected naming the field, because a document cannot have two parent orders depending on where you look.

received_on.description: Date the goods arrived (`YYYY-MM-DD`), chosen by whoever receives them and not by the server clock. Required.

warehouse_id.description: Receiving warehouse ID (UUID v7), active and belonging to the company in the path. Optional: when it is absent the receipt does not publish it and resolving the effective warehouse does not belong to this surface.

notes.description: Free text attached to the receipt, up to 1000 characters.

lines.description: Lines received. Required and never empty: a receipt with no lines is not a document.

purchase_order_line_id.description: ID (UUID v7) of the PURCHASE ORDER line this quantity consumes. It must belong to that order and to the company in the path; a line of another order — even within the same company — is rejected pointing at the entry, because whoever receives goods needs to know which one is wrong.

quantity.description: Quantity received, greater than zero, with up to ten integer digits and four decimals, expressed IN THE PURCHASE UNIT of that order line: if it was bought in boxes of twelve, boxes are received. The base-unit equivalent is derived with the conversion factor the order froze and is not sent.

RejectReturnRequest.description:
Rejecting a return.

The body carries the reason for the rejection, `rejection_reason`, and — only
when that reason is a manual decision — a free note, `rejection_note`.

## The reason belongs to a closed catalog of three values

`window_expired` and `exceeds_delivered` are the two rejections the platform
decides on its own: the first when the return window of the company has
already closed, the second when what is asked back is more than what the
origin document delivered. `manual_decision` is the merchant turning the
return down.

The three are accepted here on purpose. A rejection decided by a policy and a
rejection decided by a person are then recorded in the same vocabulary, so
rejected returns can be counted by cause without reading any free text.
Anything outside the catalog is refused naming the field.

## The note is admitted ONLY with the manual decision

The two automatic reasons already carry their own explanation — the window
that applied and its closing date, or the quantity still returnable — and
writing a second one over them would publish two accounts of the same fact
with no way to tell which of them governs. The manual decision is the
opposite case: there is no automatic text, and without the note nobody can
reconstruct afterwards why the return was turned down. A blank note is read
as no note at all, never as an error.

## What this body does not settle

Whether the return can be rejected at this point is not decided here. A
return whose goods have already been received is refused as a business rule
violation, because the merchandise is in the warehouse and no operation of
this API takes it back out. Repeating that check in the form would give two
copies of the same state machine, and the second copy is the one that falls
behind.

## Idempotency key

Rejecting is declared irreversible — a rejected return is a terminal state
and nothing moves after it — so this operation asks for an idempotency key
header whenever the policy of the credential in use requires one. Send a
unique key per operation and repeat exactly the same key when you retry, so
an answer lost on the wire never becomes a second rejection.

rejection_reason.description: Why the return is turned down: `window_expired` (the period for returning it had passed), `exceeds_delivered` (it asks for more than was delivered) or `manual_decision` (somebody decided so). The first two are the two automatic reasons; only the third is a judgement call, and only the third admits a note.

rejection_note.description: Free note explaining the rejection, up to 1000 characters. Admitted ONLY when the reason is `manual_decision`: with an automatic reason the note would explain something the reason already states, and it is rejected naming the field instead of being silently dropped. An empty note is the same as not sending one.

RejectReturnRequest.title: RejectReturnRequest

reason.description: Required rejection reason.

ReleaseStockReservationsByHolderRequest.description: Release everything a holder still keeps on hold, in a single call. Required: `holder_type` and `holder_id`, exactly the pair used when the stock was held. The response reports how many reservations were actually released; repeating the call for a holder that no longer holds anything succeeds with a count of zero. The operation is irreversible — released is a terminal state — and requires an idempotency key when the policy of your credential demands it.

holder_type.description: Kind of holder whose holds are released, exactly the one used when reserving.

holder_id.description: Public ID (UUID v7) of that holder, exactly the one sent when the goods were held. A holder of another company releases exactly nothing, and answers like one that holds nothing.

ReorderSuggestion.description: One line of the replenishment report: a catalog item below its reorder point, with the quantity it would be worth buying and the supplier offer that quantity comes from. Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/purchase-reorder-suggestions` inside `{ "data": [ReorderSuggestion, …], "actionable_count": …, "not_actionable_count": … }`. It is a COMPUTED report and not a stored collection: it is recalculated on every call, it is not paginated, and its size grows with the catalog.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the catalog item that is below its reorder point.

product_name.description: Name of that item, so the report is readable without a second call.

product_variant_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the variant, or `null` when the suggestion is about the item itself.

current_quantity.description: Stock on hand, in BASE units, as a decimal string with FOUR decimal places.

threshold.description: Reorder point that triggered the suggestion, in BASE units, with the same scale.

suggested_quantity.description: Quantity worth ordering, in the PURCHASE unit of the preferred offer and already rounded up to its minimum order quantity, with the same four-decimal scale. It is `null` when the item is NOT actionable: without an active offer there is no purchase unit to express a quantity in.

purchase_unit_code.description: Code of the purchase unit of the preferred offer, or `null` when the item is not actionable.

conversion_factor.description: How many BASE units one purchase unit of that offer holds, as a decimal string with SIX decimal places, or `null` when the item is not actionable.

unit_cost.description: Cost of one purchase unit in that offer, as a decimal string with FOUR decimal places, or `null` when the item is not actionable.

lead_time_days.description: Delivery lead time in days that the offer declares, or `null` when it declares none. It is the field that tells apart "order it now" from "it can wait".

supplier_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the supplier of the preferred offer, or `null` when the item is not actionable.

supplier_name.description: Name of that supplier, or `null` when there is none.

offer_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the supplier offer the suggestion is built from, or `null` when the item is not actionable. It is the value the acceptance takes to know which offer it is buying at.

actionable.description: Whether this line can be turned into a purchase order line. An item below its minimum WITHOUT an active supplier offer is reported anyway, marked `false`: hiding it would hide the very item that needs attention the most.

not_actionable_reason.description: Why the line cannot be ordered, in Spanish, or `null` when it is actionable.

ReorderSuggestionAcceptance.description: Result of accepting a replenishment suggestion: the partial-success counters shared by every bulk endpoint of this API, plus the purchase orders that were created — one per SUPPLIER, grouped server-side. Returned by `POST /v1/companies/{company}/purchase-reorder-suggestions/accept`. The orders are created as DRAFTS, so nothing was sent to any supplier and the operation is not irreversible; what it is NOT is idempotent by itself: accepting the same proposal twice creates a SECOND set of drafts, because a suggestion is not a document with an identity. Send an `Idempotency-Key` when you retry.

total.description: Number of items sent in the request (`successful + failed`).

successful.description: Number of items that became a line of a created purchase order.

failed.description: Number of items that could not be ordered. Equals `failures` length.

failures.description: One entry per item that could not be ordered. An omitted item does NOT abort the rest: the acceptance reports it and carries on with the others. Always a list (empty, never `null`).

items.description: One item the acceptance could not order, identified by its 0-based POSITION in the request body — not by its catalog identifier, so a row whose item does not even resolve can still be pointed at.

index.description: 0-based position of the item within the `items` array of the request.

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code from the v1 error catalog (stable across languages).

example.error_message: El artículo no tiene ninguna oferta de proveedor activa con la que pedirlo.

examples.error_message: El artículo no tiene ninguna oferta de proveedor activa con la que pedirlo.

purchase_orders.description: Purchase orders created by this acceptance, one per supplier. Empty when every accepted item failed.

id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the created purchase order. It is a DRAFT: it still has to be sent to the supplier.

number.description: Number of that order, stamped on creation.

scheduled_for.description: New instant at which the scheduled invoice will be issued, as an ISO 8601 date-time strictly in the future (422 otherwise). An explicit offset (`Z`, `+01:00`) is honoured; without one it is read in `Europe/Madrid`. Only the date moves: the `scheduled_action` chosen when scheduling (`issue` or `issue_and_send`) is kept.

options.description: Options already chosen, ONE value per group: two values of the same group are an invalid request, not a partial selection.

ResolvePurchaseInvoiceMatchRequest.description: Body shared by the two decisions that close a three-way match: accepting the deviation it found, and rejecting the match. It carries ONE property, `reason`, the written reason of whoever decides — required, up to 500 characters, it travels with the decision and is what an audit reads afterwards. Accepting leaves the invoice matched, stops it blocking its own status transitions and closes its purchase order as billed, and it is irreversible: no published operation moves a billed purchase order back to an earlier state. Rejecting leaves the invoice blocked on purpose — it can be neither recorded nor paid, and its order is not closed —, which is the state of an invoice that goes back to the supplier.

reason.description: Reason written by whoever accepts or rejects the deviation. Required, up to 500 characters. It travels with the decision and is what an audit reads afterwards.

ResolvePurchaseInvoiceMatchRequest.title: ResolvePurchaseInvoiceMatchRequest

ResolveStorefrontCatalogSelectionRequest.description: Ask whether what a shopper has chosen CAN BE OFFERED, before asking for its price and before putting it in a cart. The body carries the COMPLETE selection: `product_id` is required, and `variant_id`, `presentation_id`, `configuration_id`, `selection_signature` and `options` travel when the shopper has already chosen them. `options` is a list of PAIRS of `group_id` and `value_id` — one value per group, at most 50 — and never a flat list of values, so the same choice cannot be written in two ways.
