Sending the configuration AND the cross that produces it at the same time is legitimate here: a cart line holds both, so checking one again resends both. A combination that cannot be offered is NOT an error of the request: it comes back with 200 saying so and why, because the rejection belongs to the operations that CONFIRM — the cart and the order — and this one exists precisely so a storefront can warn before. It stores nothing. Every reference is checked against the shop that owns the key, and one of another shop is rejected exactly like one that does not exist; a field this operation does not know is rejected naming it, because a selection written with the vocabulary of another operation would otherwise be answered as if it were this one.

product_id.description: Public id of the article chosen, of the shop that owns the key. Required. An article of another shop is rejected exactly like one that does not exist.

variant_id.description: Public id of the variant chosen, when the article has variants.

presentation_id.description: Public id of the presentation chosen — the way the article is sold, such as a box of twelve or a 15 L drum — when the article has presentations.

configuration_id.description: Public id of the configuration already chosen, for when you are checking one you already had rather than building it from the option values.

selection_signature.description: Fingerprint of the configuration already chosen: 64 hexadecimal characters, for the same case as the configuration id.

options.description: Option values chosen so far, as a list of PAIRS of `group_id` and `value_id`: one value per group and at most 50. It is never a flat list of values, so the same choice cannot be written in two ways and the answer can say which groups are still pending.

items.description: Each chosen option, with its group and its value

group_id.description: Public id of the option group the choice belongs to.

value_id.description: Public id of the value chosen inside that group.

ResolveStorefrontCatalogSelectionRequest.title: ResolveStorefrontCatalogSelectionRequest

ResolveStorefrontPriceRequest.description: Resolve what a shopper would pay for ONE selection, with the same pricing engine the merchant uses. The body carries the complete selection — `product_id` required, plus `variant_id`, `presentation_id`, `configuration_id`, `selection_signature` and `options` as a list of pairs of `group_id` and `value_id` — and `quantity`, which is required, greater than zero and with at most four decimals. There is NO price-list field: the rate applied is the one the shop declares for its storefront and the server resolves it, because being able to propose it from the browser would be being able to choose the price. You get back the unit price, the currency, the unit that price refers to, the applicable tax and the line total; what you deliberately do NOT get is which price list won, the source amount or the breakdown of option adjustments, which are commercial data of the seller. Read the result as a PREVIEW: the amount an order line freezes is resolved again when the order is created, and any amount sent in a body is ignored. It stores nothing. A reference of another shop is rejected exactly like one that does not exist, and a field this operation does not know is rejected naming it.

product_id.description: Public id of the article priced, of the shop that owns the key. Required. An article of another shop is rejected exactly like one that does not exist.

variant_id.description: Public id of the variant chosen, when the article has variants.

presentation_id.description: Public id of the presentation chosen. It changes the UNIT the price refers to, which is why the answer publishes that unit alongside the amount.

configuration_id.description: Public id of the configuration chosen, when there is one.

selection_signature.description: Fingerprint of the configuration chosen: 64 hexadecimal characters.

options.description: Option values chosen, as a list of pairs of `group_id` and `value_id`: one value per group and at most 50. Each value may carry a price adjustment, and how those adjustments add up is not published.

items.description: Each chosen option, with its group and its value

group_id.description: Public id of the option group the choice belongs to.

value_id.description: Public id of the value chosen inside that group.

quantity.description: Units asked for: required, greater than zero, with at most four decimals and up to 9999999999.9999. It travels and is compared as a decimal, because in floating point four decimals lose scale before anybody compares them.

ResolveStorefrontPriceRequest.title: ResolveStorefrontPriceRequest

configuration_id.description: Commercial combination against which the price was resolved. It may be present even when the request sent only the signature: a signature that matches a materialized combination is normalized to its identity before pricing.

selection_signature.description: Canonical signature (64 hexadecimal characters) of the resolved selection.

price_list_id.description: Price list CONSULTED, not necessarily the source of the price: it is present even when `source` is `product`. To know where the amount came from, look at `source`.

unit_semantics.description: Semantics of the amount of the winning source. `per_base_unit` is converted once by the factor of the presentation; `per_commercial_unit` is never converted.

source_amount.description: Amount of the winning source, already converted to `price_unit` and BEFORE the option adjustments: `source_amount + option_adjustment_total = unit_price`.

option_adjustment_total.description: Sum of the adjustments of the chosen option values, per commercial unit.

option_adjustments_absorbed.description: Whether the winning source already included the option adjustments. `null` means the resolver did not take a position, never `false`.

ResolvedCatalogPriceList.description: Prices resolved for the batch, one per selection sent. The order is not part of the contract: pair them by `index`.
ResolvedCatalogPriceList.title: ResolvedCatalogPriceList

ResolvedCatalogPricePreview.description: One repricing line: the price the selection resolves to today, the price the line has frozen and the difference between the two.

index.description: Position of the selection in `targets`. It is what pairs each price with its line without depending on the order of the response.

unit_semantics.description: Semantics of the amount of the winning source. `per_base_unit` is converted once by the factor of the presentation; `per_commercial_unit` is never converted.

source_amount.description: Amount of the winning source, already converted to `price_unit` and BEFORE the option adjustments: `source_amount + option_adjustment_total = unit_price`.

option_adjustment_total.description: Sum of the adjustments of the chosen option values, per commercial unit.

option_adjustments_absorbed.description: Whether the winning source already included the option adjustments. `null` means the resolver did not take a position, never `false`.

current_unit_price.description: Unit price the line has frozen today, as it was sent.

changed.description: `null` when `current_unit_price` was not sent: without it there is nothing to compare.

ResolvedCatalogPricePreview.title: ResolvedCatalogPricePreview

ResolvedCatalogSelection.description: Outcome of checking a (possibly partial) selection against a product catalog. An ambiguous or incomplete selection is NOT an error here: this operation exists to BUILD the line, so it answers 200 with what is still missing. The 422 is raised by whoever confirms the line.

mode.description: `open` for explicit open availability, `allow_list` for explicit closed availability. `legacy` is retained only for backwards-compatible historical payloads.

status.description: `resolved`: the selection identifies one combination. `incomplete`: something is still to be chosen (see `pending_option_groups`). `ambiguous`: it matches several combinations at once. `incompatible`: no active combination admits it.

configuration_name.example: Superior · Garrafa de 5 L · Calidad: Superior
examples: Superior · Garrafa de 5 L · Calidad: Superior

configuration_price.description: Own FINAL price of the resolved combination, per commercial unit. This is CONTEXT, not the final price of the line: the full precedence (exact price-list entry, combination, presentation, variant, product) is resolved by `POST /v1/companies/{company}/price-lists/resolve`.

option_adjustment_total.description: Sum of the adjustments of the chosen option values. Always present, but INFORMATIONAL when `configuration_price` is set: that price already absorbs them and they are not added again.

compatible_option_groups.description: Groups still in play, each with ONLY the values some candidate combination still admits. That is the progressive filtering: a value no compatible combination contains disappears instead of being offered to end in a 422.

pending_option_groups.description: Groups that still need a choice before the line can be confirmed.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable cause when the selection is not resolved.

reason.description: Actionable Spanish message naming what is missing.

ResolvedCatalogSelection.title: ResolvedCatalogSelection

RetiredPriceListTarget.description: Frozen description of the catalog target a withdrawn price entry pointed at.

selection_signature.description: Canonical 64-hex signature when the entry targeted a normalized selection instead of a stored combination.

RetiredPriceListTarget.title: RetiredPriceListTarget

Return.description: A return: the goods a customer sends back, and what has to happen with the money. It is a document of its own —it has its own number and its own lifecycle— and it hangs on the document the goods came out of. Its four transitions (approve, reject, receive, refund) are IRREVERSIBLE sub-resources with different effects, which is why there is no generic status-change operation on it: approving numbers it, receiving books the stock back in and refunding issues the corrective invoice.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the return, a UUID v7. No internal numeric key is ever published, not of the return and not of its origin.

object.description: Always `return`. Discriminator of the resource, published by the twenty-five live v1 resources and by these five since the return landed its Resources.

number.description: Readable number of the return, unique per company. It is `null` while the return is only REQUESTED and it is stamped when it is approved. The absent number is never invented: it is not a provisional and it is not an empty string.

status.description: Lifecycle status: `requested` (asked for, and the only status where it can be edited or deleted), `approved` (authorised and numbered), `received` (the goods came back and the stock is booked in), `refunded` (the money was returned, with its corrective invoice) and `rejected` (turned down, terminal).

status_label.description: Label of the status in Spanish, ready to display, derived from the same single source as the catalog.

status_color.description: Colour token of the status (`gray`, `blue`, `purple`, `green`, `red`), for a client that paints a badge. It names the SEVERITY of the status, not a CSS colour.

origin_type.description: Kind of document the goods came out of. It is a CLOSED catalog and it decides which lines can be returned and how much of them.

origin_id.description: Opaque identifier of the origin document, of the kind `origin_type` says.

origin_number.description: Readable number of the origin document, or `null` when it has none yet.

reason.description: HEADER reason of the return, out of a closed catalog, or `null`. It is the optional one: the reason of each LINE is mandatory, and when the header one is not sent it is derived from the lines.

reason_label.description: Label of the header reason in Spanish, or `null` when there is no header reason.

rejection_reason.description: Why the return was rejected, out of a closed catalog: `window_expired` and `exceeds_delivered` are the two AUTOMATIC ones and `manual_decision` is the one a person takes. `null` while the return has not been rejected.

rejection_reason_label.description: Label of the rejection reason in Spanish, or `null`.

rejection_note.description: Note explaining the rejection. It is admitted ONLY with `manual_decision`, because the two automatic reasons explain themselves and a note on them would be a second, divergent explanation. `null` when there is none.

warehouse_id.description: Opaque identifier of the DESTINATION warehouse, where the goods are booked back in when the return is received. `null` when none is pinned.

business_contact_id.description: Opaque identifier of the business contact the return belongs to. It is the CANONICAL reference of the holder, and it is the only one published: publishing the client reference as well would give two identities for the same holder.

target_invoice_id.description: Opaque identifier of the invoice that will be corrected by the refund, when one has been chosen. `null` while it has not.

target_invoice_number.description: Readable number of that invoice, or `null`.

corrective_invoice_id.description: Opaque identifier of the CORRECTIVE invoice the refund issued. `null` until the return is refunded. Under VeriFactu that invoice is not deleted, which is why a refunded return cannot be deleted either.

corrective_invoice_number.description: Readable number of the corrective invoice, or `null`.

refundable_amount.description: Amount that can be refunded for this return, derived from its lines, as a decimal string with two decimal places (e.g. `"242.00"`).

refunded_amount.description: Amount actually refunded, as a decimal string with two decimal places, or `null` while the return has not been refunded.

refund_scope.description: Whether the refund covered the whole origin document or only part of it. `null` while the return has not been refunded.

notes.description: Free-text notes of the return, or `null`.
notes.example: Dos tableros con el canto dañado en la descarga.
examples: Dos tableros con el canto dañado en la descarga.

lines.description: Lines of the return, each one with the quantity coming back and its own reason. They are fixed at REQUEST time: the partial update does not accept any line field, and correcting them means deleting the return and requesting it again while it is still requested.

requested_at.description: When the return was requested (ISO 8601). It is put by the clock of the server and never chosen by the client: letting the client choose that moment would be letting it choose whether the return window has expired.

approved_at.description: When the return was approved (ISO 8601), or `null`.

received_at.description: When the goods were received back (ISO 8601), or `null`.

refunded_at.description: When the refund was issued (ISO 8601), or `null`.

rejected_at.description: When the return was rejected (ISO 8601), or `null`.

updated_at.description: When the record was last modified (ISO 8601).

Return.title: Return

ReturnCorrectiveCandidate.description: An invoice that the refund of a return could correct. It is the second PRE-FLIGHT read: the refund resolves the target invoice on its own when there is EXACTLY ONE candidate, rejects when there is none and rejects as AMBIGUOUS when there are several without a choice — and this operation is the question that answers which ones they are, so the client can pick one and send it. A return with no candidate returns the EMPTY collection and not an error: an empty collection is the right answer to a legitimate question, and the rejection belongs to the refund.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the candidate invoice. The internal numeric key of the invoice is deliberately NOT published: it is the only integer that could have travelled in this resource and the public-identifier gate rejects it.

object.description: Always `return_corrective_candidate`. Discriminator of the resource, published by the twenty-five live v1 resources and by these five since the return landed its Resources.

number.description: Readable number of the candidate invoice.

total.description: Total of the candidate invoice, as a decimal string with two decimal places, so the amount can be compared against what is being returned.

issue_date.description: Issue date of the candidate invoice (`YYYY-MM-DD`), or `null`. It is published because it is what tells two candidates of the same origin apart.

ReturnCorrectiveCandidate.title: ReturnCorrectiveCandidate

ReturnLine.description: One line of a return: ONE item coming back, with the quantity and the reason. The unit price and the tax rate are INHERITED from the line of the origin document and are never accepted from the client: the amount that will be corrected is not decided by whoever asks for the return, and a corrective invoice that VeriFactu will not let you delete hangs on it.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the return line, a UUID v7.

object.description: Always `return_line`. Discriminator of the resource, published by the twenty-five live v1 resources and by these five since the return landed its Resources.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of the item coming back, inherited from the origin line. `null` on a free-text line.

product_variant_id.description: Opaque identifier of the variant, inherited from the origin line. `null` when the line does not pin one.

description.description: Description of what is coming back, inherited from the origin line.

quantity.description: Quantity coming back, as a decimal string with four decimal places. It is a string and never a floating-point number: this is the figure the ceiling against the delivered quantity hangs on, and serialising it as a float would lose precision exactly there.

conversion_factor.description: Conversion factor INHERITED from the origin line between its commercial unit and the base unit of the item, as a decimal string with six decimal places, or `null` when the origin line carries none and `quantity` is already in the base unit. It is not accepted on write.

base_quantity.description: Quantity coming back expressed in the base unit of the item (`quantity` × `conversion_factor`), as a decimal string with four decimal places: it is what re-enters stock when the return is received. `null` on a line without an item.

reason.description: Reason of THIS line, out of a closed catalog. It is MANDATORY per line — the header one is the optional one — because two items of the same return can come back for different reasons.

reason_label.description: Label of the reason in Spanish, ready to display.

unit_price.description: Unit price INHERITED from the origin line, as a decimal string with four decimal places (e.g. `"100.0000"`). It is not accepted on write.

tax_rate.description: Tax rate INHERITED from the origin line, as a percentage. It is not accepted on write.

discount.description: Discount INHERITED from the origin line, as an amount. It is not accepted on write.

surcharge_rate.description: Equivalence surcharge rate INHERITED from the origin line, as a percentage. It is not accepted on write.

retention_rate.description: Retention rate INHERITED from the origin line, as a percentage. It is not accepted on write.

line_amount.description: Amount of the line, as a decimal string with two decimal places: base after discount + tax + surcharge − retention, derived from the quantity and the inherited price and conditions.

counted_quantity.description: Pieces that come back from a variable-weight line sold by count, as a decimal string with four decimal places, or `null`. Informational: it never drives stock or amounts.

counted_unit.description: Unit (UN/ECE code) of those pieces, inherited from the origin line, or `null` exactly when `counted_quantity` is `null`.

ReturnLine.title: ReturnLine

ReturnStatusItem.description: A return status from the closed catalog, with its label and its colour token. Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/returns/statuses` as a flat list, without pagination. The three fields are DERIVED from the value object of the lifecycle and never from a hand-written list: a parallel list drifts at the first extension and the catalog starts publishing statuses that no longer exist. Unlike the delivery note, the return does NOT translate any internal status into a different public vocabulary: the catalog is the same on both surfaces.

object.description: Always `return_status_item`. Discriminator of the resource, published by the twenty-five live v1 resources and by these five since the return landed its Resources.

value.description: Status token. It is the identity of the status: a token of a closed catalog, not a row of any table.

label.description: Label of the status in Spanish, ready to display.

color.description: Colour token of the status (`gray`, `blue`, `purple`, `green`, `red`), for a client that paints a badge.

ReturnStatusItem.title: ReturnStatusItem

ReturnableLine.description: One line of an origin document that can still be returned, with how much of it is left. It is the PRE-FLIGHT read of the request: it answers "what can I send back, and how much" BEFORE asking for the return, so a client does not discover the ceiling as a rejection. It is a projection of the origin document and NOT a resource with a life of its own: it has no identity in our system, no lifecycle and no operations.

origin_line_id.description: Reference of the line of the ORIGIN document. It is the value the body of the request echoes back to say which line is coming back, and it is the ONLY place the API publishes it: neither the detail nor the listing of a return exposes any origin line reference. It travels as an integer because the lines of a delivery note and of an invoice do not carry a public identifier of their own; a closed round trip within one company, and never an identifier of the return itself.

object.description: Always `returnable_line`. Discriminator of the resource, published by the twenty-five live v1 resources and by these five since the return landed its Resources.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of the item of the line. `null` on a free-text line.

product_variant_id.description: Opaque identifier of the variant of the line. `null` when the line does not pin one.

description.description: Description of the line of the origin document.

delivered_quantity.description: Quantity that was delivered on this line, as a decimal string with four decimal places. It is the ceiling everything else is measured against.

returned_quantity.description: Quantity already coming back on LIVE returns, with the same scale. A rejected return does NOT count here: turning one down gives the quantity back.

returnable_quantity.description: Quantity that can still be returned: delivered minus already returned, with the same scale. It is DERIVED by the read model and never stored, so there is a single definition of what is left.

unit_price.description: Unit price the return would INHERIT from this line if it were requested, as a decimal string with four decimal places (e.g. `"100.0000"`). It is published so a client can show the amount at stake before asking.

tax_rate.description: Tax rate the return would inherit from this line, as a percentage.

discount.description: Discount the return would inherit from this line, as an amount.

surcharge_rate.description: Equivalence surcharge rate the return would inherit from this line, as a percentage.

retention_rate.description: Retention rate the return would inherit from this line, as a percentage.

counted_unit.description: Unit (UN/ECE code) of the pieces of the origin line, or `null` when the line carries none. Only a line with a counted unit admits `counted_quantity` when the return is requested; sending pieces for any other line is rejected with `return_line_pieces_not_allowed`.

ReturnableLine.title: ReturnableLine

reason.description: Why the payment is being reverted. One of the closed catalog: `direct_debit_return` (returned SEPA direct debit), `card_dispute` (card chargeback or reversal), `misapplied_payment` (booked against the wrong invoice), `bounced_effect` (dishonoured bill) or `recording_error`. `issued_in_error` also belongs to the catalog but is reserved to annulling the invoice (`POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/annul` with `revert_collections=true`): sent here it returns 422 `reversal_reason_reserved`. Any other value returns 422 `payment_reversal_reason_invalid`.

note.description: Optional free-text remark kept with the reversal trail, up to 500 characters. A longer note returns 422 `payment_reversal_invalid`.

RevokeApiKeyV1Request.description: Optionally record why the API key is being revoked. `reason` (string, ≤500 chars) is optional; when omitted a default reason is stored for auditing.

reason.description: Optional reason for the revocation (recorded in the audit log).

RevokeApiKeyV1Request.title: RevokeApiKeyV1Request

RevokeNifTransferV1Request.description: Optional body of the tax ID transfer revocation. `reason` (string, up to 500 characters) is optional and is recorded in the audit trail; everything that decides the operation — which transfer, which account — comes from the path and the credential.

reason.description: Optional reason for the revocation (up to 500 characters, recorded in the audit log).

RevokeNifTransferV1Request.title: RevokeNifTransferV1Request

RevokeStorefrontKeyRequest.description: Optionally record why the publishable storefront credential is being revoked. `reason` (string, at most 255 chars) is optional — revoking a credential that ships inside a browser is incident response, so no reason is required to act. A blank reason is stored as none. Revocation is permanent: the credential cannot be reactivated, rotated or edited afterwards.

reason.description: Why the credential is being revoked, up to 255 characters. Optional — revoking one that ships inside a browser is incident response, so no reason is required to act — and a blank one is stored as none. It is kept with the credential and published in its detail and in the listing.

RevokeStorefrontKeyRequest.title: RevokeStorefrontKeyRequest

SalesOrder.description: A sales order: the commitment to serve goods or services to a buyer, and the document the delivery notes and invoices that fulfil it are derived from. It is NOT a fiscal document, so it only takes a number from its series when it is confirmed and `number` stays `null` while it is a draft. Amounts are decimal strings with two decimal places; line quantities are decimal strings with four.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the sales order, a UUID v7. Every reference of this document travels the same way: no internal numeric key is ever published.

number.description: Number stamped from the series when the order is confirmed. `null` while the order is a draft, because a draft has consumed no correlative yet: an empty number and the draft status are the same fact seen twice.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the order: `draft` (editable, no number yet), `confirmed` (numbered and committed), `partially_served` and `served` (goods handed over in part or in full), `partially_invoiced` and `invoiced` (invoiced in part or in full), `closed` and `cancelled` (both terminal, neither reopens). The four consumption states are DERIVED from the quantities of the lines and are not destinations you can ask for: they move when a delivery note, an invoice or a return consumes the order, and they move BACK when such a consumption is reverted.

status_label.description: Label of the status in Spanish, ready to display.

status_color.description: Suggested colour token for rendering the status.

channel.description: Origin the order came in through: `manual` (entered by hand), `store` (connected shop), `storefront` (custom web shop), `api` (this public API), `quote` or `proforma` (converted from one of them) and `assistant` (conversational assistant). It is set on creation and no operation accepts it afterwards: the origin of an order is history, not a field.

channel_label.description: Label of the channel in Spanish, ready to display.

order_date.description: Date of the order, as a plain calendar date.

expected_delivery_date.description: Date the goods are expected to be delivered, as a plain calendar date, or `null` when none was agreed.

series_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the numbering series that stamps the number on confirmation, or `null` while none has been chosen. It is set with a partial update BEFORE confirming.

warehouse_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the warehouse the order is served from, or `null` when it is not tied to one. Each line may override it.

business_contact_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the commercial contact this order is linked to, or `null` when the buyer has no record. The identity published under `buyer` is a snapshot taken when the order was placed and does not move if the contact changes later.

buyer.description: Identity of the buyer frozen on the order. `tax_id` is OPTIONAL on purpose: a private individual can place an order without one, which is also why converting that order into a COMPLETE invoice is rejected until the identity is filled in. The order accepts what the invoice cannot. On write the same fields travel FLAT, one level up: the asymmetry is deliberate and documented on both sides.

name.description: Name or company name of the buyer.

email.description: Contact email of the buyer, or `null` when not reported.

phone.description: Contact phone of the buyer, or `null` when not reported.

tax_id.description: Spanish fiscal identifier (NIF, CIF or NIE) of the buyer, or `null` for a private individual who did not provide one.

billing_address.description: Billing address of the buyer. It is independent of the shipping address: changing one does not drag the other.

address_line.description: Street and number, or `null` when not reported.

city.description: Town or city, or `null` when not reported.

postal_code.description: Postal code, or `null` when not reported.

country.description: Country, free text and not an ISO code, or `null` when not reported.

shipping_address.description: Shipping address of the buyer. It is independent of the billing address: an order can be invoiced to one and delivered to another.

address_line.description: Street and number, or `null` when not reported.

city.description: Town or city, or `null` when not reported.

postal_code.description: Postal code, or `null` when not reported.

country.description: Country, free text and not an ISO code, or `null` when not reported.

subtotal.description: Amount of the order before taxes, as a decimal string with two decimal places.

total_vat.description: Output VAT (IVA repercutido) accrued by the order: sum of the VAT of its lines.

total_retention.description: Withholding (retencion de IRPF) of the order: sum of the withholding of its lines, as a POSITIVE amount that SUBTRACTS from the total.

total_surcharge.description: Equivalence surcharge (recargo de equivalencia) of the order: sum of the surcharge of its lines. It ADDS to the total exactly like VAT does.

total.description: Total of the order, reconstructed with the identity shared by every document family: `total = subtotal + total_vat + total_surcharge - total_retention`.

currency.description: Currency of every amount of this document, as an ISO 4217 code. Always `EUR`.

external_id.description: External integration key (ERP/CRM/e-commerce) mapping this document to a record in a third-party system. Free-format, unique per company, filterable via `?external_id=`. `null` when not set. Persistent synchronization key, independent of the request-level `Idempotency-Key`.

notes.description: Free-text notes of the order, or `null` when there are none.
notes.example: Entregar en horario de mañana; avisar al portero automático.
examples: Entregar en horario de mañana; avisar al portero automático.

lines.description: Lines of the order, each with its four quantities, the derived pending one and the ledger of what consumed it.

can_be_edited.description: Whether the current status still admits editing the contents of the order. Only a draft does: once confirmed, what changes are the consumed quantities, and those are not edited, they are allocated.

can_be_deleted.description: Whether the current status still admits deleting the order. Only a draft does: a confirmed order has consumed a correlative of its series, and the way out of one that should not exist is to cancel it, which leaves a trace.

is_terminal.description: Whether the order reached a closing status (`closed` or `cancelled`), which no operation reopens.

updated_at.description: When the order was last modified (ISO 8601).

SalesOrder.title: SalesOrder

SalesOrderEmailDelivery.description: Acknowledgement that the sales order confirmation was accepted and queued for delivery by email.

sales_order_id.description: Opaque identifier of the sales order whose confirmation was queued, a UUID v7. It is also the key with which the delivery is located afterwards on the email deliveries surface.

status.description: Always `queued`: the acknowledgement states that the email was accepted and queued, never that it was delivered. Delivery is observed afterwards through the email deliveries surface.

SalesOrderEmailDelivery.title: SalesOrderEmailDelivery

SalesOrderLine.description: A line of a sales order. It carries the four quantities that describe how much of the commitment has been served, invoiced and returned, the pending one derived from them, and the ledger of the documents that consumed it.

id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the line. Unlike the lines of the invoice, the quote, the pro forma and the delivery note, a sales order line DOES publish its identity: the line sub-resource edits and deletes it by this identifier, and a partial conversion picks which lines it converts by naming them.

sales_order_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the order this line belongs to.

description.description: Concept of the line, frozen when the line was added.
description.example: Silla ergonómica Nordic, tapizada en gris
examples: Silla ergonómica Nordic, tapizada en gris

product_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the catalog item, or `null` when the line is free text.

warehouse_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the warehouse this line is served from; it inherits the one of the order when it is not set.

quantity_ordered.description: Quantity committed on the line, as a decimal string with FOUR decimal places (the scale of the sales family). Quantities travel as strings and not as numbers because they are the figures a partial delivery note and a partial invoice use to decide what is left, and a binary float turns that arithmetic into a line nobody can close.

quantity_served.description: Quantity already handed over, accumulated, with the same four-decimal scale. No public operation writes it: it moves when a delivery note consumes the line and back when that consumption is reverted.

quantity_invoiced.description: Quantity already invoiced, accumulated, with the same four-decimal scale. It is never written directly either: an invoice consuming the line moves it.

quantity_returned.description: Quantity returned by the buyer, accumulated, with the same four-decimal scale. A return gives quantity back to the pending figure.

quantity_pending.description: Quantity still to serve, DERIVED as `quantity_ordered - quantity_served + quantity_returned` with a floor of zero, with the same four-decimal scale. A return REOPENS pending quantity: ten ordered, ten served and two returned leave two pending again.

counted_quantity.description: Pieces of a variable-weight line sold by count, as a decimal string with four decimal places, or `null` when the line carries none. Informational: pieces never drive stock or amounts, which follow the real weight in `quantity_*`.

counted_unit.description: Unit (UN/ECE code) in which the pieces are counted, or `null` exactly when `counted_quantity` is `null`.

unit_price.description: Unit price of the line, as a decimal string with four decimal places (e.g. `"100.0000"`).

discount.description: Discount percentage applied to the line (0-100). A percentage is not money, so it travels as a number.

vat_rate.description: VAT percentage applied to the line (0-100).

retention_rate.description: IRPF withholding percentage applied to the line (0-100). Its amount subtracts from the total.

surcharge_rate.description: Equivalence surcharge percentage applied to the line (0-100). Its amount adds to the total.

subtotal.description: Amount of the line before taxes, as a decimal string with two decimal places.

retention_amount.description: Withholding amount of the line, as a POSITIVE amount that subtracts from the line total.

surcharge_amount.description: Equivalence surcharge amount of the line.

total.description: Total of the line: `subtotal + vat_amount + surcharge_amount - retention_amount`.

consumption.description: Ledger of what took quantity away from this line. The four quantities are an accumulated figure; this is the list of documents behind them, so `served 7 of 10` stops being a number without an author. Empty while nothing has consumed the line.

SalesOrderLine.title: SalesOrderLine

SalesOrderLineConsumption.description: One consumption of a sales order line: the document that took a quantity away from it, and how much. The sum of the consumptions of one concept matches EXACTLY the corresponding quantity of the line. It publishes neither the identity of the allocation nor the instant it was recorded: an integrator does not operate on allocations, they move by registering or reverting the consumption of a document.

document_type.description: Type of the document that consumed the quantity.

document_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the consuming document, so the order can be reconciled against it.

concept.description: What the consumption did: `service` when a delivery note handed the quantity over, `invoicing` when an invoice billed it, `return` when the buyer gave it back.

quantity.description: Quantity of this consumption, as a decimal string with FOUR decimal places, the same scale as the quantities of the line. It is not money and does not travel with the two decimals of an amount.

SalesOrderLineConsumption.title: SalesOrderLineConsumption

SalesOrderStats.description: Aggregated headline figures of the sales orders of the authenticated company, narrowed to the date range of the query when one is given. Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/sales-orders/stats`, wrapped in `{ "data": SalesOrderStats }`.

total_count.description: Number of orders in the period. It is a COUNT, not money: it does not travel with the two decimals of an amount, unlike `total_amount` of this very object.

total_amount.description: Accumulated total of the orders in the period, as a decimal string with two decimal places.

count_by_status.description: Number of orders per status, keyed by the token of the closed catalog. It carries one entry per status INCLUDING the ones at zero, so a client never has to tell `zero` apart from `did not come`.

pending_quantity.description: Total quantity still to serve, as a decimal string with FOUR decimal places. It is a sum of line quantities and not an amount: publishing it with two decimals would truncate the very figure that answers whether anything is left to deliver.

pending_orders.description: Number of orders with at least one line still pending to serve.

SalesOrderStats.title: SalesOrderStats

SalesOrderStatusItem.description: A sales order status from the closed catalog, with its label, its colour and what it allows. The three permissions are the contract that spares the integrator a round of trial and error: they say, BEFORE trying, which statuses admit editing the order, deleting it or converting it into a delivery note or an invoice.

value.description: Status token. It is the identity of the status: a token of a closed catalog, not a row of any table. The four consumption states are derived from the quantities of the lines and are not transition targets.

label.description: Label of the status in Spanish, ready to display.

color.description: Suggested colour token for rendering the status.

can_edit.description: Whether the status admits editing the contents of the order.

can_delete.description: Whether the status admits deleting the order.

can_convert.description: Whether the status admits converting the order into a delivery note or an invoice.

SalesOrderStatusItem.title: SalesOrderStatusItem

lines.description: Partial edits preserve omitted fields and lines. Add omits line_id (allocated by the server); update/remove use the existing line_id.

ScheduleAssignment.description: The effective-dated assignment of a work schedule to an employee. Assigning a schedule closes the employee’s previously open assignment and opens a new one, preserving history. `effective_to` is `null` while the assignment is still open.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the assignment, a UUID v7.

work_schedule_id.description: UUID v7 of the assigned work schedule.

employee_id.description: UUID v7 of the assigned employee.

effective_from.description: Date the assignment starts being effective, in `Y-m-d`.

effective_to.description: Date the assignment stops being effective, in `Y-m-d`; `null` while open.

ScheduleAssignment.title: ScheduleAssignment

ScheduleInvoiceRequest.description: Schedule the future issuance of a `draft` invoice. Required: `scheduled_for` (ISO 8601 date-time, strictly in the future) and `scheduled_action` (`issue` to issue it without sending, or `issue_and_send` to issue it and email it to the customer). The legacy value `draft` is still accepted as an alias of `issue` in every API version.

scheduled_for.description: Instant at which the invoice will be issued, as an ISO 8601 date-time strictly in the future. An explicit offset (`Z`, `+01:00`) is honoured; without one it is read in `Europe/Madrid`.

scheduled_action.description: What happens at `scheduled_for`: `issue` issues the invoice without sending it; `issue_and_send` issues it and emails it to the customer. `draft` is still accepted as an alias of `issue` in every API version (it always meant "issue without sending").

ScheduleInvoiceRequest.title: ScheduleInvoiceRequest

SendAccountWebhookTestV1Request.description: Queue a signed test delivery to the account webhook endpoint of the path. `type` is optional: when omitted the first subscribed event type is used; when set it must be an event type an account endpoint can subscribe to (a company event of the public catalog or an `account.*` event) AND one the endpoint subscribes to, otherwise 422.

type.description: Event type to simulate. It must be one the endpoint subscribes to; when omitted the first subscribed type is used.

SendAccountWebhookTestV1Request.title: SendAccountWebhookTestV1Request

SendDeliveryNoteRequest.description: Email a delivery note. Required: `email`. Optional: `subject`, `message` (up to 2,000 characters) and `template_id`, the integer identifier of an email template of the global catalog (a shared system catalog, so it is not a UUID v7).

template_id.description: Integer id of the email template, from the shared catalog of templates (it is not a UUID).

SendDeliveryNoteRequest.title: SendDeliveryNoteRequest

email.description: Email of the employee to invite (the `employee` role is set by the server).

SendInvoiceReminderV1Request.description: Fields of the payment reminder, shared by `POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/send-reminder` and `POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/{invoice}/reminder-preview`. Every field is optional: without overrides the standard payment reminder template is used.

email.description: Recipient other than the client email.

message.description: Additional message for the reminder body.

attach_pdf.description: Per-send override for "attach the invoice PDF". If omitted (or `null`), the company default (`email_settings`) is used.

stripe_payment_button.description: Per-send override for the "Stripe payment button". If omitted (or `null`), the company default is used.

SendInvoiceReminderV1Request.title: SendInvoiceReminderV1Request

SendInvoiceRequest.description: Email an invoice. Optional body: `to` (string), `cc[]` and `bcc[]` (arrays of emails), `subject` (max 200 characters) and `body` (string). If the client has no email and `to` is absent, it returns 422 `missing_required_param`.
SendInvoiceRequest.title: SendInvoiceRequest

SendProformaRequest.description: Email a proforma. Optional body: `to` (string), `cc[]` and `bcc[]` (arrays of emails), `subject` (max 200 characters) and `body` (string). If the client has no email and `to` is absent, it returns 422 `missing_required_param`.
SendProformaRequest.title: SendProformaRequest

SendPurchaseOrderV1Request.description: Send a purchase order to its supplier by email, with the printable document attached. `to` is the list of recipient addresses, `cc` and `bcc` are optional lists, `subject` (up to 200 characters) and `body` (up to 5000) override the defaults of the template. Every list validates its entries as email addresses, and none of them is checked against your contacts: sending the document to an address that is not on file is a legitimate case. NO language field is accepted — the language of the message is sealed from the issuing company, so the same document always leaves in the same language whatever the caller asks. The answer is 202 with an acknowledgement that the email was accepted and QUEUED, never that it was delivered. When `to` is omitted the order falls back to the email of its supplier; an order whose supplier has no email and no `to` is rejected with 422 and the missing parameter named.
SendPurchaseOrderV1Request.title: SendPurchaseOrderV1Request

SendQuoteRequest.description: Email a quote. Optional body: `to` (string), `cc[]` and `bcc[]` (arrays of emails), `subject` (max 200 characters) and `body` (string). If the client has no email and `to` is absent, it returns 422 `missing_required_param`.
SendQuoteRequest.title: SendQuoteRequest

SendSalesOrderV1Request.description: Send the confirmation of a sales order to its buyer by email, with the printable document attached. `to` is the list of recipient addresses, `cc` and `bcc` are optional lists, `subject` (up to 200 characters) and `body` (up to 5000) override the defaults of the template. Every list validates its entries as email addresses, and none of them is checked against your contacts: sending the document to an address that is not on file is a legitimate case. NO language field is accepted — the language of the message is sealed from the issuing company, so the same document always leaves in the same language whatever the caller asks. The answer is 202 with an acknowledgement that the email was accepted and QUEUED, never that it was delivered. When `to` is omitted the order falls back to the email of its buyer; an order with no buyer email and no `to` is rejected with 422 and the missing parameter named.
SendSalesOrderV1Request.title: SendSalesOrderV1Request

SendStockTransferV1Request.description: Send the note of a stock transfer by email, with the printable document attached. `to` is the list of recipient addresses, `cc` and `bcc` are optional lists, `subject` (up to 200 characters) and `body` (up to 5000) override the defaults of the template. Every list validates its entries as email addresses, and none of them is checked against your contacts: sending the document to an address that is not on file is a legitimate case. NO language field is accepted — the language of the message is sealed from the issuing company, so the same document always leaves in the same language whatever the caller asks. The answer is 202 with an acknowledgement that the email was accepted and QUEUED, never that it was delivered. `to` is REQUIRED here and optional on the other two document families, and that asymmetry is the one thing to read before wiring your integration: a warehouse is not a contact and carries no email address, so there is no default recipient to fall back on. Omitting it is rejected at the border with 422 and `param: to`.
SendStockTransferV1Request.title: SendStockTransferV1Request

SendTestEventRequest.description: Trigger a test delivery to the webhook endpoint. `type` is optional: when omitted the endpoint first subscribed event is used; when set it must belong to the closed event catalog and be one of the endpoint subscribed events (otherwise 422).
SendTestEventRequest.title: SendTestEventRequest

SendTransportDocumentRequest.description: Email the current PDF of the transport document. Optional `to`, `cc` and `bcc` (lists of emails, up to 5 distinct addresses in total; an address repeated within or across the lists, ignoring letter case, counts and is sent once) plus `subject` and `message`. Without `to`, the email of the carrier contact is used.
SendTransportDocumentRequest.title: SendTransportDocumentRequest

Series.description: A document numbering series. It can be edited with `PATCH /v1/companies/{company}/series/{series}` under the fiscal guards of the numbering (code, mask and purpose are fixed once documents exist) and it is never deleted: archive it instead.

document_type.description: Document type the series numbers. The public API accepts CREATING a series for `invoice`, `quote`, `delivery_note`, `proforma`, `sales_order` and `purchase_order`, whose default codes are `F`, `P`, `ALB`, `PRF`, `PED` and `PC`. Transport control documents (`transport_document`, default code `DC`) are not created through this API: their series is created on the first issuance of a document. A company may also hold series of types this API does not create, so read this field as an open value and not as a closed set.

invoice_kind.description: Fixed purpose of an invoice series (RD 1619/2012 arts. 6.1.a, 7.1.a and 15): `complete` (complete invoices `F1` and the `F3` that replaces simplified invoices — the usual series), `simplified` (simplified invoices `F2`), `corrective` (corrective invoices `R1`–`R4`) or `simplified_corrective` (corrective invoices of simplified invoices `R5`). An invoice can only be issued in a series of its own purpose, otherwise issuing fails with `series_invoice_kind_mismatch`. Set on creation (default `complete`), editable with `PATCH /v1/companies/{company}/series/{series}` until the series has any invoice (`series_invoice_kind_locked`) and never on the default series of its purpose (`series_default_kind_change`). `null` for series of other document types.

prefix.description: Legacy alias for code. Use code field. Will be removed in v2.

number_format.description: Canonical numbering mask describing how the document number is rendered: padding (the block of zeros), year token (`{YYYY}` 4 digits / `{YY}` 2 digits / omitted for no year), optional month token (`{MM}` 2 digits) and separator. Example: `{code}-{YYYY}-{000}` (default) or `{code}-{YYYY}-{00000}` for 5-digit padding. When `counter_reset` is `monthly`, the mask must include the `{MM}` token (e.g. `F-{YYYY}-{MM}-{000}`) so the rendered number stays unique across months; otherwise two months would both start at `1`. Set on creation and editable with `PATCH /v1/companies/{company}/series/{series}` until the first document is issued; fixed afterwards (`series_format_immutable_with_documents`). Mirrors Holded's `format`.

next_number.description: Next correlative that will be assigned on the next real emission.

current_number.description: Last correlative actually emitted in the current fiscal year (0 for a brand-new series).

initial_number.description: Number the counter starts from. Set on creation to continue an existing numbering when migrating (e.g. 235). Defaults to 1. It can be changed with `PATCH /v1/companies/{company}/series/{series}` as long as it does not open a gap after documents of the current year (`series_initial_number_creates_gap`) and no record of the series has been accepted by AEAT.

counter_reset.description: Counter reset policy (source of truth): `never` (the counter never resets), `annual` (resets on January 1st) or `monthly` (resets on the 1st of each month). `monthly` requires the `number_format` mask to include the `{MM}` token to keep rendered numbers unique across months.

year_reset.description: Deprecated alias of `counter_reset`. `true` is equivalent to `counter_reset: "annual"`, `false` to `counter_reset: "never"`. Use `counter_reset` instead; this field will be removed in v2.

Series.title: Series

SeriesActivity.description: An event in the activity timeline of a numbering series. Groups domain events originated by changes to the series itself (creation, archive/unarchive, marked as default, number consumption).

description.description: Human-readable description of the event in Spanish.

metadata.description: Event metadata. Internal identifiers (PKs) are stripped; `*_uuid` values are preserved.

type.description: Type of actor that originated the event: `user` for a human in the internal app, `api_key` for an action performed through the public v1 API.

id.description: UUID v7 of the actor: the user when `type=user`, or the API key when `type=api_key`.

name.description: Actor name at the time of the event: the user name or the API key name. `null` if it could not be resolved.

performed_by.description: Actor that originated the event. `{type:"user",...}` for an internal user, `{type:"api_key",...}` when performed via the public v1 API, or `null` when the event is system-generated (scheduler, periodic sweep) with no attributable actor.

SeriesActivity.title: SeriesActivity

SeriesBootstrapCandidate.description: An active series eligible to become the default of its document type. Only appears on `no_default` entries, where the bootstrap deliberately refuses to choose for you.

id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the series. Pass it to `POST /v1/companies/{company}/series/{series}/default` to promote it.

code.description: Code of the series, so the choice is informed rather than blind.

SeriesBootstrapCandidate.title: SeriesBootstrapCandidate

SeriesBootstrapEntry.description: Outcome of the bootstrap for one document type. The three states describe different business situations, not cosmetic variants: `created` and `existing` leave the type ready to issue documents, `no_default` does not.

document_type.description: Document type this entry reports on. The `contract` type is outside the public surface and is never bootstrapped, and neither are `sales_order` and `purchase_order`: the public API accepts creating a sales order or a purchase order series, but the bootstrap does not create one.

status.description: `created`: the type had no active series and its default one was created. `existing`: it already had a default series and nothing was touched. `no_default`: it has active series but none marked as default — nothing was created and nothing was promoted.

series_id.description: Opaque identifier (UUID v7) of the resulting default series. `null` only on `no_default`, where there is no default series to point at.

code.description: Code of the resulting default series (`F` invoices, `P` quotes, `ALB` delivery notes, `PRF` pro formas). `null` only on `no_default`.

candidates.description: Active series you can promote to default. Always present; empty except on `no_default`.

SeriesBootstrapEntry.title: SeriesBootstrapEntry

SeriesBootstrapResult.description: Result of bootstrapping the numbering of a company: one entry per document type of the public surface, always in the same order (`invoice`, `quote`, `delivery_note`, `proforma`).

results.description: One entry per document type evaluated.

SeriesBootstrapResult.title: SeriesBootstrapResult

level.description: Access level of the grant on the tax ID of the path: `view` (read-only) or `operate`.

company_id.description: Public identifier (UUID v7) of the company the access level is set on.

restrictions.description: Map of section to WITHDRAWN capabilities (`access`, `create`, `edit`, `delete`, `send`, `export`). Required; it can be empty.

grants.description: Administrator-only sections GRANTED to the member in that tax ID (for example `verifactu`); never the Administrator keys (user management, plan and subscription, API and developers, digital certificate). Optional: omitted, the grants are left as they are; sent — even empty — it replaces them entirely.

value.description: Value of the field: text, number, boolean, a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, an option or a list of options (`multiselect`). `null` clears the value.

ShipmentPackage.description: One package of a shipment: a box, a pallet or a parcel, with its weight and its three dimensions. Its nine keys ALWAYS travel — `null` on the ones that are not measured — because a package with nothing filled in is a legitimate state and not a different shape. Deleting one is published as irreversible, and it verifies the company of the delivery note AND of the package before writing.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the package, a UUID v7. It is the key the partial update and the deletion address.

position.description: Deterministic position of the package inside the shipment, assigned as the next one on creation.

reference.description: Reference of the package as the carrier labels it (the number on the sticker), or `null`.

weight_kg.description: Weight of the package in kilograms, as a decimal string with two decimal places, or `null` when it has not been weighed. It is a string and never a floating-point number, and a value above the ceiling of its column is rejected with a validation error BEFORE the shipment is touched. An unweighed package does NOT count as zero towards the total of the shipment.

length_cm.description: Length of the package in centimetres, decimal string with two decimal places, or `null` when it has not been measured.

width_cm.description: Width of the package in centimetres, with the same scale and the same rule, or `null`.

height_cm.description: Height of the package in centimetres, with the same scale and the same rule, or `null`.

notes.description: Free-text notes about the package (fragile, this side up), or `null`.

ShipmentPackage.title: ShipmentPackage

ShopifyConnectionCheck.description: The outcome of testing the connection with one of your connected Shopify stores. The public `id` is the UUID v7 of the STORE that was tested, so you can tell which shop this diagnosis is about. Nothing is stored: this resource is a diagnosis, not a record. Read `reachable` and `credential_accepted` together — `reachable: false` means the shop did not answer, while `reachable: true` with `credential_accepted: false` means it answered and rejected the access token — and read `failure_code` for the concrete cause, which is what tells «your token is no longer valid» apart from «the Admin API version we speak has expired».

id.description: UUID v7 of the store that was tested. Public identity (KEY `id`).

object.description: Stripe-like discriminator. Always `shopify_connection_check` for this resource.

reachable.description: Whether the shop answered at all. `false` covers a timeout, a transport failure, a 5xx from Shopify, an exhausted query cost budget and a destination your company has not authorised for outbound traffic.

credential_accepted.description: Whether the shop accepted the stored access token. Always `false` when `reachable` is `false`: we never got to ask.

store_version.description: The Shopify plan the shop reports, or `null` when it does not report one. Shopify publishes no «store version»; the plan display name is the closest equivalent it exposes. Informational: nothing is gated on it.

api_version.description: The pinned Admin API version this connector talked to the shop with (`YYYY-MM`), or `null` when it could not be resolved. It is OUR pin, not something the shop reports: Shopify serves whatever version you ask for and, once yours expires, silently falls forward to the oldest stable one with HTTP 200. Read it together with `supported_until`.

supported_until.description: The date the pinned Admin API version is supported until (ISO 8601 date), or `null` when there is no version to ask about or the version is not in our calendar. This is the field to watch: when an Admin API version expires Shopify does not fail, it answers 200 with the fields of another version, so the breakage is silent and shows up as data quietly going missing.

failure_code.description: Code naming the concrete cause when the check did not succeed, or `null` when it did. Today `shopify_store_unreachable` (the shop did not answer, or the query cost budget was exhausted — the only one worth retrying), `shopify_credentials_rejected` (the shop rejected the access token, or there was none to use), `shopify_api_version_expired` (the pinned Admin API version is no longer served) and `store_url_not_allowed` (your company has not authorised that destination for outbound traffic). Not an exhaustive enumeration: new causes may appear without a breaking change, so treat an unknown value as a failure you cannot classify.

checked_at.description: When the check ran (ISO 8601). Nothing is cached: every call tests the shop again.

ShopifyConnectionCheck.title: ShopifyConnectionCheck

SignDeliveryNoteRequest.description: Sign a delivery note on receipt. Required: `signed_by` (name of the person who receives it), `recipient_dni` (Spanish DNI/NIE of the signer) and `signature_image_base64` (the signature as a raw base64 PNG, without the `data:` prefix). Optional: `signed_at` (ISO 8601, defaults to now). A signature image that cannot be decoded or is too large returns 422 `invalid_param_format` or `payload_too_large`.
SignDeliveryNoteRequest.title: SignDeliveryNoteRequest

SimplifiedInvoiceEligibility.description: Result of checking whether an invoice can be issued as simplified (F2) under RD 1619/2012 art. 4.

can_be_simplified.description: Whether the invoice can be issued as a simplified invoice (F2).

must_be_complete.description: Whether the invoice must be issued as a full invoice (F1). It is the complement of `can_be_simplified`.

reason_code.description: Code of the blocking reason when it cannot be simplified (`intra_community`, `reverse_charge`, `export_operation`, `client_deduction_required`, `over_absolute_limit`). Empty string `""` when it can be simplified.

reason_message.description: Human-readable (Spanish) message of the blocking reason. Empty string `""` when it can be simplified.
reason_message.example: El importe 5.000,00 EUR supera el límite de 3.000,00 EUR para una factura simplificada.
examples: El importe 5.000,00 EUR supera el límite de 3.000,00 EUR para una factura simplificada.

sector_limit.description: Absolute legal limit (EUR) above which a simplified invoice is not allowed, as a 2-decimal string.

SimplifiedInvoiceEligibility.title: SimplifiedInvoiceEligibility

SimplifiedInvoiceEligibilityV1Request.description:
Public REST API v1 — POST /v1/companies/{company}/invoices/simplified-eligibility.

Checks whether an invoice with a given `total` amount (and, optionally,
client data) can be issued as simplified (F2) or must be issued as a
full invoice (F1) under Royal Decree 1619/2012 (art. 4).
SimplifiedInvoiceEligibilityV1Request.title: SimplifiedInvoiceEligibilityV1Request

StartConnectedAccountAuthorizationV1Requ.description: Start the Stripe Connect authorization of a company. `return_url` is required: an absolute `https` URL (up to 2048 characters, no credentials, no fragment, port 443 or none) whose host is one of the return domains of the account of the credential. Any other key in the body or the query returns 400 `parameter_unknown`.

return_url.description: HTTPS URL the person is sent back to when Stripe finishes (up to 2048 characters). Its host must be one of the return domains of the account of the credential, otherwise the request returns 422 `connect_return_url_not_allowed`. Factuarea appends these query parameters on the way back: `status` (`success` or `error`), `provider` (always `stripe`) and `authorization_id` always; on success also `company_id` (the company `id`, UUID v7), `connected_account_id` and `account`; on error also `error` and, when there is one, `error_subcode`.

StartConnectedAccountAuthorizationV1Requ.title: StartConnectedAccountAuthorizationV1Request

StartStorefrontCheckoutRequest.description: Ask for the payment link of an order so the shopper can pay it. BOTH fields are optional and an EMPTY body is the normal case — what is being asked for already travels in the path: the shop and the order. This body accepts NO amount, NO currency and NO gateway account: the total is computed by the server from the order itself and the account is resolved from the seller configuration, because being able to propose the amount from the browser would be being able to choose the price. An amount that arrives anyway is IGNORED rather than rejected, so a storefront that echoes back the order object it received keeps working. `return_path` is the RELATIVE path of YOUR site the shopper is sent back to after paying — the domain is never taken from the body, it comes from the origins the publishable credential declares — and an ABSOLUTE address is rejected even when it points at your own domain, together with a query string, a fragment, braces, a `..` segment, a double leading slash, a backslash, control characters and anything longer than 512 characters. Omitted, the path configured for the storefront is used (`/pedido` by default). `full_invoice_requested` says whether the shopper is asking for a full invoice instead of a simplified one, which raises the identity bar. Asking twice within the validity of the link returns the SAME address and the same expiry instead of opening a second payment session.

return_path.description: RELATIVE path of your own site the shopper is sent back to after paying, up to 512 characters, for example `/pedido`. The domain is NEVER taken from here: it is one of the origins the publishable credential declares, and the path is appended to it, which is why an ABSOLUTE address is rejected even when it points at your own domain. Rejected as well: a query string, a fragment, braces, a `..` segment, a double leading slash, a backslash and control characters — the answer names the path received and what is wrong with it. Omitted, the path configured for the storefront is used.

full_invoice_requested.description: Whether the shopper is asking for a full invoice instead of a simplified one. Absent counts as not asking. It is an explicit REQUEST and not a deduction: below the legal threshold of the simplified invoice a shopper may still want an invoice with a tax id, and above it the full invoice is compulsory and this flag changes nothing. Asking for it raises the identity bar, so the fiscal identification and the address become necessary to issue.

StartStorefrontCheckoutRequest.title: StartStorefrontCheckoutRequest

StockAvailability.description: What can still be SOLD of an item: the physical balance minus what reservations are holding. It is the figure a storefront has to read — publishing the physical one oversells, because units already committed to a paid order would be offered again. An item that does not manage stock publishes its three totals as `null` and not as zero: zero is a figure and reads as `sold out`.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of the item the figures belong to.

variant_id.description: Opaque identifier of the managing variant, or `null` when the stock target is the item itself.

stock_managed.description: Whether the item carries inventory at all. `false` describes a service or a fee: its three totals come as `null` and its breakdown empty, and there is nothing to run out of.

physical_total.description: Physical balance, as a decimal string with four decimal places; it may be negative. `null` when the item does not manage stock.

committed_total.description: Sum of what LIVE reservations are holding, with the same scale. An expired reservation does not count, and nothing has to sweep it for that to be true. `null` when the item does not manage stock.

available_total.description: Physical minus committed, with the same scale; it may be negative and it is NOT floored at zero. It is the authoritative figure and it is NOT derived by adding up the breakdown. `null` when the item does not manage stock.

per_warehouse.description: Availability broken down by warehouse. Empty when the item manages no stock, and possibly empty for a company whose initial move onto the physical axis has not run yet — which is why the total is not rebuilt from here.

warehouse_breakdown_complete.description: Whether the breakdown accounts for the whole of `available_total`. `false` says that part of the balance is not attributed to any warehouse —stock that predates the physical axis— so an empty breakdown with a positive total is readable instead of looking like a contradiction.

calculated_at.description: The instant the figures were decided with (ISO 8601) — the one that settled which reservations were still live. It is what makes the number interpretable: expiry stops committing on its own, so the same row read two minutes later is worth something else.

StockAvailability.title: StockAvailability

StockAvailabilityBatchItem.description: One row of the batch availability query: the reference that was sent and what came back for it. There is one row per reference SENT and in the order they were sent, so the caller pairs the answer with its request without matching identifiers.

reference.description: The reference exactly as it was sent — an opaque identifier or a catalog code.

found.description: Whether the reference resolves to an item of the company. A reference of ANOTHER company answers exactly like one that does not exist.

not_found_reason.description: Why the reference did not resolve, or `null` when it did. It is a RESULT code of the body and not an error code of the catalog: an unknown reference travels in the green inside a 200, because a 404 would abort the references that were good.

StockAvailabilityBatchItem.title: StockAvailabilityBatchItem

StockAvailabilityCommitment.description: One live commitment that is lowering the availability of an item: which reservation, whose it is, from which warehouse and for how long. It is the only way to answer `why is my available lower than my physical` in a single call.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the reservation holding the goods.

holder.description: Who holds them, as the integration declared it.

id.description: Identifier of the holder in the system of the integration.

warehouse_id.description: Opaque identifier of the warehouse the units are held from.

quantity.description: Quantity held, as a decimal string with four decimal places.

expires_at.description: When the commitment stops counting (ISO 8601), or `null` when it does not expire.

StockAvailabilityCommitment.title: StockAvailabilityCommitment

StockMovement.description: One row of the append-only stock ledger of a product, from the most recently applied movement to the oldest. Lets an integration audit and reconcile inventory instead of only seeing the current balance.

delta.description: Signed change in BASE units, decimal string with scale 4. Positive = stock in, negative = stock out. Never zero.

stock_after.description: Balance right after this movement was applied, decimal string with scale 4. Derived from the COMPLETE ledger, so it does not change when `direction` hides the interleaved rows.

reason.description: Why the movement happened. Closed catalog: `invoice_sent`, `invoice_annulled`, `invoice_unsent`, `corrective_created`, `delivery_note_delivered`, `delivery_note_cancelled`, `purchase_invoice_registered`, `purchase_invoice_reverted`, `manual_adjustment`, `initial`, `base_unit_replacement_out`, `base_unit_replacement_in`. The last two are the pair a base unit replacement writes: `_out` empties the old product (in its unit) and `_in` fills the new one (in its unit).

source_type.description: Kind of document that caused the movement. `manual` for an adjustment with no source document; `base_unit_replacement` for the transfer of a base unit replacement.

source_id.description: Id of the source document, `null` for a manual adjustment or when the document is no longer reachable. For `base_unit_replacement` it is the id of the OTHER product of the replacement: the new one on the `_out` row and the old one on the `_in` row.

source_label.description: Human-readable number of the source document. For `base_unit_replacement`, the name of the other product.

performed_by.description: Name of the user who caused the movement. `null` means the system did.

base_unit_code.description: UN/ECE code of the unit `delta` and `stock_after` are measured in. Always present.

commercial_quantity.description: Commercial magnitude the delta came from, decimal string with scale 4. All-or-nothing with `commercial_unit_code` and `conversion_factor`.

commercial_unit_code.description: UN/ECE code of the commercial unit. All-or-nothing with `commercial_quantity` and `conversion_factor`.

conversion_factor.description: Base units per commercial unit, decimal string with scale 6. All-or-nothing with the other two. Informational: it is NOT applied again here.

variant_id.description: Managing variant the balance belongs to, `null` when it is the base product.

warehouse_id.description: Warehouse the movement was booked to, `null` for a movement recorded before the physical axis existed. It is NOT replaced by the company default warehouse: attributing it would invent a fact about the past.

warehouse_name.description: Name of that warehouse as the master has it, `null` in the same case. Travels next to the id so rows served from different warehouses are readable without resolving ids one by one.

StockMovement.title: StockMovement

StockReservation.description: A stock reservation: units of an item held for a HOLDER —a cart, an order, whatever the integration calls it— so that nobody else can sell them while that holder decides. It is what lets a bespoke storefront hold goods without inventing its own set-aside table. It does NOT move the ledger: a held reservation lowers the AVAILABLE quantity and leaves the physical balance untouched.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the reservation, a UUID v7.

holder.description: Who holds the goods. It is an OPAQUE pair on purpose: the API does not know what a `cart` is in your system and does not validate it against any table of ours.

type.description: Kind of holder, as the integration declared it when the reservation was created (for example `cart`).

id.description: Identifier of the holder in the system of the integration.

holder_line_id.description: Identifier of the LINE of the holder this reservation answers to. This key is ABSENT — not `null` — when the hold belongs to the holder as a whole.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of the item whose units are held.

variant_id.description: Opaque identifier of the managing variant. This key is ABSENT when the stock target is the item itself.

warehouse_id.description: Opaque identifier of the warehouse the units are held from. A reservation always names one: availability is answered per warehouse.

quantity.description: Quantity held, in BASE units, as a decimal string with four decimal places.

status.description: Lifecycle status: `held` (holding units), `released` (given back) and `consumed` (turned into a real stock movement when the order was served). The two last ones are TERMINAL: nothing holds again what was released.

expires_at.description: When the hold stops counting (ISO 8601). This key is ABSENT when the reservation does not expire. Expiry needs no sweep to take effect: an expired reservation stops lowering availability by itself, which is why releasing one is rejected with its own code instead of answering success.

origin.description: Operation that created the hold. A reservation created through this API reads `public_api`.

held_at.description: When the units were held (ISO 8601). It always travels: every reservation is born held.

released_at.description: When the reservation was released (ISO 8601). This key is ABSENT while it has not been.

consumed_at.description: When the reservation was consumed (ISO 8601). This key is ABSENT while it has not been.

StockReservation.title: StockReservation

StockReservationBatchResult.description: The acknowledgement of an operation that touches SEVERAL reservations at once: the creation, which holds one line after another, and the release BY HOLDER, which sweeps everything a holder was keeping. One single shape answers both, so an integration models one type and not two.

count.description: Number of reservations the acknowledgement covers: created by the creation, effectively released by the release by holder. Releasing a holder that was keeping nothing answers in the green with zero, which is what makes that operation safe to repeat.

reservations.description: Body of each reservation CREATED. The creation fills it —and it may be shorter than the lines that were sent, because holds for the same destination are grouped—; the release by holder always returns it EMPTY, because its contract is the count and not the bodies.

StockReservationBatchResult.title: StockReservationBatchResult

StockReservationStatusItem.description: A reservation status from the closed catalog, with its label and its colour. Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/stock-reservations/statuses` as a flat list. It publishes NO permissions, and that is the answer of the domain and not an omission: the status of a reservation is not a destination a person picks — releasing and consuming stamp it.

value.description: Status token of the closed catalog.

label.description: Label of the status in Spanish, ready to display.

color.description: Suggested colour token for rendering the status.

StockReservationStatusItem.title: StockReservationStatusItem

StockTransfer.description: A stock transfer: goods moving from one warehouse of the company to another. It is NOT a fiscal document —it has no series, no customer and no amounts— and it carries no price at all: its lines count units. Dispatching it books the stock OUT of the origin and receiving it books the stock IN at the destination, so the ledger of the product shows both legs; cancelling it moves nothing.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the transfer, a UUID v7.

number.description: Readable number of the transfer (`TR-YYYY-N`), unique per company and stamped on creation. It is NOT a fiscal sequence: it guarantees uniqueness and not density, so a creation that rolls back leaves a permanent gap.

status.description: Lifecycle status: `draft` (being composed — the only status where lines can be added or removed), `dispatched` (the goods left the origin), `received` (everything dispatched arrived at the destination) and `cancelled` (terminal). Receiving PART of what was dispatched leaves the transfer in `dispatched` with the rest pending.

origin_warehouse_id.description: Opaque identifier of the ORIGIN warehouse, frozen when the transfer was created. It cannot be the same as the destination.

destination_warehouse_id.description: Opaque identifier of the DESTINATION warehouse, frozen when the transfer was created.
