dispatched_at.description: When the transfer was dispatched (ISO 8601). This key is ABSENT — not `null` — while the transfer is still a draft.

received_at.description: When the transfer was FULLY received (ISO 8601). This key is ABSENT while anything is still pending, including a transfer that has been partially received.

notes.description: Free-text notes of the transfer, or `null` when there are none. Unlike the two timestamps, this key always travels.
notes.example: Reposición de tienda: 12 tableros y 6 rollos de canto.
examples: Reposición de tienda: 12 tableros y 6 rollos de canto.

lines.description: Lines of the transfer, each one with its three quantities. A draft with no lines cannot be dispatched.

StockTransfer.title: StockTransfer

StockTransferEmailDelivery.description: Acknowledgement that the stock transfer note was accepted and queued for delivery by email.

stock_transfer_id.description: Opaque identifier of the stock transfer whose note was queued, a UUID v7. It is also the key with which the delivery is located afterwards on the email deliveries surface.

status.description: Always `queued`: the acknowledgement states that the email was accepted and queued, never that it was delivered. Delivery is observed afterwards through the email deliveries surface.

StockTransferEmailDelivery.title: StockTransferEmailDelivery

StockTransferLine.description: A line of a stock transfer: ONE item travelling between the two warehouses. It carries QUANTITIES and no amount, and the three of them are decimal strings with FOUR decimal places — the scale of the quantities of the catalog, never the two-decimal scale of money, because a transfer has no price to round.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the line, a UUID v7. It is the key the reception addresses: the body of `POST .../receive` says how much of EACH line arrived.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of the item being transferred. It travels as an identifier and NOT with its name or its SKU: resolving those would only serve presentation, and the contract already publishes the detail of the item in its own resource.

product_variant_id.description: Opaque identifier of the variant. This key is ABSENT — not `null` — when the line does not pin one.

quantity_dispatched.description: Quantity that left the origin warehouse, as a decimal string with four decimal places.

quantity_received.description: Quantity received at the destination so far, with the same scale. Receiving ADDS to it, so the same line can be received several times until it is complete, and never above what was dispatched.

quantity_pending.description: What is still on its way: dispatched minus received, floored at zero, with the same scale. It is DERIVED by the read model and never stored, so there is a single definition of what is pending and the two representations of the line cannot disagree.

StockTransferLine.title: StockTransferLine

StockTransferStatusItem.description: A stock transfer status from the closed catalog, with its label and what it allows. Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/stock-transfers/statuses` as a flat list. The catalog enumerates STATUSES and not transition targets: `draft` is in it and is the target of no transition at all.

value.description: Status token. It is the identity of the status: a token of a closed catalog, not a row of any table.

label.description: Label of the status in Spanish, ready to display.

permissions.description: What the status admits over the transfer, answered by its state machine. The vocabulary is the one of THIS family —the three transitions plus editing— and not the one of the warehouse master: there is no `delete`, because a live transfer is CANCELLED and never erased.

edit.description: Whether the status admits adding or removing lines. Only `draft` does: once dispatched, what the document says is what left through the door.

dispatch.description: Whether the status admits dispatching the transfer. Only `draft` does.

receive.description: Whether the status admits receiving goods against the transfer. Only `dispatched` does.

cancel.description: Whether the status admits cancelling the transfer. `draft` and `dispatched` do; the two terminal statuses do not.

StockTransferStatusItem.title: StockTransferStatusItem

Store.description: A connected e-commerce store of your company. The public `id` is the store UUID v7. `integration_id` is the UUID of the provider connection that backs it, and `external_store_id` is the identifier the provider gives to the shop — an opaque string, not a foreign key of ours. The settings decide how the orders of the store become invoices.

id.description: UUID v7 of the store. Public identity (KEY `id`).

object.description: Stripe-like discriminator. Always `store` for this resource.

integration_id.description: UUID of the provider connection (integration) that backs the store. Several stores of the same provider may hang from one connection.

external_store_id.description: Identifier the provider gives to the shop. Unique per provider within your company; an opaque string, NOT a foreign key of ours.

name.description: Editable display name of the store.

simplified_threshold.description: Order total, in EUROS, up to which the store issues a simplified invoice (F2). Capped at 3000.00, the legal maximum. Defaults to 400.00, the general legal limit.

require_tax_id.description: Whether the buyer tax ID is required for an order to be invoiced. Defaults to `false`: a retail store sells to consumers who do not provide one.

prices_include_tax.description: Whether the prices of the store already include taxes. Defaults to `true`, which is how Spanish retail displays prices.

autoinvoicing_enabled.description: Whether paid orders are invoiced automatically. Defaults to `false`: a freshly connected store does not invoice on its own until you turn it on.

autosend_enabled.description: Whether the invoice is emailed to the buyer automatically. Defaults to `false`.

remote_base_url.description: Base address of the remote shop, or `null` when none is declared. Credentials embedded in the address are removed before it is returned.

environment.description: Environment the store reports as. `live` invoices for real; `test` discards its events with a typed reason. Defaults to `test`.

status.description: Store status. `active` while connected; `disconnected` after disconnecting.

connected_at.description: When the store was connected (ISO 8601), or `null` if unknown.

invoice_note.example: Pedido pagado en la tienda online. Gracias por su compra.
invoice_note.description: Optional note written in the notes of the invoices auto-created from this store's orders, or `null` when none is configured (the default: invoices carry no note). When an order needed a currency conversion to EUR, the conversion trace is appended to the note. Editable with `PATCH /v1/companies/{company}/stores/{store}`; `null` or an empty string clears it.

Store.title: Store

StoreProductLink.description: The link between an item of your catalog and the object that represents it in an online store. It is a READ-ONLY sub-resource of the store: the link is created and repaired by the synchronisation, never through this API, because a second way of writing it would create a second truth about what is published where.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the link, a UUID v7.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of your own item.

variant_id.description: Opaque identifier of your own variant. This key is ABSENT — not `null` — when the link targets the whole item.

external_product_id.description: The item in the store, as the STORE identifies it. It travels as an opaque string and exactly as the platform returns it. It is `null` —and the key does travel— while the link is claimed and its remote identity has not been sealed yet.

external_variant_id.description: The variant in the store. This key is ABSENT when the platform or the item does not tell variants apart.

external_inventory_item_id.description: The inventory unit in the store. This key is ABSENT when the platform does not tell it apart from the variant.

status.description: State of the link: `linked` (paired both ways), `pending` (claimed, waiting for the remote identity) and `conflict` (the pairing is ambiguous and a person has to settle it).

link_source.description: How the link came to be: `auto_reference` (matched by reference), `manual` (paired by a person) and `created_by_push` (the object was created in the store by our own push).

conflict_reason.description: Why the link ended up in conflict. This key is ABSENT when there is no conflict.

catalog_pushed_at.description: Last time the product sheet was pushed to the store (ISO 8601). This key is ABSENT when it never was.

price_pushed_at.description: Last time the price was pushed (ISO 8601). This key is ABSENT when it never was.

inventory_pushed_at.description: Last time the stock figure was pushed (ISO 8601). This key is ABSENT when it never was.

StoreProductLink.title: StoreProductLink

StorefrontAddress.description: A postal address of the buyer. Its five keys ALWAYS travel, `null` on the ones that are not filled in: an address with half its fields empty is a real state, not a different shape.

address_line.description: Street, number and any additional detail, or `null`.

StorefrontAddress.title: StorefrontAddress

StorefrontAvailability.description: What the buyer is allowed to know about the stock of an item: ONE figure, the available total. It is the physical stock MINUS what live reservations already hold, so it is what can still be sold and not what is in the building. There is NO breakdown per warehouse, and its absence is the contract and not an omission: how many warehouses a merchant has and how the goods are spread across them is information about the merchant, and this credential travels in the browser of an anonymous visitor. Neither the physical quantity, nor the committed one, nor the reorder point, nor the cost, nor the supplier are published.

object.description: Always `storefront_availability`. It opens the body because an availability has no identity of its own: it is the answer about an item at an instant.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of the item that was asked about.

variant_id.description: Opaque identifier of the variant that holds the stock, or `null` when the stock target is the item itself.

available_total.description: Available units, as a decimal string with four decimal places: the physical stock minus what live reservations hold. It is a string and never a floating-point number. It is a figure at an INSTANT and not a promise: if it drops below what was asked for between this read and the order, the order is rejected naming the line that no longer fits.

stock_managed.description: Whether the item is managed by stock. In `false` the shop window offers it without a ceiling and MUST NOT read the figure as a limit: an item that is not managed by stock never runs out.

StorefrontAvailability.title: StorefrontAvailability

StorefrontAvailabilityResult.description: One entry of a batch availability query, addressed by the INDEX of the selection that was sent. Same contract as the batch price: one entry per selection sent, in the same order, and a selection that does not resolve comes back with its reason without invalidating the rest.

index.description: Position of the selection in the request, counting from zero.

error_code.description: Token saying why this selection could not be resolved, or `null` when it was. A selection pointing at an item of another company answers as a resource that does not exist, exactly like one that never existed.

error_message.description: Message explaining that failure, in Spanish, or `null`.

StorefrontAvailabilityResult.title: StorefrontAvailabilityResult

StorefrontBuyer.description: Identity of the buyer, the same shape on the cart and on the order it becomes. The fiscal identifier is OPTIONAL and its key is ABSENT —not `null`— when there is none: a private individual without one is not a buyer with an empty field, it is a buyer this lane does not ask it of, and without it the order is born with no commercial contact attached. Neither the IP of the buyer nor any browser tracking identifier is published or stored anywhere in this lane.

name.description: Name of the buyer. It is required to be able to serve the order.

email.description: Email address of the buyer. It is required to tell them about their order, and it is used for nothing else without explicit consent.

tax_id.description: Fiscal identifier of the buyer. This key is ABSENT —never `null` and never an empty string— when the buyer has none. Turning an order without it into a COMPLETE invoice is what gets rejected later, not placing the order.

StorefrontBuyer.title: StorefrontBuyer

StorefrontBuyerOrder.description: The order as the BUYER is shown it in their own window, opened with the public link the seller gave them. It is the SAME sales order the merchant works with, published with the eleven keys the buyer is allowed to see: what they ordered, what it costs, where the order stands, where its collection stands and which invoice was issued for it. The identity of the buyer is NOT republished here —whoever opens the window already knows who they are, and repeating their fiscal identity and their addresses on every read would put them in a response the browser caches for nothing—, and neither is the status of the public link, which is what the SERVER uses to decide whether to serve the order at all.

id.description: Public identifier of the order, a UUID v7. It is the key the buyer keeps, and the one every operation of this window addresses. No internal numeric key is ever published.

number.description: Readable number of the order, or `null` while it has not been numbered. An absent number is never invented: it is not a provisional one and it is not an empty string.

order_date.description: Date of the order, as a plain calendar date and not a timestamp.

lines.description: Lines of the order, each with the amount the server froze when it was placed.

subtotal.description: Sum of the line totals, before tax, as a decimal string with two decimal places.

tax_total.description: Total tax of the order, with the same scale. It is the DIFFERENCE between the total and the base, and not the VAT alone: published as the VAT, an order with withholding would show the buyer three figures that do not add up.

total.description: Total with tax, with the same scale. It is the figure that gets charged.

currency.description: Currency of the three amounts, as an ISO code.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the ORDER. It is the same axis the merchant sees, published as a token so the shop window can tell the buyer where their order is without inventing a vocabulary of its own. A cancelled order is not served through this window at all.

payment_status.description: What the system REMEMBERS about the collection of this order: `not_started` (no payment link has been asked for yet), `link_issued` (a payment session is live and the buyer has not come back from it), `verified` (the gateway confirmed the money and issuing the invoice was rejected), `paid` (invoice issued and a payment recorded against it) and `simulated` (the company is in test mode, so the lane ran end to end with no real effect). In THIS window only `not_started` and `paid` are ever observed, and that is a property of what is stored rather than a simplification: `link_issued` lives in the cache of the payment link, `verified` is money taken with no document to record it against, and `simulated` is a test company where there is no session, no invoice and no payment. Those three are published by the operation that has just produced them — `simulated` by the payment link, and `verified`, `simulated` or `paid` by the confirmation.

invoice.description: Reference to the invoice issued for the order, or `null` while there is none. An order can be paid and still have no invoice —the money was taken and issuing the document was rejected—, and in that case this key is `null` and `payment_status` says `verified`.

StorefrontBuyerOrder.title: StorefrontBuyerOrder

StorefrontBuyerOrderLine.description: One line of the order as the BUYER is shown it: what was ordered, how much of it, at what unit amount and for what line total. The amount is the one the server FROZE when the order was placed, so later moves of the catalog or of the price list do not rewrite what the buyer agreed to pay. It carries NO catalog identifiers —item, variant, presentation or combination—: the storefront already received them in the response that created the order, and republishing them from this window would widen the surface with nothing asking for it. No cost, no margin, no supplier, no warehouse and no internal key either.

description.description: Description of what was ordered, frozen with the order. Without it a line is a figure with no subject.
description.example: Aceite de oliva virgen extra D.O. — garrafa de 5 L
examples: Aceite de oliva virgen extra D.O. — garrafa de 5 L

quantity.description: Commercial quantity ordered, as a decimal string with four decimal places.

unit_price.description: Unit amount FROZEN by the server when the order was placed, as a decimal string with four decimal places. Never the one a browser sent.

line_total.description: Total of the line before tax, as a decimal string with two decimal places.

tax_rate.description: Tax rate applied to the line as a decimal string, or `null` when the line carries no tax.

StorefrontBuyerOrderLine.title: StorefrontBuyerOrderLine

StorefrontBuyerOrderWithContact.description: The order of the buyer right after completing their fiscal identity, plus the reference of the business contact that completion promoted. It is the SAME eleven keys of the order —so a storefront can paint the updated order without asking for it again— with one more that only this operation emits: a buyer who now carries a fiscal identity becomes a business contact of the seller, reused by tax id when it already exists, and the reference says which one so the storefront can name it.

id.description: Public identifier of the order, a UUID v7. It is the key the buyer keeps, and the one every operation of this window addresses. No internal numeric key is ever published.

number.description: Readable number of the order, or `null` while it has not been numbered. An absent number is never invented: it is not a provisional one and it is not an empty string.

order_date.description: Date of the order, as a plain calendar date and not a timestamp.

lines.description: Lines of the order, each with the amount the server froze when it was placed.

subtotal.description: Sum of the line totals, before tax, as a decimal string with two decimal places.

tax_total.description: Total tax of the order, with the same scale. It is the DIFFERENCE between the total and the base, and not the VAT alone: published as the VAT, an order with withholding would show the buyer three figures that do not add up.

total.description: Total with tax, with the same scale. It is the figure that gets charged.

currency.description: Currency of the three amounts, as an ISO code.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the ORDER. It is the same axis the merchant sees, published as a token so the shop window can tell the buyer where their order is without inventing a vocabulary of its own. A cancelled order is not served through this window at all.

payment_status.description: What the system REMEMBERS about the collection of this order: `not_started` (no payment link has been asked for yet), `link_issued` (a payment session is live and the buyer has not come back from it), `verified` (the gateway confirmed the money and issuing the invoice was rejected), `paid` (invoice issued and a payment recorded against it) and `simulated` (the company is in test mode, so the lane ran end to end with no real effect). In THIS window only `not_started` and `paid` are ever observed, and that is a property of what is stored rather than a simplification: `link_issued` lives in the cache of the payment link, `verified` is money taken with no document to record it against, and `simulated` is a test company where there is no session, no invoice and no payment. Those three are published by the operation that has just produced them — `simulated` by the payment link, and `verified`, `simulated` or `paid` by the confirmation.

invoice.description: Reference to the invoice issued for the order, or `null` while there is none. An order can be paid and still have no invoice —the money was taken and issuing the document was rejected—, and in that case this key is `null` and `payment_status` says `verified`.

id.description: Public identifier of the business contact, a UUID v7. Never its internal key.

business_contact.description: Reference to the business contact of the buyer, or `null` when this update promoted nobody. `null` is the normal answer for a private individual with no fiscal identity and for an order below the threshold that requires a full invoice: a business contact needs a fiscal identity, and inventing one from a name would put a contact with no tax id in the address book of the seller.

StorefrontBuyerOrderWithContact.title: StorefrontBuyerOrderWithContact

StorefrontCatalogSelection.description: What the buyer has chosen so far, resolved against the catalog: which variant, which presentation and which combination it lands on, what is still missing and whether it can be offered at all. This operation ANSWERS instead of failing — a combination that cannot be offered comes back with its flag in `false` and its reason, and the status is still 200 — because a shop window has to be able to grey out an option, not to handle an error while the buyer is still choosing. The refusal with an error belongs to the operations that CONFIRM.

object.description: Always `storefront_catalog_selection`. It opens the body because a resolution has no identity of its own: it is the answer to what was asked, not a stored record.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of the item the selection is about.

variant_id.description: Opaque identifier of the resolved variant, or `null` when the selection does not land on one.

presentation_id.description: Opaque identifier of the resolved presentation, or `null`.

configuration_id.description: Opaque identifier of the resolved combination, or `null` while the selection is not complete. It is the value the cart line keeps, so what was offered and what is ordered are the same combination.

selected_options.description: What the buyer has already chosen, normalised as pairs of group and value.

pending_option_groups.description: What is still to be chosen: the group and its name, so the shop window can ask for it by name without reading the sheet again. Empty list when nothing is pending.

group_id.description: Opaque identifier of the option group still to be answered.

group_name.description: Name of that group, ready to display.

offerable.description: Whether the combination can be offered. Only then does asking for its price make sense, and only then can it be added to a cart.

complete.description: Whether the selection is complete: no required group is left to answer. A selection can be complete and still not offerable — the combination exists and the merchant has withdrawn it — and the two flags are published apart precisely so a shop window can tell those two cases apart.

exact_list_policy.description: Whether the company only offers the combinations it has listed one by one. In `false` the crossing of groups is open except where a restriction says otherwise, so an unlisted combination is still offerable.

reason_code.description: Why the combination cannot be offered, out of the closed set of selection reasons of the catalog (they all start with `catalog_selection_`), or `null` when it can. It is published as a token so a shop window can map it to its own copy instead of showing a sentence it did not write.

StorefrontCatalogSelection.title: StorefrontCatalogSelection

StorefrontCategory.description: One category of the shop window, with how many publishable items carry it. It is the classification the merchant already uses on the catalog, published with a stable identifier so a shop window can build a menu out of it and filter the listing with the same value it rendered. The count only counts PUBLISHABLE items: a category whose items are all withdrawn publishes zero, and that is the honest answer.

id.description: Stable identifier of the category. It is exactly the value the `category` filter of the listing takes.

name.description: Name of the category as the merchant wrote it.

product_count.description: Publishable items of the company that carry this category. It is a COUNT and not an identifier.

StorefrontCategory.title: StorefrontCategory

StorefrontCategoryRef.description: Reference to one category of the shop window from inside an item: its stable identifier and its name, and nothing else. The count of items of the category travels only in the category catalog, where it means something; repeating it on every item would publish the same figure as many times as items the page shows.

id.description: Stable identifier of the category. It is the value the `category` filter of the listing accepts, so what the item publishes and what the filter takes are the same string.

name.description: Name of the category as the merchant wrote it.

StorefrontCategoryRef.title: StorefrontCategoryRef

StorefrontCheckoutConfirmation.description: The outcome of confirming the collection of an order: where the collection stands, where the order stands and which invoice was issued. A guard that is NOT met is not an error and has no public code: when the payment session cannot be read, is not paid, or does not belong to THAT order, nothing is marked and this same body publishes the CURRENT situation of the order — there is no "reason" key on purpose, because publishing one would turn the answer into an oracle for finding out, by trying session identifiers, which one belongs to which order. The reason is logged instead, with the order and the session and with no data of the credential or of the means of payment. Confirming is repeatable: the same confirmation twice records one single payment and answers the same thing.

payment_status.description: Status of the COLLECTION after the confirmation, out of the same five-value catalog the order publishes. `paid` is the ordinary outcome —money taken, invoice issued and payment recorded against it—; `verified` is money taken with the issuing REJECTED (an overlap with recurring invoicing, an incomplete buyer identity, an exhausted series), which is a legitimate outcome published as it is instead of inventing an intermediate state; `simulated` is a company in test mode, where the lane runs end to end and produces no effect. A guard that is not met publishes here whatever the order already was.

order_status.description: Status of the ORDER after the confirmation, out of the same catalog its own window publishes.

invoice.description: Reference to the invoice issued on confirming, or `null` when none was issued. `null` with `payment_status` in `verified` is the money taken with the document rejected, and `null` with `simulated` is the test company: in neither case is an invoice invented, and `paid` is never said over an order with no invoice.

StorefrontCheckoutConfirmation.title: StorefrontCheckoutConfirmation

StorefrontKey.description: A publishable credential of the shop window: the key the web shop of the merchant carries in the browser of an anonymous visitor to read the catalog and operate the cart. It is PUBLIC by design —anyone who opens the shop can read it— which is why it is fenced by the origins it may be used from, why it only carries the permissions of the buyer lane, and why it can be revoked and rotated without touching anything else. This representation never carries the secret: the secret is shown once, at issuing or after rotation, and never again.

object.description: Always `storefront_key`. It is the same resource whether it was just issued or only read: what changes between the two is one field, not the kind of object.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the publishable credential, a UUID v7. It is the key every operation of this resource addresses; the row of the table is never published.

name.description: Name the merchant recognises the credential by in their panel.

prefix.description: VISIBLE prefix of the secret (for example `sf_pk_live_9f2c5a8e`). It is the only part of the secret that is kept, and it exists so a credential can be identified afterwards in a log or in a panel. It does NOT authenticate on its own.

allowed_origins.description: Web origins the browser is allowed to use this credential from. It is the fence of a credential that travels in public: a request coming from an origin that is not on this list is rejected, so a copied credential does not work outside the shop window it was issued for.

scopes.description: Permissions of the buyer lane the credential carries (`storefront:read` to read the shop window, `storefront:write` to operate the cart and place the order). It can never carry the permissions that MANAGE credentials: those belong to the merchant with their integration key, not to a credential that runs in the browser of an anonymous visitor. `GET /storefront-keys/scopes` publishes the whole assignable set.

status.description: Status of the credential: `active` or `revoked`. Revoking is TERMINAL —a revoked credential is never brought back— and it is published as its own axis because a credential can also stop working by expiring, which is a different fact.

expires_at.description: Expiry instant (ISO 8601), or `null` when the credential does not expire.

last_used_at.description: Last observed use (ISO 8601), or `null` while it has never been used. It is what tells a credential that is still in service from one that can be retired.

last_used_origin.description: Origin the last use was observed from, or `null`. It is published because it is what turns "somebody is using this" into "somebody is using this from where I expected".

rotated_at.description: Last rotation of the secret (ISO 8601), or `null` while it still holds the original one.

revoked_at.description: Revocation instant (ISO 8601), or `null` while the credential is alive.

revoke_reason.description: Reason the credential was revoked, when one was given, or `null`.

is_active.description: Whether it can authenticate TODAY: neither revoked nor expired. It is DERIVED from the status and the expiry, so the two representations of the same credential cannot disagree.

StorefrontKey.title: StorefrontKey

StorefrontKeyList.description: Cursor-paginated page of publishable credentials of the company (`{ data, has_more, next_cursor }`). No element of the page carries a secret or a fingerprint, and it is not a matter of remembering to strip them: what the listing carries has nowhere to hold them.

data.description: Page of publishable credentials, published exactly like the read by identifier: the listing and the detail cannot diverge in shape.

has_more.description: `true` when there are more credentials beyond this page.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or `null` when there is none left.

StorefrontKeyList.title: StorefrontKeyList

StorefrontKeyWithSecret.description: A publishable credential returned ONCE, at issuing or right after rotating its secret. It is the same credential the read publishes plus the plaintext `secret`: store it now, because it cannot be retrieved later —what is kept of it is its visible prefix and a fingerprint that never travels—. The secret appears exactly once in the body and under no second name, so there is only one place a consumer can copy it from.

object.description: Always `storefront_key`. It is the same resource whether it was just issued or only read: what changes between the two is one field, not the kind of object.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the publishable credential, a UUID v7. It is the key every operation of this resource addresses; the row of the table is never published.

name.description: Name the merchant recognises the credential by in their panel.

prefix.description: VISIBLE prefix of the secret (for example `sf_pk_live_9f2c5a8e`). It is the only part of the secret that is kept, and it exists so a credential can be identified afterwards in a log or in a panel. It does NOT authenticate on its own.

allowed_origins.description: Web origins the browser is allowed to use this credential from. It is the fence of a credential that travels in public: a request coming from an origin that is not on this list is rejected, so a copied credential does not work outside the shop window it was issued for.

scopes.description: Permissions of the buyer lane the credential carries (`storefront:read` to read the shop window, `storefront:write` to operate the cart and place the order). It can never carry the permissions that MANAGE credentials: those belong to the merchant with their integration key, not to a credential that runs in the browser of an anonymous visitor. `GET /storefront-keys/scopes` publishes the whole assignable set.

status.description: Status of the credential: `active` or `revoked`. Revoking is TERMINAL —a revoked credential is never brought back— and it is published as its own axis because a credential can also stop working by expiring, which is a different fact.

expires_at.description: Expiry instant (ISO 8601), or `null` when the credential does not expire.

last_used_at.description: Last observed use (ISO 8601), or `null` while it has never been used. It is what tells a credential that is still in service from one that can be retired.

last_used_origin.description: Origin the last use was observed from, or `null`. It is published because it is what turns "somebody is using this" into "somebody is using this from where I expected".

rotated_at.description: Last rotation of the secret (ISO 8601), or `null` while it still holds the original one.

revoked_at.description: Revocation instant (ISO 8601), or `null` while the credential is alive.

revoke_reason.description: Reason the credential was revoked, when one was given, or `null`.

is_active.description: Whether it can authenticate TODAY: neither revoked nor expired. It is DERIVED from the status and the expiry, so the two representations of the same credential cannot disagree.

secret.description: FULL plaintext secret. Delivered once and never recoverable: rotating issues a new one and kills the previous one on the spot, which is why rotation is published as irreversible. `null` only in an idempotent replay of that creation or rotation, because the secret is never stored.

StorefrontKeyWithSecret.title: StorefrontKeyWithSecret

StorefrontOrder.description: The order placed from the shop window. It is the SAME sales order the merchant works with afterwards, published with what the buyer is allowed to see: no price list, no margin, no supplier and no internal note. Placing it is NOT irreversible —an order can be cancelled— but it is the point where the cart stops being editable, so what it publishes is what the buyer agreed to: their identity, their lines with the amount the server froze, and their totals.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the order, a UUID v7. It is what the buyer keeps to ask about their order afterwards.

number.description: Readable number of the order, or `null` while it has not been numbered. An absent number is never invented: it is not a provisional one and it is not an empty string.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the order. It is the same axis the merchant sees, published as a token so the shop window can tell the buyer where their order is without inventing a vocabulary of its own.

channel.description: Origin the order came in through, always `storefront` here. The value travels because it is what tells this order apart from the ones born by hand, from a connected shop, from the integration API or from a quote: the origin of an order is history and no operation accepts it afterwards.

external_id.description: External key of the system that originated the order, unique per company, or `null`. It is the idempotency of the BUSINESS —sending the same order twice with the same key updates the one that exists instead of creating a second one— and it is a different thing from the per-request idempotency key.

order_date.description: Date of the order, as a plain calendar date and not a timestamp.

expected_delivery_date.description: Date the goods are expected to be delivered, as a plain calendar date, or `null` when none was agreed.

lines.description: Lines of the order, each with the amount the server froze when it was placed.

example.description: Aceite de oliva virgen extra D.O. — garrafa de 5 L
Aceite de oliva virgen extra — botella 1 L

examples.description: Aceite de oliva virgen extra D.O. — garrafa de 5 L
Aceite de oliva virgen extra — botella 1 L

subtotal.description: Sum of the line totals, before tax, as a decimal string with two decimal places.

tax_total.description: Total tax of the order, with the same scale.

total.description: Total with tax, with the same scale.

currency.description: Currency of the three amounts, as an ISO code.

marketing_consent.description: Whether the buyer EXPLICITLY consented to commercial communications. It is never presumed from having given an email address: an email is how the buyer is told about their order, and nothing else without this flag.

session_id.description: Opaque identifier of the cart the order came from, or `null` when it was placed without one.

StorefrontOrder.title: StorefrontOrder

StorefrontOrderInvoiceRef.description: Reference to the invoice issued for the order: its public identifier and its readable number, and nothing else. It travels as ONE object and never as two loose keys, because an order with no invoice has neither: two parallel null keys invite publishing one without the other. The internal key of the invoice is never published, and neither is its status — the invoice of an order is a document of the seller and what the buyer needs from it is how to name it.

id.description: Public identifier of the issued invoice, a UUID v7.

number.description: Readable number of the issued invoice, as it was stamped by its series.

StorefrontOrderInvoiceRef.title: StorefrontOrderInvoiceRef

StorefrontOrderLine.description: One line of the order placed from the shop window, with its amount FROZEN at the moment the order was placed. Freezing is the point: later moves of the catalog or of the price list do not rewrite what the buyer agreed to pay.

id.description: Public identity of the order line. No internal numeric key is published, not of the line and not of its order.

description.description: Description of what was ordered, frozen with the order.
description.example: Aceite de oliva virgen extra D.O. — garrafa de 5 L
examples: Aceite de oliva virgen extra D.O. — garrafa de 5 L

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of the item, or `null` on a line with no catalog item behind it.

variant_id.description: Opaque identifier of the variant, or `null`.

presentation_id.description: Opaque identifier of the presentation, or `null`.

configuration_id.description: Opaque identifier of the configurable combination, or `null`.

selected_options.description: Configurable values chosen for this line, normalised as pairs of group and value.

quantity.description: Commercial quantity ordered, as a decimal string with four decimal places.

unit_price.description: Unit amount FROZEN by the server when the order was placed, as a decimal string with four decimal places. Never the one a browser sent.

line_total.description: Total of the line before tax, as a decimal string with two decimal places.

tax_rate.description: Tax rate applied to the line as a decimal string, or `null` when the line carries no tax.

StorefrontOrderLine.title: StorefrontOrderLine

StorefrontOrderTracking.description: Where the SHIPMENT of an order is, as the buyer is shown it. The eight keys ALWAYS travel: an order with no shipment yet answers with `has_shipment` in `false`, the six data keys in `null` and `package_count` in `0`, and that is a SUCCESS and not an error — answering "not found" would confuse "there is no shipment yet" with "that order does not exist", and the buyer who has just paid would read the second one. When several shipments have gone out for the same order, what travels is the most recent one. It carries no source warehouse, no picking list, no delivery signature, no personal data of whoever received the goods, no shipping cost and not even the identifier of the delivery note: the buyer bought an order, not a delivery note, and the document of the seller is not theirs.

has_shipment.description: Whether the order already has a shipment. `false` is the EXPLICIT mark of the empty variant, so a storefront can say "not shipped yet" without deducing it from six nulls.

status.description: Status of the shipment out of the closed catalog of the physical cycle, or `null` when there is no shipment.

status_label.description: That same status in Spanish, resolved on the SERVER so the storefront does not duplicate the catalog and leave its copy stale the day it grows. `null` when there is no shipment.

carrier.description: Readable name of the carrier, taken from the carrier master when the shipment references one and from the free text the delivery note keeps when it does not. ONE name travels and not the two sources: publishing both would ask the buyer to choose. `null` when there is no shipment or no carrier on it.

expected_delivery_date.description: Date the goods are expected to be delivered, as a plain calendar date, or `null` when none was agreed.

tracking_number.description: Tracking number of the carrier, or `null` when the shipment has none.

tracking_url.description: Tracking address, DERIVED on every read from the template of the carrier and the tracking number, or `null`. It travels whole or not at all: half an address is worse than none, and a carrier whose tracking is manual or provided by the shop has no template to compose.

package_count.description: Number of packages declared for the shipment. A shipment with none declared publishes `0`, which is true, and not `null`, which would invite painting "unknown" where what there is is "none declared".

StorefrontOrderTracking.title: StorefrontOrderTracking

StorefrontPaymentLink.description: The payment link issued for an order: where to send the buyer, until when it works and whether the effect was simulated. Asking twice for the link of the same order does NOT create two payment sessions while the first one is still live: the second call returns the same address. The identifier of the gateway session is deliberately NOT published — the storefront receives it from the gateway itself on the return, and putting it in a body the browser stores would publish exactly what legitimises confirming a collection.

url.description: Address of the payment session to send the buyer to. Always over a secure scheme: the value object of the issued link rejects anything else.

expires_at.description: Instant (ISO 8601) until which that address keeps working. It stays BELOW the life the gateway gives its own session, because publishing a longer validity would promise an address that no longer exists.

simulated.description: Whether the effect was SIMULATED because the company is in test mode. It is part of the published contract and not an implementation detail: a simulated link is not a link that is missing, it is a link that exists and does not charge, so the storefront can say "this was a simulation" instead of deducing test mode from a gap. In a company that is not in test mode it travels `false` and never disappears.

StorefrontPaymentLink.title: StorefrontPaymentLink

StorefrontPrice.description: The price of a selection FOR THIS BUYER, resolved by the server. It is the only price that counts: whatever a browser sends as an amount is discarded, and the cart and the order keep what this resolution returned. What the merchant sees behind it —which price list won, the amount of the source, the breakdown of the option adjustments, whether they were absorbed and which resolver answered— is NOT published: it is the commercial policy of the merchant and it would travel in the browser of an anonymous visitor.

object.description: Always `storefront_price`. It opens the body because a resolved price has no identity of its own.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of the item the price belongs to.

variant_id.description: Opaque identifier of the variant of the resolved target, or `null`.

presentation_id.description: Opaque identifier of the presentation of the resolved target, or `null`.

configuration_id.description: Opaque identifier of the resolved configurable combination, or `null`.

unit_price.description: Unit amount resolved by the SERVER, as a decimal string with four decimal places — the scale of the quantities and unit prices of the selling side. It is a string and never a floating-point number, and it is always the multiplicand of the commercial quantity: nobody multiplies it again by the conversion factor.

currency.description: Currency of the amounts, as an ISO code.

price_unit_code.description: Unit the unit amount refers to, out of the closed catalog of units of measure.

unit_semantics.description: Where the unit amount came from: `per_base_unit` (per base unit of the item) or `per_commercial_unit` (per commercial unit of the presentation). It describes the SOURCE and not the amount, so a shop window can label "€/L" or "€/drum" without recomputing anything.

quantity.description: Quantity the total was computed for, as a decimal string with four decimal places.

line_total.description: Total of the line before tax, as a decimal string with two decimal places — the scale of the totals of the selling side.

StorefrontPrice.title: StorefrontPrice

StorefrontPriceResult.description: One entry of a batch price resolution, addressed by the INDEX of the selection that was sent. The batch answers a whole cart in one request and a selection that cannot be resolved does NOT invalidate the rest: it comes back in its own entry with its reason, and the others carry their price. The index is the only thing that ties an entry to the line the caller sent, which is why the answer never comes back compacted.

index.description: Position of the selection in the request, counting from zero. Entries travel for EVERY selection sent, resolved or not, and in the same order.

error_code.description: Token saying why this selection could not be resolved, or `null` when it was. A selection pointing at an item of another company answers exactly like one pointing at an item that does not exist: from outside, the two are indistinguishable.

error_message.description: Message explaining that failure, in Spanish, or `null` when the selection resolved.

StorefrontPriceResult.title: StorefrontPriceResult

StorefrontProduct.description: The full sheet of an item of the shop window: the fourteen keys of its row plus its four collections —variants, presentations, option groups and gallery— so a product page can be painted with ONE read instead of five. The four collections carry exactly what the sub-collection operations return, so reading the sheet and reading its parts can never disagree.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the item, a UUID v7. No internal numeric key is ever published.

sku.description: Commercial reference of the item, or `null` when the merchant does not use one.

name.description: Name of the item as the merchant wrote it.
name.example: Aceite de oliva virgen extra D.O.
examples: Aceite de oliva virgen extra D.O.

description.description: Publishable description of the item, or `null`.
description.example: Aceite de oliva virgen extra de cosecha temprana, extraído en frío y envasado en origen.
examples: Aceite de oliva virgen extra de cosecha temprana, extraído en frío y envasado en origen.

categories.description: Categories the item belongs to. An empty list is a legitimate state.

base_unit_code.description: Code of the base unit of measure of the item, out of the closed catalog of units.

item_kind.description: Nature of the item: `product` for goods and `service` for services.

primary_image_url.description: Absolute URL of the main image, or `null`.

stock_managed.description: Whether the item is managed by stock. The FIGURE of available units is published only by the availability operation, never here.

has_variants.description: Whether the item has variants. It is the same fact the `variants` collection shows, published as a flag so a client can branch without walking a list.

has_presentations.description: Whether the item has commercial presentations.

has_options.description: Whether the item has configurable option groups.

variants.description: Publishable variants of the item, so the page does not need a second read to render the selector. Empty list when it has none.

presentations.description: Publishable commercial presentations, with the unit semantics the shop window needs to label a price. Empty list when it has none.

options.description: Configurable option groups with their eligible values, already ordered. Empty list when the item is not configurable.

images.description: Publishable gallery of the item, in order, with the main image flagged. Empty list when it has none.

StorefrontProduct.title: StorefrontProduct

StorefrontProductImage.description: One image of the gallery of an item, with an absolute URL the browser of the buyer can load directly. There is no image table behind it: the gallery is an ordered list of the item, so the identifier of an image is stable within its item and nowhere else.

id.description: Stable public identity of the image inside its item. It is NOT a UUID and it is not a row of any table: there is no internal key to publish, so the identity is composed of the item and the position the image occupies.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of the item the image belongs to.

url.description: Absolute URL of the image, servable by the browser of the buyer.

alt.description: Alternative text of the image, or `null` when there is none. It is published even empty because it is what an accessible shop window needs, and inventing one from the name of the item would put the same text on every picture.

position.description: Position of the image in the gallery, so two reads render it in the same order.

is_primary.description: Whether this is the main image of the item — the one published as `primary_image_url` on the row and on the sheet.

StorefrontProductImage.title: StorefrontProductImage

StorefrontProductOption.description: One configurable option group of an item, with the values the buyer can choose from. What the buyer picks is a value of each group; the combination of all of them is what the selection resolution turns into an offerable item. A group whose values are all withdrawn is not published: an option nobody can choose is not an option.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the option group, a UUID v7.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of the parent item.

name.description: Name of the group as the merchant wrote it.

required.description: Whether the buyer MUST choose a value of this group for the selection to be complete. A selection with a required group still pending is published as incomplete, with that group named, instead of being rejected.

position.description: Deterministic position of the group in the order the merchant set, so two reads render the same form.

scope_id.description: Opaque identifier of the variant or presentation the group is narrowed to, or `null` when it applies to the whole item. A group narrowed to something that is not published does not travel at all: it is dropped whole, never published pointing at something the buyer cannot see.

values.description: Eligible values of the group, already in their order. The withdrawn ones are not here: the list is what can be chosen right now.

items.description: One eligible value of the group. It has no discriminator of its own because it never travels outside its group: it is identified by the pair of group and value everywhere a choice is made.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the value, which is what travels as the chosen value of this group.

name.description: Name of the value, ready to display.

position.description: Deterministic position of the value inside its group.

price_adjustment.description: Adjustment this value adds to the price, as a decimal string, or `null` when it adds nothing. It is what the catalog declares; the price actually charged is always the one the price resolution returns, which already takes it into account.

StorefrontProductOption.title: StorefrontProductOption

StorefrontProductPresentation.description: One commercial presentation of an item: the format it is sold in (a case of twelve, a five-litre drum, loose weight). It is what decides the unit a price refers to, which is why it travels with its unit code and its conversion: without them a shop window cannot tell "€ per litre" from "€ per drum".

id.description: Opaque identifier of the presentation, a UUID v7. It travels in the cart line when the buyer picks a format.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of the parent item.

name.description: Commercial name of the presentation, as the merchant wrote it.

mode.description: How the presentation converts into base units: `fixed` (a closed format, a case of twelve) and `variable_measure` (a format measured at the till, loose weight). The mode is what tells apart a format whose content is known in advance from one that is weighed.

unit_code.description: Code of the commercial unit of the presentation, out of the closed catalog of units of measure.

conversion_factor.description: Base units contained in one commercial unit, as a decimal string, or `null` when the presentation does not convert. It is a string and never a floating-point number: it is a factor a price is derived from.

nominal_base_quantity.description: Nominal quantity in base units of the presentation, as a decimal string, or `null`. On a format measured at the till it is the declared nominal content, which is what a shop window shows before the real one is known.

specifications.description: Sheet attributes the merchant declared for this presentation, as free key-value pairs. Informational, not selectable. It travels empty when it has none.

StorefrontProductPresentation.title: StorefrontProductPresentation

StorefrontProductSummary.description: One row of the shop window: an item that the merchant publishes, with what a grid or a search result needs to paint it. It is the SAME item as the full sheet, seen with fourteen keys instead of eighteen — it does not carry the variants, the presentations, the option groups or the gallery, which are four collections per row and would turn a page of twenty items into eighty collections. Whoever needs them reads the sheet of the item, or its sub-collections one by one.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the item, a UUID v7. It is the key every other operation of the shop window addresses: the sheet, the price, the availability and the cart line. No internal numeric key is ever published.

sku.description: Commercial reference of the item, or `null` when the merchant does not use one. It is also the value the `sku` filter of the listing matches EXACTLY.

name.description: Name of the item as the merchant wrote it.
name.example: Aceite de oliva virgen extra D.O.
examples: Aceite de oliva virgen extra D.O.

description.description: Publishable description of the item, or `null`.
description.example: Aceite de oliva virgen extra de cosecha temprana, extraído en frío y envasado en origen.
examples: Aceite de oliva virgen extra de cosecha temprana, extraído en frío y envasado en origen.

categories.description: Categories the item belongs to. An item can be in several, and an empty list is a legitimate state: an uncategorised item is still published.

base_unit_code.description: Code of the base unit of measure of the item, out of the closed catalog of units (`C62` for units, `KGM`, `GRM`, `LTR`, `MLT`, `MTR`, `MTK`, `HUR`, `DAY`). It is the multiplicand of the quantity.

item_kind.description: Nature of the item: `product` for goods and `service` for services. A shop window can render both, and only goods are ever managed by stock.

primary_image_url.description: Absolute URL of the main image, servable by the browser of the buyer, or `null` when the item has no gallery.

stock_managed.description: Whether the item is managed by stock. It says WHETHER there is a figure, never WHAT the figure is: the number of available units is published only by the availability operation, so a listing cannot be used to scan the warehouse of the merchant item by item.

has_variants.description: Whether the item has variants. In `true`, the shop window knows it has to ask for the selector before the item can be added to the cart.

has_presentations.description: Whether the item has commercial presentations (a bottle, a case, loose weight), which is what decides the unit the price refers to.

has_options.description: Whether the item has configurable option groups. In `true`, the combination has to be resolved before asking for a price.

StorefrontProductSummary.title: StorefrontProductSummary

StorefrontProductVariant.description: One variant of an item of the shop window: the same article in another size, colour or finish, with its own reference and its own stock. Its price is NOT published here — it is asked for with the price resolution, because it depends on the quantity and on the presentation — and neither is its stock figure.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the variant, a UUID v7. It is what travels in the cart line when the buyer picks one.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of the parent item.

name.description: Name of the variant as the merchant wrote it.

sku.description: Commercial reference of the variant itself, or `null`.

stock_managed.description: Whether this variant is the one that holds the stock. When it is, the availability of the item has to be asked for naming the variant, because the figure belongs to it and not to the parent item.

specifications.description: Sheet attributes the merchant declared for the shop window (size, colour, finish), as free key-value pairs. It is informational and NOT selectable: what the buyer chooses are the option groups. It travels empty when the variant has none.

StorefrontProductVariant.title: StorefrontProductVariant

StorefrontRevalidation.description: The answer to "is my cart still valid?": the cart already brought up to date plus the verdict line by line. It carries the WHOLE cart —with the same shape its own read has— so the shop window can carry on without a second call, which is what makes it usable right before paying. The two summary flags are derived from the lines so a client does not have to walk them to know whether to warn the buyer.

object.description: Always `storefront_revalidation`. It opens the body because the result of revalidating has no identity of its own.

lines.description: Detail line by line, in the order of the cart. There is one entry per line, including the ones nothing happened to.

has_changes.description: Whether any line changed its amount. It is the flag a shop window hangs the "prices have changed" notice on.

all_sufficient.description: Whether every line still has enough units. In `false` the order will be rejected naming the first line that does not fit, so it is better to say so here.

StorefrontRevalidation.title: StorefrontRevalidation

StorefrontRevalidationLine.description: The verdict on one line of the cart after revalidating it: what it cost before, what it costs now, whether there are still enough units and whether the combination can still be offered. The three axes are published apart because they fail apart: a line can have gone up in price and still fit, and it can still be cheap and no longer be offered at all.

line_id.description: Public identity of the line inside the cart, the same one the cart publishes.

previous_unit_price.description: Unit amount the cart had FROZEN, as a decimal string with four decimal places, or `null` if none had ever been resolved.

unit_price.description: Unit amount the server resolves NOW, with the same scale, or `null` when the combination is no longer offerable and therefore has no price.

price_changed.description: Whether the amount moved between the two. It is the warning a shop window shows before paying, and it is derived here so the client does not have to compare decimal strings itself.

quantity.description: Quantity ordered in the line, as a decimal string with four decimal places.

available_total.description: Units available now, with the same scale, or `null` when the item is not managed by stock — which is not zero, it is "there is no ceiling here".

sufficient.description: Whether the current availability covers the quantity of the line. An item that is not managed by stock is always sufficient.

offerable.description: Whether the combination of the line can still be offered. In `false` the line cannot go into an order, whatever its price says.

reason_code.description: Why it can no longer be offered, or `null` when it still can. It carries the selection reasons of the catalog (all starting with `catalog_selection_`) and also `product_not_found`, which is the answer when the item stopped being published while it sat in the cart.

StorefrontRevalidationLine.title: StorefrontRevalidationLine

StorefrontSelectedOption.description: One configurable choice already made, normalised as a pair of group and value. The pair is the unit: a loose value would not say which group it answers, and two groups can offer values with the same name.

group_id.description: Opaque identifier of the option group the choice answers.

value_id.description: Opaque identifier of the chosen value inside that group.

StorefrontSelectedOption.title: StorefrontSelectedOption

StorefrontSession.description: The cart of an anonymous buyer: what they have picked, what it added up to the last time the server priced it, and who they say they are. Its identifier is unguessable and IS the only authorisation over it: whoever holds it can read and change it, and nobody else can. It does NOT hold stock — nothing is set aside for it — so what it shows can stop fitting, and that is what the revalidation is for. Expiry is NOT one of its statuses: it is derived from the expiry instant against the clock of the read, so no scheduled sweep is needed to make a cart stale.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the cart, a UUID v7, unguessable on purpose: it is the only authorisation over the cart, so it is never derived from anything the buyer typed.

status.description: Status of the cart: `open` (it can still be changed), `converted` (it became an order and is now history) and `abandoned` (given up). Expiry is NOT here: an expired cart stays `open` and publishes it through its own flag, because "it ran out of time" and "the buyer gave up" are different facts with different remedies.

lines.description: Lines of the cart, in their order, each with the LAST amount the server resolved for it.

example.product_name: Aceite de oliva virgen extra D.O.
Aceite de oliva virgen extra — botella 1 L

examples.product_name: Aceite de oliva virgen extra D.O.
Aceite de oliva virgen extra — botella 1 L

totals.description: Totals FROZEN at the last price resolution. They are not a promise of what will be charged: between this read and the order the catalog can move, which is exactly what the revalidation reports before paying.

subtotal.description: Sum of the line totals, before tax, as a decimal string with two decimal places. It is ALWAYS the sum of the lines: it cannot be set apart from them.

tax_total.description: Tax computed over those lines, with the same scale.

total.description: Total with tax, with the same scale.

currency.description: Currency of the three amounts, as an ISO code.

price_list_id.description: Opaque identifier of the price list applied to this lane, when the company has one declared, or `null`. Only the identifier travels: never its name and never its structure, which are the commercial policy of the merchant.

prices_resolved_at.description: When the prices of the cart were last resolved (ISO 8601), or `null` while none has been. It is what tells a stale total from a fresh one without comparing amounts.

expires_at.description: When the cart expires (ISO 8601). It is set when the cart is created, out of the lifetime the merchant configured, and it does not move every time the cart is read.

is_expired.description: Whether the cart is already past its expiry. It is DERIVED by comparing the expiry with the clock of this read, never stored: no background task has to run for an expired cart to say so.

converted_at.description: When the cart became an order (ISO 8601), or `null`.

sales_order_id.description: Opaque identifier of the order born from this cart, reported only once it is converted, or `null`. It is what lets a shop window recover the order after a reload without keeping anything of its own.

abandoned_at.description: When the cart was given up (ISO 8601), or `null`.

StorefrontSession.title: StorefrontSession

StorefrontSessionLine.description: One line of the cart: one selection with its quantity and the amount the SERVER resolved for it. The amounts are the ones the server put there and never the ones a browser sent: a line created with an amount of its own is rejected as a validation error before the cart is touched.

line_id.description: Stable public identity of the line inside its cart. It is the name the revalidation and the stock errors use, so "this line does not fit" points at one line and not at a position that moves when another is removed.

product_id.description: Opaque identifier of the item of the line.

variant_id.description: Opaque identifier of the chosen variant, or `null`.

presentation_id.description: Opaque identifier of the chosen presentation, or `null`.

configuration_id.description: Opaque identifier of the resolved configurable combination, or `null`.

selected_options.description: Configurable values chosen for this line, normalised as pairs of group and value.

quantity.description: Commercial quantity ordered, as a decimal string with four decimal places.

unit_price.description: Unit amount resolved by the server, as a decimal string with four decimal places, or `null` while no price has been resolved for the line yet.

line_total.description: Total of the line before tax, as a decimal string with two decimal places, or `null` while it has not been resolved.

product_name.description: Name of the item as it was rendered, so the cart can be shown without reading the catalog again.
product_name.example: Aceite de oliva virgen extra D.O.
examples: Aceite de oliva virgen extra D.O.

price_unit_code.description: Unit the unit amount refers to, out of the closed catalog of units of measure.

StorefrontSessionLine.title: StorefrontSessionLine

StorefrontTax.description: The tax that applies to an item of the shop window, as the buyer needs it to render a price: its opaque identifier, its name and its rate. Its three keys ALWAYS travel, `null` on all three when the item carries no tax: "this item has no tax" is a fact about the item and not the absence of a field.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the tax, or `null` when the item carries none.

name.description: Name of the tax, ready to display, or `null`.

rate.description: Rate of the tax as a decimal string, or `null`. It is a string and never a floating-point number: it is a figure a total is built from.

StorefrontTax.title: StorefrontTax

StripeAutoinvoicedPayment.description: A Stripe charge that generated an invoice (one-shot flows A/B and subscription cycles). The public `id` is the UUID v7 of the payment; `invoice_id`/`client_id` link to the generated invoice and client. Subscription-origin context (`subscription_id`, `stripe_invoice_id`, `period_start`, `period_end`) is `null` for one-shot charges.

id.description: UUID v7 of the payment record. Public identity (KEY `id`).

object.description: Stripe-like discriminator. Always `stripe_autoinvoiced_payment` for this resource.

invoice_id.description: UUID v7 of the invoice generated by this charge.

stripe_reference.description: Stripe transaction reference of the payment record.

subscription_id.description: External Stripe subscription id (`sub_xxx`) when the charge comes from a subscription cycle; `null` for one-shot charges. This is an external Stripe id, NOT an internal UUID.

stripe_invoice_id.description: Stripe invoice id (`in_xxx`) of the billed cycle; `null` for one-shot charges.

period_start.description: Start of the billed subscription period (YYYY-MM-DD); `null` for one-shot charges.

period_end.description: End of the billed subscription period (YYYY-MM-DD); `null` for one-shot charges.

updated_at.description: When the payment record was last updated (ISO 8601).

StripeAutoinvoicingConfig.description: Stripe Connect integration status and auto-invoicing configuration for your company. Singleton resource (one configuration per company), so it exposes `object` but no navigable `id`.

object.description: Stripe-like discriminator. Always `stripe_autoinvoicing_config` for this resource.

connected.description: Whether the Stripe Connect integration is connected (active) for the company.

enabled.description: Whether auto-invoicing of Stripe charges is enabled. Defaults to `false`.

series_id.description: UUID v7 of the document series used for auto-created invoices. `null` means the company default series is used.

available_for_current_plan.description: Whether the current plan includes auto-invoicing (effective plan gating, derived from config — not hardcoded).

required_plans.description: Plans that unlock auto-invoicing (derived from config, not hardcoded).

simplified_threshold_cents.description: Simplified invoice (F2) threshold in cents, range `[0, 300000]` (0–3,000 €). Charges without a tax ID at or below this amount are auto-issued as simplified invoices; above it they are routed to manual review. Defaults to 40000 (400 €).

require_nif.description: Whether a Spanish tax ID (NIF) is required for auto-invoicing. When enabled, Factuarea-created Checkouts mark the tax ID as required and charges without a tax ID are never auto-issued as simplified invoices (they go to manual review). Defaults to `false`.

refunds_enabled.description: Whether a Stripe refund (`charge.refunded`) automatically generates a linked corrective invoice (with the original invoice and the VeriFactu R record). Only acts while auto-invoicing is enabled. Defaults to `true`.

subscription_autoinvoicing_enabled.description: Whether Stripe subscription cycles (`invoice.paid` with a standard `billing_reason`) are auto-invoiced. Both this toggle and the general `enabled` flag must be on for a cycle to be invoiced. Defaults to `false`.

StripeAutoinvoicingConfig.title: StripeAutoinvoicingConfig

StripePayout.description: A Stripe payout ingested from `payout.paid`, together with its bank-reconciliation state. The public `id` is the payout UUID v7. `connected_account_id` (`acct_xxx`) and `stripe_payout_id` (`po_xxx`) are external Stripe ids, not foreign keys. `bank_transaction_ref` is the UUID v7 of the reconciled bank statement transaction (`null` while `status` is `ingested`). `composition` is the informative breakdown reported by Stripe (component charges + fees), referencing opaque Stripe ids — payouts are read-only on the public API; reconciliation happens in the dashboard.

id.description: UUID v7 of the payout. Public identity (KEY `id`).

object.description: Stripe-like discriminator. Always `stripe_payout` for this resource.

connected_account_id.description: External Stripe connected account id (`acct_xxx`) the payout was paid out from. NOT an internal UUID nor a foreign key.

stripe_payout_id.description: Opaque Stripe payout identifier (`po_xxx`), unique in Stripe.

amount_net.description: Net amount transferred to the bank account (gross minus fees), in the payout currency.

fee_total.description: Total Stripe fees deducted from the payout.

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency code of the payout.

arrival_date.description: Expected arrival date of the payout in the bank account (YYYY-MM-DD).

status.description: Reconciliation state. `ingested` once persisted; `reconciled` (terminal) once matched against a bank statement transaction.

reconciled_at.description: When the payout was reconciled against the bank statement (ISO 8601), or `null` while `ingested`.

bank_transaction_ref.description: UUID v7 of the reconciled bank statement transaction, or `null` while `ingested`.

composition.description: Informative breakdown of the payout reported by Stripe (component charges and fees). Component references are opaque Stripe ids (`payment_intent` = `pi_xxx`, `charge_id` = `ch_xxx`), NOT internal payment UUIDs. May be empty when the breakdown could not be read.

amount.description: Amount of the component charge, as a 2-decimal string in the payout currency.

fee.description: Fee of the component charge, as a 2-decimal string in the payout currency.

fee_total.description: Sum of the component fees, as a 2-decimal string in the payout currency.

gross_total.description: Sum of the component amounts, as a 2-decimal string in the payout currency.

StripePayout.title: StripePayout

Tax.description: A tax rate configuration. Catalog partially global (`is_system=true` for system taxes, without `company_id`) and partially custom per company.

name.description: Human-readable name of the tax (e.g. "IVA 21%").

code.description: Short tax code (e.g. "IVA21").

rate.description: Applied tax rate, e.g. `21` for 21% VAT.

applies_to.description: Scope where it applies: `sales` (sales only), `purchases` (purchases only), `both` (both).

is_default.description: true if this is the default tax for its `type` (independent of the `default_for_documents` map).

is_active.description: Indicates whether the tax is enabled for use on new documents.

is_system.description: true if the tax is from the global system catalog (not editable, without `company_id`).

ownership.description: Who owns the tax: `global` (Factuarea catalog, read-only for companies) or `company` (a tax created by your company, which only your company sees and can edit or delete).

description.description: Free-text description of the tax.

examples: IVA general aplicable en territorio peninsular y Baleares.

default_for_documents.description: Map `DocumentType -> bool` indicating for which document types this tax is default. Replaces the 5 legacy booleans `is_default_invoice/quote/delivery_note/proforma/purchase_invoice`.

customer_visible_label.description: Tax label shown to the end customer on documents (PDF, public link, email).

external_reference.description: AEAT-SII / VeriFactu key (closed catalog: S1..S3 subject, E1..E6 exempt, N1..N2 not subject).

valid_from.description: Legal effective start date of the rate (BOE). Format `YYYY-MM-DD`.

valid_until.description: Legal effective end date of the rate. Invariant: `valid_until >= valid_from` when both are non-null.

country_aeat_zone.description: AEAT tax zone: `peninsula` (including the Balearic Islands), `canarias` (IGIC), `ceuta` (IPSI) or `melilla` (IPSI).

indirect_tax_regime.description: Indirect tax regime DERIVED from the AEAT zone, read-only: `iva` (Península), `igic` (Canarias), `ipsi` (Ceuta/Melilla). Only set for `type=vat`; `null` otherwise.

linked_surcharge_taxes_id.description: Identity (UUID v7) of the linked equivalence-surcharge tax. Foreign key to the global `taxes` table (key suffix `_taxes_id` per the UUID policy). `null` when there is no link.
