TaxCatalog.description: The Spanish tax catalog as a single document: indirect tax regimes with their legal rates and VeriFactu code, header-level operation regimes, exemption causes with their article and legal wording, system withholding rates, and the legal VAT/equivalence-surcharge pairs. It carries no data of the authenticated company, so two different companies receive byte-identical bodies for the same language, and it is not an entity: it has no `id` and no `object`.

primary_language.description: Language resolved from `Accept-Language` (`es`, `en` or `ca`; `es` when the header is absent or names no supported language). It declares the primary language of the document; it does not filter it — every entry always carries all three translations. It travels inside the body on purpose, which is why two languages yield different `ETag`s.

indirect_tax_regimes.description: Indirect tax regimes (IVA, IGIC, IPSI) with their legal rates, standard rate, VeriFactu L1 code and the AEAT zones that determine each one.

operation_regimes.description: Header-level operation regimes with the legal wording each one requires and whether it forces a zero VAT amount.

exemption_causes.description: Exemption, non-subjection and special-regime causes with their AEAT codes, legal wording, applicable article and whether they can be declared per line.

retention_rates.description: System withholding rates, expressed in positive. Mostly IRPF withholdings, plus one contractual retainer that is not a tax and one IRNR rate (see the entry schema). The catalog of what the platform offers, not an exhaustive list of every rate Spanish law defines.

equivalence_surcharge_pairs.description: Closed matrix of the legal VAT/equivalence-surcharge pairs of article 161 of the Spanish VAT Act.

TaxCatalog.title: TaxCatalog

TaxCatalogExemptionCause.description: An exemption, non-subjection or special-regime cause, with the AEAT code it projects to, the legal wording the invoice must carry and the article of the Spanish VAT Act (Ley 37/1992) it relies on. The three AEAT codes are mutually exclusive: every cause derives at most one of them, and the other two are `null`.

code.description: Stable identifier of the cause.

calificacion_operacion.description: Code of the AEAT L9 list (transaction qualification): `S2` for reverse charge, `N1`/`N2` for the two non-subjection cases. `null` when the cause is an exemption or a special regime.

causa_exencion.description: Code of the AEAT L10 list (exemption reason), `E1` to `E6`. `null` when the cause is not an exemption.

clave_regimen.description: Code of the AEAT L8A/L8B list (special regime key): `19` farming, `03` second-hand goods, `05` travel agencies, `51` equivalence surcharge, `07` cash accounting. `null` when no special regime applies.

legal_mention.example: Operación intracomunitaria sujeta y exenta conforme al artículo 25 de la Ley 37/1992.
legal_mention.description: Full legal wording (in Spanish) that the invoice must carry when this cause is declared.

article.description: Article of the Spanish VAT Act (Ley 37/1992) the cause relies on. `null` only for `otro`, whose wording is written by hand and has no determined article — `null` means "no article", never "not mapped".

line_level.description: `true` when the cause can be declared per invoice line (its projected code is one of `E1`-`E6`, `N1`, `N2`). `false` for the special regimes, `otro` and reverse charge, which can only be declared in the document header.

TaxCatalogExemptionCause.title: TaxCatalogExemptionCause

TaxCatalogIndirectRegime.description: An indirect tax regime determined by the territory the issuer operates from (IVA on the mainland and the Balearic Islands, IGIC in the Canary Islands, IPSI in Ceuta and Melilla). This is the "which tax applies" axis; it is orthogonal to the operation regime, which answers "how is this transaction taxed".

code.description: Stable identifier of the regime.

aeat_code.description: Code of the AEAT L1 list used by VeriFactu: `01` for IVA, `02` for IPSI, `03` for IGIC. Send this value, not the `code`, when a VeriFactu field expects the L1 list.

valid_rates.description: Every legal rate of the regime, in percentage points. Any other rate is rejected when the invoice line is created.

general_rate.description: Standard rate of the regime, the sensible default when the line has no explicit rate.

aeat_zones.description: AEAT territorial zones that determine this regime. A company whose zone is listed here charges this tax.

TaxCatalogIndirectRegime.title: TaxCatalogIndirectRegime

TaxCatalogLocalizedText.description: A catalog text in the three languages the API supports. All three are always present: the negotiated `Accept-Language` picks the primary language of the document, it never filters the payload, so a client rendering a multilingual selector does not need three requests.
TaxCatalogLocalizedText.title: TaxCatalogLocalizedText

TaxCatalogOperationRegime.description: A header-level operation regime: how a transaction is taxed regardless of which indirect tax applies. Three of the four require the invoice to be issued with no VAT amount and to carry a legal wording; sending a rate above zero on those is a fiscal error, not a formatting one.

code.description: Stable identifier of the operation regime.

legal_mention.example: Operación intracomunitaria sujeta y exenta - Art. 25 LIVA
legal_mention.description: Legal wording (in Spanish) that the invoice must carry for this regime. `null` for `general`, the ordinary domestic transaction, which requires none.

requires_zero_vat.description: `true` when the regime forces a zero VAT amount on every line of the document.

TaxCatalogOperationRegime.title: TaxCatalogOperationRegime

TaxCatalogRetentionRate.description: A system withholding rate offered by the platform. Most entries are IRPF withholdings, but not all of them, and the `IRPF_` prefix of the `code` is no proof otherwise — codes are stable identifiers, not a tax classification. Two entries are not IRPF: `IRPF_5_GARANTIA` is contractual retention money on a construction contract, with no tax nature at all (it is not reported on form 111 and nothing is paid over to AEAT), and `IRPF_24` belongs to IRNR (RDL 5/2004), the non-resident income tax. Read each `label` for the nature of its own rate instead of assuming every entry is an IRPF withholding. This block is the catalog of what Factuarea ships, NOT an exhaustive list of every rate Spanish law defines, and it never includes the custom taxes a company creates in the application, which `GET /v1/companies/{company}/taxes` lists.

code.description: Stable identifier of the withholding type. It is the key, not the `rate`: two different types can share the same percentage and `applies_to` and differ only in the case they cover.

rate.description: Withholding percentage, always POSITIVE. Apply it as a deduction from the taxable base; the sign convention of the contract is positive regardless of how the rate is stored internally.

applies_to.description: `sale` for withholdings you apply on your own invoices, `purchase` for withholdings a supplier applies on theirs.

TaxCatalogRetentionRate.title: TaxCatalogRetentionRate

TaxCatalogSurchargePair.description: A legal pairing of a VAT rate with its equivalence surcharge (recargo de equivalencia). The rates are the ones article 161 of the Spanish VAT Act (Ley 37/1992) fixes; article 154, which anchors the special regime, governs its content and not its rates. The matrix is closed: any other combination is rejected when the invoice line is created. It pairs a surcharge with a VAT rate, so it cannot express the 1.75% rate article 161 reserves for supplies of manufactured tobacco, which depends on the product and not on the VAT rate.

vat.description: VAT rate of the pair, in percentage points.

surcharge.description: Equivalence surcharge that legally accompanies that VAT rate.

TaxCatalogSurchargePair.title: TaxCatalogSurchargePair

TaxDefaultsForDocuments.description: Defaults grouped by tax category for a given document type. Each key contains the (possibly empty) list of taxes marked as default for that `docType` within its `type`.

vat.description: Taxes with `type=vat` that are default for the requested docType.

TaxReport.description: A generated Spanish tax declaration (Modelo 303 quarterly VAT, or Modelo 347 yearly informational). Downloadable via `GET /v1/companies/{company}/tax-reports/{tax_report}/download`.

id.description: Opaque UUID v7 of the generated report.

period_year.description: Fiscal year covered by the declaration (backward compat, also available in `period.year`).

period_quarter.description: Quarter (1-4) for Modelo 303; null for Modelo 347 (yearly). Backward compat, also available in `period.quarter`.

period.description: Fiscal period covered by the declaration (nested form).

label.description: Human-readable period label (e.g. `2026 Q1` or `2026`).

format.description: Output format. `txt_aeat` is the official format accepted by the AEAT submission portal.

hash.description: SHA-256 of the generated file (audit trail).

generated_by_id.description: UUID v7 of the user who generated the declaration (audit trail).

download_url.description: Relative download URL of the generated resource (`/v1/companies/{company}/tax-reports/{tax_report}/download`).

warnings.description: Non-blocking warnings emitted during generation (e.g. invoices with incomplete data).

warning_codes.description: Stable machine-readable codes paired one-to-one (same index) with `warnings`. Branch on these instead of matching the Spanish text; unknown codes should fall back to the corresponding `warnings` entry.

TaxReportActivity.description: An event in the activity timeline of a tax report generation (creation, download, etc.). The `metadata` is sanitized (internal PKs removed) before being exposed.

examples: Se generó la declaración Modelo 303 del segundo trimestre de 2026.

metadata.description: Event metadata. Internal identifiers (PKs) are stripped; `*_uuid` values are preserved.

type.description: Type of actor that originated the event: `user` for a human in the internal app, `api_key` for an action performed through the public v1 API.

id.description: UUID v7 of the actor: the user when `type=user`, or the API key when `type=api_key`.

name.description: Actor name at the time of the event: the user name or the API key name. `null` if it could not be resolved.

performed_by.description: Actor that originated the event. `{type:"user",...}` for an internal user, `{type:"api_key",...}` when performed via the public v1 API, or `null` when the event is system-generated (scheduler, periodic sweep) with no attributable actor.

clients_347.description: Operations with clients that exceed the Modelo 347 threshold (Modelo 347 only). Empty for Modelo 303.

partyName.description: Name or legal/business name of the client.

base.description: Total annual amount of operations, in cents.

quarters.description: Amount per quarter (quarter key → amount in cents).

suppliers_347.description: Operations with suppliers that exceed the Modelo 347 threshold (Modelo 347 only). Empty for Modelo 303.

partyName.description: Name or legal/business name of the supplier.

base.description: Total annual amount of operations, in cents.

quarters.description: Amount per quarter (quarter key → amount in cents).

invoice_count.description: Number of issued invoices considered in the period.

purchase_invoice_count.description: Number of expenses considered in the period.

warnings.description: Non-blocking warnings detected during the computation (e.g. invoices with incomplete data).

warning_codes.description: Stable machine-readable codes paired one-to-one (same index) with `warnings`. Branch on these instead of matching the Spanish text; unknown codes should fall back to the corresponding `warnings` entry.

TaxReportStats.description: Aggregated summary of the history of tax reports generated by the authenticated company: totals by type, by format, accumulated size and current fiscal period. Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/tax-reports/stats`.

by_type.description: Report count by type. Covers every declaration type, so the three values add up to `total_reports`.

txt_aeat.description: Files in the official AEAT format.

total_size_bytes.description: Accumulated size (bytes) of all generated files.

TaxReportStats.title: TaxReportStats

TaxStats.description: Aggregated KPIs over the company tax catalog (includes global system taxes). Broken down by `type` and by AEAT `external_reference`.

total.description: Total taxes visible to the company (system + custom).

system_count.description: Taxes from the global system catalog (`is_system=true`).

custom_count.description: Visible taxes with `is_system=false` (usually your company's own taxes).

by_aeat_code.description: Tax count by AEAT `external_reference`. The `"(null)"` key groups taxes without an assigned AEAT code.

TaxTotals.description: Aggregated totals of a set of lines. Returned by `POST /v1/companies/{company}/taxes/calculate-totals`. Total formula: `subtotal + total_vat + total_surcharge − total_retention`.

subtotal.description: Sum of the taxable bases of all lines (EUR), as a 2-decimal string.

total_vat.description: Sum of the VAT of all lines, as a 2-decimal string.

total_surcharge.description: Sum of the equivalence surcharge of all lines, as a 2-decimal string.

total_retention.description: Sum of the withholding (IRPF) of all lines, as a 2-decimal string.

total.description: Grand total, as a 2-decimal string.

lines.description: Calculated breakdown for each received line, in the same order.

TaxTotalsLine.description: Calculated breakdown of a single line within `POST /v1/companies/{company}/taxes/calculate-totals`.

subtotal.description: Taxable base of the line (quantity × price − discount), as a 2-decimal string.

vat_amount.description: VAT amount of the line, as a 2-decimal string.

surcharge_amount.description: Equivalence surcharge amount of the line, as a 2-decimal string.

retention_amount.description: Withholding (IRPF) amount of the line, as a 2-decimal string.

total.description: Total of the line (subtotal + vat + surcharge − retention), as a 2-decimal string.

TaxTotalsLine.title: TaxTotalsLine

TaxUsage.description: Where a tax is used across your catalog and documents. It lets you decide whether it is safe to delete or deactivate the tax (`in_use=false` means it is safe to delete).

taxes_id.description: UUID v7 of the requested tax.

used_by.description: Number of references by kind of resource. Purchase invoice lines (they store a rate, not a tax reference) are not counted.

suppliers.description: Suppliers that use the tax as their default tax.

supplier_profiles.description: Supplier contact profiles that use the tax as their default tax and are not already counted in `suppliers` (a supplier is never counted twice).

invoice_lines.description: Invoice lines that reference the tax as VAT, withholding, surcharge or generic tax.

sales_order_lines.description: Sales order lines that reference the tax as VAT, withholding, surcharge or generic tax.

recurring_invoices.description: Recurring invoice templates with at least one line that references the tax (each template counts once).

company_tax_defaults.description: Document and category slots of your company tax configuration that use the tax as the default.

TeamAbsenceCalendar.description: The monthly team absence calendar for the Control Horario (time tracking) module: for a given year and month, every active employee with their approved absences of that month (each coloured by its absence type) plus the public holidays that apply, kept separate from the absences. A computed resource with no entity identity: it is keyed by company + year/month and never exposes an `id`.

members.description: Active employees of the team, each with their approved absences overlapping the month.

absences.description: Approved absences of the employee overlapping the month.

color.description: Hex color `#RRGGBB` of the absence type, used to render it on the calendar.

status.description: Status of the absence (always `approved` on the calendar).

holidays.description: Public holidays that apply to the team during the month.

name.description: Name of the holiday.

scope.description: Scope of the holiday: national, regional (autonomous community) or local.

TeamAbsenceCalendar.title: TeamAbsenceCalendar

TeamTimeBalanceRow.description: A single row of the team time balance summary: the monthly totals of one active employee for the Control Horario (time tracking) module. The `total_*` fields project the whole month; `to_date` holds the accumulation of the closed days.

total_expected_minutes.description: Total expected working minutes of the whole month, including today and the remaining days (projection).

total_worked_minutes.description: Total worked minutes of the month so far, today included.

total_balance_minutes.description: Month balance in minutes as the sum of the daily balances. In the current month it is a projection that already subtracts the expected minutes of today and of the remaining days; use `to_date.balance_minutes` for the actual balance.

total_overtime_minutes.description: Total overtime minutes of the month.

TeamTimeBalanceRow.title: TeamTimeBalanceRow

TeamTimeBalanceSummary.description: The team time balance summary (manager view) for a month for the Control Horario (time tracking) module. A computed resource with no entity identity: it is keyed by company + month and holds one row per active employee with their monthly totals and their accumulation of the closed days (`to_date`). Totals are in minutes.

employees.description: One row per active employee with their monthly totals.

TeamTimeBalanceSummary.title: TeamTimeBalanceSummary

TimeBalance.description: The time balance of an arbitrary period (`from`/`to`) of an employee for the Control Horario (time tracking) module. A computed resource with no entity identity: it is keyed by employee + period, so it exposes `employee_id` (UUID v7) and never an `id`. It is the same contract the monthly close reuses over closed periods. Totals are in minutes; `days` is the daily breakdown.

employee_id.description: UUID v7 of the employee the balance belongs to.

total_expected_minutes.description: Total expected working minutes of the period (holidays and approved absences already discounted).

total_worked_minutes.description: Total worked minutes of the period.

total_balance_minutes.description: Period balance in minutes as the sum of the daily balances. Days without a schedule in effect or outside the employment period add 0, so it can differ from worked − expected when minutes were clocked on those days.

total_overtime_minutes.description: Total overtime minutes of the period.

days.description: Daily breakdown of the period. Each day includes `is_unscheduled` and `is_outside_employment`.

TimeBalance.title: TimeBalance

TimeBalanceToDate.description: The month-to-date accumulation of the closed days (every day before today) for the Control Horario (time tracking) module. It is computed from the same daily breakdown as the `total_*` fields, which instead cover the whole month and are a projection: in the current month they already subtract the expected minutes of today and of the remaining days. Today is left out because its workday is still in progress. In a finished month it equals the `total_*` fields; when no day of the month has closed yet (its first day, or a future month), `through_date` is `null` and the four figures are 0.

through_date.description: Last closed day included in the accumulation (YYYY-MM-DD), normally yesterday; `null` when no day of the month has closed yet.

expected_minutes.description: Expected working minutes of the closed days.

worked_minutes.description: Worked minutes of the closed days.

balance_minutes.description: Balance of the closed days in minutes: the sum of the daily `balance_minutes`, so days without a schedule or outside the employment period add 0.

overtime_minutes.description: Overtime minutes of the closed days.

TimeBalanceToDate.title: TimeBalanceToDate

TimeCorrection.description: A time entry correction request for the Control Horario (time tracking) module (RD-ley 8/2019). A correction is an append-only entry that references the original time entry without mutating it (analogous to a corrective invoice); its status is derived from the ledger — there is no status column. The workflow is request → approve/reject, always resolved by a manager and never self-approved.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the correction request, a UUID v7 (e.g. `01931b3e-7c4a-7f2e-9a8b-3c5d6e7f8a9b`).

status.description: Derived workflow state: `pending` (awaiting resolution), `approved` or `rejected`.

time_entry_id.description: UUID v7 of the original time entry the correction refers to.

employee_id.description: UUID v7 of the employee the corrected entry belongs to.

requested_by_id.description: UUID v7 of the user who requested the correction.

resolved_by_id.description: UUID v7 of the user who approved or rejected the request; `null` while it is still pending.

reason.description: Reason supplied with the request (or the rejection); `null` if none.
reason.example: El fichaje de salida se registró con 30 minutos de retraso.
examples: El fichaje de salida se registró con 30 minutos de retraso.

proposed.description: Map of the proposed values of the correction (shape depends on `kind`).

resolved_at.description: When the request was resolved (ISO 8601); `null` while it is still pending.

TimeCorrection.title: TimeCorrection

TimeEntry.description: A single entry of the immutable time record ledger (a clock event) for the Control Horario (time tracking) module. Every clock-in, pause, resume and clock-out — live or retroactive — is an entry chained by fingerprint. The workday state is derived from these entries; there is no session table. Fingerprints are never exposed.

id.description: Opaque identifier of the time entry, a UUID v7 (e.g. `01931b3e-7c4a-7f2e-9a8b-3c5d6e7f8a9b`).

employee_id.description: UUID v7 of the employee the entry belongs to.

entry_type.description: Type of clock event: `clock_in` (opens a work span), `pause_start`, `pause_end` or `clock_out` (closes the span).

occurred_at.description: When the clock event happened (ISO 8601). For retroactive entries this is the past instant supplied by the manager.

recorded_at.description: When the entry was appended to the ledger (ISO 8601).

source.description: Origin of the entry: `web` or `mobile` (live self-service) or `manual` (retroactive entry recorded by a manager).

is_retroactive.description: Whether the entry was recorded retroactively (a manual entry by a manager) rather than clocked live.

reason.description: Reason for the retroactive entry; `null` for live entries.

TimeEntry.title: TimeEntry

TimeRecordChainValidation.description: Result of recomputing and verifying the SHA-256 hash chain (`huella`) of your company time record ledger without mutating data. Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/time-entries/chain/validate`. Fingerprints are never exposed.

is_valid.description: Indicates whether the hash chain is intact.

total_records.description: Total number of time record entries considered.

first_invalid_record_id.description: UUID v7 of the first invalid entry, or `null` if the chain is intact.

TimeRecordChainValidation.title: TimeRecordChainValidation

TimeTrackingSettings.description: The per-company time tracking configuration for the Control Horario module: the overtime computation basis and thresholds, the rounding tolerance and the forgotten-clock-in reminder settings. The public `id` is the UUID v7 of the settings row, or `null` until the first PUT materialises it.

id.description: UUID v7 of the settings row, or `null` while the company has not materialised it yet (the first PUT creates the row).

overtime_basis.description: Overtime computation basis: `weekly` aggregates the week, `daily` computes per day.

overtime_daily_threshold_minutes.description: Daily overtime threshold in minutes, or `null` to derive it from the schedule.

overtime_weekly_threshold_minutes.description: Weekly overtime threshold in minutes, or `null` to derive it from the schedule.

TransitionFulfilmentStatusRequest.description:
Moving a delivery note along its physical axis.

The body carries the DESTINATION state, `target_status`, and — only when the
destination is a failed delivery — the reason, `failure_reason`. There is ONE
operation for the whole axis instead of one per step: the warehouse handles
it as a single control, and publishing an operation per step would give ten
endpoints for one decision.

`target_status` is one of the seven states of the physical axis: `pending`,
`picking`, `prepared`, `handed_over`, `in_transit`, `delivered` and `failed`.
Anything outside that catalog is rejected naming the field.

Belonging to the catalog is NOT the same as being reachable. Which
destinations are admitted depends on where the delivery note is right now,
and a destination the state machine does not admit from the current state is
rejected as a business-rule violation naming the current state and the
admitted ones — never as a permission problem: the caller has permission, it
is the document that does not admit the step. Delivery to the recipient is
TERMINAL and nothing moves after it; a failed delivery admits a second
attempt back into transit; and a delivery note cancelled on its commercial
side does not advance at all, which is the only rule that crosses the two
axes.

`failure_reason` is required when the destination is a failed delivery and
rejected with any other destination: with a destination that is not a failure
it would be a note nobody ever reads back, and a failed delivery with no
reason is a dead end for whoever has to decide whether to try again. It is
free text of up to 500 characters — the length of an operational note, not of
a column — and it travels with the event the transition emits.

Moving along this axis NEVER changes the commercial status of the delivery
note and never emits an event of the commercial axis: whoever subscribes to
the status of the document receives exactly what it received before this axis
existed.

The operation is declared IRREVERSIBLE as a whole, and the flag is per
OPERATION and not per destination value: two of its destinations are
irreversible — handing the goods to the carrier has an effect on a third
party, and delivery to the recipient is terminal — so the reversible steps
ask for an idempotency key as well when the policy of the credential requires
one. Over-marking costs one header; under-marking loses the guarantee on the
two steps that need it.

target_status.description: DESTINATION state of the physical axis: `pending`, `picking`, `prepared`, `handed_over`, `in_transit`, `delivered` or `failed`. Belonging to that catalog is NOT the same as being reachable: which destinations are admitted depends on where the delivery note is right now, and one the state machine does not admit is rejected as a business-rule violation naming the current state and the admitted ones — never as a permission problem, because the caller does have permission and it is the document that does not admit the step. Delivery to the recipient is terminal; a failed delivery admits a second attempt back into transit; and a delivery note cancelled on its commercial side does not advance at all. This never changes the commercial status of the document.

failure_reason.description: Why the delivery did not succeed. REQUIRED when the destination is `failed` and REJECTED with any other destination: with a destination that is not a failure it would be a note nobody ever reads back, and a failed delivery with no reason leaves whoever has to decide whether to try again with nothing to go on. Free text of up to 500 characters — the length of an operational note — and it travels with the event the transition emits.

UpdateCarrierRequest.description:
Partially update a carrier of the company master data.

Every field is optional and an empty body changes nothing and is not an error.
What you leave out keeps the value it has, so changing the name touches
neither the code, nor the tracking kind, nor the contact. There is no full
replacement operation: this is the only way to edit a carrier.

A field that is SENT and a field that is LEFT OUT mean two different things,
and the difference is the whole point of this operation. Leaving a key out
keeps the current value; sending it as `null` clears it. An empty string is
neither of the two and is rejected naming the field, so that a form that
blanks a text box cannot wipe the template or the contact of a carrier without
anybody having asked for it.

`name`, `code` and `tracking_kind` cannot be cleared: a carrier without a
name, without a code or without a tracking kind is not a carrier, so sending
any of the three as `null` or empty is rejected. Whoever does not want to
change them leaves them out. A new `code` keeps the same uniqueness rule as
creation, unique within the company, and resending the code the carrier
already holds is legitimate and collides with nothing.

`tracking_url_template` may be sent, cleared or left alone, and it is checked
the same way as on creation: it has to carry the `{tracking_number}`
placeholder and its scheme has to be `http` or `https`. Moving the carrier to
the `url_template` kind and clearing the template in the same request is
rejected, because that pair would promise a tracking link and hold nothing to
build it with; moving it to that kind WITHOUT touching the template is
accepted when the carrier already holds one and rejected as a business rule
violation when it does not.

`contact` is one piece: sending it REPLACES the whole block, so a key left out
inside it is cleared, and sending `contact` as `null` withdraws the contact
altogether. It is published the same way, as one object with `name`, `email`
and `phone`, so what you send and what you read back have the same shape.

`is_active` withdraws the carrier from service without deleting it: a
withdrawn carrier is still readable, still resolves the tracking address of
the delivery notes that already reference it, and merely stops being
assignable to a new shipment. It takes `true` or `false` and never `null`.

The body takes neither the company, which comes from the path, nor the
identifier of the carrier, which the route carries. Internal notes are not
part of the published carrier and are not accepted here either.

name.description: Human-readable name of the carrier, up to 120 characters. Left out, it keeps its current value

code.description: Short code that identifies the carrier within your company. Omitting it keeps the current one; a code held by another LIVE carrier of your company is rejected naming this field.

tracking_kind.description: Where the tracking link of a shipment comes from: `url_template`, `manual` or `store_provided`. Declaring `url_template` and clearing the address in the SAME request is rejected, because it would leave a carrier that promises a link it cannot build; moving to that kind without touching the address is accepted when the carrier already has one.

tracking_url_template.description: Address the tracking link is built from, with the same rules as on creation: the `{tracking_number}` placeholder is mandatory and only `http` and `https` are accepted. Sending it as `null` REMOVES it, which is the one operation that tells «clear the address» apart from «leave it as it is» — leaving the key out keeps the current value.

contact.description: Operational contact of the carrier. Sending it REPLACES the whole block and `null` withdraws it: there is no way to change just the phone number, because the three fields describe one person and a partial change would silently keep the name of somebody who is no longer there.

name.description: Person to call about a shipment

email.description: Email address of the person to call about a shipment.

is_active.description: Whether the carrier can still be assigned to a NEW shipment. Sending `false` withdraws it WITHOUT deleting it: the shipments already handed to it keep naming it, its code stays taken, and it stops being offered for new ones.

UpdateDeliveryNoteShipmentRequest.description:
Partial update of the shipment of a delivery note.

## What partial means here

Every property is optional and the body may arrive empty: a body with no
properties changes nothing and is not an error. A property you do not send
keeps the value it has; a property you send with `null` is REMOVED. What
tells those two apart is whether the KEY is present in the body, never the
value it carries, and an empty string is read as the same order as `null`.
There is no full-replacement operation for the shipment: this is the only way
to edit it.

## What this body accepts

 - `carrier_id` — public identifier of a carrier of the same company. `null`
   detaches the carrier, and with it the tracking URL that is derived from
   its template. A carrier held by another company is rejected exactly like
   one that does not exist, with no way to tell the two apart. A carrier that
   is no longer active is rejected as a business rule violation, and the
   shipment keeps the carrier it already had.
 - `expected_delivery_date` — expected delivery date, as `YYYY-MM-DD` with no
   time part. `null` removes it.
 - `packages_reference` — the reference the carrier prints for the shipment
   as a whole, up to 60 characters. `null` removes it.

## What this body does not accept, and where those values are changed

The tracking number and the free carrier text of the delivery note are NOT
written here. Both keep a single writing path, the update of the delivery
note itself, so that one value cannot be moved by two operations that could
disagree; the shipment reading keeps publishing both, and the tracking URL it
publishes is built from the tracking number every time it is read.

The stage of the physical cycle is not written here either: it moves through
its own operation, which applies the transition matrix. Packages are their own
sub-resource, and the total weight of the shipment is always the sum of them,
so neither the package count nor the total weight is accepted as a property.

carrier_id.description: Public ID of the carrier of the shipment, from your carrier master data. Omitting it keeps the current one and `null` DETACHES it. A carrier of another company is rejected exactly like one that does not exist, naming this field, so the rejection never tells you whether it exists.

expected_delivery_date.description: Date the goods are expected to reach the recipient, as a calendar date `YYYY-MM-DD` with no time of day. Omitting it keeps the current one and `null` removes it. It is what the preparation queue is prioritized by, so leaving it empty takes the delivery note out of that ordering rather than putting it last.

packages_reference.description: Reference the carrier prints for the WHOLE shipment — the consignment note or manifest number — as opposed to the label of each individual package. Omitting it keeps the current one and `null` removes it. The TRACKING NUMBER is not a field of this operation and sending it changes nothing: it is written with the operation that updates the delivery note itself.

operation_on.description: Date the operation took place (YYYY-MM-DD) when it differs from the issue date. It can only be changed while the invoice is a draft, and it cannot be later than `issued_on` (422 `operation_date_after_issue_date`) unless the first line that declares a `regime_key` uses 14 or 15.

unit_price.description: Unit price. Send a JSON number or a decimal string with up to 4 decimals (`"0.0125"`, `"100.0000"`): the string is the exact form the response returns, so a line read from the API can be sent back unchanged. Derived amounts are computed from it and keep 2 decimals.

tax_rate.description: VAT rate of the line (0–100). Optional, and it matters whenever `lines` is sent, because a `PUT` replaces the whole set of lines: a line that omits it (or sends `null`) takes the tax it references or the tax assigned to its product and otherwise the DEFAULT TAX of your company for this kind of document, inherited as a whole: its rate, its indirect-tax regime (IVA, IGIC or IPSI) and its AEAT qualification; an exempt or not-subject default also declares its cause (`exemption_reason`) on the line unless the line sends its own. If none of them exists the request is rejected with 422 `missing_required_param`, with `error.param` = `lines.N.tax_rate` and `error.line_index` = N (the zero-based index of the line); a rate already stored on a line is NOT kept if you resend the line without it. A `0` you send is honoured as a real 0 % rate.

line_type.description: Kind of line: `NORMAL` (default) for an ordinary line of your own operation, or `SUPLIDO` for a DISBURSEMENT — an amount you paid in the name and on behalf of the client and now re-invoice at cost, which stays out of the taxable base (art. 78.Tres.3 LIVA). Replacing the lines of a draft re-applies the same rules, so keep the field when you resend a line you read from the invoice: sending it as `NORMAL` (or omitting it) turns the disbursement into an ordinary taxable line and changes the invoice amount.

source_invoice_reference.description: Reference of the supporting document that originated the disbursement — the receipt or fee number issued by the public body (up to 100 characters). REQUIRED when `line_type` is `SUPLIDO`; leave it out on a normal line.

source_invoice_ids.description: Optional traceability of a disbursement: list of IDs (UUID v7) of your own expenses that back it. An expense of another company is rejected with 422.

unit.description: Unit of measure printed next to the quantity on the document (`hours`, `kg`, `units`, …), up to 20 characters. Presentation only: free text, no closed catalog and no fiscal effect.

exemption_reason_text.description: Free-text wording of the exemption provision of this line (up to 255 characters), printed under the line description to satisfy the mention required by art. 6.1.j of Royal Decree 1619/2012 when the catalogued cause does not cover it.

line_total.description: Optional CHECKSUM of the line total. When sent, it is compared against the total this API computes and the request is rejected with 422 (`line_total_checksum_mismatch`, with the expected and received values in `error.details`) when they differ by more than one cent. Never stored and never returned.

UpdateReturnRequest.description:
Partially update a return that is still requested.

Every field is optional and a body with no fields at all is accepted and
changes nothing: that is what partial means, and answering with an error to a
legitimate request without effect would turn a no-op into a failure. What is
not sent keeps the value it already had, so changing the notes does not touch
the warehouse, the header reason or the invoice to be corrected.

A key sent as null is a different thing from a key left out: null withdraws
the value, and leaving the key out keeps it. That difference is the whole
point of a partial update, and it is the reason why an empty text is rejected
instead: withdraw with null, keep by omitting, and never by typing a space.

## What can be changed

 - `reason` — header reason of the return, out of the closed set of four
   values. Null withdraws it, and it is derived again from the lines.
 - `warehouse_id` — public identifier of the warehouse that will take the
   goods in, active and of the company in the path. Null withdraws it.
 - `target_invoice_id` — public identifier of the invoice that will be
   corrected on refund, of the company in the path. Null withdraws it.
   Choosing an invoice that is not among the candidates of the origin is
   rejected as a business rule violation: correcting a document unrelated to
   what came back is not an option.
 - `notes` — free text of the return, up to 1000 characters. Null withdraws
   them.

## What this body does not accept

 - **Lines.** A body carrying a lines field is rejected naming that parameter.
   Lines are fixed when the return is requested, and correcting them through
   this API is done by deleting the return and asking for a new one while it
   is still requested. There is no replacement of the whole collection, so
   accepting one here would mean working out the difference between what was
   sent and what is stored, which is a decision that belongs to the return and
   not to the transport.
 - **Origin.** Neither the kind of origin nor the origin document can be
   changed: the lines of the return point at lines of that document and
   inherit their price and their tax rate from them, so swapping it would
   leave every line inheriting from somewhere else. Rejecting the return,
   which frees the quantity, and asking for a new one is how that is done.
 - **State, number and series.** Every step of the cycle has an operation of
   its own, and the state of a return is not a destination that is chosen.
 - **Refunded amount and issued corrective invoice.** Both are stamped by the
   refund.
 - **Company and actor.** Both come from the path and from the credential.

## When it is rejected

Only a return that is still requested admits a content change. On a return
that is already approved, received, refunded or rejected the request is turned
down as a business rule violation naming the state that prevents it. That
check is not repeated here: a second guard in the transport would drift from
the first one at the first correction.

## Company

The warehouse and the invoice are checked against the company in the path, so
a reference of another company is rejected exactly like one that does not
exist, without revealing that it exists.

reason.description: Header reason of the return, out of the closed set of four. Omitting it keeps the current one and `null` WITHDRAWS it, after which it is derived again from the lines: a return always ends up with a reason.

warehouse_id.description: Public ID of the warehouse that takes the goods back in, active and of the company in the path. Omitting it keeps the current one and `null` withdraws it.

target_invoice_id.description: Public ID of the invoice that will be corrected when the money goes back, of the company in the path. Choosing it up front is what settles the ambiguity when the origin resolves to several candidate invoices. Omitting it keeps the current one and `null` withdraws the choice.

notes.description: Free text of the return, up to 1000 characters. Omitting it keeps the current one and `null` withdraws it.

UpdateShipmentPackageRequest.description:
Partial update of one package of the shipment of a delivery note.

## What partial means here

The six properties are optional and the body may arrive empty: a body with no
properties changes nothing and is not an error. A property you do not send
keeps the value it has; a property you send with `null` is REMOVED, which is
how a weight entered by mistake is taken back. What tells those two apart is
whether the KEY is present in the body, never the value it carries, and an
empty string is read as the same order as `null`.

## What this body accepts

The same six properties as adding a package, with the same limits.
`reference` is the label the carrier prints for this package, up to 60
characters. `weight_kg` is in kilograms and `length_cm`, `width_cm` and
`height_cm` are in centimetres, all four sent as numeric strings with at most
eight whole digits and two decimals, which is what their storage holds; a
value above that ceiling, or one carrying a third decimal, is rejected as a
validation error naming the property at fault, before the shipment is touched.
Zero is accepted and a negative value is not. `notes` is free internal text.

## What this body does not accept

The position of the package is not written here: it is the order inside the
shipment, it belongs to the whole set and not to one package, and it is
assigned when the package is added. The total weight of the shipment is not
written either, because it is always the sum of its packages and never a
stored value.

A package that belongs to another delivery note, or to another company,
answers exactly like one that does not exist.

reference.description: Label the carrier prints for this package. Omitting it keeps the current one and `null` removes it — that difference is the whole point of this operation, so an update that only corrects the weight cannot wipe the label along the way.

weight_kg.description: Weight of the package in kilograms, with at most two decimals and up to 99999999.99. Omitting it keeps the current one and `null` removes it, which also takes it out of the total weight of the shipment.

length_cm.description: Length of the package in centimetres, with the same limits and the same absent-versus-null rule.

width_cm.description: Width of the package in centimetres, with the same limits and the same absent-versus-null rule.

height_cm.description: Height of the package in centimetres, with the same limits and the same absent-versus-null rule.

notes.description: Free text about the package. Omitting it keeps the current one and `null` removes it.

UpdateShipmentPackageRequest.title: UpdateShipmentPackageRequest

UpdateStoreV1Request.description:
Public REST API v1 — PATCH /v1/companies/{company}/stores/{store}.

Partial update of the settings of a connected store: every field is optional
and a field you do not send keeps its current value. The identity of the
store —its provider connection, its provider and the identifier of the remote
shop— cannot be changed here: pointing an existing store at a different shop
would keep the invoicing history of the old one.

Three fields accept an explicit `null` and it means something: `series_id: null`
goes back to the default series of your company, `remote_base_url: null`
removes the declared address, and `invoice_note: null` removes the note of the
automatic invoices. Omitting either one leaves it untouched.
`simplified_threshold` is expressed in EUROS and capped at the legal maximum
for a simplified invoice.

name.description: Display name of the store.

series_id.description: Series (UUID v7, type invoice) the store numbers into; send `null` to go back to the default series of your company.

simplified_threshold.description: Order total, in euros, up to which the store issues a simplified invoice. Maximum 3000.00.

require_tax_id.description: Whether the buyer tax ID is required for the order to be invoiced.

prices_include_tax.description: Whether the prices of the store already include taxes.

autoinvoicing_enabled.description: Whether paid orders are invoiced automatically.

autosend_enabled.description: Whether the invoice is emailed to the buyer automatically.

remote_base_url.description: Base address of the remote shop; send `null` to remove it. Checked against the outbound policy of your company.

environment.description: Environment the store reports as: `live` invoices for real, `test` discards with a typed reason.

invoice_note.description: Note written in the notes of every invoice issued automatically from this store (up to 500 characters). Send `null` or an empty string to remove it: invoices then carry no note.

authorize_remote_host.description: Authorize the host of `remote_base_url` as an outbound destination in the same call.

UpdateStoreV1Request.title: UpdateStoreV1Request

UpdateStorefrontBuyerIdentityRequest.description: PARTIAL update of the fiscal identity of the buyer of an order: every field is optional, what you do not send is NOT touched, and an empty body is a valid request that changes nothing. It is the call a storefront makes when the order needs a full invoice and the buyer has to complete what the cart did not ask for. `buyer_tax_id` is the fiscal identification, and the billing block is street, town, province, postal code and two-letter country; `full_invoice_requested` says whether the buyer is asking for a full invoice instead of a simplified one. Country becomes required as soon as any other field of the billing address travels: an address with no country can neither be invoiced nor validated. Completing the identity is what PROMOTES the buyer to a business contact of the seller —reused by tax id when one already exists— and the response returns the updated order together with the reference of that contact, or `null` when nobody was promoted. An order that no longer admits collection rejects the call, and an order of another shop answers as not found.

buyer_tax_id.description: Fiscal identification of the buyer, up to 20 characters. Leaving it out keeps the one the order already had.

billing_address_line.description: Street and number of the billing address, up to 255 characters.

billing_city.description: Town or city of the billing address, up to 120 characters.

billing_province.description: Province of the billing address, up to 120 characters.

billing_postal_code.description: Postal code of the billing address, up to 20 characters.

billing_country.description: Country of the billing address as a two-letter code. It becomes required as soon as any other field of the billing address is sent.

full_invoice_requested.description: Whether the buyer is asking for a full invoice instead of a simplified one. It raises the identity bar: above the simplified-invoice threshold, or with this flag, the fiscal identification and the address become necessary to issue.

UpdateStorefrontBuyerIdentityRequest.title: UpdateStorefrontBuyerIdentityRequest

UpdateStorefrontKeyRequest.description: Partial update of a live publishable storefront credential. All three editable fields are optional: an omitted key keeps its current value and never clears it. `allowed_origins` and `scopes` REPLACE the current list rather than adding to it, and when present they follow exactly the same rules as on creation (non-empty, at most 10 origins, same origin format with no wildcards, buyer-lane scopes only). An empty body `{}` is accepted as a no-op and returns the credential unchanged. `expires_at`, status, prefix and secret are not accepted here: expiry is fixed at issuance, the status only changes through revocation and the secret only through rotation.

name.description: Label that tells your publishable credentials apart, from 1 to 120 characters. Omitting it keeps the current one: it is never cleared by omission.

allowed_origins.description: Web origins the browser may use this credential from. When present it REPLACES the current list rather than adding to it, and it keeps the rules of the creation: between 1 and 10 entries, `scheme://host[:port]`, no path, no query string, no fragment and no wildcards. Retiring an origin takes effect on the very next request, which is how a domain that is no longer yours is cut off WITHOUT rotating the secret.

scopes.description: Scopes granted to the credential. When present it REPLACES the current list and stays restricted to the shopper lane. Narrowing it is the cheap way to stop a credential from writing while it keeps reading the catalog.

UpdateStorefrontKeyRequest.title: UpdateStorefrontKeyRequest

UpdateStorefrontSessionRequest.description: Partially update a cart session: every field is optional, what you do not send is not touched, and an EMPTY body is a valid request that changes nothing — it is how you check that the cart is still alive without touching it. `lines`, when it travels, REPLACES the whole collection: it is the cart exactly as it stands, not an addition and not a tweak of one line, and an empty list empties the cart. It works that way because a cart is a short list the storefront already has whole on screen, and a language of per-line tweaks would let the screen and the server drift apart without anybody noticing. Each line takes the same shape as on creation and the ceiling of 50 lines still applies. THE PRICE IS NOT SENT: no amount field is accepted and one that arrives is ignored; changing the lines makes the server resolve the amount of each one again and keep it with the moment it was resolved. The buyer is given WHOLE: as soon as any of its fields travels, `buyer_name`, `buyer_email` and the shipping address become required, and sending nothing about the buyer leaves the one the cart already had. A cart that has EXPIRED, one already turned into an ORDER and one that was ABANDONED each reject this call saying which of the three happened, because the remedy of each one is different: open another cart, read the order that already exists, or start again. A cart of another shop answers as not found, with no effect and without revealing that it is there.

lines.description: The cart EXACTLY as it stands. When it travels it REPLACES every line — it is not an addition and not a per-line tweak — and an empty list empties the cart; leaving the key out keeps the lines untouched. Capped at 50 lines, and no amount is accepted inside a line: changing the lines makes the server resolve the price of each one again.

product_id.description: Public id of the article of the line, of the shop that owns the key. Required in every line.

variant_id.description: Public id of the variant chosen, when the article has variants.

presentation_id.description: Public id of the presentation chosen, when the article has presentations.

configuration_id.description: Public id of the configuration chosen, when there is one.

selection_signature.description: Fingerprint of the configuration chosen: 64 hexadecimal characters.

options.description: Option values chosen for the line, as a list of pairs of `group_id` and `value_id`: one value per group and at most 50.

items.description: Each chosen option, with its group and its value

group_id.description: Public id of the option group the choice belongs to.

value_id.description: Public id of the value chosen inside that group.

quantity.description: Units of the line: required inside each line, greater than zero, with at most four decimals and up to 9999999999.9999.

buyer_name.description: Name of the shopper, up to 255 characters. Sending nothing about the buyer leaves the one the cart already had; sending any of its fields makes this one required, because the identity is stored whole or not at all.

buyer_email.description: Email of the shopper, up to 191 characters. Required as soon as any other field of the buyer travels.

buyer_phone.description: Phone of the shopper, up to 40 characters. Optional.

buyer_tax_id.description: Fiscal identification of the shopper, up to 20 characters. OPTIONAL: a private individual may not have one.

shipping_address_line.description: Street and number the order is delivered to, up to 255 characters. Required as soon as any other field of the buyer travels.

shipping_city.description: Town or city of delivery, up to 120 characters. Required as soon as any other field of the buyer travels.

shipping_province.description: Province of delivery, up to 120 characters. Optional.

shipping_postal_code.description: Postal code of delivery, up to 20 characters. Optional.

shipping_country.description: Country of delivery as a two-letter code. Required as soon as any other field of the buyer travels.

billing_address_line.description: Street and number of the billing address, up to 255 characters. The whole billing block is optional.

billing_city.description: Town or city of the billing address, up to 120 characters.

billing_province.description: Province of the billing address, up to 120 characters.

billing_postal_code.description: Postal code of the billing address, up to 20 characters.

billing_country.description: Country of the billing address as a two-letter code. It becomes required as soon as any other field of the billing block is sent.

UpdateStorefrontSessionRequest.title: UpdateStorefrontSessionRequest

UpdateStripeAutoinvoicingConfigRequest.description: Update the Stripe auto-invoicing configuration. `enabled` toggles auto-invoicing; `series_id` (UUID v7, nullable) sets the series for auto-created invoices (`null` uses the company default); `simplified_threshold_cents` (0-300000), `require_nif`, `refunds_enabled` and `subscription_autoinvoicing_enabled` are optional partial fields.
UpdateStripeAutoinvoicingConfigRequest.title: UpdateStripeAutoinvoicingConfigRequest

name.description: New name.

type.description: Type: immutable; a value different from the current one returns 422 `invalid_custom_field_definition`.

default_value.description: Default value (text, number, boolean, a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, an option or a list of options); `null` removes it.

options.description: Complete resulting list of options (up to 100).

name.description: New label name (1-60 characters); omitted = unchanged.

color.description: New color: palette key or hexadecimal `#RGB`/`#RRGGBB`; omitted = unchanged.

started_at.description: New start, ISO 8601 with time zone. `null` is not accepted.

ended_at.description: New end, ISO 8601 with time zone; `null` removes the end.

description.description: Description; `null` clears it.

billable.description: Whether the time is billable. `null` is not accepted.

title.description: New title (1 to 500 characters). `null` is not accepted.

priority.description: New priority: `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high` or `urgent`. `null` is not accepted.

description.description: Description in Markdown; `null` clears it.

assignee_id.description: `id` of the member user the task is assigned to; `null` leaves the task unassigned.

customer_visible_label.description: Custom label for this tax shown to the customer on documents (e.g. "IVA 21% incluido"). Up to 200 characters.

valid_until.description: End date of the tax validity window (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Must be on or after `valid_from`.

linked_surcharge_taxes_id.description: FK to the linked equivalence-surcharge tax; `null` unlinks it. UUID v7 value referencing the Factuarea catalog plus your company's own taxes.

default_for_documents.description: Sets this tax as the default per document type. Object with optional booleans: `invoice`, `quote`, `delivery_note`, `proforma`, `purchase_invoice`, `recurring_invoice`.

overtime_basis.description: Overtime computation basis: `weekly` or `daily`. Optional: when omitted it keeps its current value.

overtime_daily_threshold_minutes.description: Daily overtime threshold in minutes (null = derive from the schedule).

overtime_weekly_threshold_minutes.description: Weekly overtime threshold in minutes (null = derive from the schedule).

overtime_tolerance_minutes.description: Overtime rounding tolerance in minutes. Optional: when omitted it keeps its current value.

clock_in_reminder_enabled.description: Whether the missed clock-in reminder is enabled. Optional: when omitted it keeps its current value.

clock_in_reminder_grace_minutes.description: Grace minutes after the scheduled time before reminding. Optional: when omitted it keeps its current value.

UpdateTransportDocumentRequest.description: Partial update of a draft transport document: an absent field is kept, an explicit `null` clears it and `shipments` replaces the whole list. Same fields and rules as the creation body, without `delivery_note_ids`. Inside `shipments`, `id` only identifies a shipment of THIS document (any other identifier returns 422 `parameter_invalid_value` on `shipments.N.id`) and a new shipment goes without `id`; an explicit `origin: null` clears the origin of that shipment.
UpdateTransportDocumentRequest.title: UpdateTransportDocumentRequest

remission_mode.description: Who remits your records to AEAT: `own_certificate` (your own certificate, the default), `social_collaborator` or `power_of_attorney` (Factuarea remits with its certificate). A third-party mode requires an active representation of the kind it asks for — register it first with `POST /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/representation` — otherwise 422 with subcode `representation_required`.

UpdateWarehouseLocationRequest.description: Partially update a location. Both `code` and `name` are optional and an empty body is a no-op; neither accepts null, since a location cannot be left without a code or a label. The code stays unique within its warehouse among the active locations, and resending the code the location already has is accepted. The warehouse is part of the location identity and cannot be changed, the parent location is declared when the location is created, and withdrawing a location has its own operation: all three are rejected if sent in the body.

code.description: Short code used to label the location within its warehouse; unique among the active ones. Resending the code the location already has is accepted.

name.description: Human-readable label of the location, up to 120 characters.

warehouse_id.description: The warehouse of a location is part of its identity and cannot be changed.

parent_id.description: The parent location is declared when the location is created and cannot be re-hung here.

status.description: Withdrawing a location has its own operation.

UpdateWarehouseLocationRequest.title: UpdateWarehouseLocationRequest

UpdateWarehouseRequest.description: Partially update a warehouse. Every field is optional and an empty body is a no-op, not an error; omitted fields keep their current value and a field that is sent may not be empty. Sending `address` replaces the WHOLE address: `line1`, `city`, `province`, `postal_code` and `country` are required inside the block and omitting `line2` clears it. A new `code` keeps the same uniqueness rule as creation (live warehouses of the same company, 422 pointing at `code`) and never collides with the warehouse being edited. The archived status and the default-warehouse flag are not accepted here: each has its own operation.

code.description: Short code of the warehouse, up to 20 characters of letters, digits and hyphens, stored trimmed and upper-cased. Omitting it keeps the current one. It stays unique among the LIVE warehouses of your company and never collides with the warehouse being edited.

name.description: Human-readable label of the warehouse, up to 120 characters.

type.description: Operational nature of the warehouse: `own`, `external`, `store` or `transit`.

address.description: COMPLETE postal address of the warehouse: sending the block REPLACES it whole, and omitting `line2` inside it clears that line.

line1.description: Street and number. Required as soon as the address block is sent.

line2.description: Second address line: unit, floor or door. Omitting it clears it.

city.description: Town or city. Required as soon as the address block is sent.

province.description: Province. Required as soon as the address block is sent.

postal_code.description: Postal code. Required as soon as the address block is sent.

country.description: Country as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Required as soon as the address block is sent: an address with no country can neither be delivered to nor validated.

UpdateWarehouseRequest.title: UpdateWarehouseRequest

api_version.description: New payload version (date-based, `YYYY-MM-DD`) pinned for the events delivered to this endpoint. Supported values: `2026-05-22`, `2026-10-01` and `2026-10-05`. Omit the field to keep the current value; send `null` to unpin the endpoint, which then receives the payload version of the default REST version (currently `2026-05-22`), never the latest one. Endpoints that existed before version `2026-10-01` was released were pinned to `2026-05-22`, so they keep receiving invoices in the previous vocabulary until you change this value. A value that is not a `YYYY-MM-DD` date returns 422 (subcode `api_version_invalid_format`), and an unsupported one 422 (subcode `api_version_unsupported`).

status.description: Optional endpoint status: `active` re-enables the endpoint and `disabled` pauses it; omit it to leave the status unchanged. `degraded` cannot be set by hand. Re-enabling an endpoint that was paused because its company tax ID was transferred to another account makes the caller its new owner, so the degraded-endpoint email reaches that person from then on.

name.description: Weekly schedule name. Optional: when omitted it keeps its current value.

mode.description: Schedule mode: `validated` (assumed fulfilled) or `real_clocking` (computed from real clock entries). Optional: when omitted it keeps its current value.

week_pattern.description: Full weekly pattern: list of days with their time ranges. Optional: when omitted the current pattern is kept; when sent it replaces the whole pattern.

day.description: Day of the week in ISO 8601 format (1 Monday .. 7 Sunday).

ranges.description: Time ranges for the day (empty = rest day).

end.description: Range end time (HH:MM; 24:00 is allowed as end of workday).

certificate_file.description: The digital certificate file in PKCS#12 format (`.p12` or `.pfx`).

UploadProductGalleryImageRequest.description: Upload an image to the product gallery as `multipart/form-data`: the `photo` field (`image` is accepted as an alias) — jpeg, png, jpg, gif or webp, max 3 MB.
UploadProductGalleryImageRequest.title: UploadProductGalleryImageRequest

UploadProductVideoRequest.description: Upload the product video as `multipart/form-data`: the `video` field — mp4, mov, avi or webm, max 50 MB.
UploadProductVideoRequest.title: UploadProductVideoRequest

files[].description: PDF, JPEG or PNG originals, one multipart part per file, each named `files[]`. At most 20 files, 20.0 MiB per file and 100.0 MiB per batch. Send the Idempotency-Key header; per-file rejection results use the same batch envelope even when status is 422.

file.description: Attachment file (multipart). The type is detected from the content, never from the extension.

target.description: Target: `comment` (default, creates a comment with the note and the attachment) or `description`.

note.description: Note of the comment that accompanies the attachment; only used with `target=comment`.

User.description: A member of your company: someone tasks can be assigned to.

id.description: UUID of the user.

object.description: Stripe-like discriminator. Always `user` for this resource.

User.title: User

UserList.description: Page of users (`{ data, has_more, next_cursor }`).

has_more.description: `true` when there are more objects after this page.

next_cursor.description: Value to pass as `starting_after` to get the next page (the `id` of the last object), or `null` when `has_more` is `false`.

VeriFactuActivity.description: An event in the activity timeline of a VeriFactu record (creation, transmission attempts, AEAT acceptance/rejection).

description.description: Human-readable description of the event in Spanish.
description.example: AEAT aceptó la transmisión del registro de alta.
examples: AEAT aceptó la transmisión del registro de alta.

metadata.description: Event metadata. Internal identifiers (PKs), `huella` and certificate secrets are stripped; `*_uuid` values are preserved.

type.description: Type of actor that originated the event: `user` for a human in the internal app, `api_key` for an action performed through the public v1 API.

id.description: UUID v7 of the actor: the user when `type=user`, or the API key when `type=api_key`.

name.description: Actor name at the time of the event: the user name or the API key name. `null` if it could not be resolved.

performed_by.description: Actor that originated the event. `{type:"user",...}` for an internal user, `{type:"api_key",...}` when performed via the public v1 API, or `null` when the event is system-generated (scheduler, periodic sweep) with no attributable actor.

VeriFactuActivity.title: VeriFactuActivity

VeriFactuConfig.description: VeriFactu configuration of your company (mode, environment, enrollment). Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/config` and `PATCH /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/settings`. The certificate password is never exposed.

enabled.description: Indicates whether VeriFactu is enabled for the company.

auto_transmit.description: Indicates whether transmissions to AEAT are sent automatically.

is_locked_until.description: Date until which the mode change is locked, or `null` if not locked.

has_active_certificate.description: Whether there is an active certificate configured.

active_certificate_id.description: UUID v7 of the active certificate, or `null` if there is none.

remission_mode.description: Who remits your records to AEAT: `own_certificate` (the default: your own certificate), `social_collaborator` (Factuarea remits with its certificate as social collaborator, annex I of the Resolution of 18-12-2024) or `power_of_attorney` (Factuarea remits under a power of attorney registered with AEAT). A third-party mode requires an active representation of the kind it asks for (`POST /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/representation`); change it with `PATCH /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/settings`.

has_active_representation.description: Whether the company has a current representation that has NOT expired — the one that enables third-party remission — regardless of the mode. A representation that has expired keeps `active_representation_id` and `_kind` but this field is `false` (see `active_representation_is_expired`).

active_representation_id.description: UUID v7 of the current (not revoked) representation, even if it has expired, or `null` if there is none.

active_representation_kind.description: Kind of the current (not revoked) representation, even if it has expired, or `null` if there is none.

active_representation_valid_until.description: Last day of validity (YYYY-MM-DD, Europe/Madrid) of the current representation, or `null` when there is none or it does not expire.

active_representation_is_expired.description: Whether the current representation has expired. `false` when there is none.

social_collaborator_available.description: Whether this instance offers the `social_collaborator` remission mode (the social-collaboration agreement with AEAT is in force). It is a fact of the instance, the same for every company: while it is `false`, `PATCH /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/settings` with that mode returns 422 `social_collaborator_unavailable` and `power_of_attorney` covers the same use case.

presenter_certificate_status.description: State of the certificate that the remission would present given `remission_mode`: yours in `own_certificate`, the one of Factuarea in a third-party mode. `valid`: usable; `invalid`: configured but expired, revoked or for another tax ID; `not_configured`: there is none. The certificate of Factuarea never exposes its holder, tax ID, serial number or identifier.

VeriFactuConfig.title: VeriFactuConfig

VeriFactuEvent.description: A VeriFactu SIF event (Art. 8.1.b): a transmission/retry/AEAT-response entry of the system. The hash chain is never exposed here.

id.description: UUID v7 of the event.

event_data.description: Non-PII descriptive data of the event (label, description, CSV, error code/message). Empty object `{}` when there is no data. Sanitized via MetadataSanitizer.

example.description: Transmisión de alta aceptada por AEAT.

examples.description: Transmisión de alta aceptada por AEAT.

status.description: AEAT status of the event.

VeriFactuEvent.title: VeriFactuEvent

VeriFactuEventSummary.description: Aggregated summary of the VeriFactu events of the company: total and breakdown by type and by status. Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/events/summary`.

last_event_at.description: Date of the last event, or `null` if there is none.

VeriFactuEventSummary.title: VeriFactuEventSummary

VeriFactuRecord.description: A VeriFactu (Spanish AEAT SIF) record (alta/anulación) associated with an invoice. Includes the hash chain (`huella`), AEAT CSV and transmission status for reconciliation.

id.description: UUID v7 of the VeriFactu record.

invoice_type.description: AEAT invoice type (F1, F2, F3, R1-R5, …).

amount.description: Total amount of the associated invoice.

status.description: Transmission status (pending, submitted, accepted, rejected, error).

huella.description: Chained SHA-256 fingerprint of the record (VeriFactu fingerprint).

aeat_submission_id.description: Submission identifier assigned by AEAT (column `aeat_submission_id`). `null` until AEAT returns it. Never the internal PK of the record.

aeat_csv.description: Secure Verification Code (Código Seguro de Verificación) returned by AEAT on acceptance. `null` until AEAT assigns it.

transmitted_at.description: ISO 8601 date of the last transmission that reached AEAT. `null` in PENDING/REJECTED/ERROR states.

is_substitute_for_simplified.description: Whether it substitutes one or more simplified invoices (F3).

aeat_error_code.description: Error code of the last AEAT rejection or failure (for example `1110` or `4112`), the internal code of a record that is stopped (`MISSING_CERTIFICATE`, `MISSING_REPRESENTATION`, `SYSTEM_CERTIFICATE_UNAVAILABLE`), `SCHEMA_INVALID` on a `rejected` record that was never sent because it does not meet the AEAT XML schema (fix it with a subsanation), or the warning code of a record accepted with errors; `null` when there is none. Without it you cannot tell a `4112` (presenter not enabled by AEAT) from a network failure.

is_blocked.description: Whether the record is BLOCKED: it is in `error` with NO automatic retry, so it does not go out again until someone reactivates it (fix the cause, then `POST /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/records/retry-blocked`, or `POST /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/records/{record}/retry` one by one), and it holds back the rest of the chain of the company. `false` for a record that retries by itself, with a backoff of at most one hour (art. 16.4 of Order HAC/1177/2024).

block_reason.description: Why the remission of the record is stopped, or `null`. `MISSING_CERTIFICATE`: your company has no usable certificate (missing, expired, revoked or for another tax ID). `MISSING_REPRESENTATION`: the remission mode is a third-party one and there is no current representation of the kind it asks for. `PRESENTER_NOT_ENABLED`: AEAT says the presenter is not enabled (`4112` or `3003`). `SUBMISSION_REJECTED`: AEAT rejected the submission for a client-side fault. These four need an action from you and make `is_blocked` true. `SYSTEM_CERTIFICATE_UNAVAILABLE`: the certificate of Factuarea that remits in the third-party modes is not available; it is on our side, does NOT block (`is_blocked` stays `false`) and the record retries by itself.

can_subsanar.description: Whether the record admits `POST /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/records/{record}/subsanar`: an `alta` that is ACCEPTED (or accepted with errors) or REJECTED by AEAT and is the last one of its invoice, which has not been annulled. It is the very rule that endpoint applies, so `true` guarantees it will not refuse the record by its state; whether there is something to correct and whether it changes a field of the hash (`requires_annulment`) is only known when you subsanar.

aeat_warning_requires_subsanation.description: For a record AEAT accepted with errors (`status` `accepted` with an `aeat_error_code`), whether AEAT requires a subsanation of that admissible error: every `2xxx` code does except `2004` (FechaHoraHusoGenRegistro) and `2009` (ClaveRegimen with IPSI), which AEAT exempts (AEAT «Validaciones» v1.2.2, §4.3.1). `false` for a warning that is not an AEAT code (`duplicate_annulled`: review the invoice instead). `null` when the record is not accepted with a warning.

VeriFactuRecord.title: VeriFactuRecord

VeriFactuStats.description: Aggregated summary of the VeriFactu records of the authenticated company: counts by status and breakdown by type. Returned by `GET /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/stats`.

submitted.description: Records submitted to AEAT (without a final response yet).

by_invoice_type.description: Count by AEAT invoice type (F1, F2, F3, …).

last_transmission_at.description: Date of the last transmission to AEAT, or `null` if there is none.

pending_incident_count.description: Records still waiting to be remitted to AEAT: `pending` (or without a state yet), `error` of ANY kind (those that retry by themselves and the blocked ones), `submitted` (in flight, or orphaned until the next sweep) and `rejected` records that have already been subsanados. NOT counted: `accepted`, `rejected` records still waiting for your correction, and sandbox (test mode) companies. The query filters never affect it. Art. 16 of Order HAC/1177/2024 requires the taxpayer to see how many records are pending.

blocked_incident_count.description: Of the pending records, the BLOCKED ones: `error` with NO automatic retry (missing certificate or representation, presenter not enabled by AEAT, or a client-side rejection). They do not go out until someone reactivates them (`POST /v1/companies/{company}/verifactu/records/retry-blocked`) and they hold back the chain of the company. It is a subset of `pending_incident_count`; the query filters never affect it.

oldest_pending_at.description: Generation timestamp of the oldest of the pending records counted by `pending_incident_count`, or `null` when there is none. The query filters never affect it.
